notes.label: n
notes.text: God doth not punish al ſinners preſently, but often differreth.

verses.text: <na>(o)</na> Vnleſſe you wil be conuerted, he shal shake his ſword; he hath bent his bow, and prepared it.

notes.label: o
notes.text: expecting if they wil amend.

verses.text: And in it he hath prepared the veſſels of death: he hath made his arrowes for them that burne. <cr>[1]</cr>
Behold <na>(p)</na> he hath bredde with iniuſtice: he hath conceiued ſorow, and brought forth iniquitie.

notes.label: p
notes.text: The iniurious perſecutor purpoſing iniuſtice, conceiueth enuie, and bringeth forth iniquitie. · Iſa. 59. Iob. 15.

verses.text: He hath opened a pit, and digged it vp: and he is fallen into the diche, which he made.
His <na>(q)</na> ſorrow shal be turned vpon his head: and his iniquitie shal deſcend vpon his crowne.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Enuie, & deſire to hurt others turneth to the ruine of the enuiers.

verses.text: I wil confeſſe to our Lord according to his iuſtice: and wil ſing to the name of our Lord moſt high.

chapters.summary: Dauid in confidence of his iuſt cauſe, and vniuſt perſecution. prayeth for Gods helpe, 7. and iuſt reuenge of his enemies. 15. deſcribing their malitious intention, and ruine. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David's prayer in tribulation.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end <na>(b)</na> for preſſes, the Pſalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Belonging to the newe Teſtament.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Suffering of Christ, and of Chriſtians.

verses.text: O LORD <na>(c)</na> our Lord, how meruelous is thy name in the whole earth! Becauſe thy magnificence is eleuated, aboue <na>(d)</na> the heauens.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God the lord of al by creation, is our ſingular lord, that beleue and truſt in him.

notes.label: d
notes.text: God more excelent then the heauens, he being the creator, they a creature.

verses.text: Out of the mouth of <na>(e)</na> infantes and ſucklinges, thou haſt perfected praiſe becauſe of thine enemies, that thou mayeſt deſtroy the enemie and reuenger. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: e
notes.text: fulfilled whē Chriſt coming into Ieruſalem, children ſang Ozanna Mat. 21. · Mat. 21.

verses.text: Becauſe I shal ſee thy heauens, the workes of thy fingers: the moone and the ſtarres, which thou haſt founded.
What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the ſonne of man, that thou viſiteſt him?
Thou haſt <na>(f)</na> minished him a litle leſſe then Angels; with <na>(g)</na> glorie and honour thou haſt crowned him: <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: f
notes.text: The Sonne in aſſumpted humāe nature became leſſe then Angels.

notes.label: g
notes.text: But in him mans nature is exalted aboue Angels.

verses.text: and haſt appointed him <na>(h)</na> ouer the worke of thy handes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Chriſt the Lord of al creatures.

verses.text: Thou haſt ſubiected <na>(i)</na> al thinges vnder his feete, al <na>(k)</na> sheepe and oxen: moreouer alſo the beaſtes of the field.

notes.label: i
notes.text: yea of Angels. Heb. 2.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Not only al reaſonable creatures, but al beaſtes, and other thinges obey him. The ſea and the windes obey him. Mat. 8.

verses.text: The birdes of the ayre, and fishes of the ſea; that walke the pathes of the ſea.
<na>(l)</na> O Lord our Lord, how meruelous is thy name in the whole earth!

notes.label: l
notes.text: The ſame end & beginning ſignifie, that as God was meruelous in creating man in ſo happie ſtate, that if he would, he might haue auoyded both ſinne & death: ſo he is meruelous in that he ſo rewardeth the bleſſed in the reſurrection, that they can neither ſinne non dye.

chapters.summary: God is magnified & praiſed for his meruelous worke of creatures, 5. but eſpecially of mankind, ſingularly exalted by the Incarnation of Chriſt. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt's Incarnation.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for the <na>(a)</na> ſecrets of the ſonne, the Pſalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Chriſts coming in humilitie, and Chriſtians afflictions, are hidden from the world, in Gods prouidence.

verses.text: I WIL <na>(b)</na> confeſſe to thee ô Lord with al my hart: I wil tel al thy meruelous thinges.

notes.label: b
notes.text: geue thanks.

verses.text: I wil be <na>(c)</na> glad and <na>(d)</na> reioyce in thee: I wil ſing to thy name ô moſt High.

notes.label: c
notes.text: in mind.

notes.label: d
notes.text: and bodie.

verses.text: In <na>(e)</na> turning mine enemie backward: they shal be weakened, and perish before thy face.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God repelleth the enemie, when man is not able to reſiſt.

verses.text: Becauſe thou haſt done <na>(f)</na> my iudgement and my cauſe: thou haſt ſitte vpon the throne which iudgeſt iuſtice.

notes.label: f
notes.text: A iuſt man doth his endeuour, not of him ſelfe, but by Gods grace ouercometh the enemie.

verses.text: Thou haſt rebuked the <na>(g)</na> Gentiles, and the impious hath perished: their <na>(h)</na> name thou haſt deſtroyed for euer, and for euer and euer.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Al ſinners called gentils, becauſe they were generally accounted wicked.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The vaine glorious fame of ſinners partly decayeth in this world but moſt eſpecially in the world to come.

verses.text: The ſwordes of the enemie haue fayled vnto the end: and their cities thou haſt deſtroyed.
Their memorie hath perished wirh a ſound: and our Lord abideth for euer. He hath prepared his throne in <na>(i)</na> iudgement:

notes.label: i
notes.text: Iudicial ſeates of men are often corrupted but Gods neuer.

verses.text: & he wil iudge the whole world in equitie, he wil iudge the people in iuſtice.
And our Lord is made a refuge for the poore: an helper <na>(k)</na> in opportunities, in tribulation.

notes.label: k
notes.text: God doth not preſently deliuer the good from afflictions: but when it is to their ſpiritual profite.

verses.text: And let them hope in thee that know thy name: becauſe thou haſt not forſaken them that ſeeke thee ô Lord.
Sing to our Lord, which dwelleth in Sion: declare his <na>(l)</na> ſtudies among the Gentiles:

notes.label: l
notes.text: His precepts which men ought chiefly to ſtudie.

verses.text: Becauſe he <na>(m)</na> requiring bloud remembred them: he hath not forgotten the crie of the poore.

notes.label: m
notes.text: God reuengeth the blood of Martyrs.

verses.text: Haue mercie on me ô Lord: See my humiliation <na>(n)</na> by my enemies.

notes.label: n
notes.text: procured by mine enemies.

verses.text: Which exalteſt me from the gates of death, that I may declare al thy prayſes in <na>(o)</na> the gates of the daughter of Sion.

notes.label: o
notes.text: In the publique view of the Church.

verses.text: I wil reioyce in thy ſaluation: the Gentiles are <na>(p)</na> faſtened in the deſtruction, which they made. In this ſnare, which they hid, is their foote taken.

notes.label: p
notes.text: The wicked are intangled in the ſnares which they lay for others.

verses.text: Our Lord shal be knowen doing iudgements: the ſinner is taken in the workes of his owne handes.
<na>(q)</na> Let ſinners be turned into hel, al nations that forget God.

notes.label: q
notes.text: As the firſt workes of Chriſt in al humility and patience were ſtrange, and hidden to the world: (v. 1.) ſo his laſt iudgement shal be in maieſty and manifeſt to al in exalting the bleſſed and ſuppreſſing the wicked.

verses.text: Becauſe to the end there shal not be obliuion of the poore man: the patience of the poore, shal not perish in the end.
Ariſe Lord, let not man be ſtrengthned: let the <na>(r)</na> Gentiles be iudged in thy ſight.

notes.label: r
notes.text: By Gentiles is often vnderſtood al great ſinners. For the Iewes deſpiſed Gentiles: as the Romans did al Barbarous nations.

verses.text: Appoint Lord <na>(s)</na> a lawgeuer ouer them: that the Gentiles may know that they be men.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Suffer a tyrant to rule ouer them that thereby they may lerne what it is to vſe others vniuſtly. It ſemeth to S. Auguſtine a prophecie, that ſuch as receiue not Chriſt, shal beleue Antichriſt.

verses.text: <na>(v)</na> Why Lord haſt thou departed far of, deſpiſeſt in opportunities, in tribulation?

notes.label: v
notes.text: In great perſecution it ſemeth to the weake, that God differreth his aſſiſtance very long.

verses.text: Whiles the impious is proude, the poore is <na>(w)</na> ſet on fyre: <na>(x)</na> they are caught in the counſels which they deuiſe.

notes.label: w
notes.text: Extremely vexed & tormented.

notes.label: x
notes.text: The Prophet anſwereth to the complaint of the iuſt, that in deede the wicked are caught in their owne ſnares.

verses.text: Becauſe the ſinner is prayſed in the deſires of his ſoule: and the vniuſt man is bleſſed.
The ſinner hath exaſperated our Lord, according to the multitude of his wrath he shal <na>(y)</na> not ſeeke.

notes.label: y
notes.text: not ſeeke to recouer Gods fauour.

verses.text: There is no God in his ſight: his waies are defiled at al time. Thy iudgementes are taken away from his face: he shal <na>(z)</na> rule ouer al his enemies

notes.label: z
notes.text: The wicked doth dominier for a time, and thinketh he shal do ſo ſtil.

verses.text: For he hath ſayd in his hart: I wil not be moued from generation vnto generation, <na>(a)</na> without euil.

notes.label: a
notes.text: and neuer fal into any aduerſitie but ſtil remaine without miſerie or anie euil.

verses.text: Whoſe mouth is ful of curſing, and bitterneſſe, and guile: vnder his tongue labour and ſorrow. <cr>[1]</cr>
He ſitteth in waite with the rich in ſecrete places, to kil the innocent.
His eyes looke vpon the poore: he lyeth in wayte in ſecret, as a lyon in his denne.
He lyeth in wayte to take the poore man violently: violently to take the poore man whiles he draweth him. In his ſnare he wil humble him ſelfe, and shal fal when he shal haue dominion ouer the poore.
For he hath ſayed in his hart; God hath forgotten, he hath turned away his face not to ſee for euer.
<na>(b)</na> Ariſe Lord God, let thy hand be axalted: forget not the poore.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The prayer of the iuſt in tribulation.

verses.text: Wherfore hath the impious prouoked God? for he hath ſaid in his hart; He wil not enquire.
Thou ſeeſt, that thou conſidereſt labour and ſorrow: that thou mayeſt deliuer them into thy handes. To thee is the poore left: to the orphane thou wilt be an helper
Breake the arme of the ſinner and malignant: his ſinne shal be ſought, and shal not be found.
Our Lord shal reigne for euer, and for euer and euer: ye <na>(c)</na> Gentiles shal perish from his land.

notes.label: c
notes.text: ye vileſt men.

verses.text: Our Lord hath heard the deſire of the poore: thy eare hath heard the <na>(d)</na> preperation of their hart,

notes.label: d
notes.text: The iuſt ought alwayes to be readie prepared in hart, to ſuffer patiently al that shal happen vnto them.

verses.text: To iudge <na>(e)</na> for the pupil and the humble, that man adde no more to magnifie him ſelfe vpon the earth.

notes.label: e
notes.text: As the firſt workes of Chriſt in al humility and patience were ſtrange, and hidden to the world: (v. 1.) ſo his laſt iudgement shal be in maieſty and manifeſt to al in exalting the bleſſed and ſuppreſſing the wicked.

chapters.summary: The Church prayſeth God for her protection, 4. in repelling the enemies force, 8. in punishing the wicked, and rewarding the iuſt. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence in protecting the good and permitting evil.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end the pſalme of Dauid I TRVST in our Lord: how ſay <na>(b)</na> ye to my ſoule: Paſſe ouer vnto the mountayne as a ſparrow?

notes.label: a
notes.text: S. Auguſtin applieth it to heretikes, perſwading Catholiques to repare vnto their ſeparate congregation, falſly calling it the montayne.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Ye my freindes ſay thus.

verses.text: For behold ſinners <na>(c)</na> haue bent the bow, they haue prepared their arrowes in the quiuer, that they may shoote in <na>(d)</na> the darke, at them that be right of hart.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Perſecuters vſing al rigor and force,

notes.label: d
notes.text: falſly pretēd other cauſes againſt the innocent to deſtroy them.

verses.text: For they haue <na>(e)</na> deſtroyed the thinges, which thou didſt perfite: but the iuſt what hath he done?

notes.label: e
notes.text: It is the maner of perſecuters, and eſpecially of heretikes, to deſtroy and pul downe that others haue built.

verses.text: Our Lord is in his holie temple, our Lord his ſeate is in heauen. <cr>[1]</cr>
His eies haue reſpect vnto the poore: his <na>(f)</na> eieliddes examine the ſonnes of men.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Though God ſeme to winke or ſleepe, yet his prouidence ſtil watcheth, and obſerueth al mens actions.

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(g)</na> examineth the iuſt, and the impious: but he that <na>(h)</na> loueth iniquity, hateth his owne ſoule.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Proueth by tribulations.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Continuance in ſinne bringeth damnation to the ſoule.

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> He shal rayne ſnares vpon ſinners: fyre and brimſtone, and blaſt of ſtormes the portion of their cuppe.

notes.label: i
notes.text: God ſparing for the time at laſt muſt needes of iuſtice punish ſeuerely.

verses.text: Becauſe our Lord is iuſt and hath loued iuſtice: his countenance hath ſeene equitie.

chapters.summary: Dauids freindes aduiſing him to flee from the perſecution of Saul, he anſwereth, that his truſt is in Gods protection. 2. Though the perſecutor be very malitious, 4. yet God wil ouerthrow him, 5. and deliuer the iuſt. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's provident care of the juſt.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end for <na>(b)</na> the octaue, the <na>(c)</na> Pſalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Chriſts firſt,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and laſt comming,

notes.label: c
notes.text: wil bring ioy to the elect.

verses.text: SAVE <na>(d)</na> me Lord, becauſe the holy hath fayled <na>(e)</na> becauſe verities are diminished from among the children of men.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Chriſt calleth his myſtical bodie, him ſelfe. Act. 9. v. 4.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Falſe and duble dealing hinder from true faith.

verses.text: They haue ſpoken vaine thinges euerie one to his neighbour, deiceitful lippes, they haue ſpoken in hart and hart,
Our Lord deſtroy al deceitful lippes, & the tongue that ſpeaketh <na>(f)</na> great thinges

notes.label: f
notes.text: Inſolent & arrogant.

verses.text: Which haue ſaid: We wil magnifie our tongue, our lippes are of vs, who is our Lord?
For the miſerie of the needie, and mourning of the poore, now wil I ariſe, ſaith our Lord: I wil put in <na>(g)</na> a ſaluation: I wil do confidently in him.

notes.label: g
notes.text: VVhen ſinne moſt abunded Chriſt came into this world: and in like caſe wil come to iudge.

verses.text: Wordes of our Lord, be chaiſt wordes: ſiluer examined by fire, tryed from the earth, purged ſeuen fold. <cr>[1]</cr>
Thou Lord wilt <na>(h)</na> preſerue vs: and keepe vs from this generation for euer.

notes.label: h
notes.text: yet ſtil there remaine ſome iuſt whom God preſerueth.

verses.text: The impious walke round about: according to thy highnes thou haſt <na>(i)</na> multiplied the children of men.

notes.label: i
notes.text: God ſometimes ſuffereth the wicked to do what euil they deſire.

chapters.summary: The Prophet deſcribeth the paucity of iuſt men, and abundanc of wicked, both at Chriſts firſt coming in flesh, 6. and ſecond in maieſtie, in the end of the world. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The ſtate of the Church in the firſt and laſt times of Chriſt.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, the Pſalme of Dauid. HOw long ô Lord wilt thou forget me vnto the end? How long doeſt thou turne away thy face from me?

notes.label: a
notes.text: It more perteyneth to the new teſtament then to the old.

verses.text: How long shal I put <na>(b)</na> counſels in my ſoule, ſorrow in my hart <na>(c)</na> by day?

notes.label: b
notes.text: Carful and almoſt perplex cogitatiōs by reaſon of long perſecution and mans weaknes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Very often euerie day.

verses.text: How long shal mine enemies be exalted ouer me? Regard and heare me ô Lord my God.
Illuminate mine eies that I ſleepe not <na>(d)</na> in death at any time: leſt ſometime mine enemie ſay: I haue preuailed againſt him.

notes.label: d
notes.text: fal not into mortal ſinne.

verses.text: They that truble me, wil reioyce if I be moued: but I haue hoped in thy mercie.
My hart shal reioyce in thy ſaluation: I wil ſing to our Lord which geueth me <na>(e)</na> good thinges: and I wil ſing to the name of our Lord moſt high.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Patience in tribulation, and reward for victory.

chapters.summary: A general prayer of the Church, in tribulation, either temporal or ſpiritual. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer in tribulation.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, the Pſalme of Dauid. THE <na>(a)</na> foole hath ſaid in his hart: There is no God. They are corrupt, and are become <na>(b)</na> abominable in their ſtudies: there is <na>(c)</na> not that doth good no not one. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: wicked men drowned in ſinne are at laſt ſo beſotted in their vnderſtanding, that they thinke in their hart (though they dare not vtter it) that there is no God: that is, none that hath diuine prouidence in gouerning the world, nor that wil iudge al in the end.

notes.label: b
notes.text: defiled with al ſortes of ſinne.

notes.label: c
notes.text: not only the moſt wicked, but alſo al mankind were vnable without a Redemer to do good.

verses.text: Our Lord hath looked forth from heauen vpon the children of men, to ſee if there be that vnderſtandeth, and ſeeketh after God.

Al haue declined, they are become <na>(d)</na> vnprofitable together: there is not that doth good, no not one. Their throte is an open ſepulchre: with theit tongues they did deceitfully, the poyſon of aſpes vnder their lippes. Whoſe mouth is ful of curſing and bitterneſſe: their feete ſwift to sheed bloud. <na>(e)</na> Deſtruction and infelicitie in their waies, and the way of peace they haue not knowen: there is no feare of God before their eies. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: d
notes.text: Without faith in Chriſt none had meritorious workes. · Theſe three verſes being not in the Hebrew, nor Greke, yet are in the Engliſh. an. 1577. and are three diſtinct verſes in other pſalmes. 5. 9. & 35.

notes.label: e
notes.text: They are wholly occupied in vexing others.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Shal not al they know that worke iniquitie, that deuoure my people <na>(g)</na> as foode of bread?

notes.label: f
notes.text: The Prophet ſpeaketh this in the perſon of God.

notes.label: g
notes.text: With greedines to hurt the good.

verses.text: They haue not inuocated our Lard, <na>(h)</na> there haue they trembled for feare, <na>(i)</na> where no feare was:

notes.label: h
notes.text: Not beleeuing in God, they feared Idols, that is, diuels:

notes.label: i
notes.text: who in dede can not hurt Gods ſeruants.

verses.text: Becauſe our Lord is in <na>(k)</na> the iuſt generation, you haue <na>(l)</na> confounded the counſel of the poore man: becauſe our Lord is his hope.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Though innumerable be very wicked, yet ſome are iuſt.

notes.label: l
notes.text: mocked and derided thoſe that trust in God.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> Who wil geue from Sion the ſaluation of Iſrael? when our Lord shal haue <na>(n)</na> turned away the captiuitie of his people, <na>(o)</na> Iacob shal reioyce, and <na>(p)</na> Iſrael shal be glad.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The Prophet wisheth, and withal prophecieth that Christ our Sauiour wil come, who is promiſed to Iſrael.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Redemed man from the captiuitie of the diuel.

notes.label: o
notes.text: thoſe that ſupplant vice

notes.label: p
notes.text: and contemplate God.

chapters.summary: After general groſſe ignorance and impiety in the World, 7. Chriſt shal be incarnate, the Redemer of mankind. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Of Chriſt's Incarnation.
The 5. key.

verses.text: The Pſalme of Dauid. LORD who shal dwel in <na>(a)</na> thy tabernacle? or who shal reſt in thy holie hil?

notes.label: a
notes.text: In heauē, as appeareth by the laſt verſe.

verses.text: He that walketh <na>(b)</na> without ſpot, and <na>(c)</na> worketh iuſtice.

notes.label: b
notes.text: One requiſite thing is to be free, or cleanſed from ſinne.

notes.label: c
notes.text: the ſecond is to do good.

verses.text: He that ſpeaketh truth in his <na>(d)</na> hart, that hath not done guile in his <na>(e)</na> tongue. Nor hath <na>(f)</na> done euil to his neighbour, and hath not taken <na>(g)</na> reproch againſt his neighbour,

notes.label: d
notes.text: Sincerely in thought,

notes.label: e
notes.text: word, and

notes.label: f
notes.text: dede:

notes.label: g
notes.text: nor harkened to detraction.

verses.text: The malignant is brought to nothing in his ſight; but them that feare our Lord, he <na>(h)</na> glorifieth: he that ſweareth to his neighbour, and deceiueth not,

notes.label: h
notes.text: Glorie is the reward of good workes.

verses.text: that hath not geuen his money to <na>(i)</na> vſurie, and hath not taken <na>(k)</na> giftes vpon the innocent: He that doeth theſe thinges, shal not be moued for euer.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Vſurie excludeth from heauen.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Likewise doing wrong for bribes.

chapters.summary: For attayning eternal glorie in heauen, it is neceſſarie to flee from ſinnes, and do good workes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Of eternal Beatitude.
The 10. key.

verses.text: The <na>(a)</na> inſcription of the title <na>(b)</na> to Dauid him ſelf. PRESERVE <na>(c)</na> me ô Lord, becauſe I haue hoped in thee.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Stylographia ſignifieth a thing moſt worthie to be noted, towitte, Chriſt crucified.

notes.label: b
notes.text: and moſt worthie of the prophets conſideration.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Chriſt as man did often pray, as appeareth in the Goſpel.

verses.text: I haue ſaid to our Lord: Thou art my God, becauſe thou <na>(d)</na> needeſt not my goods.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Chriſts paſſion was not needful nor profitable to God, but to man.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> To the ſainctes, that are in his land, he hath made al my willes meruelous in them.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God ſpeaketh shewing that Chriſt should make his meruelous charity knowen to his Apoſtles, and other ſeruantes.

verses.text: Their infirmities were <na>(f)</na> multiplied: afterward they <na>(g)</na> made haſt. I wil not aſſemble their <na>(h)</na> conuenticles of bloud: neither wil I be mindful of their <na>(i)</na> names by my lippes.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Men feeling their infirmities and miſeries,

notes.label: g
notes.text: make haſt in ſeeking remedies.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Sacrifices to idols shal ceaſe in Gentiles.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Their names shal be changed from heathen to be called Chriſtians.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> Our Lord the portion of myne inheritance, and of my <na>(l)</na> cuppe: thou art he, that wil reſtore myne inheritance vnto me.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Eternal glorie conſiſteth in ſeing God.

notes.label: l
notes.text: God is the reward of ſuffering paines for Chriſt.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> Cordes are fallen to me in goodly places: for <na>(n)</na> mine inheritance is goodlie vnto me.

notes.label: m
notes.text: In diuiſion of temporal inheritance, land is meaſured by cordes: as Ioſue 10. ſo portions in heauen are geuen with large meaſure.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Chriſt alſo receiued al nations for his inheritance.

verses.text: I wil bleſſe our Lord, who hath <na>(o)</na> geuen me vnderſtanding: moreouer alſo euen til <na>(p)</na> night, my <na>(q)</na> veines haue rebuked me.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Wiſdome to make good election of ſpiritual thinges rather then temporal.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Not only by day, but alſo by night.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Alſo my corporal paines geue me inſtruction.

verses.text: I <na>(r)</na> forſaw our Lord in my ſight alwaies: becauſe he is <na>(s)</na> at my right hand, that I be not moued. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: r
notes.text: Chriſt had God continually before his eyes: euerie man ought to thincke frequently of God.

notes.label: s
notes.text: for God ſtil protecteth the iuſt.

verses.text: For this thing my hart hath beene glad, and my tongue hath reioyced: moreouer alſo my flesh shal reſt in hope.

Becauſe thou wilt not leaue my ſoule in <na>(t)</na> hel: neither wilt geue <na>(v)</na> thy holie one to ſee corruption. <cr>[1]</cr>Thou haſt made <na>(w)</na> the waies of life knowen to me, thou shalt make me ful of ioy with <na>(x)</na> thy countenance: delectations on thy right hand, euen to <na>(y)</na> the end.

notes.label: t
notes.text: in limbo patrum.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Chriſts body corrupted not in the graue.

notes.label: w
notes.text: death and reſurrection is the way to life.

notes.label: x
notes.text: Perfect glorie conſiſteth in ſeing God.

notes.label: y
notes.text: in eternity.

chapters.summary: Chriſt, by the mouth of Dauid, declareth his future victory, and triumph ouer the world, 9. and death. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Of eternal Beatitude.
The 8. key.

verses.text: The prayer of Dauid. HEARE ô Lord my <na>(a)</na> iuſtice: attend my petition: With thine eares heare my prayer, <na>(b)</na> not in deceitful lippes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: in my iuſt cauſe heare my petition.

notes.label: b
notes.text: ſeing I pray ſincerly, not in feaned affection.

verses.text: From <na>(c)</na> thy countenanee let my iudgement procede: let thine eies ſee equities.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Thou that ſeeſt al thinge declare my right againſt mine aduerſaries.

verses.text: Thou haſt proued <na>(d)</na> my hart, and viſited it <na>(e)</na> by night: <na>(f)</na> by fire thou haſt examined me, <na>(g)</na> and there is no iniquitie found in me.

notes.label: d
notes.text: my intention

notes.label: e
notes.text: moſt ſecret cogitations.

notes.label: f
notes.text: by tribulations

notes.label: g
notes.text: whoſe conſcience is pure from greuous ſinne, may pray with this confidence, otherwiſe repentance is firſt neceſſarie. But the whole Church may euer pray in this maner, becauſe there be alwayes ſome iuſt and holy, in reſpect of whom it is truly called holy.

verses.text: That my mouth ſpeake not the workes of men: for the <na>(h)</na> wordes of thy lippes I haue kept the <na>(i)</na> hard wayes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: for thy precepts.

notes.label: i
notes.text: the narrow way of vertue.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> Perfite my paſes in thy pathes: that my ſteppes be not moued.

notes.label: k
notes.text: none can of them ſelues walke rightly, but by Gods helpe.

verses.text: I haue cried, becauſe thou haſt heard me ô God: incline thyne eare to me, and heare my wordes.
Make thy mercies meruelous, which ſaueſt them that hope in thee.
From them that reſiſt <na>(l)</na> thy right hand keepe me, as the apple of the eie. Vnder the shadowe of thy winges protect me:

notes.label: l
notes.text: againſt thy omnipotent powre.

verses.text: from the <na>(m)</na> face of the impious, that haue afflicted me. Mine enemies haue compaſſed my ſoule,

notes.label: m
notes.text: from their cruel and furious countenance.

verses.text: they haue shut vp their <na>(n)</na> fatte; their mouth hath ſpoken pride.

notes.label: n
notes.text: they haue shut out al pittie or commiſeration.

verses.text: Caſting me forth now haue they compaſſed me: they haue ſette their eies to bend them <na>(o)</na> vnto the earth.

notes.label: o
notes.text: They intend vtterly to deſtroy me euen to the ground.

verses.text: They haue taken me as a lion readie to the pray: and as a lions whelpe dwelling in hid places.
Ariſe Lord, <na>(p)</na> preuent him, and ſupplant him: deliuer my ſoule from the impious, <na>(q)</na> thy ſword

notes.label: p
notes.text: Except God preuent, mans induſtry is not ſufficient.

notes.label: q
notes.text: reſtraine their powre, which they haue by thy permiſſion, that they may not perſecute ſo much as they intend.

verses.text: from the enemies of thy hand. Lord from <na>(r)</na> a few out of the land diuide them, <na>(s)</na> in their life: their bellie is filled of <na>(t)</na> thy ſecretes. They are filled with children: and they haue leaft their remnantes to their litle ones.

notes.label: r
notes.text: This is a prophecy, that the wicked which are many, shal at the day of iudgement be ſeparated from the elect.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Which iudgement beginneth ſometimes in this life.

notes.label: t
notes.text: the pleaſures of this world, which God approueth not, nor acknowledgeth amongst good thinges.

verses.text: But <na>(v)</na> I in iuſtice shal appeare to thy ſight: I shal be <na>(w)</na> filled when thy glorie shal appeare?

notes.label: v
notes.text: the iuſt shal be approued.

notes.label: w
notes.text: Nothing doth ſatiate mans mind, but the ſight of God in eternal glorie.

chapters.summary: A iuſt mans prayer in tribulation, 10. deſcribing his enemies cruelty, 13. by way of imprecation foresheweth their deſtruction, 15. and declareth that the iuſt shal be ſatisfied in glorie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence protecting the juſt.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> to the ſeruant of our Lord Dauid, who ſpake to our Lord the wordes of this canticle, in the day, that our Lord deliuered him out of the hand of al his enemies, and out of the hand of <na>(c)</na> Saul, and he ſaid: (2. Reg. 22.) <na>[1]</na> I wil <na>(d)</na> loue thee ô Lord <na>(e)</na> my ſtrength:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Though literally this Pſalme perteyned to Dauid, yet in figure of Chriſt: and of the Church, or euerie iuſt ſoule.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The Holie Ghoſt inſpired Dauid to render theſe thankes for his often deliuerie from dangers.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Saul is ſpecially named becauſe he was his moſt potent worldlie enimie.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Theſe firſt wordes ( as alſo diuers others ) are added, and many changed in this and other Pſalmes by the Septuagint, who often leauing the Hebrew text render the ſenſe, and ſo this agreeth in ſubſtance with the ſame Pſalme recorded. 2. Reg. 22.

notes.label: e
notes.text: by whom I am ſtrong.

verses.text: Our Lord is my firmament, and my refuge, and my deliuere.
My God is my helper, and I wil hope in him. My protectour and the <na>(f)</na> horne of my ſaluation, and my receiuer. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: f
notes.text: high & firme ſaluation.

verses.text: Prayſing I wil inuocate our Lord: and I shal be ſaued from mine enemies.
The <na>(g)</na> ſorrowes of <na>(h)</na> death haue compaſſed me: and <na>(i)</na> torrentes of iniquitie haue trubled me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: This is aptly applied to al mankind after his fal, declaring our ſtate in ſinne, and inducing to penance, in the office of Maſſe on Septuageſima ſunday.

notes.label: h
notes.text: mortal flesh ſubiect to death.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Violent incurſions of tentions to ſinne.

verses.text: The ſorrowes of <na>(k)</na> hel haue compaſſed me: the <na>(l)</na> ſnares of death haue preuented me.

notes.label: k
notes.text: exceding great afflictiōs of mind, like to torments of hel, which I alſo feare.

notes.label: l
notes.text: ſecrete tentations haue deceiued me.

verses.text: In my tribulation I haue inuocated our Lord, and haue <na>(m)</na> cried to my God: And <na>(n)</na> he hath heard my voice from his holie temple: and my crie in his ſight, hath entered into his eares.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Earneſt prayer is the beſt remedie in al tribulations.

notes.label: n
notes.text: As it is certaine that God heard Dauids prayers; ſo he aſſuredly heareth al that ſincerly flee vnto him.

verses.text: The earth was shaken & trembled: the fundations of mountaines were trubled, and were moued, <na>(o)</na> becauſe he was wrath with them.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Gods anger againſt ſinne maketh high and loftie thinges to shake, euen the moſt obſtinate preſumptuous ſinners.

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> Smoke aroſe in his wrath: and fire flamed vp from his face: coles were kindled from him.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Diuine wrath is like to ſmoke of the noſethrles, or flaming fire, and burning coles.

verses.text: He <na>(q)</na> bowed the heauens, and deſcended: and <na>(r)</na> darkeneſſe vnder his feete.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Gods punishment ſometimes cometh ſo ſwiftly, as if the heauens bowed towards the earth.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Gods furie is as a darke deſolate night, or horrible miſt.

verses.text: And he <na>(r)</na> aſcended vpon the cherubs, and flew: he flew vpon the wings of windes.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Yet whẽ ſinners repēt God moſt ſpeedely, as fleing with winges of mercie, comforteth & protecteth them.

verses.text: And he put darkeneſſe his <na>(s)</na> couert, his tabernacle is round about him: darkeſome water in the cloudes of the aire.

notes.label: s
notes.text: God being in him ſelfe incõprehenſible, is alſo ſecret in his determinations, and couert in his procedinges or actes.

verses.text: Becauſe of the <na>(t)</na> brightneſſe in his ſight the cloudes paſſed, hayle and coles of fire.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Gods ſplēdor oppreſſing mãs ſenſe, yet inſtructeth him by his meruelous vvorkes. VVhich myſtically ſignifieth, that Chriſt illuminateth the vvorld by his Apoſtles, and other preachers denouncing his iuſtice, peace, and his vvil in al thinges perteyning to man.

verses.text: And our Lord thundered from heauen, and the Higheſt gaue his voice: haile and coles of fire.
And he shot his arrowes, and diſſipated them: he multiplied lightnings, and trubled them.
And the fountaynes of waters appeared, and the fundations of the world were reueled. At thy rebuke ô Lord, at the blaſt of the ſpirit of thy wrath.
He ſent from on high, and tooke me: and he receiued me out of manie <na>(v)</na> waters.

notes.label: v
notes.text: from tribulations.

verses.text: He deliuered me <na>(w)</na> from my moſt ſtrong enemies, and from them that hated me: becauſe they were made ſtrong ouer me.

notes.label: w
notes.text: From Saul, Abſolō, Moabites, Ammonites, and al temporal and ſpiritual enemies.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> They preuented me in the day of mine affliction: and our Lord was made my protectour.

notes.text: So in the reſt of this Pſalme the Prophet ſpeaketh for moſt part in proper termes, vvithout Metaphores or other figures. Yet in the myſtical ſenſe of Chriſt, and Chriſtians.

verses.text: And he brought me out into largeneſſe: he ſaued me, becauſe he <na>(x)</na> would me.

notes.label: x
notes.text: Of his good pleaſure without my deſertes.

verses.text: And our Lord wil reward me according to my iuſtice, and according to the purity of my handes he wil reward me.
Becauſe I haue kept the waies of our Lord, neither haue I done impiouſly from my God.
Becauſe al his iudgementes are in my ſight: and his iuſtices I haue not repelled from me.
And I shal be immaculate <na>(y)</na> with him; and shal keepe me from mine iniquitie.

notes.label: y
notes.text: by his grace

verses.text: <na>(z)</na> And our Lord wil reward me according to my iuſtice: and according to the puritie of my handes in the ſight of his eies.

notes.label: z
notes.text: He repeteth the 21. verſe, inculcating that God wil render to euerie one as they deſerue.

verses.text: With the holie thou shalt be holie, and with the innocent man thou shalt be innocent.
And with the elect thou shalt be elect: and with the peruerſe thou shalt be peruerted.
Becauſe thou wilt ſaue the humble people: and the eies of the proud thou wilt humble.
Becauſe thou doſt illuminate my lampe ô Lord: my God illuminate my darkeneſſe.
Becauſe in thee I shal be deliuered from tentation, and in my God I shal <na>(a)</na> goe ouer the wal.

notes.label: a
notes.text: paſſe ouer al difficulties.

verses.text: My God his <na>(b)</na> way is vnpolluted: the wordes of our Lord are examined by fire: he is protector of al that hope in him.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Gods precepts.

verses.text: For <na>(c)</na> who is God but our Lord? or who is God but our God?

notes.label: c
notes.text: One only God, Creator and Sauiour of al.

verses.text: God that girded me with ſtrength: and made my way immaculate.
That perfited my feete as it were of hartes: and ſetting me vpon high thinges.
That teacheth my handes to battel: and haſt put mine armes, <na>(d)</na> as a bow of braſſe.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Amongſt other actes, Dauid killed a lion, and a beare, & Goliath. 1. Reg. 17.

verses.text: And haſt geuen me the protection of thy ſaluation: and thy right hand hath receiued me: And thy diſcipline hath corrected me vnto the end: and thy diſcipline the ſame shal teach me.
Thou haſt enlarged my paſes vnder me: and my ſteppes are not weakened:
I wil purſew myne enemies, and ouertake them: and wil not returne til they faile.
I wil breake them, neither shal they be able to ſtand: they shal fal vnder my feete.
And thou haſt girded me with ſtrength to battel: and haſt ſupplanted them that riſe againſt me vnder me.
And <na>(e)</na> myne enemies thou haſt geuen me their backe, and them that hate me thou haſt deſtroyed.

notes.label: e
notes.text: As God geueth ſtreingth to his ſeruāts; ſo he diminisheth the natural ſtreingth and corage of his enemies.

verses.text: They cried, neither was there that would ſaue them, to our Lord; neither did he heare them.
And I wil breake them to powder, as the duſt before the face of winde: as the durt of the ſtreates I wil deſtroy them.
Thou wilt deliuer me from the contradictions of the people: thou wilt appoynte me to be head of the Gentiles.
A people, <na>(f)</na> which I knew not, hath ſerued me: in the hearing of the eare it hath obeyed me.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Conuerſion of Gentiles to Chriſt, as the Moabites, Idumeans, and others were ſubdued by Dauid. 1. Par. 11. 14. 18. 19. 20.

verses.text: The <na>(g)</na> children being alienes haue lyed to me, the children alienes are inueterated, and haue halted from their pathes.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The reuolting and reprobation of the Iewes prefigured by Abſolons rebellion and others. 2. Reg. 15. 16.

verses.text: Our Lord liueth, and bleſſed be my God, and the God of my ſaluation be exalted.
O God <na>(h)</na> which geueſt me reuenges, & ſubdeweſt peoples vnder me, my deliuerer from mine angrie enemies.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God ſtil protecteth the Church of Chriſt, as he preſerued Dauid.

verses.text: And from them that riſe vp againſt me thou wilt exalt me: from the vniuſt man thou wilt deliuer me.
Therfore wil I confeſſe to thee among nations ô Lord: and wil ſay <na>(i)</na> a pſalme to thy name,

notes.label: i
notes.text: Vſe of Pſalmes is most frequent in the Church of Gentiles. See the proemial Annotations. page. 12.

verses.text: Magnifying the ſaluations of his king, and doing mercie to his Chriſt Dauid, and to his ſeede for euer.

chapters.summary: King Dauids thankes to God for his often deliuerie from great dangers, firſt in general, 9. then more particularly deſcribeth Gods terrible maner of fighting for him, 18. againſt his cruel, and otherwiſe potent enimies: 22. attributing the ſame to Gods good pleaſure, and iuſtice of his cauſe, 31. praiſeth God, 33. his only protector. 41. and depreſſer of his enemies. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David ſingularly protected by God.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, the pſalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: perteyning to the beloued of the new Teſtament.

verses.text: THE <na>(b)</na> heauens shew forth the glorie of God, and the firmament declareth the workes of his handes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The ſilent workes of God declare his Maieſtie to them that conſider therof; his preachers declare the ſame by wordes, to al that wil heare.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Day vnto day vttereth word: and night vnto night sheweth knowledge.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The conſtant courſe of times sheweth that the ſame was diſpoſed by Gods powre, and dayly propagation of faith, eſpecially of Chriſtian doctrine sheweth Chriſts powre, & aſſured perpetuitie of his Church.

verses.text: There are <na>(d)</na> no languages, nor ſpeaches, whoſe voyces are not heard.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Some of euery language or natiõ haue beleued in Chriſt, receiuing the Catholique Religion.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Their ſound hath gone forth into al the earth; and vnto the endes of the round world the wordes of them.

notes.label: e
notes.text: S. Paul affirmeth that this hath bene fulfilled by the Apoſtles preaching in al the world. Rom. 10.

verses.text: He put his tabernacle in <na>(f)</na> the ſunne: & himſelf as a <na>(g)</na> bridgrome coming forth of his bridechamber. He hath reioyced as a giant to runne the way,

notes.label: f
notes.text: By the ſunne a moſt excellent and ſuperelemental creature, the Prophet deſcribeth Chriſt, making his courſe through this world, illuminating, comforting and ſtreingthning the Church his tabernacle, wherein he perpetually dwelleth.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Chriſt the bridgrome, and the Church his bride are neuer diuorſed; his loue, wiſdome, and powre, euer conſeruing her by his immaculute law.

verses.text: his comming forth from the toppe of heauen: And his recourſe euen to the toppe therof: neither is there that can hide him ſelfe from his heate.
The law of our Lord is immaculate <na>(h)</na> conuerting ſoules: the teſtimonie of our Lord is faithful, geuing wiſedome to litle ones.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The old law was likewiſe pure in it ſelfe and holy, but the new alſo maketh the obſeruers immaculate.

verses.text: The iuſtices of our Lord be right, making hartes ioyful: the precept of our Lord lightſome; illuminating the eies.
The feare of our Lord is holie, permanent for euer and euer: the iudgmentes of our Lord be true, iuſtified in themſelues.
To be deſired aboue gold and much pretious ſtone: and more ſweete aboue honie and the honie combe.
For thy ſeruant <na>(i)</na> keepeth them, in keeping them is <na>(k)</na> much reward.

notes.label: i
notes.text: How ſwete the law of God is, his ſeruantes finde not by reading, or by hearing only, but by keping it.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Conformably to this text the prophete profeſſeth (Pſal. 118. v. 12.) that he kept them for reward, in which place the heretikes tranſlation is corrupted.

verses.text: Sinnes <na>(l)</na> who vnderſtandeth? from my ſecrete ſinnes cleanſe me:

notes.label: l
notes.text: None in this life knoweth and feareth perfectly his owne eſtate, whether he be worthie of loue or hate, Eccle. 9 but hopeth.

verses.text: and from other mens ſpare thy ſeruant. If <na>(m)</na> they shal not haue dominion ouer me, then shal I be immaculate; and shal be cleanſed from the greateſt ſinne.

notes.label: m
notes.text: If mortal ſinnes haue not dominion in the ſoule it is iuſt: and shal be in time immaculate from al ſinne.

verses.text: And the wordes of my mouth shal be ſuch as may pleaſe: and the meditation of my hart in thy ſight alwayes. O Lord <na>(n)</na> my helper, and my <na>(o)</na> redemer.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Gods helping grace is ſtil neceſſarie to perſeuer,

notes.label: o
notes.text: as his firſt grace redeeming man is neſſarie for our firſt conuerſion,

chapters.summary: Gods perfect goodnes and glorie is shewed by his great workes, and by his Apoſtles ſent with heauenlie commiſſion, to preach in al tongues to al nations. 6. Chriſt coming into the world, and returne vnto heauen. 8. his immaculate Law: 13. Wherin notwiſtanding the iuſt shal haue nede to pray for remiſſion of ſmaller and daylie ſinnes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: Propagation of the Catholic faith.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, the Pſalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Though ſuch a prayer was very fitly made for Dauid, Ezechias, or other kinges of Iuda, yet it more properly ſerueth for Chriſtian Kinges and Prelates.

verses.text: OVr Lord heare <na>(b)</na> thee in the day of tribulation: the name of the God of Iacob protect thee.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The king, or other ſuperior praying for him ſelfe, his ſubiects pray with him, and for him. It may alſo be applied to Chriſt, praying whiles he vvas mortal, or novv praying for his myſtical body the Church, but in both theſe caſes, our prayers are only neceſſary for his ſeruantes not for him.

verses.text: Send he ayde to thee from the holie place: and from Sion defend he thee.
Be he mindeful of al thy <na>(c)</na> ſacrifice: and be thy holocauſt made <na>(d)</na> fatte.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The Hebrevv vvord MINCA ſignifieth ſacrifice of floure, and vnbloudy, ſo perteyneth to the Euchariſt, in forme of bread, and vvine.

notes.label: d
notes.text: be acceptable for him, for vvhom it is offered.

verses.text: Geue he vnto thee according to thy hart: and confirme he al thy counſel.
We shal reioyce <na>(e)</na> in thy ſaluation: and in the name of our God we shal be magnified.

notes.label: e
notes.text: in the proſperous ſtate of thee our ſuperiour.

verses.text: Our Lord accomplish al thy petitions: now haue I knowen that our Lord hath ſaued <na>(f)</na> his <sc>CHRIST</sc>. He shal heare him from his holie heauen: the ſaluation of his righthand is, <na>(g)</na> in powers.

notes.label: f
notes.text: his anointed king, or Prieſt, Myſtically faithful people acknovvlege the victory of Chriſt our Sauiour ouer death and al enemies.

notes.label: g
notes.text: in great ſtreingth, or heauenlie forces.

verses.text: Theſe in chariotes, and theſe in horſes: but we wil inuocate in the name of the Lord our God.
<na>(i)</na> They are bound, and haue fallen: but we haue riſen and are ſet vpright.

notes.label: i
notes.text: men truſting in humane and worldly powre fal into captiuitie.

verses.text: Lord <na>(k)</na> ſaue the king, and heare vs in the day, that we shal inuocate thee.

notes.label: k
notes.text: By protection of the head the body is alſo conſerued.

chapters.summary: Faithful people ioyne their prayer, for their Prince or Prelate, 4. with ſacrifice offered for his preſeruation, and proſperous ſucceſſe. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The ſubiects prayer for their ſuperior.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, the Pſalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the nevv Teſtament, principally to Chrriſt, partly to godly and victorious kinges, and generally to al the bleſſed, vvhich ouercome ſpiritual enemies.

verses.text: LOrd in <na>(b)</na> thy power the king shal be glad: and vpon thy ſaluation he shal reioyce excedingly.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Chriſt our king as man ouercoming his enemies by his diuine povvre, reioyceth in victorie.

verses.text: The <na>(c)</na> deſire of his hart thou haſt geuen him: and of the wil of his lippes thou haſt not defrauded him.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Chriſts moſt ſpecial deſire was the ſaluation of his people.

verses.text: Becauſe thou haſt <na>(d)</na> preuented him in bleſſinges of ſweetneſſe: thou haſt put on his head a crowne of pretious ſtone.

notes.label: d
notes.text: This moſt principally verified in Chriſt, is alſo applied to Martyres, vvhich ſuffer or are readie in preparation of mind to ſuffer death for the truth.

verses.text: He asked life of thee: and thou gaueſt him length of daies for euer, and for euer and euer.
Great is his glorie in thy ſaluation: glorie and great beautie thou shalt put vpon him.
Becauſe thou shalt geue him <na>(e)</na> to be a bleſſing for euer and euer: thou shalt make him ioyful in gladeneſſe with thy countenance.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Al Sainctes receiue bleſſing of glorie, but only Chriſt imperteth ſuch grace to others: for in him al are bleſſed that are eternally glorified. Gen. 21. Ioan. 1.

verses.text: Becauſe the king hopeth in our Lord: and in the mercie of the Higheſt he shal not be moued.
Let <na>(f)</na> thy hand be found of al thy enemies: let thy righthand find al, that hate thee.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The iuſt conforming their deſires to Gods vvil, do pray that the vvicked may be punished. It is alſo a prophecie, that ſo it shal come to paſſe.

verses.text: Thou <na>(g)</na> shalt put them as an ouen of fyre <na>(h)</na> in the time of thy countenance: our Lord in his wrath <na>(i)</na> shal truble them, and fyre shal deuoure them.

notes.label: g
notes.text: And ſo it folovveth in the next verſe: Thou shalt put them &c.

notes.label: h
notes.text: This alſo can not be vnderſtood of anie but of Chriſt, vvho in the general or particular iudgement ſhal geue ſentence vpon the vvicked.

notes.label: i
notes.text: And immediatly hel fire shal deuoure them.

verses.text: Their <na>(k)</na> fruite thou shalt deſtroy from the land: and their ſeede from the children of men.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Al the wicked, and namely the Iewes who perſecuted Chriſt, faile in their deuiſes.

verses.text: Becauſe they haue turned the euils vpon thee: they haue deuiſed counſels, which they could not eſtablish.
Becauſe thou shalt put them backe: in thy remnantes thou shalt prepare their countenance.
Be exalted Lord in thy powre: <na>(l)</na> we wil chaunte and ſing thy powers.

notes.label: l
notes.text: whiles the wicked perish, the iuſt reioyce and praiſe God in ſongue and Pſalme.

chapters.summary: Praiſe to God for Chriſts exaltation after his paſſion: 9. and depreſſion of his enemies. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt's exaltation.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end for the <na>(a)</na> morning enterpriſe, the Pſalme <na>(b)</na> of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Redemptiõ of mankind vndertakē by Chriſt, and performed by his death, beganne to be shewed by his Reſurrection in the morning of the third day. S. Aug.

notes.label: b
notes.text: in figure of Chriſt the beloued of God.

verses.text: GOD <na>(c)</na> my God haue reſpect to me: <na>(d)</na> why haſt thou forſaken me? <na>(e)</na> far from my ſaluation are the wordes of my ſinnes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God is God of al his creatures, but in more peculiar ſorte God of Chriſt by perſonal vnion.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Thou neither deliuereſt me frõ dying: nor yeldeſt me ſuch comforth, as thou voutſafeſt to other Sainctes. · v. 6. Mat. 27.

notes.label: e
notes.text: I am neither deliuered from dying, nor comforted in my paſſion, hauing vndertaken to dye for the ſinnes of mankind, & reputed them as myn owne wordes or factes.

verses.text: My God I shal crie <na>(f)</na> by day, <na>(g)</na> and thou wilt not heare: and by night, and <na>(h)</na> not for follie vnto me.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Albeit I crie by day,

notes.label: g
notes.text: and by night, on the croſſe and in the garden, to haue the chalice of death remoued from me, and shal not be heard,

notes.label: h
notes.text: Yet there is no follie, nor fault in this petition, which is with ſubmiſſion of mans wil to Gods wil.

verses.text: But <na>(i)</na> thou dwelleſt in the holie place, <na>(k)</na> the prayſe of Iſrael.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thou from heauen wilt heare when it is conuenient.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Whoſe wiſdome and goodnes the Church worthely praiſeth.

verses.text: In thee <na>(l)</na> our fathers haue hoped: they hoped, and thou didſt deliuer them.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Patriarkes, Prophets, and other holy mẽ praying in their diſtreſſes obtained their requeſtes.

verses.text: They cried to thee, and were <na>(m)</na> ſaued: they hoped in thee, and were <na>(n)</na> not confounded.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Were temporally deliuered by thy mightie hand from their perſecuters.

notes.label: n
notes.text: not fruſtrate of their humble prayers.

verses.text: <na>(o)</na> But I am a <na>(p)</na> worme and no man: a <na>(q)</na> reproch of men and <na>(r)</na> outcaſt of the people.

notes.label: o
notes.text: God that comforted his ſeruantes in their tribulations, leift Chriſt without his ordinarie conſolation, to ſuffer more then euer any other did.

notes.label: p
notes.text: wicked perſecuters reſpected not Chriſt as a man, but contemned him, as a very worme

notes.label: q
notes.text: as moſt reprochful of al men.

notes.label: r
notes.text: as the baſeſt of al the people.

verses.text: <na>(s)</na> Al that ſee me haue ſcorned me: they haue ſpoken with the lippes, and wagged the head.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Almoſt al became Chriſts cruel enimies at the time of his paſſion, afflicting, blaſpheming, and ſcorning him, as the Euangeliſtes record.

verses.text: <na>(t)</na> He hoped in the Lord, let him deliuer him: let him ſaue him, becauſe he <na>(v)</na> wil him.

notes.label: t
notes.text: The Euangeliſtes write how al theſe thinges were fulfilled by wicked men ſpeaking theſe blaſphemies, and reproches.

notes.label: v
notes.text: God ſemed to be wel pleaſed with Chriſt, as with his owne Sonne: if it be ſo, let him deliuer him from theſe afflictions, ſay theſe blaſphemers.

verses.text: Becauſe thou art he that <na>(w)</na> haſt drawen me out of the wombe: my hope from the breſtes of my mother.

notes.label: w
notes.text: diuine powre without man formed me in the wombe of my mother a virgin.

verses.text: Vpon thee I <na>(x)</na> haue bene caſt from the matrice: <na>(y)</na> from my mothers wombe thou art my God,

notes.label: x
notes.text: As I haue no father but thee O God: ſo without intermiſſion from myn incarnation to this time, I haue had thee my protector:

notes.label: y
notes.text: leaue me not now without comforte ſeing I muſt dye as thou haſt determined, and I freely conſented: yet leaue me not in death but raiſe me againe to life. Pſal. 15. v. 9. 10.

verses.text: depart not from me. Becauſe tribulation is verie nigh: becauſe there is <na>(z)</na> not that wil helpe.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Almoſt al are become myn enemies, and thoſe few that would, can not helpe me.

verses.text: Manie <na>(a)</na> calues haue compaſſed me: <na>(b)</na> fatte bulles haue beſieged me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Delicate laſciuious yongmen,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and the ſcribes Phariſes and elders of the people haue al conſpired againſt me.

verses.text: They haue <na>(c)</na> opened their mouth vpon me, as a lion rauening and roaring.

notes.label: c
notes.text: condemning me and perſwading the people to crie: Crucifie, crucifie him.

verses.text: As <na>(d)</na> water I am powred out: and al <na>(e)</na> my bones are diſperſed. <na>(f)</na> My hart is made as waxe melting in the middes of my bellie.

notes.label: d
notes.text: So weakned with paines of torments, as fluide water not able to conſiſt.

notes.label: e
notes.text: My bones and ſtrongeſt partes of my bodie are weakned, verified, when our Sauiour fel downe vnder his croſſe.

notes.label: f
notes.text: the part that firſt and laſt liueth is weakened as ſoft waxe by heat of the fire, and ready to faile.

verses.text: My ſtrength is withered as a <na>(g)</na> pot-shard, and my tongue <na>(h)</na> cleaued to my iawes: and thou haſt <na>(i)</na> brought me downe into the duſt of death.

notes.label: g
notes.text: al my powres, and radical humiditie is dried vp, as a potters veſſel is baked in the furnace.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Through exceding great drught, which our Sauiour profeſſed on the croſſe ſaying: I thirſt.

notes.label: i
notes.text: thus thou O God haſt ſuffered me to come to the laſt breath of life, next to death. Yet finally our Sauiour gaue vp his ſpirite, before he ſhould haue died. v. 21.

verses.text: Becauſe manie <na>(k)</na> dogges haue compaſſed me: the counſel of the malignant hath beſieged me. They haue digged my handes and my feete:

notes.label: k
notes.text: Agane this royal Prophet recounteth by whom, and how our B. Sauiour ſhould ſuffer, euen as clere as the Euangeliſtes afterwards haue written the hiſtorie.

verses.text: they haue <na>(l)</na> numbered al my bones. But themſelues haue <na>(m)</na> conſidered and beheld me:

notes.label: l
notes.text: Ioan. 19. · Our Sauiours body was ſo racked on the croſſe, that his bones might be ſeene and counted.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The perſecuters vvittingly determined al this crueltie, beheld it vvith their eyes, and vvithout al compaſſion perſiſted in malice, reioyced, and blaſphemed.

verses.text: they haue <na>(n)</na> deuided my garmentes among them, and vpon my <na>(o)</na> veſture they haue caſt lot.

notes.label: n
notes.text: the ſouldiars that crucified our Sauiour, taking his garmentes for their praye:

notes.label: o
notes.text: yet in myſterie of his Church, diuided not his coate.

verses.text: But thou Lord <na>(p)</na> prolong not thy helpe from me: looke toward my defenſe.

notes.label: p
notes.text: He prophecieth Chriſts ſpeedy reſurrection.

verses.text: Deliuer, ô God, <na>(q)</na> my ſoule from the ſword: and myne <na>(r)</na> onlie one from <na>(s)</na> the hand of the dog.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Chriſts ſaul vvas not ſeperated from his bodie by force of the torments, but he preuenting death freely yelded vp his ſpirite. Ioan. 10. v. 9. & 10.

notes.label: r
notes.text: the moſt pure, and ſanctified ſoule, of vvhoſe fulnes al other iuſt ſoules are ſanctified:

notes.label: s
notes.text: that it ſtay not in hel, vvhich deuoured al other ſoules in the old Teſtament.

verses.text: Saue me out of the lions mouth: and my humilitie from the hornes of vnicornes.
I wil <na>(t)</na> declare thy name to my bretheren: in the middes of the Church I wil prayſe thee.

notes.label: t
notes.text: The propagation of the Church of Chriſt in al nations.

verses.text: Ye that feare our Lord praiſe him: al the <na>(v)</na> ſeede of Iacob glorifie ye him:

notes.label: v
notes.text: not the carnal but ſpiritual children of Iacob, Iſaac, and Abraham. Rom. 9. v. 8.

verses.text: Let al the ſeede of Iſrael feare him: becauſe he hath not contemned, nor deſpiſed the petition of the poore. Neither hath he turned away his face from me: and when I cried to him he heard me.
With thee is my praiſe in <na>(w)</na> the great Church: I <na>(x)</na> wil render my vowes in the ſight of them that feare him.

notes.label: w
notes.text: the Church gethered both of Ievves and Gentiles is very great and vniuerſal.

notes.label: x
notes.text: Our Sauiour promiſed to geue his ovvne bodie, the bread of life Ioan. 6. and performed the ſame at his laſt ſupper.

verses.text: The <na>(y)</na> poore shal eate, and shalbe filled: and they shal praiſe our Lord that ſeeke after him: their hartes <na>(z)</na> shal liue for euer and euer.

notes.label: y
notes.text: thoſe that be faithful, humble and poore in ſpirit participat the fruict of this moſt excellent Sacrament.

notes.label: z
notes.text: The effect of this B. Sacrament is the reſurrection in glorie, and life euerlaſting.

verses.text: Al the endes of the earth <na>(a)</na> shal remember, and be conuerted to our Lord: And al the families of the Gentiles shal adore in his ſight.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Gentiles which haue bene idolaters shal recollect themſelues, when they heare Chriſt preached, and shal turne to true Religion.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Becauſe the kingdome is our Lords: and he shal haue dominion ouer the Gentiles.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Although men can neither deſerue to be conuerted, nor to perſeuere in iuſtice; yet Chriſt meriteth to haue a continual kingdom; which is the perpetual viſible Catholique Church.

verses.text: Al the <na>(c)</na> fatte ones of the earth haue eaten, and <na>(d)</na> adored: in his ſight shal al fal, <na>(e)</na> that deſcend into the earth.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Not only the poore ſorte, but alſo the mightie ones of the world shal be conuerted to Chriſt, participate his B. Bodie in the Sacrament:

notes.label: d
notes.text: and religiouſly adore the ſame.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Al that adore God, ſhad adore him in this Sacraments.

verses.text: And <na>(f)</na> my ſoule shal liue to him: and my <na>(g)</na> ſeede shal ſerue him.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Death being once ouercome, it shal haue no more powre.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Againe the prophet inculcateth the continuance of the Catholique Church.

verses.text: The generation to come shal be shewed to our Lord: and the <na>(h)</na> heauens shal shew forth his iuſtice to the people that shal be borne, whom our Lord hath made.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Apoſtles, and other preachers of Chriſt.

chapters.summary: Chriſt prayeth in his Paſſion, 7. deſcribeth the acerbitie therof; 20. foresheweth by way of prayer his Reſurrection: 23. more clerly the fundation and propagation of his Church ( 27. & 30. interpoſing the ſingular foode of the moſt bleſſed Sacrament ) euen to the endes of the earth in al nations. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt's Paſſion & effects thereof.
The 5. key.

verses.text: The Pſalme of Dauid. OVr <na>(a)</na> Lord ruleth me, and nothing shal be wanting to me:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Chriſt the good paſtor, gouerneth, protecteth,

verses.text: in place <na>(b)</na> of paſture there he hath placed me <cr>[1]</cr>. Vpon <na>(c)</na> the water of refection he hath brought me vp:

notes.label: b
notes.text: and feedeth his faithful flocke.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Baptiſme of regeneration,

verses.text: he hath <na>(d)</na> conuerted my ſoule. He hath conducted me vpon <na>(e)</na> the pathes of iuſtice, <na>(f)</na> for his name.

notes.label: d
notes.text: which is the firſt iuſtification.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Gods precepts which the baptiſed muſt obſerue. Mat. 28. v. 20.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Saluation is in the name and powre of Chriſt, not in mans owne merites.

verses.text: For, although I shal walke in <na>(g)</na> the middes of the shadow of death, I wil <na>(h)</na> not feare euils: becauſe thou art with me. Thy <na>(i)</na> rod and thy <na>(k)</na> ſtaffe: they haue comforted me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: in great dangers of tentations to mortal ſinne,

notes.label: h
notes.text: yet by Gods grace we may reſiſt.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Gods direction and law is ſtreight,

notes.label: k
notes.text: and ſtrong.

verses.text: Thou haſt prepared in my ſight <na>(l)</na> a table, <na>(m)</na> againſt them; that truble me. Thou <na>(n)</na> haſt fatted my head with oyle: and my <na>(o)</na> chalice inebriating how goodlie is it!

notes.label: l
notes.text: Chriſt hath prepared for our ſpiritual foode the B. Sacrament of the Euchariſt. S. Cyprian. Epiſt. 63. Eutim. in hunc Pſal.

notes.label: m
notes.text: againſt al ſpiritual enemies, the world, the flesh, and the diuel.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Chriſtian ſoules are alſo ſtreingthned by the Sacraments of Confirmation, Penance, holie Orders, Matrimonie, and Extreme Vnction.

notes.label: o
notes.text: The B. Sacrament and Sacrifice of Chriſts bodie and bloud.

verses.text: And thy mercie shal folow me <na>(p)</na> al the dayes of my life: And that I may dwel in the houſe of our Lord, <na>(q)</na> in longitude of dayes.

notes.label: p
notes.text: continual and final peſeuerance is by Gods ſpecial grace.

notes.label: q
notes.text: in eternal life.

chapters.summary: A forme of thankeſgeuing for al ſpiritual benefites ( deſcribed vnder the metaphor of temporal proſperitie ) euen from a ſinners firſt conuerſion, to final perſeuerance, and eternal beatitude. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Thanks-giving for God's protection.
The 7. key.

verses.text: The <na>(a)</na> firſt of the Sabbath, the Pſalme of Dauid. THE earth is our Lordes, and <na>(b)</na> the fulneſſe therof: the round world, and al that dwel therein.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Chriſt riſing from death the firſt day of the weeke, had al powre geuen him in heauen and in earth. Mat. 28.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Not only the ſoile it ſelfe but al the fruict, and al that dwel therin are Gods.

verses.text: Becauſe he hath founded it vpon the ſeas: and vpon the riuers hath prepared it.
Who <na>(c)</na> shal aſcend into the mount of our Lord? or who shal ſtand in his holie place?

notes.label: c
notes.text: Though Chriſt created and redeemed al, yet only the iuſt shal inherite heauen.

verses.text: The innocent of handes, and of cleane hart, that hath not taken his ſoule <na>(d)</na> in vayne, nor ſworne to his neighbour in guile.

notes.label: d
notes.text: not occupied himſelfe in vaine and vnprofitable thinges, but in commendable workes.

verses.text: He shal receiue bleſſing of our Lord: and <na>(e)</na> mercie of God his Sauiour.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Gods mercy goeth before iuſtifications iuſt workes folow, and ſo glorie is the reward of al.

verses.text: This is <na>(f)</na> the generation of them that ſeeke him, of them that ſeeke the face of the God of Iacob.

notes.label: f
notes.text: This ſorte of people thus ſeruing God, shal receiue euerlaſting bliſſe.

verses.text: Lift vp your gates <na>(g)</na> ye princes, and be ye lifted vp ô eternal gates: and the king of glorie shal enter in,

notes.label: g
notes.text: The prophet contemplating in ſpirite Chriſts Aſcenſion, inuiteth Angels to receiue him, and ( by proſopopeia ) ſpeaketh alſo to the gates of heauen, by which he is to enter.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Who is this king of glorie? Our Lord <na>(i)</na> ſtrong & mightie, our Lord mightie in battel.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Angels anſwer admiring, & demanding as in a dialogue, how Chriſt is become ſo glorious!

notes.label: i
notes.text: The Prophet anſwereth that Chriſt by his powre hath ouercome al enemies in battel.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> Lift vp your gates ye princes, and be ye lifted vp ô eternal gates: and the king of glorie shal enter in.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Againe he willeth Angels to open the gates, and biddeth the gates to enlarge them ſelues.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> Who is this king of glorie? <na>(m)</na> The Lord of powers he is the king of glorie.

notes.label: l
notes.text: the Angels demand as before:

notes.label: m
notes.text: the prophet anſwereth: that Chriſt is Lord alſo of Angels, and al heauenlie powres vnder God.

chapters.summary: Chriſt is Lord of the whole earth, being Creatour, and Redemer of man. 3. Good life (with faith in him) is the way to heauen. 7. whither Chriſt aſcending with triumph Angels admire him. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt Lord of al the world.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, the Pſalme of Dauid. TO THEE ô Lord I haue lifted vp <na>(b)</na> my ſoule:

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Pſalme perteyneth more properly to the new teſtament. And is artificially compoſed: the verſes beginning with diſtinct letters in order of the Hebrew Alphabet, to the laſt verſe.

notes.label: b
notes.text: my mind, to be attentiue.

verses.text: my God in thee is my confidence, let me <na>(c)</na> not be ashamed:

notes.label: c
notes.text: not be fruſtrate of my petition.

verses.text: Neither let mine enemies ſcorne me: for al <na>(d)</na> that expect thee, shal not be confounded.

notes.label: d
notes.text: that patiently expect the time when God wil aſſiſt.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Let al be confounded that do vniuſt thinges in vayne. Lord shew me thy wayes: and teach me thy pathes.

notes.label: e
notes.text: This maner of praying is frequent in the Pſalmes, ſignifying as a prophecie, that ſo it wil come to paſſe and the conformitie of the iuſt to Gods iuſtice.

verses.text: Direct me <na>(f)</na> in thy truth, and teach me: becauſe thou art God my Sauiour, and thee haue I expected <na>(g)</na> al the day.

notes.label: f
notes.text: in true faith and religion.

notes.label: g
notes.text: al our life we muſt deſire more and more knowlege of true doctrin.

verses.text: Remember ô Lord thy commiſerations, and thy mercies: that are from the beginning of the world.
The ſinnes <na>(h)</na> of my youth, and <na>(i)</na> my ignorances doe not remember. According to thy mercie remember thou me: for thy goodneſſe ô Lord.

notes.label: h
notes.text: from the firſt vſe of reaſon, at which time manie are careles,

notes.label: i
notes.text: & negligent to lerne how to ſerue God.

verses.text: Our Lord is <na>(k)</na> ſweete, and <na>(l)</na> righteous: for this cauſe he wil geue a law to them that ſinne in the way.

notes.label: k
notes.text: As God is ſweete in geuing good motions:

notes.label: l
notes.text: ſo he is ſeuere to them that reſiſt his grace.

verses.text: He wil direct the milde in iudgement: he wil teach the meeke his wayes.
Al the wayes of our Lord, be <na>(m)</na> mercie and <na>(n)</na> truth, to them that ſeeke after his <na>(o)</na> teſtament and his <na>(p)</na> teſtimonies.

notes.label: m
notes.text: God mercifully preuenteth with his grace:

notes.label: n
notes.text: and iuſtly rewardeth good workes.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Gods law is his couenant with man:

notes.label: p
notes.text: and teſtimonie of his wil.

verses.text: For thy name ô Lord thou wilt be propitious to my ſinne: for <na>(q)</na> it is much.

notes.label: q
notes.text: ſinne in reſpect of auerſion from God is great & nedeth his grace.

verses.text: Who is the man that <na>(r)</na> feareth our Lord? he <na>[1]</na> appoynteth him a law in the way, that he hath choſen.

notes.label: r
notes.text: He that feareth God which is the beginning of wiſdome, receiueth fiue ſpiritual commodities by his law here mentioned:
1. God inſtructeth him by his law:

verses.text: His ſoule <na>[1]</na> shal abide in good things: and <na>[2]</na> his ſeede shal inherite the land.

notes.text: 2. beſtoweth al neceſſaries vpon him:
3. others shal imitate his good example.

verses.text: Our Lord is <na>[1]</na> a firmament to them that feare him: & <na>[2]</na> his teſtament that it may be made manifeſt to them.

notes.text: 4. God wil protect him:
5. According to Gods couenant he shal enioy the manifeſt ſight of God for his eternal reward.

verses.text: Myne eies are alwayes to our Lord: becauſe he wil plucke my feete out of the ſnare.
Haue reſpect to me, and haue mercie on me: becauſe I am <na>(s)</na> alone and poore.

notes.label: s
notes.text: mans weaknes without Gods helpe.

verses.text: The tribulations of my hart are multiplied: deliuer me from <na>(t)</na> my neceſſities.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Tribulatiõs can not be auoided, but muſt neceſſarily be ſuffered: therfore ô God geue vs grace to paſſe through them without ſinne.

verses.text: See my <na>(v)</na> humiliation, and my labour: and <na>(w)</na> forgeue al my ſinnes.

notes.label: v
notes.text: myn affliction.

notes.label: w
notes.text: take away the cauſe and affliction wil be mitigated.

verses.text: Behold mine enemies, becauſe they are multiplied, and with <na>(x)</na> vniuſt hatred hated me.

notes.label: x
notes.text: wicked men of hatred do endeuour to draw others into ſinne.

verses.text: Keepe my ſoule, and deliuer me: I shal <na>(y)</na> not be ashamed, becauſe I hoped in thee.

notes.label: y
notes.text: Thoſe that hope in God shal neuer be confounded.

verses.text: The innocent and righteous haue cleaued to me: becauſe I expected thee.
<na>(z)</na> Deliuer Iſrael ô God, out of al his tribulations.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Al The letters of the Alphebet being complete in this Pſalme, this laſt verſe beginneth with Pere, Redeeme, praying God to redeme and deliuer Iſrael, that is, the whole Church from tribulations.

chapters.summary: A general prayer of the faithful againſt al enemies, 4. with deſire to be directed in the way of godlines, 7. and to be pardoned for ſinnes paſt. 9. acknowledging Gods meeknes, 17. our weaknes, neceſſitie of helpe, and hope in God: 22. concludeth with prayer for the whole Church. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer of the faithful.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end the Pſalme of Dauid. IVDGE <na>(b)</na> me ô Lord becauſe I haue walked in my innocencie: and hoping in our Lord I shal not be weakened.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Pſalme is alſo a conuenient prayer for anie Chriſtian in tribulation.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Be thou ô God arbiter of the cauſe betwen Saul and me, thou knoweſt myn innocencie in this behalfe, though I am vniuſtly charged by Saul, and his freindes.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Proue me Lord, and tempt me: burne my reynes and my hart.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Leſt perhaps I be not ſo innocent as I deſire, and as in reſpect of Saul I hope that I am, do thou O God proue me as thou wilt by tribulations.

verses.text: Becauſe thy mercie is before mine eies: and I am wel pleaſed in thy truth.
I <na>(d)</na> haue not ſitten with the councel of vanitie: and with them that doe vniuſt thinges. I wil not enter in

notes.label: d
notes.text: Dauid in a good conſcience, and zele againſt the wicked, alleageth his ſincere confidence of proceding, more then ordinarie men may do, God ſo inſpiring him extraordinarily.

verses.text: I haue hated the Church of the malignant: and with the impious I wil not ſitte.
I <na>(e)</na> wil wash my handes among innocentes: <na>(f)</na> and wil compaſſe thy altar ô Lord:

notes.label: e
notes.text: The reſt of this Pſalme euerie Prieſt reciteth in Maſſe, before he offer the holie Sacrifice, profeſſing, & putting him ſelfe in memorie, that he muſt only communicate with the innocent, or of pure conſcience; · Epi. 120. c. 11.

notes.label: f
notes.text: and ſo approch to the Altar. prefigured Leuit. 16. v. 4.

verses.text: That I <na>(g)</na> may heare the voice of praiſe, and <na>(h)</na> shew forth al thy meruelous workes.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Shutting the eares of my hart from euil and vaine thoughtes I wil attend to godlie inſpirations,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and ſo with mental prayer, and external voice (as the holie order of this ſacred office requireth) praiſe thee ô God in thy meruelous workes.

verses.text: Lord I haue loued <na>(i)</na> the beautie of thy houſe, and the place of <na>(k)</na> the habitation of thy glorie.

notes.label: i
notes.text: I can not but ſingularly loue the excellencie of this place dedicated to thy ſeruice: where is true faith, vnitie, and charitie of thy people, the guard of holie Angels, the adminiſtration of ſacred myſteries, aſſiſtance of the Holie Ghoſt, real preſence of Chriſt our Lord, al replenished with Diuine maieſtie.

notes.label: k
notes.text: This repreſenteth vnto me the glorious heauenlie kingdom of God and al Sainctes.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> Deſtroy not ô God my ſoule with the impious, and my life with bloudie men.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Suffer me not therfore to be contaminate by the wicked, nor to be deuoured with them.

verses.text: In whoſe <na>(m)</na> handes are iniquities: their <na>(n)</na> righthand is replenished with giftes.

notes.label: m
notes.text: They are ſtil readie to committe more and more iniquities.

notes.label: n
notes.text: themſelues being corrupted, endeuour by giftes of wordly commodities to corrupt others.

verses.text: But <na>(o)</na> I haue walked in mine innocencie: <na>(p)</na> redeme me, and haue mercie on me.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Euerie one ought ſo to purge his conſcience, that he may be innocent, or free from great ſinne.

notes.label: p
notes.text: deliuer me from this neceſſitie of dwelling among the wicked.

verses.text: My <na>(q)</na> foote hath ſtood in the direct way: in <na>(r)</na> the Churches I wil bleſſe thee ô Lord.

notes.label: q
notes.text: I intend to walke right.

notes.label: r
notes.text: I deſire to praiſe thee amongſt thy true faithful ſeruantes.

chapters.summary: Dauid in banishment among the Philiſtines, truſteth in the iuſtice of his cauſe, 9. and prayeth God earneſtly to deliuer him, that he may with more freedom and commodity ſerue him as he deſireth. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David'ſ prayer diſtreſſed in perſecution.
The 8. key.

verses.text: The Pſalme of Dauid <na>(a)</na> before he was annoynted. OVr Lord is <na>(b)</na> my illumination, and <na>(c)</na> my ſaluation, <na>(d)</na> whom shal I feare? Our Lord is the protectour of my life, of whom shal I be afrayd?

notes.label: a
notes.text: Before his ſecond annointing, as is probable. 2. Reg. 2.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Againſt ignorance God illuminateth his ſeruantes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: againſt infirmitie he geueth ſtreingth.

notes.label: d
notes.text: ſo he nedeth not to feare anie mans malice, ſuteltie, nor force. Luc. 21. v. 15.

verses.text: Whiles the harmeful approch vpon me, to eate my flesh. Mine enemies that truble me, them ſelues are weakened and are fallen.
If campes ſtand together againſt me, my hart shal not feare. If battel riſe vp againſt me, in this wil I hope.

One thing I haue asked of our Lord, this wil I ſeeke for, that I <na>(e)</na> may dwel in the houſe of our Lord al the dayes of my life. That I may ſee the pleaſentnes of our Lord, and viſite his temple.

notes.label: e
notes.text: How ſpecial a benefite Dauid eſtemed it to be in the Catholique Church the only true houſe of God!

verses.text: Becauſe he hath <na>(f)</na> hid me in his tabernacle: in the day of euils he hath protected me, in <na>(g)</na> the ſecrete of his tabernacle.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Albeit the ſpiritual or carnal enemie ſeke to ouerthrow me, yet I am ſecure in the Catholique Church.

notes.label: g
notes.text: God either ſuffereth not the enemie to find his ſeruant.

verses.text: In <na>(h)</na> a rocke he hath exalted me: and now he hath <na>(i)</na> exalted my head ouer mine enemies. I <na>(k)</na> haue gone round about, and haue immolated in his tabernacle an hoſt of iubilation: I <na>(l)</na> wil ſing, and ſay a Pſalme to our Lord.

notes.label: h
notes.text: or not to be able to hurt him ſpiritually

notes.label: i
notes.text: when a martyr or confeſſour dieth, then he getteth the victorie againſt the perſecutors.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Diligently recounting al thy benefites, I render thankes by ſacrifice and praiſe.

notes.label: l
notes.text: not only in hart, but alſo ſinging with loud voice and inſtrument.

verses.text: Heare ô Lord my voice, wherwith I haue cried to thee: haue mercie on me, and heare me.
My <na>(m)</na> hart hath ſayd to thee, my face hath ſought thee out: <na>(n)</na> thy face ô Lord I wil ſeeke.

notes.label: m
notes.text: In my inward ſincere cogitation I deſire, and ſeeke that I may ſee thee,

notes.label: n
notes.text: face to face 1. Cor. 13. v. 12.

verses.text: Turne <na>(o)</na> not away thy face from me: <na>(p)</na> decline not in wrath from thy ſeruant. Be <na>(q)</na> thou my helper: forſake me not, neither deſpiſe me ô God my Sauiour.

notes.label: o
notes.text: In the meane time ô Lord, grant me thy fauour,

notes.label: p
notes.text: leaue me not though thou be angrie with me.

notes.label: q
notes.text: He ſpeaketh in the perſon of orphanes.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(r)</na> my father and my mother haue forſaken me: but our Lord hath taken me.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Though carnal parentes forſake the iuſt man in tribulation, yet God hath then moſt ſpecial care of him.

verses.text: Geue me <na>(s)</na> a law ô Lord in thy way: <na>(t)</na> and direct me in the right path, becauſe of mine enemies.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Eſtablish my hart in thy law.

notes.label: t
