notes.text: conſerue me in the right way, which thou haſt already taught me, and it is the more neceſſarie, becauſe myne enemies labour to peruert me.

verses.text: Deliuer me not into <na>(v)</na> the ſoules of them that truble me: becauſe <na>(w)</na> vniuſt witneſſes haue riſen vp againſt me, and iniquity hath lyed <na>(x)</na> to it ſelfe.

notes.label: v
notes.text: the willes.

notes.label: w
notes.text: falſe witneſſes accuſed Dauid, others accuſed Chriſt: Mat. 26. others do ſtil accuſe the iuſt Mat. 5.

notes.label: x
notes.text: the wicked pleaſe themſelues in lying, but the chief hurt finally turneth vpon themſelues.

verses.text: I <na>(y)</na> beleue to ſee the good things of our Lord, in the land of the liuing.

notes.label: y
notes.text: The prophet and al iuſt men are comforted by God, and hope of reward in heauen.

verses.text: <na>(z)</na> Expect our Lord, doe manfully: and <na>(a)</na> let thy hart take courage, and <na>(b)</na> expect thou our Lord. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: z
notes.text: The iuſt exhorteth his owne ſoule to patience,

notes.label: a
notes.text: fortitude,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and longanimitie. · Pſal. 30.

chapters.summary: Dauid being in great diſtreſſe through perſecution, and hauing aſſured confidence in God, deſcribeth the great ſecuritie of Gods protection. 7. sheweth the ſame experienced in him ſelf. 12. prayeth for continuance therof 13. and incorageth his owne ſoule, in hope of life euerlaſting, to perſeuer in vertue. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
An other confident prayer of David in tribulation.
The 3. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme to Dauid him ſelfe. TO THEE ô Lord I wil crie, my God <na>(a)</na> keepe not ſilence from me: leſt at any time thou hold thy peace from me, and I shal be like to them that goe downe into the lake.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Omitte not to comfort me.

verses.text: Heare ô Lord the voice of my petition whiles I pray to thee: whiles I lift vp my handes to thy holie temple.
<na>(b)</na> Draw me not together with ſinners: and with them that worke iniquitie deſtroy me not. Which ſpeake peace with their neighbour, but euils in their hartes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Suffer me not to be ouercome: for God tempteth none to euil. Iac. 1.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Geue them according to their workes, and according to the wickedneſſe of their inuentions. According to the workes of their handes geue vnto them: render them their retribution.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The iuſt in zele of iuſtice pray that ſinne may be punished.

verses.text: Becauſe they haue <na>(d)</na> not vnderſtood the workes of our Lord, and in the workes of his handes thou shalt deſtroy them, and <na>(e)</na> not build them vp.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Ignorance doth not excuſe when men may and wil not vnderſtand.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God ſaueth not without our cooperation with his grace.

verses.text: Bleſſed be our Lord: becauſe he hath heard the voice of my petition.
Our Lord is my helper, and my protectour: in him my hart hath hoped, and I was holpen. And <na>(f)</na> my flesh florished againe: and <na>(g)</na> with my wil I wil confeſſe to him.

notes.label: f
notes.text: being comforted in ſpirite my bodie is as it were refreshed.

notes.label: g
notes.text: freely and gladly.

verses.text: Our Lord is the ſtrength of his people: and he is <na>(h)</na> the protector of the ſaluations of his annoynted.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God protecteth and proſpereth the kings good endeuoures for his people.

verses.text: Saue <na>(i)</na> thy people ô Lord, and bleſſe thine inheritance: and rule them, and extol them for euer.

notes.label: i
notes.text: As Pſal. 19. and often elswhere the ſubiectes pray for their Superior: ſo mutually the ſuperior prayeth for the ſubiectes.

chapters.summary: Dauid prayeth to be defended from the eternal deſtruction of the wicked, 4. which ( by way of imprecation, or conformitie to Gods iuſtice ) he prophecieth 6. Feeling by inſpiration that his prayer is heard, rendereth thankes to God, 9. and prayeth for al the people. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Another prayer of David for delivery from evils.
The 8. key.

verses.text: The Pſalme of Dauid, in the conſummation <na>(a)</na> of the tabernacle. BRING <na>(b)</na> to our Lord ye children of God: bring to our Lord <na>(c)</na> the ſonnes of rammes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Offer ſacrifice of thankes for the ſingular benefites after recounted in this Pſalme.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Rammes were of the more principal thinges that were offered in the law of Moyſes. But the ſonnes of rammes importe in myſtical ſenſe better hoſtes then rammes.

verses.text: Bring to our Lord <na>(d)</na> glorie and honour, bring to our Lord glorie vnto his name: adore ye our Lord <na>(e)</na> in his holie court.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The firſt thing in ſacrifice is to glorifie, honour, and adore God in ſinceritie of ſpirite,

notes.label: e
notes.text: in his holie Catholique Churh.

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(f)</na> vpon waters, the God of <na>(g)</na> maieſtie hath <na>(h)</na> thundered: Our Lord vpon <na>(i)</na> manie waters.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Here is a greater matter intimated then happened in the bringing of the Arke into a tabernacle prepared in Sion, when Dauid danced, and offered hoſtes for ſacrifice, others ioyning with him in that ſolemnitie. But this voice of out Lord vpon waters is rather verified of our Bleſſed Sauiours owne preaching with

notes.label: g
notes.text: maieſtie

notes.label: h
notes.text: thundering, & by his Apoſtles vpon

notes.label: i
notes.text: manie waters, manie nations:

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(k)</na> in powre: the voice of our Lord <na>(l)</na> in magnificence.

notes.label: k
notes.text: in powre of miracles.

notes.label: l
notes.text: in magnificence preaching as hauing in dede powre, not as the Scribes and Phariſes. Mat. 7. v. 29.

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(m)</na> breaking ceders: and our Lord shal breake the <na>(n)</na> ceders of Libanus:

notes.label: m
notes.text: breaking cedars among innumerable others, conuerting higheſt Potentates

notes.label: n
notes.text: of Libanus, Emperoures, kinges and greateſt Princes of the world:

verses.text: And he shal breake them in peeces as a <na>(o)</na> calfe of Libanus. <na>(p)</na> and the beloued as <na>(q)</na> the ſonne of vnicornes.

notes.label: o
notes.text: as a calfe of Libanas ſo meekly ſubmitting them ſelues to Chriſts yoke, and ſpiritual obedience of his Church.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Al which is done by Chriſt our Lord the beloued of God,

notes.label: q
notes.text: as the ſonne of vnicornes, is moſt tenderly beloued by the parentes.

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(r)</na> diuiding the flame of fire:

notes.label: r
notes.text: This voice of our Lord diuiding the flame of fire. the Holie Ghoſt proceding from the Father and the Sonne, came vpon the Apoſtles, as in diuided tongues of fire.

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(s)</na> shaking the deſert; and our Lord shal moue <na>(t)</na> the deſert of Cades.

notes.label: s
notes.text: wherwith the deſert, the Gentiles of the wide and wild world, vvere shaken and moued,

notes.label: t
notes.text: the deſert of Cades, ſome of the Iewes alſo compunct in hart with remorſe of conſcience hearing the voice of S. Peter, and other Apoſtles.

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(v)</na> preparing <na>[1]</na> hartes, and he shal <na>(w)</na> diſcouer thicke woodes: and <na>(x)</na> in his temple al shal ſay glorie.

notes.label: v
notes.text: The ſame voice of our Lord preparing hartes, inſpiring the mindes of men with ſpede, like hyndes and does, to aſcend the high hilles of free and perfect life, in contemplatiue vertues.

notes.label: w
notes.text: So our Sauiour shal diſcouer the thicke woodes, reueile the hidden Myſteries of the old Law, by preaching Chriſtian doctrine, and vſe of Chriſtian Religion.

notes.label: x
notes.text: in his holie Temple, the Catholique Church, wherin al true Chriſtians shal glorifie God.
ceruos.

verses.text: Our Lord maketh <na>(y)</na> to inhabite the floud: and our Lord <na>(z)</na> shal ſit king for euer.

notes.label: y
notes.text: making the great abundance of people, who are like the ſea when it ouerfloweth the land, to dwel in the ſame Church.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Chriſt our Lord ſitting, & ruling king ouer al foreuer:

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(a)</na> wil geue ſtrength to his people: our Lord <na>(b)</na> wil bleſſe his people in peace.

notes.label: a
notes.text: by his grace geuing ſtreingth to his people, to paſſe through the tentations of this life;

notes.label: b
notes.text: and bleſſee the iuſt with eternal peace in heauen.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet ſeing in ſpirite the moſt ſacred Myſteries, brought by Chriſt into this world, inuiteth al to offer their beſt thinges, euen themſelues wholly, as ſacrifice of thankes, for ſo excellent benefites, preached with magnificence. 5. VVherby innumerable are gethered into his Church here replenished with grace, and in heauen with glorie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church of Chriſt endowed with excellent myſteries.
The 6. key.

verses.text: A <na>(a)</na> Pſalme of Canticle, <na>(b)</na> in the dedication of Dauids houſe.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The general name of Pſalme common to this whole booke conteyning in al 150. is more particularelie appropriated to ſome, which more ſpecially were playde vpon muſical inſtruments as on the Pſalter, Harpe, &c. Others are called Canticles, which were moſt vſuallie ſongue with humaine voices. So this, called a Pſalme of Canticle, ſignifieth that voyces begane the muſike and inſtruments were adioyned. As contrariwiſe others are called Canticles of Pſalmes, where inſtruments begane and voices folowed.

notes.label: b
notes.text: After manie great tribulations, King Dauid proſpering built an excellent houſe or palace. (2. Reg. 5. v. 11. Paralip. 14. v. 1.) And at his firſt dwelling therein, made this Pſalme, beginning himſelfe to ſing the ſame with voice, other muſitians ioyned with him in the praiſes of God and thankeſgeuing for his benefites.

verses.text: I WIL <na>(c)</na> exalt thee ô Lord, <na>(d)</na> becauſe thou haſt receiued me: neither haſt <na>(e)</na> delighted myne enemies ouer me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Though God in himſelfe is moſt high, and neither nedeth, nor can be exalted by men, yet the royal prophet knew it vvas his dutie to ſing thankes and praiſes to him,

notes.label: d
notes.text: for his deliuerie from manie trubles, and dangers.

notes.label: e
notes.text: not ſuffering his enemies to be delighted in his ruine.

verses.text: O Lord my God I haue cried to thee, and thou haſt <na>(f)</na> healed me.

notes.label: f
notes.text: conſerued my bodie in health amõgſt innumerable dangers.

verses.text: Lord thou haſt <na>(g)</na> brought forth my ſoule out of hel: thou haſt ſaued me from them that goe downe into the lake.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Preſerued my ſoule from greater dãgers of ſinnes, and ſo from hel.

verses.text: Sing to our Lord <na>(h)</na> ye his ſainctes: and <na>(i)</na> confeſſe to the memorie of his holines.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Ye that are iuſt and holie praiſe God for it, from vvhom it cometh, and not from your ſelues:

notes.label: i
notes.text: confeſſe his mere goodnes vvithout your deſertes.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(k)</na> wrath is in his indignation: <na>(l)</na> and life in his wil. At <na>(m)</na> euening shal weeping abide: and in the morning gladneſſe.

notes.label: k
notes.text: vvhen he is angrie,

notes.label: l
notes.text: yet he meaneth vvel vnto vs.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The ſtate of a iuſt mans life is often changed from ſorovv to comforte, and from comforte to ſorovv.

verses.text: And I ſaid in my abundance: <na>(n)</na> I wil not be moued for euer.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Though vve ſuppoſe our ſelues firmly eſtablished:

verses.text: O Lord <na>(o)</na> in thy wil, thou haſt geuen ſtrength to my beautie. Thou haſt <na>(p)</na> turned away thy face from me, and I became trubled.

notes.label: o
notes.text: yet God of his good vvil tovvardes vs ſometimes geueth ſtrength, and corege,

notes.label: p
notes.text: ſometimes ſuffereth vs to our ovvne vveakenes,

verses.text: To thee ô Lord <na>(q)</na> I wil crie: and I wil pray to my God.

notes.label: q
notes.text: therfore we muſt ſtil crie and pray for Gods helpe,

verses.text: <na>(r)</na> What profite is in my bloud, whiles I deſcend into corruption? Shal duſt confeſſe to thee, or declare thy truth?

notes.label: r
notes.text: in manner here expreſſed or the like.

verses.text: Our Lord hath heard, and had mercie on me: our Lord is become my helper.
Thou haſt turned my mourning into ioy vnto me: thou haſt cut my ſackcloth, and haſt compaſſed me with gladnes.
That <na>(s)</na> my glorie may ſing to thee: and I be not compunct: Lord my God for euer <na>(t)</na> wil I confeſſe to thee.

notes.label: s
notes.text: finally in this my good ſtate

notes.label: t
notes.text: I shal alvvayes confeſſe and praiſe thee.

chapters.summary: King Dauid by voice and inſtrument rendereth thankes to God for his peaceable ſtate in the kingdom, 5. inuiteth others to reioyce in Gods benefites, teaching by his owne example that God ſometimes geueth more conforth ſometimes sheweth his wrath, but al for our good. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David rendereth thanks for his eſtablishment in his Kingdom.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, the Pſalme of Dauid, for <na>(b)</na> exceſſe of minde.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the new Teſtament.

notes.label: b
notes.text: eſpecially to the iuſt trubled and almoſt diſtracted in mind in great affliction. See v. 23.

verses.text: IN THEE ô Lord <na>(c)</na> haue I hoped, <na>(d)</na> let me not be confounded for euer: in thy iuſtice deliuer me. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: c
notes.text: How greuouſly ſoeuer I am afflicted yet I truſt in thee,

notes.label: d
notes.text: therfore I pray thus.

verses.text: Incline thine eare to me, make haſt to deliuer me. Be vnto me for a God protector: and for a houſe of refuge, that thou mayſt ſaue me.
Becauſe thou art my ſtrength, and my refuge: and for thy name thou wilt conduct me, and wilt nourish me.
Thou wilt bring me out of this ſnare, which they haue hid for me: becauſe thou art my protector.
Into <na>(e)</na> thy handes I commend my ſpirit: thou haſt <na>(f)</na> redeemed me ô Lord God of truth. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: e
notes.text: I offer and reſigne my ſelfe to thee:

notes.label: f
notes.text: Luc. 23. · Thou haſt often deliuered me. This verſe is moſt aptly applied in al reſignatiõs of our ſoules to Gods wil, namely whenſoeuer we receiue the B. Sacrament; likewiſe in the houre of death, and at manie other times.

verses.text: Thou haſt hated them that obſerue vanities, vnprofitably. But I haue hoped in our Lord:
I shal reioyce and be ioyful in thy mercie. Becauſe thou haſt reſpected my humilitie, thou haſt ſaued my ſoule out of neceſſities.
Neither <na>(g)</na> haſt thou shut me vp in the handes of the enemie: thou haſt ſet me feete in a large place.

notes.label: g
notes.text: not ſuffered me to be shut vp.

verses.text: Haue mercie vpon me ô Lord becauſe I am in tribulation: myne eie is trubled for wrath, my ſoule, and my bellie:
Becauſe <na>(h)</na> my life is decayed for ſorrowe: and my yeares for gronings. My ſtrength is weakened for pouertie; and by bones are trubled.

notes.label: h
notes.text: al my partes external and internal, body and mind are trubled.

verses.text: Aboue al myne enemies I am made a reproch both to my neighbours excedingly: and <na>(i)</na> a feare to my acquantance. They that ſaw me, fled forth from me:

notes.label: i
notes.text: My freindes dare not conuerſe with me, leſt they incurre diſpleaſure for my ſake.

verses.text: I am forgotten, from the hart as one dead. I am made as a veſſel deſtroyed:
becauſe I haue heard the reprehenſion of manie that abide round about: In that whiles, they aſſembled together againſt me, they conſulted to take my ſoule.
But I haue hoped in thee ô Lord: I ſayd: Thou art my God:
my lottes are in thy handes. Deliuer me out of the handes of my enemies, and from them that perſecute me.
<na>(k)</na> Illuſtrate thy face vpon thy ſeruant, <na>(l)</na> ſaue me in thy mercie:

notes.label: k
notes.text: Make thy light ſo ſhine in my ſoule, that I may vnderſtand that is right.

notes.label: l
notes.text: and through thy mercie deliuer me from the force of myne aduerſaries.

verses.text: Lord let me not be confounded, becauſe I haue inuocated thee. Let the impious be ashamed, and brought downe into hel:
let the deceitful lippes be made mute. Which ſpeake iniquitie againſt the iuſt, <na>(m)</na> in pride, and <na>(n)</na> abuſe.

notes.label: m
notes.text: ſo proudly behauing them ſelues, as if they had no ſuperior, neither in earth nor in heauen, to whom they shal at laſt render account:

notes.label: n
notes.text: and abuſing their preſent powre and authoritie, which they haue of God.

verses.text: How great is the multitude of thy ſweetneſſe ô Lord, which thou <na>(o)</na> haſt hid for them that feare thee. Thou haſt perfited it for them that hope in thee, <na>(p)</na> in the ſight of the children of men.

notes.label: o
notes.text: As yet in this preſent life the reward of the iuſt is hidde:

notes.label: p
notes.text: but shal be made manifeſt in ſight of al men.

verses.text: Thou <na>(q)</na> shalt hide them in the ſecrete of <na>(r)</na> thy face from the diſturbance of men. Thou shalt protect them in thy tabernacle from the contradiction of tongues.

notes.label: q
notes.text: In the meane time the iuſt is in great eſtimation in the ſecrete knowledge of God.

notes.label: r
notes.text: title of honoure, as we ſpeake to a king; your maieſtie: or to a noble man, your Lordshippe.

verses.text: Bleſſed be our Lord: becauſe he hath made his mercie merueilous to me in the fenſed citie.
But I haue ſaid in <na>(s)</na> the exceſſe of my minde: I am caſt away from the ſight of thine eies. Therfore thou haſt heard the voice of my praier, whiles I cried to thee.

notes.label: s
notes.text: in myn extreme affliction being almoſt diſtracted in my mind, I ſaid that in reaſon I would not haue ſayd. Holie Iob ſpake ſome thinges in ſuch ſtate of affliction. ch. 3. & 42.

verses.text: <na>(t)</na> Loue our Lord al ye his ſainctes: becauſe our Lord wil require truth, & wil repay them abundantly that doe proudly.

notes.label: t
notes.text: the prophet, or other iuſt perſon exhorteth al the ſeruants of God

verses.text: Do ye <na>(v)</na> manfully, and let your <na>(w)</na> hart take courage, al ye that <na>(x)</na> hope in out Lord.

notes.label: v
notes.text: to conſtancie.

notes.label: w
notes.text: longanimitie,

notes.label: x
notes.text: and final perſeuerance to the end.

chapters.summary: A prayer of a iuſt man excedingly afflicted ſtil confident in God, 11. deſcribing his manie calamities (in reſpect of his enemies) vndeſerued, 18. prayeth for his owne deliuerie, and their iuſt punishment. 20. praiſeth and thanketh God for his goodnes. 24. exhorteth al others to do the ſame. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
How to pray in affliction.
The 7. key.

verses.text: To <na>(a)</na> Dauid him ſelfe vnderſtanding. BLESSED are they, <na>(b)</na> whoſe iniquities are forgeuen: and whoſe ſinnes <na>(c)</na> be couered. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Pſalme ſheweth how Dauid was brought to vnderſtand his ſinnes, to confeſſe, bewayle, and obtaine remiſſion of them.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The firſt bleſſing of a ſinner is the forgeuenes of his ſinnes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: by charitie, which couereth the multitude of ſinnes. 1. Pet. 4.

verses.text: Bleſſed is the man, to whom <na>(d)</na> our Lord hath not imputed ſinne, neither is there <na>(e)</na> guile in his ſpirit.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Satisfaction being made.

notes.label: e
notes.text: VVhen ſinners repent ſincerly without guile, then God forgeueth: without which cooperation none is iuſtified.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(f)</na> I held my peace, my bones are <na>[1]</na> inueterated, <na>(g)</na> whiles I cried al the day.

notes.label: f
notes.text: becauſe I acknowledged not my greuous ſinnes, I was ſtil ſore afflicted.

notes.label: g
notes.text: though otherwiſe I ceaſed not to pray but without any fruict or good effect.
vvaxed as if they vvere old.

verses.text: Becauſe day and night thy hand is made heauie vpon me: I <na>(h)</na> am turned in my anguish, whiles <na>(i)</na> the thorne is faſtened.

notes.label: h
notes.text: thy diuine prouidence reducing me,

notes.label: i
notes.text: by remorſe of myn owne conſcience which telleth me that I deſerue al this affliction.

verses.text: I <na>(k)</na> haue made my ſinne knowen to thee: and my iniuſtice I haue not hid. I ſaid: I wil confeſſe againſt me my iniuſtice to our Lord: and thou haſt forgeuen the impietie of my ſinne.

notes.label: k
notes.text: therfore I do no longer diſsẽble with men nor am ſilent to thee, but expreſly acknowlege my ſinnes.

verses.text: For this <na>(l)</na> shal euerie holie one pray to thee, in time conuenient. But yet <na>(m)</na> in the floud of manie waters, they shal <na>(n)</na> not approche to him.

notes.label: l
notes.text: As I do now recal my ſelfe being ſtricken with Gods heauie hand; ſo muſt euerie one that wil be purged from his ſinnes and ſanctified pray to thee, when he is afflicted.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Though calamities be meruelous great like to a diluge:

notes.label: n
notes.text: yet they ſhal not opreſſe him, that relieth vpon God.

verses.text: Thou art my refuge from tribulation, which hath compaſſed me: my exultation, deliuer me from them that compaſſe me.
I <na>(o)</na> wil geue thee vnderſtanding, and wil inſtruct thee in the way, that thou shalt goe; I <na>(p)</na> wil faſten mine eies vpon thee.

notes.label: o
notes.text: God ſpeaketh: promiſing by theſe tribulations to geue his ſeruants vnderſtanding, and inſtruction:

notes.label: p
notes.text: with perpetual protection.

verses.text: Doe <na>(q)</na> not become as horſe and mule, which haue no vnderſtanding. In <na>(r)</na> bit and bridle binde faſt their cheekes, that approch not to thee.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Be not therfore careles, like to brute beaſtes, but conſideratiue of your actions.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The Prophet or anie iuſt ſoul beſecheth God to hold this ſtraict hand of diſcipline ouer ſinners, for their conuerſion.

verses.text: Manie <na>(s)</na> are the ſcourges of a ſinner, but <na>(t)</na> him that hopeth in our Lord mercie shal compaſſe.

notes.label: s
notes.text: sinners deſerue much punishment.

notes.label: t
notes.text: but repenting, and truſting in God shal finde his mercie.

verses.text: Be <na>(v)</na> ioyful in our Lord and reioyſe ye iuſt, and glorie al ye right of hart.

notes.label: v
notes.text: The end of true penance is ioy to which therfore the prophet inuiteth al penitents.

chapters.summary: Forgeuenes of ſinnes is a happie thing: 3. wherto manie are brought by affliction geuing them vnderſtanding, ſo mouing them to confeſſe their ſinnes, 6. pray for remiſſion, 10, not deſpaire, but hope in Gods mercie, and ſo reioyce with ſincere hart. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The ſecond penitential Pſalm.
The 7. key.

verses.text: REIOYCE ye iuſt <na>(a)</na> in our Lord: <na>(b)</na> prayſing becometh the righteous.

notes.label: a
notes.text: not in your ſelues

notes.label: b
notes.text: praiſe is not comelie in the mouth of a ſinner. Eccli. 15.

verses.text: Confeſſe ye to our Lord on <na>(c)</na> the harpe: on <na>(d)</na> a pſalter of ten ſtrings ſing to him.

notes.label: c
notes.text: in mortificacion offering your bodies a liuing hoſte, Rom. 12.

notes.label: d
notes.text: of this inſtrument this booke is called the Pſalter and it ſignifieth the obſeruation of the tenne commandments, withoutwhich no praiſe pleaſeth God.

verses.text: Sing ye to him <na>(e)</na> a new ſong: ſing wel to him in iubilation.

notes.label: e
notes.text: praiſing God for the grace of Chriſt in the new teſtament.

verses.text: Becauſe the <na>(f)</na> word of our Lord is right, and al his workes are <na>(g)</na> in faith.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Gods rules and precepts are moſt iuſt and right.

notes.label: g
notes.text: he performeth whatſoeuer he promiſeth.

verses.text: He loueth <na>(h)</na> mercie and iudgement: the earth is ful of the mercie of our Lord.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God euer ioyneth theſe vertues together.

verses.text: By <na>(i)</na> the word of our Lord the heauens are eſtablished: and by the ſpirit of his mouth al the power of them.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Gods word is omnipotent.

verses.text: Gathering together the waters of the ſea, as it were in a bottel: putting the depthes <na>(k)</na> in treaſures.

notes.label: k
notes.text: vnknowen, as riches hid in ſecrete places.

verses.text: Let al the earth feare our Lord: and let al the inhabitantes of the world be moued at him.
Becauſe he ſaid, and they were made: he commanded and they were created,
Our Lord <na>(l)</na> diſſipateth the counſels of nations: and he reproueth the cogitations of people, and he reproueth the counſels of princes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: As in Babylon he confounded their tongues.

verses.text: But the counſel of our Lord abydeth for euer: the cogitations <na>(m)</na> of his hart in generation and generation.

notes.label: m
notes.text: his abſolute wil is alwayes fulfilled.

verses.text: Bleſſed is the nation, whoſe God is our Lord: the people <na>(n)</na> whom he hath choſen for his inheritance.

notes.label: n
notes.text: the people of Iſrael in the old teſtament: and Chriſtians of al nations in the new.

verses.text: Our <na>(o)</na> Lord hath looked from heauen: he hath ſene al the children of men.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Gods perpetual prouidence.

verses.text: From his prepared habitation he hath looked vpon al, that inhabite the earth.
Who <na>(p)</na> made their hartes ſeuerally: who vnderſtandeth al their workes.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Gods wiſdom infinite.

verses.text: The <na>(q)</na> king is not ſaued by much powre: and the gyant shal not be ſaued in the multitude of his ſtrength.

notes.label: q
notes.text: No powre in earth is of anie force without God.

verses.text: The horſe fayleth <na>(r)</na> to ſafetie, <na>(s)</na> and in the abundance of his force he shal not be ſaued.

notes.label: r
notes.text: of his maiſter

notes.label: s
notes.text: or of him ſelfe.

verses.text: Behold the eies of our Lord be vpon them that feare him: and on them, that hope vpon his mercie.
That he may deliuer their ſoules from death: and nourish them in famine.
Our ſoule expecteth our Lord: becauſe he is our helper and protector.
Becauſe in him our hart shal reioyce: and we haue truſted in his holie name.
<na>(t)</na> Let thy mercie ô Lord be made vpon vs: as we haue hoped in thee.

notes.label: t
notes.text: O God which haſt al perfection, shew thy mercie in protecting, and ſauing al that truſt in thee.

chapters.summary: The prophet exhorteth to praiſe God, 4. deſcribing his powre, prouidence, mercie, and wiſdom. 16. no ſaluation but by him. 20. and therfore prayeth for his helpe. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The perfection of God's works deſcribed.
The 2. key.

verses.text: To <na>[1]</na> Dauid, when he changed his countenance before <na>(a)</na> Abimelech, and he diſmiſt him, and he went away. (1. Reg. 21.) <na>[2]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: His proper name was Achis 1. Reg. 21. but al kinges of Paleſtina were called Abimelech, as Pharao in Ægypt, Nabuchodonoſor in Babylon.
This Pſalme is alſo compoſed in order of the Alphabet.

verses.text: I <na>(b)</na> WIL bleſſe our Lord at <na>(c)</na> al time: his prayſe alwayes in my mouth.

notes.label: b
notes.text: I prayſe God

notes.label: c
notes.text: both in proſperitie and aduerſitie.

verses.text: In our Lord <na>(d)</na> my ſoule shal be praiſed: let the milde heare, and reioyce.

notes.label: d
notes.text: when I ſerue our Lord, my ſoule shal be praiſed in his ſeruice.

verses.text: Magnifie ye our Lord with me: and let vs exalt his name for euer.
I haue ſought out our Lord, and he hath heard me: and from al my tribulations he hath deliuered me.
Come ye to him, and be illuminated: and your faces shal not be confounded.
This <na>(e)</na> poore man hath cried, and our Lord hath heard him: and from al his tribulations he hath ſaued him.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Euerie man be he how poore ſoeuer when he prayeth shal be heard.

verses.text: The <na>(f)</na> Angel of our Lord shal put in him ſelfe about them that feare him: and shal deliuer them.

notes.label: f
notes.text: the proper guardian Angel of euerie one.

verses.text: Taſt ye, and ſee that our Lord is ſweete: bleſſed is the man, that hopeth in him.
Feare <na>(g)</na> ye our Lord al ye his ſainctes: becauſe there is no lacke to them that feare him.

notes.label: g
notes.text: with filial feare.

verses.text: The <na>(h)</na> rich haue wanted, and haue bene hungrie: but they that ſeeke after our Lord shal not be diminished of any good.

notes.label: h
notes.text: the rich of this world ſetting their mind vpon their wealth, are poore in ſpiritual giftes.

verses.text: Come children, heare me: I wil teach you the feare of our Lord.
Who is the man <na>(i)</na> that wil haue life: loueth to ſee good daies.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Euerie one deſireth to be happie, but he in dede shal be happie, that fleeth from euil, and doth good.

verses.text: Stay thy tongue from euil: and thy lippes that they ſpeake not guile.
Turne away from euil, and do good: ſeeke after peace, and purſewe it.
The eies of our Lord vpon the iuſt: and his eares vnto their prayers
But the <na>(k)</na> countenance of our Lord is vpon them that doe euil things: to deſtroy their memorie out of the earth.

notes.label: k
notes.text: God ſeing al mens actiõs & intentions, wil render as they deſerue.

verses.text: The iuſt haue cried, and our Lord hath heard them: and out of al their tribulations he hath deliuered them.
Our Lord is nigh to them, that are of a contrite hart: and the humble of ſpirit he wil ſaue.
Manie are the tribulations of the iuſt: and out of al theſe our Lord wil deliuer them.
Our Lord keepeth al their <na>(l)</na> bones: there shal not one of them be broken.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Though the iuſt ſeme for a time to be forſaken, yet God that geueth them internal ſtreingth, wil at laſt reward and crowne in them his owne giftes.

verses.text: The death of ſinners is verie il: and they that hate the iuſt <na>(m)</na> shal offend.

notes.label: m
notes.text: for their ſinne they are ſuffered to fal into more ſinne.

verses.text: Our Lord wil redeme the ſoules of his ſeruantes: and al that hope in him <na>(n)</na> shal not offend.

notes.label: n
notes.text: contrariwiſe thoſe that accept of his grace, shal finally not offend.

chapters.summary: King Dauid by his owne example being deliuered from danger, exhorteth al men to render thankes for Gods benefites. 12. shewing wherin iuſtice conſiſteth, 16. and Gods ſpecial prouidence towards the iuſt. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God'ſ providence.
The 3. key.

verses.text: To <na>(a)</na> Dauid himſelf. IVDGE <na>(b)</na> bô Lord them that hurt me: ouerthrow them that impugne me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Dauid ſignifieth beloued deſiderable, or ſtrong of hand, that is Chriſt, aboue al beloued of God, deſired of man, the ſtrong conquerour of death and hel. S. Aug. in hunc locum.

notes.label: b
notes.text: By way of imprecation he prophecieth that God wil ouerthrow the perſecutors of Chriſt, and of Chriſtians.

verses.text: Take <na>(c)</na> armour and <na>(d)</na> shield: and riſe vp to helpe me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: offenſiue

notes.label: d
notes.text: denfenſiue.

verses.text: Bring forth the ſword, and <na>(e)</na> shut vp againſt them, that perſecute me: ſay to my ſoule: I am thy ſaluation.

notes.label: e
notes.text: preoccupate and preuent the malice of the perſecutor.

verses.text: Let them <na>(f)</na> be counfounded & ashamed, that ſeeke my ſoule. Let them be turned backward, and be confounded that thinke euil againſt me

notes.label: f
notes.text: Such a punishment and confuſion shal fal in the end vpon al the malicious, after that the iuſt shal haue ouercome tribulations.

verses.text: Be they made as duſt before the face of winde; and the angel of our Lord ſtraictning them.
Let their way be made darkeneſſe and ſlippernes: and the angel of our Lord purſewing them.
Becauſe they haue hid the deſtruction of their ſnare for me without cauſe: in vaine haue they vpbrayded my ſoule.
Let the ſnare which he knoweth not, come on him; and the net, which he hath hid, catch him: and let him fal into the verie ſame ſnare.
But <na>(g)</na> my ſoule shal reioyce in our Lord: and shal be delighted vpon <na>(h)</na> his ſaluation.

notes.label: g
notes.text: In the time of truble in hope,

notes.label: h
notes.text: after deliuerie, in eternal ſaluation,

verses.text: Al my bones shal ſay: Lord, who is like to thee? Deliuering the needie from the hand of them that are ſtronger then he: the needie and poore from them that ſpoile him.
<na>(i)</na> Vniuſt witneſſes ryſing vp, asked me things that <na>(k)</na> I knew not.

notes.label: i
notes.text: ſuch falſe witneſſes did riſe againſt Chriſt Mat. 26.

notes.label: k
notes.text: thinges that were not; for God himſelfe, that knoweth al thinges knoweth not that which neither was, is, nor can be.

verses.text: They repayed me euil things for good, <na>(l)</na> ſterilitie to my ſoule.

notes.label: l
notes.text: they made priuation of my life, verified in Chriſt, not in Dauid, for he was killed by his enemies.

verses.text: But I when they were trubleſome to me, <na>(m)</na> did put on cloth of heare. I humbled my ſoule in faſting: and my prayer shal be turned into my boſome.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Al our Sauiours life was penance for others, needing none for himſelfe.

verses.text: As a <na>(n)</na> neighbour, as our brother, ſo did I pleaſe: as mourning and ſorowful ſo was I humbled.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Chriſt the good Samaritane that releeued the wounded man. Luc. 10.

verses.text: And they <na>(o)</na> reioyced againſt me, and <na>(p)</na> came together: <na>(q)</na> ſcourges were gathered together vpon me, and I was <na>(r)</na> ignorant.

notes.label: o
notes.text: al this was fulfilled according to the letter in our Sauiours paſſion.

notes.label: p
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: q
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: r
notes.text: Our Lord knoweth not anie iuſt cauſe, why the Iewes ſo perſecuted him, for they had no iuſt cauſe but meere malice.

verses.text: They were diſſipated, and not compunct, they tempted me, they ſcorned me with ſcorning: they gnashed vpon me with their teeth.
Lord <na>(s)</na> when wilt thou regard? <na>(t)</na> reſtore thou my ſoule from their malignitie, myne only one from the lions.

notes.label: s
notes.text: as Pſal. 21. and Mat. 27. God why haſt thou forſaken me? not deliuered me from temporal death, nor yelded me ſuch conſolation, as thou gaueſt other Sainctes in their agonies?

notes.label: t
notes.text: a prophecie of Chriſts reſurrection.

verses.text: I wil confeſſe to thee in <na>(v)</na> the great Church, in a graue people I wil prayſe thee.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Prophecie of the Catholique Church. as Pſal. 21.

verses.text: Let them not reioyce ouer me that are my aduerſaries vniuſtly: <na>(w)</na> that hate me without cauſe, and twinckle with the eies.

notes.label: w
notes.text: This place is applied by our Sauiour to himſelfe. Ioan. 15.

verses.text: Becauſe they ſpake in deede <na>(x)</na> peaceably to me: and in the anger of the earth ſpeaking they meant guiles.

notes.label: x
notes.text: The Phariſes and Herodians ſaid: Maſter we know that thou art a true ſpeaker &c. meaning to intrappe him with treaſon. Mat. 22.

verses.text: And they <na>(y)</na> opened their mouth a wide vpon me: they ſaid; Wel, wel, our eies haue ſeene.

notes.label: y
notes.text: The ſame Phariſes and Prieſtes iudged him woorthy of death, and procured the people to crie: Crucifie him, crucifie, him.

verses.text: Thou haſt ſene ô Lord, keepe not ſilence: <na>(z)</na> Lord depart not from me.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Againe his Reſurrection is prophecied.

verses.text: Ariſe and attend to my iudgement: my God, and my Lord vnto my cauſe.
Iudge me according to thy iuſtice ô Lord my God, and let them not reioyce ouer me
Let them not ſay in their hartes: Wel, wel, to our ſoule: neither let them ſay: We haue deuoured him.
Let <na>(a)</na> them blush and be ashamed together, that reioyce at my euils. Let them be clothed with confuſion and shame; that ſpeake great things vpon me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: At the day of iudgement the Wicked shal receiue ſentence of damnation.

verses.text: Let <na>(b)</na> them reioyce and be glad, that wil my iuſtice: and let them ſay alwayes: Our Lord be magnified, that wil the peace of his ſeruant.

notes.label: b
notes.text: the bleſſed of eternal glorie.

verses.text: And my tongue shal meditate thy iuſtice, thy prayſe al the day.

chapters.summary: Dauid, in figure of Chriſt, prophetically by way of inuocating Gods helpe, forsheweth his perſecution, and the iuſt reuenge vpon his perſecutors, 9. with praiſe to God. 13. his charitie towards his cruel aduerſaries. 17. whom neuertheles God punisheth, 20. for pretending peace in wordes, and in fact perſecuting, 23. rendering to al as they deſerue. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt's perſecution.
The 5. key.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Vnto the end, to <na>(b)</na> the ſeruant of our Lord Dauid him ſelfe.

notes.label: a
notes.text: More ſpecially deſcribing the ſtate of men in the new teſtament, then in the old.

notes.label: b
notes.text: inſtruction for Dauid not as a king, or a prophet, but as the poore ſeruant of God.

verses.text: THE vniuſt hath ſaid within him ſelfe, that he <na>(c)</na> would ſinne: there is no feare of God before his eies

notes.label: c
notes.text: wittingly and reſolutely preferring wicked life before vertuous.

verses.text: Becauſe he hath done deceitfully in his ſight: <na>(d)</na> that his iniquitie may be found vnto hatred.

notes.label: d
notes.text: God ſo hateth ſinne committed of meere malice, that he commonly reiecteth ſuch ſinners, and more often offereth new grace to thoſe, that ſinne of frailitie, or ignorance.

verses.text: The wordes of his mouth are iniquitie, and guile: he <na>(e)</na> would not vnderſtand that he might doe wel.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Some ignorance is inuincible whē one hath a good wil to lerne, doing his endeuour to knovv the truth in doctrin, & his dutie in manners, but can not get knowlege therof, and then he is excuſed before God; though he erre in opinion, or in fact: others are negligent to lerne, and their error is groſſe ignorance and is a ſinne, greater or leſſe, according to the importance of the thing, which they ouhgt to knovv. Others are more vvilful, deſiring to be ignorant; that they may ſinne vvith the leſſe remorſe, or repining of their ovvne conſcience, and this is affected ignorance, and moſt hainous, and odious ſinne. For which God often leauing them deſtitute of ordinarie grace, which he geueth to others, they fal into reprobate ſenſe, and into more horrible ſinnes.

verses.text: He hath meditated iniquitie in his bed: he hath ſet himſelfe on euery way not good, and malice he hath not hated.
Lord <na>(f)</na> thy mercie is in heauen: and <na>(g)</na> thy truth euen to the clowdes.

notes.label: f
notes.text: God doth not vtterly ſhut vp his mercie from the moſt wilful & wicked ſinners, but geueth them ſometimes good motions, and ſufficient helpe, thar they may repent, be iuſtified & ſaued, if they do not wittingly harden their owne hartes, and ſtil wilfully repel Gods grace.

notes.label: g
notes.text: For ſo God pomiſeth (vvho is moſt faithful) that he vvil forgeue ſinners, and receiue them into his fauoure againe, whenſoeuer they reſoluing to ſerue him, repent and ceaſe to ſinne.

verses.text: Thy iuſtice as the hilles of God: thy iudgementes are great depth. Men & <na>(h)</na> beaſtes thou wilt ſaue ô Lord:

notes.label: h
notes.text: Thou ô God that haſt care of al creatures, not only of men but alſo of brute beaſtes, art euer readie of thy part to ſaue both moderate men, in vvhom the light of reaſon remaineth, and alſo groſſe ſenſeles perſons, vvhich are become brutish like horſe and mule or other beaſtes.

verses.text: as thou <na>(i)</na> haſt multiplied thy mercie ô God. But <na>(k)</na> the children of men, <na>(l)</na> shal hope in the couert of thy winges.

notes.label: i
notes.text: For ſo our Lord multiplieth his mercie.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Yet with condition that ſenſles or brutish men, muſt become reaſonable men, the children of men, not coltes, whelpes, pigges &c.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Sinners thus conuerted shal not only haue al neceſſaries in this life, as al liuing creatures haue in this world, but alſo shal hope of ſpiritual, heauenly, & eternal glorie prepared for Angels, and children of men: as in the verſes folovving.

verses.text: They shal be inebriated with the plentie of thy houſe: and with the torrent of thy pleaſure thou shalt make them drinke,
Becauſe with thee is the fountaine of life: and in thy light we shal ſee light.
Extend thy mercie to them that know thee, and thy iuſtice to them, that are of a right hart.
Let <na>(m)</na> not the foote of pride come to me: and let not <na>(n)</na> the hand of a ſinner moue me.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Leſt anie impediment hinder the obtayning and poſſeſſion of eternal revvard, the iuſt muſt ſpecially pray not to be infected vvith pride:

notes.label: n
notes.text: nor be ouercome by the forcible tentations of other ſinners, by perſvvaſion, nor euil example.

verses.text: There <na>(o)</na> haue they fallen that worke iniquitie: they were expelled, <na>(p)</na> neither could they ſtand.

notes.label: o
notes.text: The firſt ſinne, tovvit of diuels, vvas pride, and mans ſinne vvas by perſvvaſion of the diuel.

notes.label: p
notes.text: neither of which could eſcape punishment.

chapters.summary: The prophet deſcribeth the wicked malice of obſtinate ſinners 6. Againſt which he oppoſeth Gods infinite goodnes, 9. with his prouident mercie towards the worſt, and iuſt reward of the good; 12. praying to eſcape the dangerous gulfe of pride. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence.
The 3. key.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> A Pſalme <na>(a)</na> to Dauid him ſelf. HAVE <na>(b)</na> no emulation toward the malignant: neither enuie them that doe iniquitie.

notes.label: a
notes.text: For Dauids and euery iuſt mans inſtruction.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Neither be thou offended that the wicked do proſper in this world, nor imitate them that thou maiſt alſo proſper.
This Pſalme is compoſed in order of the Alphabet, euerie diſtick beginning vvith a diuers letter, to moue the reader to diligent attention, which may ſerue in place of a larger cōmentarie,

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(c)</na> they shal quickely wither as graſſe: and as the bloſſomes of herbes they shal ſoone fal.

notes.label: c
notes.text: For al this life, and conſequently the proſperitie therof is shorte, and vncertaine.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Hope in our Lord and doe good: and inhabite the land, and thou <na>(e)</na> shalt be fed in the riches therof.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Put thy truſt in God, liuing content in this world:

notes.label: e
notes.text: & he wil geue thee that is neceſſarie.

verses.text: Be delighted in our Lord: and he wil geue thee the petitions of thy hart.
<na>(f)</na> Reuele thy way to our Lord, and hope in him: and he wil doe it.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Commend al thyn affaires to God.

verses.text: And he wil <na>(g)</na> bring forth thy iuſtice as light: and thy iudgement as midday:

notes.label: g
notes.text: Partly making vertue appeare to the comfort of the vertuous, and example of others in this life, but eſpecially in the next world.

verses.text: be ſubiect to our Lord, and pray him. Haue no emulation in him, that proſpereth in his way: in a man that doth iniuſtices.
Ceaſe from wrath, and leaue furie: haue not emulation that thou be malignant.
Becauſe they that are malignant, shal be caſt out: but they that expect our Lord, the ſame shal inherite <na>(h)</na> the land.

notes.label: h
notes.text: the land of the liuing.

verses.text: And yet a litle while, and the ſinner shal not be: and thou shalt ſeeke his place, and shal not find it.
<cr>[1]</cr> But the meeke shal inherite the land, and shal be delighted in multitude of peace.
The ſinner shal obſerue the iuſt: and shal gnash vpon him with his teeth.
But our Lord shal ſcorne him: becauſe he foreſeeth that his day shal come.
Sinners haue drawen out the ſword; they haue bent their bowe; That they may deceiue the poore and needie: that they may murder the right of hart.
Let <na>(i)</na> their owne ſwordes enter into their hartes: and let their bowe be broken.

notes.label: i
notes.text: By way of imprecation (as in manie other places) the prophet forsheweth that wicked men shal fal into the euils, which they prepare for others.

verses.text: Better is a litle to the iuſt, aboue much riches of ſinners.
Becauſe the armes of ſinners shal be broken in pieces: but our Lord comfirmeth the iuſt.
Our Lord knoweth the daies of the immaculate: and their inheritance shal be for euer.
They shal not be confounded in the euil time, and in the dayes of famine they shal be filled:
becauſe the ſinners shal perish. But the enemies of our Lord forthwith as they shal be honoured and exalted, vanishing shal vanish as ſmoke.
The ſinner shal borrow, and not pay: but the iuſt is merciful and wil geue.
Becauſe they that bleſſe him shal inherite the land: but they that curſe him shal perish.
With our Lord the ſteppe of man shal be directed: and he shal like wel of his way.
When <na>(k)</na> he shal fal, he shal not be bruſed: becauſe our Lord putteth his hand vnder.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Though the iuſt fal of frailtie or ignorance into venial ſinne, yet Gods grace shal ſtay him that he fal not into mortal. The iuſt falleth ſeuen times in the day, & riſeth. Prou. 24.

verses.text: I haue bene yong, for I am old: and I haue not ſene the iuſt forſaken, <na>(l)</na> nor his ſeede ſeeking bread.

notes.label: l
notes.text: So king Dauid obſerued: and it very rarely happeneth, that the iuſt or their children are deſtitute of neceſſarie ſuſtenance in this vvorld. If it chance in ſome, it is to their greater merite, and is manifeſtly recompenſed in ſpiritual giftes. In which ſenſe S. Baſil expoundeth, that it is alwayes verified For God euer rewardeth good workes either temporally, or ſpiritually, or both wayes. S. Auguſtin alſo (conc. 3. in hunc Pſal.) exemplifieth in Abraham, Iſaac, and Iacob with al his familie, who were forced to goe into other countries by reaſon of famine, and by Gods prouidence were there ſuſtained, Gen. 12. 26. 46. and S. Paul among his other tribulations mentioneth famine and thirſt. 2. Cor. 11. v. 27. Seing therfore theſe ſo iuſt perſons ſought their bread in neceſſitie, he expoundeth this holie Scripture in the Allegorical ſenſe, that the Church from her beginning in Ieruſalem to the end of the world, neuer wanteth the true word of God, true faith and doctrin, which is the ſpiritual bread vvhervvith the ſoule is nourished.

verses.text: Al the day he is merciful and lendeth: and his ſeede shal be in bleſſing.
<na>(m)</na> Decline from euil, and doe good: and <na>(n)</na> inhabite for euer and euer.

notes.label: m
notes.text: In theſe tvvo prīciples, declining from euil and doing good, true iuſtice conſiſteth.

notes.label: n
notes.text: and he that finally obſerueth theſe tvvo pointes, meriteth and shal poſſeſſe heauen.

verses.text: Becauſe our Lord loueth iudgement, and he wil not forſake his ſainctes: they shal be preſerued for euer. The vniuſt shal be punished: and the ſeede of the impious shal perish.
But the iuſt shal inherite the land: and shal inhabite for euer and euer vpon it.
The mouth of the iuſt shal meditate wiſedome, and his tong shal ſpeake iudgement. <cr>[1]</cr>
The law of his God in his hart: and his ſteppes shal not be ſupplanted.
The ſinner conſidereth the iuſt: and ſeeketh to <na>(o)</na> murder him.

notes.label: o
notes.text: to draw him to mortal ſinne, which is death of the ſoule.

verses.text: But our Lord wil not leaue him in his handes: neither wil he condemne him, when iudgement shal be geuen of him.
Expect our Lord, and keepe his way: and he wil exalt thee, that thou mayſt inherite the land: when the ſinners shal perish thou shalt ſee.
I haue ſeene the impious highly exalted, and aduanced as the ceders of Libanus.
And I paſſed by, and behold he was not: and I ſought him, and his place was not found.
Keepe innocencie, and ſee equitie: becauſe there are <na>(p)</na> remaynes for the peaceable man.

notes.label: p
notes.text: rewardes.

verses.text: But the vniuſt shal perish together: the remaines of the impious shal perish.
But the ſaluation of the iuſt is <na>(q)</na> of our Lord: and he is their potector in the time of tribulation.

notes.label: q
notes.text: mans iuſtice and wel doing is not of his owne powre but of Gods grace.

verses.text: And our Lord wil helpe them, and deliuer them: and he wil take them away from ſinners, and ſaue them: becauſe they haue hoped in him.

chapters.summary: An exhortation not to enuie nor imitate the euil, who for moſt part proſper in this world, and are damned eternally: but to flee euil and doe good, duly conſidering that God diuerſly permitteth and punisheth the wicked, and likewiſe comforteth and afflicteth the iuſt, al for their good. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
An exhortation to contempt of this world.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme of Dauid, in <na>(a)</na> recordation of the ſabbath.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In remembrance that by ſinne we loſt the reſt and peace, which man had in the ſtate of innocencie; ſecondly we loſt the peace of conſcience; thirdly the reſt and peace of eternal felicitie.

verses.text: LORD <na>(b)</na> rebuke me nor in thy furie: <na>(c)</na> nor chaſtiſe me in thy wrath.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Condemne me not to eternal paine:

notes.label: c
notes.text: nor punish me in purgatorie fire; but purge me ſo in this life, that the purging fire be not needful. By which fire (ſaith S. Auguſtin) though ſome ſhal be ſaued ( grauior tamen erit ille ignis, quam quicquid poteſt homo pati in hac vita) yet that fire shal be more greuous, then whatſoeuer a man can ſuffer in this llife. S. Gregory alſo expoundeth this ſame place, as if Dauid ſayd thus: I know it wil come to paſſe, that after the end of this life, ſome shal be cleanſed by purging flames, ſome ſhal be vnder the ſentence of eternal damnation. But becauſe I do eſteme that tranſitorie fire more intolerable then al preſent tribulation, I deſire not only not to be rebuked in furie of eternal damnation, but alſo I feare to be purged in the wrath of tranſitorie correption. Thou therfore ô Lord whom I ſerue in my ſpirite, whom I know to be the Sauiour of al men, rebuke me not in furie of perpetual damnation, nor chatiſe me in wrath of purging puniſhment. See Annotat. Pſal. 6.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(d)</na> thy arrowes are faſt ſticked in me: and thou haſt <na>(e)</na> faſtened thy hand vpon me.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Afflictions of mind and bodie ſent by thy iuſt iudgement.

notes.label: e
notes.text: thou haſt ſtrooke me with an heauie hand.

verses.text: There is <na>(f)</na> no health in my flesh, at <na>(g)</na> the face of thy wrath: my bones haue no peace at <na>(h)</na> the face of my ſinnes.

notes.label: f
notes.text: I already feele in my flesh, in al my bones, and powres great affliction,

notes.label: g
notes.text: conſidering thy iuſtice,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and my ſinnes.

verses.text: Becauſe mine iniquities are gone <na>(i)</na> ouer my head: and as a <na>(k)</na> heauie burden are become heauie vpon me.

notes.label: i
notes.text: which are excedingly increaſed, almoſt ouerwhelming my ſpirite.

notes.label: k
notes.text: ſinnes not washed away by penance by their weight carie the ſoule into more and more wickednes.

verses.text: My <na>(l)</na> ſcarres are putrified and corrupted, becauſe of my folishnes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: ſtil corrupting thoſe partes which were whole before, as a peſtered ſore that is not cured.

verses.text: I am become miſerable, and am made <na>(m)</na> crooked euen to the end: I went ſorowful al the day.

notes.label: m
notes.text: not able to goe ſtreight to do anie good worke, being guiltie of greuous ſinne.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(n)</na> my loynes are filled with illuſions: and there is no health in my flesh.

notes.label: n
notes.text: concupiſcence ſtriuing in me.

verses.text: I am afflicted and am humbled excedingly: I <na>(o)</na> rored for the groning of my hart.

notes.label: o
notes.text: from the ſorrow of my hart, my voice hath broken out into clamour.

verses.text: Lord, <na>(p)</na> before thee is al my deſire: and my groning is not hid from thee.

notes.label: p
notes.text: ô God thou knoweſt my deſire, to be reſtored to thy fauour.

verses.text: My hart is trubled, my ſtrength hath forſaken me: and the light of mine eies, and the ſame is not with me.
My <na>(q)</na> frendes, and my neighbores haue approched, & ſtood againſt me. And they that were neere me, ſtood far of:

notes.label: q
notes.text: thoſe that were my freindes and companions in ſinne are become myn enemies, becauſe I forſake them:

verses.text: and they did violence which ſought my ſoule. And they that ſought me euils, <na>(r)</na> ſpake vanities: and meditated guiles al the day.

notes.label: r
notes.text: ſought by al meanes to intangle me againe.

verses.text: But I as <na>(s)</na> one deafe did not heare: and as one dumme not opening his mouth.

notes.label: s
notes.text: I now renoũce al ſinne.

verses.text: And I became as a man not hearing: and not hauing reproofes in his mouth.
Becauſe <na>(t)</na> in thee ô Lord haue I hoped, thou wilt heare me ô Lord my God.

notes.label: t
notes.text: I now relie vpon thee ô God.

verses.text: <na>(v)</na> Becauſe I ſaid: Leſt ſometime mine enemies reioyce ouer me: and whiles my feete are moued, they ſpeake great thinges vpon me.

notes.label: v
notes.text: for this cauſe I am returned to thee and doe pray that mine enemies may not preuail againſt me.

verses.text: Becauſe I <na>(w)</na> am readie for ſcourges: and my ſorow is in my ſight alwaies:

notes.label: w
notes.text: I reſigne my ſelfe to thee.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(x)</na> I wil declare my iniquitie: and I wil <na>(y)</na> thinke for my ſinne.

notes.label: x
notes.text: though thou knoweſt al yet with mouth confeſſion is made to ſaluation.

notes.label: y
notes.text: and I meditate of that which my ſinne hath deſerued.

verses.text: But mine enemies liue, and are confirmed ouer me: and they are multiplied that hate me vniuſtly.
They that repay euil thinges for good, <na>(z)</na> detracted from me: becauſe I folowed goodnes.

notes.label: z
notes.text: one kind of detraction is in reueling ſecrete faultes, an other in feaning and imputing falſe crimes, the third ( here mentioned ) in calling vertue vice, as penance, hypochriſie.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Forſake me not ô Lord my God, depart not from me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Graunt me Lord final perſeuerãce in thy grace, and ſeruice.

verses.text: Attend vnto my help, ô Lord the God of my ſaluation.

chapters.summary: King Dauid, or anie other penitent, earneſtly prayeth God to remitte his ſinnes, and mitigate the paines which he acknowledgeth him ſelfe to haue deſerued, 12. lamenting the afflictions which he ſuffereth by ſuch as ſometimes were his freindes, 14. whoſe tentations he now reſiſteth, truſting in God, reſigning himſelfe to Gods wil, confeſſing his owne iniquitie, and humbly praying for Gods helpe. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The third penitential Pſalm.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, to <na>(b)</na> Idithun him ſelfe, a canticle of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Some expound this Pſalme of the Iewes in captiuitie in Babylon, but this title, and the matter conteyned shew, that it rather peteineth to the new Teſtament.

notes.label: b
notes.text: to be ſongue by Idithun and his ſcholars & ſucceſſors, or rather by Chriſtianes.

verses.text: I <na>(c)</na> HAVE ſaid: I wil keepe my waies: that I offend not in my tongue. I haue ſet a gard to my mouth, when the ſinner ſtood againſt me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: weake men in affliction not able to deliuer them ſelues, ſeeke reuenge, by murmuring and other euil ſpeaches, but the perfect reſolue to rule their tongues:

verses.text: I was dumme and humbled, and kept ſilence <na>(d)</na> from good thinges: and <na>(e)</na> my ſorrow was renewed.

notes.label: d
notes.text: euen to forbeare ſometimes from their owne iuſt defence:

notes.label: e
notes.text: though therby they indure more perſecution.

verses.text: My <na>(f)</na> hart waxed hote within me: and in my meditation a fyre shal burne.

notes.label: f
notes.text: ſorow ſuppreſſed maketh the hart to burne with zele, and indignation.

verses.text: I haue ſpoken in my tongue: Lord <na>(g)</na> make mine end knowne to me. And the number of my daies what it is: that I may know what is lacking to me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: If it may pleaſe thee let me know how long I shal liue, deſiring to dye; as Elias deſired. 3. Reg. 19.

verses.text: Behold thou haſt put my daies meaſurable, and my <na>(h)</na> ſubſtance is as nothing before thee. Doubtles al things are vanitie, euerie man liuing.

notes.label: h
notes.text: my life and al that I haue is as nothing compared to thy eternitie.

verses.text: Surely man paſſeth as <na>(i)</na> an image; yea and he is trubled <na>(k)</na> in vayne. He gathereth treaſure; and knoweth not to whom he shal gather them.

notes.label: i
notes.text: as a shadow or image appearing in a glaſſe, which is quickly forgotte.

notes.label: k
notes.text: therfore there is no cauſe man should be trubled in mind for temporal miſeries.

verses.text: And now what is my expectation? is not our Lord? and my ſubſtance is with thee.
From al mine iniquities deliuer me: <na>(l)</na> a reproch to the foolish thou haſt geuen me.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Thou haſt ſuffered me to be reproched by the foolish that proſper in this world.

verses.text: I was dumme, and opened not my mouth, <na>(m)</na> becauſe thou didſt it:

notes.label: m
notes.text: I know my tribulation is by thy prouidence.

verses.text: Remoue thy ſcourges from me.
By the ſtrength of thy hand I haue faynted in reprehenſions: for iniquitie thou haſt chaſtiſed man. And thou haſt made his <na>(o)</na> ſoule pyne away as a ſpider: but vaynly is euerie man trubled.

notes.label: o
notes.text: my life decayeth as a ſpider hauing ſpent al her moyſture.

verses.text: Heare my prayer ô Lord, and my petition; with thyne eares receiue my teares. Keepe not ſilence: becauſe I am a <na>(p)</na> ſtranger with thee, and a pilgrime, as my fathers.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Al men are ſtrangers in this life, heauen being our home.

verses.text: Forgeue me, that I may <na>(q)</na> be refreshed before I depart: and <na>(r)</na> shal be no more.

notes.label: q
notes.text: that I may recouer ſpiritual ſtreingth in this life:

notes.label: r
notes.text: after which I shal not be in ſtate to do free workes of ſatisfaction nor merite.

chapters.summary: A iuſt man in remediles perſecution reſolueth to ſuffer al with peace and ſilence: 5. praying God to take him from this world, confeſſing the vanitie therof. 8. and relying on Gods prouidence (11. who punisheth man for his ſinnes) prayeth for releaſe. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Gods prouidence.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, a Pſalme to Dauid himſelfe.

notes.label: a
notes.text: perteyning vnto the new Teſtament.

verses.text: EXPECTING <na>(b)</na> I expected our Lord, and he hath attended to me.

notes.label: b
notes.text: the faithful of the old and new Teſtament reioyce in the coming of Chriſt.

verses.text: And he heard my prayers, and brought me out of the lake of miſerie, and from the myre of dregges. And hath ſet my feete vpon a rocke: and hath directed my ſteppes.
And he hath put a new canticle into my mouth: a ſong to our God. Manie shal ſee, and shal feare: and they shal hope in our Lord.
Bleſſed is the man, whoſe hope is in the name of our Lord: and hath not had regard to vanities and falſe madnes.

Thou haſt done manie thy meruelous thinges ô Lord my God: & in thy cogitations there is none that may be like to thee. I <na>(c)</na> haue declared and haue ſpoken: they <na>(d)</na> multiplied aboue number.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Chriſt by him ſelfe and by others preached the Goſpel of ſaluation.

notes.label: d
notes.text: the multiplication of Chriſtians therby.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Sacrifice and oblation thou wouldeſt not: but <na>(f)</na> eares thou haſt perfited to me. <cr>[1]</cr> Holocauſt and for ſinne thou didſt not require:

notes.label: e
notes.text: No ſacrifice of the old teſtament ſufficed to ſatisfie Gods iuſtice for the ſinne of man.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Chriſt by the eare of obedience performed the redemption of man by his death, as was determined from eternitie. S. Paul for [eares] ſaith [bodie] See Annotations. Heb. 10.

verses.text: then ſaid I, Behold I come. In the <na>(g)</na> head of the booke it is written of me,

notes.label: g
notes.text: The ſumme of holie Scripture is of Chriſts Incarnation & death for redemption of man.

verses.text: that I should doe thy wil: my God I would, and thy law in the middes of my hart.
I haue <na>(h)</na> declared thy iuſtice in the great Church, loe I wil not ſtay my lippes: Lord thou haſt knowen it.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Againe Chriſt inculcateth the preaching and receiuing of his Goſpel in the whole world.

verses.text: Thy iuſtice I haue not hid in my hart: thy truth and thy ſaluation I haue ſpoken. I haue not hid thy mercie, and thy truth from the <na>(i)</na> great councel.

notes.label: i
notes.text: In the greateſt and wiſeſt congregations of this world, Chriſt concealeth not his mercie and truth. So himſelfe profeſſed before Annas, Caiphas, Pilate, and their councels. S. Paul preached Chriſt at Athens, and in manie nations, and ſo the other Apoſtles. For their voice went into al the coaſtes of the earth.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> But thou ô Lord make not thy commiſerations farre from me: thy mercie and thy truth haue alwayes receiued me.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The prophet now ſpeaketh in the name of Chriſts myſtical bodie the Church: praying to be made partaker of mercie, and to be deliuered from euiles.

verses.text: Becauſe euils haue compaſſed me, which haue no number: mine iniquities haue ouertaken me, & I was <na>(l)</na> not able to ſee. They are multiplied aboue the heares of my head: and <na>(m)</na> my hart hath forſaken me.

notes.label: l
notes.text: the ſinnes alſo of thoſe which beleue in Chriſt are ſo manie, that they can not be fully ſene in particular.

notes.label: m
notes.text: I almoſt faint in conſidering ſo manie and ſo great iniquities amongst thoſe that profeſſe Chriſt.

verses.text: It may pleaſe thee ô Lord to deliuer <na>(n)</na> me: Lord haue reſpect to helpe me.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The whole Church prayeth in the name of al for the infirme members.

verses.text: Let <na>(o)</na> them be confounded and ashamed together, that ſeeke my ſoule, to take it away. Let them be turned backward, and be ashamed that wil me euils.

notes.label: o
notes.text: The prophet foresheweth that the reprobate for their obſtinate malice, ſeeking to hurt others shal be confounded.

verses.text: Let them forthwith receiue their confuſion, that <na>(p)</na> ſay to me: Wel, wel.

notes.label: p
notes.text: that skornfully ſay: wel, wel: wishing al euil to good men.

verses.text: Let al <na>(q)</na> that ſeeke thee, reioyce and be glad vpon thee: and let them that loue thy ſaluation, ſay alwayes: Our Lord be magnified:

notes.label: q
notes.text: which not only in mouth and outward profeſſion, but alſo in ſinceritie of hart ſeeke thee, may with confidence reioyce, and praiſe God.

verses.text: But <na>(r)</na> I am a begger, and poore: Our Lord is careful of me. Thou art <na>(s)</na> my helper, & my protector: my God be not ſlacke.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Chriſt ſpeaketh in the name of ſinners truly repenting, whoſe ſinnes he vndertaketh to redeme, and wash away by his paſſion.

notes.label: s
notes.text: The faithful of the old teſtament pray for Chriſts firſt coming into this world, and the faithful now pray for his ſecond coming to purge his Church, and to reward the good.

chapters.summary: Chriſts faithful members after long expectation congratulate his coming in flesh. 6. He directing his ſpeach to his Father, profeſſeth to performe the Redemption of mankind, and to denounce the ſame in the whole world: 12. prayeth for his ſeruantes, vndertaking to ſatisfie for their ſinnes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_continuation.text: Redemption of mankind, and to denounce the ſame in the whole world: 12. prayeth for his ſeruantes, vndertaking to ſatisfie for their ſinnes. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Chriſts comming and redeming of mankind The 5 key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, a Pſalme to Dauid him ſelfe. <cr>[1]</cr>

cross_refs.text: Io. 13. v. 18. This Pſalm is alſo applied by the Church in the office of the ſick, whom whoſoever aſſiſteth in that caſe, may hope to have aſſiſtance in their own like neceſſity.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the new teſtament, as appeareth by the 10. verſe alleaged by our Sauiour. This Pſalme is alſo applied by the Church in the office of the ſick, whom whoſoeuer aſſiſteth in that caſe, may hope to haue aſſiſtance in their owne like neceſſitie.

verses.text: BLESSED is the man that vnderſtandeth concerning <na>(b)</na> the needie, and the poore: in <na>(c)</na> the euil day our Lord wil deliuer him.

notes.label: b
notes.text: He is happie that is not ſcandalized in Chriſt (Luc. 7 v. 23.) coming in pouertie, and ſuffering extreme afflictions.

notes.label: c
notes.text: He that truſteth in Chriſt, notwithſtanding the contrarie motiues of his wordlie miſerie, shal be deliuered by him in al diſtreſſe.

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(d)</na> preſerue him, and geue him life, and make him bleſſed in the land: and <na>(e)</na> deliuer him not vnto the wil of his enemies.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Our Lord wil geue to ſuch ſeruantes more grace in this life, and glorie in the next.

notes.label: e
notes.text: not ſuffer him to be ouercome in tentations.

verses.text: Our Lord helpe him <na>(f)</na> vpon the bed of his ſorow: thou haſt turned al his couche in his infirmitie.

notes.label: f
notes.text: When ſuch conſtant ſeruantes are ſick to death, Chriſt wil moſt eſpecially comforte and helpe them.

verses.text: I ſaid: <na>(g)</na> Lord haue haue mercie on me: heale my ſoule, becauſe I haue ſinned to thee.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Chriſt in the behalf of his myſtical bodie confeſſeth their ſinnes, and prayeth for them.

verses.text: Mine enemies haue ſpoken euils to me: When shal he die, <na>(h)</na> and his name perish?

notes.label: h
notes.text: After death ſuffered for mankind Chriſt riſeth, and his name and kingdom is glorious.

verses.text: And if <na>(i)</na> he came in to ſee, he ſpake vayne thinges: his hart hath gathered together iniquitie to him ſelfe. He went forth. and ſpake together.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thoſe that came not of good wil, but of malice to obſerue Chriſts deedes and wordes, carped at both, ſometimes ſaying, he taught againſt the law, and againſt Moyſes; ſometymes that he caſt out diuels in the powre of Beelſebub.

verses.text: Al mine enemies whiſpered againſt me: they did thinke euils to me.
They <na>(k)</na> haue determined an vniuſt word againſt me: <na>(l)</na> Shal not he that ſleepeth adde to ryſe againe?

notes.label: k
notes.text: At laſt they reſolued that he should die.

notes.label: l
notes.text: But they could not ſo ſuppreſſe his powre, for he roſe againe in glorie.

verses.text: For <na>(m)</na> the man alſo of my peace, in whom I hoped: who did eate my breades, hath greatly troden me vnder foote <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: m
notes.text: By our Sauiours application of this verſe, it is certaine that the traitor Iudas is here deſcribed. Ioa. 13. v. 18.

verses.text: But thou ô Lord haue mercie vpon me, and raiſe me vp againe: and I <na>(n)</na> wil repay them.

notes.label: n
notes.text: in the day of iudgement Chriſt Iudge of al wil render to euerie one as they deſerue.

verses.text: In this I haue knowen that thou wouldeſt me: becauſe mine enemie shal not reioyce ouer me.
But me thou haſt receiued <na>(o)</na> becauſe of innocencie: and thou haſt confirmed me in thy ſight for euer.

notes.label: o
notes.text: As before in reſpect of ſinners, Chriſt Iudge of al wil render to euerie one: ſo here in his owne perſon he auoucheth his owne innocencie, which made him apt to ſatisfie for others.

verses.text: Bleſſed be our Lord the God of Iſrael <na>(p)</na> from the beginning of the world, and for euermore: <na>(q)</na> Be it, be it.

notes.label: p
notes.text: For this mercie of Almightie God in ſauing the elect by his Sonnes death, he is to be praiſed for euer eternally.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Al the bleſſed agree in this, that God is eternally to be praiſed and therto ſay Amen, So be it, ſo be it. Some diuide the Pſalmes into fiue bookes, ſuppoſing the firſt booke to end here with theſe wordes; Be it, be it: not obſeruing that the laſt Pſalme hath not this ending. S Ierom confuteth this opinion by our Sauiours, and S. Peters naming it the booke, not bookes of Pſalmes. Luc 20. v. 42. Act. 1. Moreouer if this were the end of one booke, then the Pſalme folowing ſhould not be called the 41. Pſalme, but the firſt Pſalme of the ſecond booke.

chapters.summary: The prophet pronounceth them happie that wil beleue in Chriſt, coming in humilitie and pouertie. 5. Chriſt deſcribeth his owne poore afflicted ſtate in this life, by reaſon he is to ſatisfie for the ſinnes of the world; the malice of his aduerſaries, 10. eſpecially of Iudas, 11. and by way of prayer, prophecieth his owne Reſurrection. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt's Paſſion and Reſurrection.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, vnderſtanding to the ſonnes of <na>(a)</na> Core.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The ſonnes of Core repented, and departed from their fathers ſchiſme, and ſo eſcaped miraculoſly the horrible pitte of damnation, into which their father and his complices fel. Num. 26. v. 10. By which example al ſeduced, and deceiued Chriſtians are admonished, not to perſiſt in ſchiſme or other ſinnes. And wordlie men, ambicious of honour be warned to deſire & ſeke God aboue al thinges, firſt of al the kingdome of heauen (to be liuing members of the Catholique Church) and the iuſtice therof: to ſeke thinges which are aboue, not which are vpon the earth; leſt hel deuoure them, as it deuoured the complices of Core. Num. 16 v. 31.

verses.text: EVEN as the harte <na>(b)</na> deſireth after the fountaines of waters: <na>(c)</na> ſo doth my ſoule deſire after thee ô God.

notes.label: b
notes.text: A harte waxing old, and burdened with much heare, and great hornes, draweth a ſerpent into his noſethrels, ſo being infected with poyſon, deſireth moſt ardently to drinke, and afterwards caſteth his hornes, and heare, and becometh as it were yong againe.

notes.label: c
notes.text: with ſuch feruent deſire a true penitent, feeling him ſelfe infected with poyſou of ſinnes, ſeeketh the water of Gods grace.

verses.text: My ſoule hath thirſted after God <na>(d)</na> the ſtrong <na>(e)</na> liuing: <na>(f)</na> when shal I come and appeare before the face of God?

notes.label: d
notes.text: God is omnipotent, and in dede the only-true liuing God: diuels who are honored in idols, can do no more then God permitteth, and ſo they can kil the ſoules, that conſent vnto their tentations, but can not reſtore ſpiritual life againe.

notes.label: e
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: f
notes.text: The ſoule being iuſtified, and ſtil aſſaulted with new tentations deſireth to be with God.

verses.text: My <na>(g)</na> teares haue beene breades vnto me day and night: whiles it is ſaid to me dayly: <na>(h)</na> Where is thy God?

notes.label: g
notes.text: I haue had no other refection, but to lenifie my ſorow with weping.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The wicked exprobate the iuſt, as though God would neuer helpe them, becauſe he ſuffereth them to be ſometimes long in tribulation.

verses.text: Theſe thinges haue I remembred, and haue powred out my ſoule in me, becauſe I shal paſſe into the place <na>(i)</na> of a meruelous tabernacle, euen to the houſe of God. In the yoyce of exultation, and confeſſion: the ſound of one feaſting.

notes.label: i
notes.text: King Dauid was not permitted to build the temple, much leſſe did he enter into anie ſuch meruelous tabernacle in his mortal life, but muſt nedes be vnderſtood, to ſpeake here of the heauenlie tabernacle, prepared by Chriſt for his ſeruants.

verses.text: Why <na>(k)</na> art thou ſorowful my ſoule? and why doſt thou truble me? Hope in God, becauſe yet I <na>(l)</na> wil confeſſe to him: the ſaluation of my countenance,

notes.label: k
notes.text: The prophet conforteth him ſelfe, or anie iuſt ſoule, in the hope of euerlaſting ioy.

notes.label: l
notes.text: I render thankes and praiſes.

verses.text: and my God. My ſoule is trubled toward my ſelfe; therfore wil I be mindful of thee from the land <na>(m)</na> of Iordan, and Hermoniim from the litle mountaine.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Al this life is like to the ſmal ſtraict place betwene Iordan and a litle hil called Hermoniim; but from this ſtraictnes the hope of the iuſt is, to be placed in heauen.

verses.text: Depth <na>(n)</na> calleth on depth, in the voice of <na>(o)</na> thy flould-gates. Al thy high thinges, and thy waues haue paſſed ouer me.

notes.label: n
notes.text: One tentation ſtil ſuccedeth an other:

notes.label: o
notes.text: and the ſame ſo great, as if God opened the gates; and ſuffered them to ouerflow like fluddes of water.

verses.text: In <na>(p)</na> the day our Lord hath commanded his mercie: and <na>(q)</na> in the night a ſong of him. With me <na>(r)</na> is prayer to the God of my life:

notes.label: p
notes.text: But God helpeth in opportunitie, not ſuffering his ſeruantes to be tempted aboue their ſtreingth, geuing them fruit with tentations:

notes.label: q
notes.text: yea in the greateſt tribulation, he geueth ordinarily moſt comfort, making them ſing ſpiritually in hart, if not alſo in voice.

notes.label: r
notes.text: one ſpecial meanes to procure diuine conſolation is prayer in diſtreſſe.

verses.text: I wil ſay to God: Thou art my defender. Why haſt thou forgotten me? and why goe I ſorowful, whiles mine enemie afflicteth me?
Whiles my bones are broken, mine enemies that truble me haue vpbrayded me: Whiles they ſay to me day by day: Where is thy God?
Why art thou heauie ô my ſoule? & why doſt thou truble me? <na>(s)</na> Hope in God, becauſe yet I wil confeſſe to him: the ſaluation of my countenance, and my God.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Stil the iuſt ſoule taketh comforth in aſſured hope of ſaluation, the eternal viſion of God.

chapters.summary: The feruent deſire of the iuſt, 6. much afflicted in this life, 12. and aſſured hope of eternal ioy. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Eternal glory.
The 10. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme <na>(a)</na> of Dauid. IVDGE <na>(b)</na> me ô God, & diſcerne my cauſe from the nation not holie, from the vniuſt and deceitful man <na>(c)</na> deliuer me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Holie Dauid often prefiguring Chriſt, here repreſenteth euerie faithful ſeruant of God, and particularly when they beginne a great and holie worke; as when Prieſtes celebrate the diuine Sacrifice, they with their aſſiſtantes recite by interchangeable verſes this Pſalme.

notes.label: b
notes.text: After that we haue examined, and prepared our ſelues to the moſt holie Sacrifice and Sacrament, according to S. Paules admonition (let a man proue himſelfe, and ſo eate this bread, and drinke this chalice, 1. Cor. 11.) we pray God, to iudge betwen our true ſincere intention, and the vniuſt deceipful endeuoures of our enimie: and ſo to deliuer and protect vs from ſutle malice.

notes.label: c
notes.text: and ſo to deliuer and protect vs from ſutle malice.

verses.text: Becauſe thou art God <na>(d)</na> my ſtrength: <na>(e)</na> why haſt thou repelled me? and why goe I ſorowful, <na>(f)</na> whiles the enemie afflicteth me?

notes.label: d
notes.text: VVith thee I can do anie thing, without thee nothing,

notes.label: e
notes.text: thou ſemeſt ſometimes not to regard me,

notes.label: f
notes.text: whiles tentations are more ſenſible then thy grace.

verses.text: Send forth <na>(g)</na> thy light and thy truth: <na>(h)</na> they haue conducted me, and haue brought me into thy holy hil, and into thy tabernacles.

notes.label: g
notes.text: As thou haſt ſent Chriſt the light and truth into this world, grant vs the ſame now in particular.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Theſe two giftes of God, the light of knowing our duties and truth, with ſincere intention to performe the ſame, haue brought vs into thy Church, and vnto thy Altar.

verses.text: And <na>(i)</na> I wil goe in to the altar of God: to God, which <na>(k)</na> maketh my youth ioyful.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Accompanied with light of truth, and ſincere intention, we confidently approch to thyn Altar ô God,

notes.label: k
notes.text: vvho changeſt our old corruption into newnes of life.

verses.text: I wil confeſſe to thee <na>(l)</na> on the harpe <na>(m)</na> ô God <na>(n)</na> my God: <na>(o)</na> why art thou ſorowful ô my ſoule? and doſt thou trubel me?

notes.label: l
notes.text: But to this purpoſe we praiſe God on the harpe, mortifying our affections.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The former word is of the plural number in hebrevv, Eloim, the other of the ſingular, ſignifying the Bleſſed Trinitie, one God.

notes.label: n
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: o
notes.text: Thou needeſt not therfore my ſoule, be penſiue, or deſolate.

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> Hope in God, becauſe yet <na>(q)</na> wil I cõfeſſe to him: the ſaluation <na>(r)</na> of my countenance, and <na>(s)</na> my God.

notes.label: p
notes.text: But truſt in God,

notes.label: q
notes.text: praiſe him,

notes.label: r
notes.text: vvhom I hope to ſee face to face,

notes.label: s
notes.text: the true eternal God.

chapters.summary: The iuſt inuocateth Gods ſentence againſt the deceiptful, that ſeeke his ſpiritual ouerthrow, 4. acknowledgeth his helpe, from almightie God the B. Trinitie, in whoſe viſion glorie conſiſteth. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
One God the B. Trinity.
The 1. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, for the ſonnes of <na>(b)</na> Core to vnderſtanding.

notes.label: a
