notes.text: Though this Pſalme doth firſt and literally perteyne to the people of Iſrael, yet al thinges happening to them, vvere in figure of the Chriſtian Catholique Church, vvhich begane vvith difficulties, aftervvards proſpered, and againe ſuffereth much perſecution.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Core ſignifieth caluus, bauld; alſo caluaria a ſcul, or place of ſculles: the name of the place vvhere our Sauiour vvas crucified, ſo the children of Core ſignifie the children of Chriſt. S. Aug.

verses.text: O GOD we haue heard with our eares: our fathers haue declared to vs. The <na>(c)</na> worke, that thou haſt wrought in their dayes: and in the dayes of old.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The particular calling of Abraham out of Chaldea, protection of him, and Iſaac, and Iacob, the deliuerie of al Iſrael out of Ægypt, and eſtablishing them in the promiſed land of Chanaan, with innumerable, great, and ſtrange thinges donne for them.

verses.text: Thy hand deſtroyed the nations, and thou didſt plant them: thou didſt afflict the peoples, and expel them:

For <na>(d)</na> not by their owne ſword did they poſſeſſe the land, and their owne arme did not ſaue them: But thy right hand, and thyne arme, and the illumination of thy countenance: becauſe <na>(e)</na> thou waſt pleaſed in them.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The Iſraelites conquered not by ordinarie povvre, but by the miraculous hand of God.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Not that this people deſerued of themſelues, but of Gods free election, al the vvorld being vvicked, he gaue peculiar grace to Abraham, Iſaac, Iacob and ſome others, and then for their ſakes protected the vvhole people, in them conſeruing a viſible Church.

verses.text: Thou art the ſame my king and my God: which commandeſt the ſaluations of Iacob.
In <na>(f)</na> thee we shal turne out our enemies with <na>(g)</na> the horne, & in thy name we shal contemne them that ryſe vp against vs.

notes.label: f
notes.text: As in former examples, ſo in Dauids time, not mans ſtreingth, but Gods hand gaue them great victories.

notes.label: g
notes.text: As an oxe vvith his horne caſteth a ſmal thing into the vvind.

verses.text: For I wil not hope in my bowe: and my ſword wil not ſaue me.
For thou haſt ſaued vs from them that afflict vs: and them that hate vs thou haſt confounded. <cr>[1]</cr>
In God we shal be prayſed al the day: and in thy name we wil confeſſe for euer.
But <na>(h)</na> now thou haſt repelled and confounded vs: and thou wilt not goe forth ô God in our hoſtes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The prophet fortelleth that after proſperitie God vvould ſuffer the Ievves to falle into captiuitie, & manie afflictions, which alſo ſignified allegorically diuers ſtates of Chriſts Church.

verses.text: Thou haſt turned vs backe behind our enemies: and they that hated vs, ſpoyled for themſelues.
Thou haſt geuen vs as sheepe that are to be eaten: and thou <na>(i)</na> haſt diſperſed vs among the nations.

notes.label: i
notes.text: The Iewes are now meruelouſly diſperſed, and depreſſed.

verses.text: Thou haſt ſold thy people <na>(k)</na> without price: and there was <na>(l)</na> no multitude in the exchanges of them.

notes.label: k
notes.text: In the deſtruction of Ieruſalem the remnant of the people were ſold for ſmal, as it wree for no price. They had ſold Chriſt for thirtie pence;

notes.label: l
notes.text: and now no multitude, nor number of money at al was geuen for them, but thirtie of them were ſold for one pennie, Ioſephus de bello Iudaico.

verses.text: Thou haſt made vs a reproche to our neighbours, a ſcorne and mocking ſtocke to them, that are round about vs.
Thou haſt made vs for a parable to the Gentiles: a wagging of the head among the peoples.
Al the day my shame is againſt me, and the confuſion of my face hath couered me.
At the voyce of the vpbrayder, and the reprocher: at the face of the enemie and perſecutor.
Al theſe thinges haue come vpon vs, <na>(m)</na> neither haue we forgotten thee: and we haue not done wickedly in thy teſtament.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Vntil Chriſts paſſion the Iewish people did not wholly fal from God, and true religion. And of them were choſen the Apoſtles, and manie others, that founded and propagated the Church of Chriſt.

verses.text: And our hart hath not reuolted backward: and <na>(n)</na> thou haſt declined our pathes from thy way:

notes.label: n
notes.text: The negatiue particle is here vnderſtood by zeugma, according to the hebrew thus: our hart hath not reuolted backward, neither haſt thou ſuffered our pathes to decline frō thy way.

verses.text: <na>(o)</na> Becauſe thou haſt humbled vs in the place of affliction, and the shadow of death hath couered vs.

notes.label: o
notes.text: An other hebrew phraiſe, If we haue, for, we haue not.

verses.text: If we haue forgotten the name of our God, and if we haue ſpred forth our handes to a ſtrange God:
Wil not God enquire of theſe thinges? For he knoweth the ſecretes of the hart. Becauſe <na>(p)</na> for thee we are killed al the day: we are eſtemed as sheepe of ſlaughter. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: p
notes.text: The Prophetes and others perſecuted partly before Chriſt, much more the Apoſtles, and other Chriſtians in the new Teſtament:

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> Ariſe why ſleepeſt thou ô Lord? Ariſe, and expel vs not to the end.

notes.label: q
notes.text: A prayer in affliction.

verses.text: Why doſt thou turne away thy face, forgetteſt our pouertie and our tribulation?
Becauſe <na>(r)</na> our ſoule is humbled in the duſt: our <na>(s)</na> bellie is glewed in the earth.

notes.label: r
notes.text: we are at deaths dore, readie to become duſt.

notes.label: s
notes.text: lying as groueling ſorowing on the earth:

verses.text: <na>(t)</na> Ariſe Lord, helpe vs: and redeme vs for thy name.

notes.label: t
notes.text: til thou deliuer vs from theſe tribulations.

chapters.summary: The prophet deſcribeth the firſt calling, and difficulte ſtate of the Iewish nation, 6. their proſperitie at other times. 10. Againe their afflictions in captiuitie, and perſecutions. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The ſtate of the Jews.
The 4. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, for them, <na>(b)</na> that shal be changed, <na>(c)</na> to the ſonnes of Core, <na>(d)</na> for vnderſtanding, <na>(e)</na> a Canticle for the beloued.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the new Teſtament.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Gentiles conuerted from paganiſme to Chriſtianitie:

notes.label: c
notes.text: and al others returning from ſchiſme, or other ſinnes,

notes.label: d
notes.text: for their inſtruction,

notes.label: e
notes.text: this Pſalme is a mariage ſongue of the beloued bridgrome and bride: Chriſt and his Church.

verses.text: MY <na>(f)</na> hart hath vttered <na>(g)</na> a good word: I tel my workes <na>(h)</na> to the king. My <na>(i)</na> tongue is the penne of a ſcribe, that <na>(k)</na> writeth ſwiftly.

notes.label: f
notes.text: I haue receiued by diuine inſpirarion in my hart and cogitation,

notes.label: g
notes.text: a moſt high Myſterie.

notes.label: h
notes.text: To the honour therfore and glorie of this king (vvhom I ſecretly ſee in my hart) I vtter and referre al my vvorkes, and this particular Canticle.

notes.label: i
notes.text: From the abundance of my hart, my tongue alſo ſpeaketh,

notes.label: k
notes.text: & that preſently without delay

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> Goodly of beautie aboue the ſonnes of men, grace is powred abrode in thy lippes: therfore hath God bleſſed thee for euer.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Deſcription of Chriſt, moſt excellent in al internal and external giftes.

verses.text: Be <na>(m)</na> girded with thy ſword vpon thy thigh, ô moſt mightie.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The prophet ſeing in ſpirite the perfections vvhich he wisheth in Chriſt, in maner of congratulating, deſcribeth his fortitude, fighting againſt the diuel for the Church.

verses.text: With thy beautie and fayrneſſe <na>(n)</na> intend, <na>(o)</na> procede proſperouſly, and <na>(p)</na> reigne, Becauſe of <na>(q)</na> truth, and <na>(r)</na> mildeneſſe, and <na>(s)</na> iuſtice: and thy right hand shal conduct thee meruelouſly.

notes.label: n
notes.text: purpoſing,

notes.label: o
notes.text: proſecuting,

notes.label: p
notes.text: and perfecting the conqueſt, and ſo eſtablishing thy ſpiritual kingdome.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Not vvith warlike armour of this world, but by aſſaulting the aduerſarie with truth:

notes.label: r
notes.text: defending thyſelfe and thy ſouldiers with the shield of mildnes,

notes.label: s
notes.text: and ſtriking the enemie with the ſword of iuſtice. VVhich right force of ſpiritual fight hath meruelous good ſucceſſe.

verses.text: Thy <na>(t)</na> sharpe arrowes, the <na>(v)</na> peoples vnderneth thee shal fal into the hartes of the kings enemies.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Preaching of Chriſts Goſpel, his grace mouing the hartes of the hearers, is liuelie and forcible, more pearcing then anie two edged ſword.

notes.label: v
notes.text: The example of people conuerted, shal moue the hartes of the aduerſaries to come alſo vnto the truth.

verses.text: Thy ſeate ô God <na>(w)</na> for euer and euer: a rod of direction the rod of thy kingdom.

notes.label: w
notes.text: Chriſts kingdom shal haue no end. Luc. 1. v. 33.

verses.text: Thou <na>(x)</na> haſt loued iuſtice, and haſt hated iniquitie: therfore God, <na>(y)</na> thy God, hath annoynted thee with the oile of gladnes <na>(z)</na> aboue thy felowes.

notes.label: x
notes.text: Thou defendeſt and rewardeſt the good, finally forſakeſt and puniſheſt the wicked.

notes.label: y
notes.text: more peculiarly the God of Chriſt, by hypoſtatical vnion.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Diuers kinges (as Dauid himſelfe, Ioſaphat, Ezechias, and Ioſias) were as godlie as Salomon, and perſeuered good to the end, which is doubted Salomon did not: but Chriſt incomparably was annointed, & indued with al graces aboue al kinges.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Myrrhe, and <na>(b)</na> Aloes, and <na>(c)</na> Caſſia from thy <na>(d)</na> garmentes, from houſes of yuorie; out of the which

notes.label: a
notes.text: Mortification which conſerueth from putrifying,

notes.label: b
notes.text: humilitie aſwaging pride,

notes.label: c
notes.text: being ſmal in the firſt ſpring grovveth great,

notes.label: d
notes.text: humanitie aſſumpted; and ſanctified perſons, in vvhom Chriſt dwelleth as in cleane, ſhining, odoriferous houſes;

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> the daughter of kinges haue delighted thee in thy honour.

notes.label: e
notes.text: ſincere faithful ſoules more deare to their ſpouſe Chriſt, then daughrers of temporal kinges.

verses.text: The <na>(f)</na> Queene ſtood on thy right hand in golden rayment: compaſſed with <na>(g)</na> varietie. <na>(h)</na> Heare daughter, and <na>(i)</na> ſee, and <na>(k)</na> incline thyne eare: and forget thy people, and the houſe of thy father.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The Catholique Church, in faith purified as gold:

notes.label: g
notes.text: vvith varietie of ſtates, as Clergie, Laity and diuers ſortes of religious Orders, and other profeſſions, al vnited in the ſame faith, hope, and charitie.

notes.label: h
notes.text: carifully al that Chriſt thy ſpouſe ſpeaketh to thee by his Spirite.

notes.label: i
notes.text: diligently put the ſame in practiſe:

notes.label: k
notes.text: vvith al obedience and readines, and returne not to former infidelitie, nor to corrupt life.

verses.text: And the king <na>(l)</na> wil couet thy beautie: becauſe he is the Lord thy God, and <na>(m)</na> they shal adore him.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Chriſt loueth the Church adorned with his giftes,

notes.label: m
notes.text: and mutually his true children loue and ſerue him.

verses.text: And the daughters <na>(n)</na> of Tyre with giftes, al the rich of the people shal beſech thy countenance.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Manie of al nations ſubmitte themſelues, and al that they haue to Chriſt.

verses.text: Al the glorie of that daughter of the king is <na>(o)</na> within, in <na>(p)</na> borders of gold

notes.label: o
notes.text: Internal vertues are moſt eſpecial ornaments:

notes.label: p
notes.text: exterior are required to edifie others in diuers ſortes of vertues.

verses.text: clothed round about with varieties. <na>(q)</na> Virgins shal be brought to the king after her: her <na>(r)</na> neighbours shal be brought to thee.

notes.label: q
notes.text: By this meanes manie more are conuerted to chriſtianitie:

notes.label: r
notes.text: and one countrie inuiteth and draweth an other.

verses.text: They shal be brought in ioy and exultation: they shal be brought into the temple of the king.
For <na>(s)</na> thy fathers there are borne ſonnes to thee: thou ſhalt make them princes ouer al the earth.

notes.label: s
notes.text: As Apoſtles came in place of Patriarches and Prophetes: ſo ſtil Biſhops, and Prieſtes ſuccede in the Church, paſtors, and gouernours therof.

verses.text: They shal <na>(t)</na> be mindeful of thy name in al generation and generation. Therfore shal <na>(v)</na> peoples confeſſe to thee for euer: and for euer and euer.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Theſe paſtores shal ſtil teach the true Chriſtian doctrin.

notes.label: v
notes.text: and ſtil there shal be Chriſtian people that wil folow and profeſſe the ſame.

chapters.summary: Dauid ſingularly moued in hart and tongue, 3. prophecieth Chriſts excellencie, indowing his Church with moſt worthie dowries. 11. by way of exhortation forshewing her internal and external beautie. 17. with perpetual ſucceſſion of Paſtors feeding the flock euen to the worlds end. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt moſt excellently endowing his Church.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, to the ſonnes of Core, for <na>(b)</na> the ſecretes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Belonging to the Church of Chriſt.

notes.label: b
notes.text: As wel the cauſe, vvhy God ſuffereth his Church to be perſecuted, as his aſſured protection in difficulties, are hidden ſecretes to the world.

verses.text: OVr God is a refuge. <na>(c)</na> and ſtrength: an <na>(d)</na> helper in tribulations, which <na>(e)</na> haue found vs excedingly.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Al refuge is not ſecure for one man is not able alwayes to defend an other: but God is a ſure and ſtrong refuge.

notes.label: d
notes.text: euer able and in conuenient time vvilling to helpe

notes.label: e
notes.text: This whole vvorld is ful of tribulations, but the Church ſuffered the greateſt in the firſt perſecutions, & shal ſuffer as great in the time of Antichriſt. English Catholiques ſuffer moſt of al nations in this age, and can not be ſuppreſſed, but ſtil increaſe in number and fortitude.

verses.text: Therfore wil we <na>(f)</na> not feare when <na>(g)</na> the earth shal be trubled: and <na>(h)</na> mountaines tranſported into the hart of the ſea.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Therfore al Catholiques may aſſuredly know, that the whole Church can not faile.

notes.label: g
notes.text: though very manie, as now in England,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and very eminent perſons, as ſome noblemen, and ſome Prieſtes haue reuolted, yet al vvil not.

verses.text: Their waters haue ſounded, and were trubled: the mountaines were trubled in his ſtrength.
The violence of the riuer <na>(i)</na> maketh the citie of God ioyful: the Higheſt hath ſanctified his tabernacle.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Such bad examples make the good to recollect themſelues more diligently, and to reioyce in Gods grace, by which they ſtand faſt.

verses.text: God is in the middes therof, it shal not be moued: God wil helpe it <na>(k)</na> in the morning early.

notes.label: k
notes.text: before the heate of perſecution ſhal inuade al, for the elect the dayes of tribulation are shortned.

verses.text: Nations are trubled, and <na>(l)</na> kingdomes are inclined: he gaue <na>(m)</na> his voice, the earth was moued

notes.label: l
notes.text: Sometimes one nation or kingdome rebelleth againſt the Church, but can not deſtroy it.

notes.label: m
notes.text: by the ſpirite of Chriſt, Antichriſt, and al his members shal be deſtroyed.

verses.text: The Lord of hoſtes is with vs: the God of Iacob is our defender.
Come ye, and ſee the workes of our Lord, what wonders he hath put vpon the earth:
<na>(n)</na> taking away warres euen vnto the end of the earth. He shal deſtroy bow, & breake weapons: and shields he shal burne with fire.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The Church ſometimes hath great peace, and tranquilitie.

verses.text: <na>(o)</na> Be quiet, and ſee that I am God: I shal be exalted among the gentiles, and I shal be exalted in the earth.

notes.label: o
notes.text: God himſelfe reſtrayneth the wicked, ſuddainly abating their furie, or cutting of their forces.

verses.text: The Lord of hoſtes is with vs: the God of Iacob is our defender.

chapters.summary: The Church in perſecution acknowledgeth Gods perpetual defence, 5. making her therby more glorious, 10. ſometimes granting reſt ( 11. God himſelf checking the perſecuters ) and euer protecting her. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church proſpereth alſo in perſecution.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for <na>(a)</na> the ſonnes of Core.

notes.label: a
notes.text: For Chriſtians that leaue the ſinnes of their fathers, and reioyce in Chriſt crucified: See Annotation. Pſal. 41.

verses.text: AL YE Nations <na>(b)</na> clappe handes: make iubilation to God in the voyce of exultation.

notes.label: b
notes.text: True ioy of the hart ſheweth it ſelfe both in voice of exultation, and alſo in geſture of body, by clapping of handes, dancing ( as king Dauid did before the Arke. 2. Reg. 6.) likevviſe vvith inſtruments.

verses.text: Becauſe our Lord is high, <na>(c)</na> terrible; a great king ouer <na>(d)</na> al the earth.

notes.label: c
notes.text: To al the wicked,

notes.label: d
notes.text: not only of one or few kingdoms, but of al the earth.

verses.text: He hath made peoples ſubiect <na>(e)</na> to vs: & gentiles vnder our feete.

notes.label: e
notes.text: VVhen kinges, and countries become Chriſtians, they are made ſubiectes to the Church that vvas before, not heades and rulers therfore.

verses.text: He hath choſen his inheritance in vs: the beautie of Iacob which he loued.
<na>(f)</na> God is aſcended in <na>(g)</na> iubilation: and our Lord in the voice of trumpet.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Chriſt God & man, after his Paſſion, roſe from death and aſcended:

notes.label: g
notes.text: not leauing his Church deſolate, but making her ioyful by an other comforter the Holie Ghoſt.

verses.text: Sing ye to our <na>(h)</na> God, ſing ye: Sing ye to our <na>(i)</na> king, ſing ye.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The ſame Chriſt is our God, by his Diuinitie:

notes.label: i
notes.text: and our king by his Humanitie.

verses.text: Becauſe God is king of al the earth: ſing ye <na>(k)</na> wiſely.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Doe your endeuour to vnderſtand vvhat you ſing, read, or heare in Gods word. At leaſt to know the principal Myſteries, and pointes of Chriſtian doctrin, euerie one according to their capacitie and ſtate or profeſſion.

verses.text: God shal reigne ouer the gentiles: God ſitteth vpon his holie ſeate.
Princes of peoples are gathered together with <na>(l)</na> the God of Abraham: becauſe the ſtrong <na>(m)</na> goddes of the earth, are excedingly aduanced.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The faithful of the old and nevv Teſtament are vnited in the ſeruice of one, and the ſame eternal God.

notes.label: m
notes.text: In reſpect of the Bleſſed Trinitie, holie Scripture here, and in manie places vſeth names of the plural number as Eloim Goddes, not diuiding Gods ſubſtance, vvhich is one, but inſinuating diſtinction of Diuine Perſons. The Father, the Sonne, and the Holie Ghoſt. VVhich Myſterie is more expreſly mentioned in Baptiſme, and profeſſed by Chriſtian gentils, then it was by the people of the Ievves.

chapters.summary: Gentiles are called, and inuited to praiſe God for his magnificence: 6. for Chriſts Aſcenſion, and powre. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Vocation of Gentiles.
The 6. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme <na>(a)</na> of Canticle to the ſonnes of Core, the <na>(b)</na> ſecond of the Sabbath.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Voices beginning the muſike inſtruments proſecuted;

notes.label: b
notes.text: eſpecially for the ſecond day of the weke, the day after the ſabbath, which is our Sunday, called Dominica, our Lords day.

verses.text: GREAT is our Lord, and to be prayſed excedingly in <na>(c)</na> the citie of our God, in his holie mount.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Ieruſalem, and mount Sion were moſt obliged to praiſe God, for greateſt benefites receiued, ſo the Catholique Church therby prefigured, and hauing receiued farre greatter, is moſt of al bonden to be gratful.

verses.text: Mount Sion is founded with the exultation of <na>(d)</na> the whole earth, <na>(e)</na> the ſides of the North, the citie of the great king.

notes.label: d
notes.text: This can not be affirmed of Sion, or Ieruſalem, but is only verified of the Catholique Chriſtian Church:

notes.label: e
notes.text: whoſe coaſtes do extend to the North, and to al quarters of the round earth.

verses.text: God shal be knowen in <na>(f)</na> the houſes therof, <na>(g)</na> when he shal receiue it.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The ſame one God, one Chriſt, one Faith, and one Religion in al particular Churches of the vvhole militant Church.

notes.label: g
notes.text: And this Vniuerſalitie, and Vnitie shal be, after that Chriſt taking mans nature ſhal be aſcended, and ſhal ſend the Holie Ghoſt, to found & beginne this Church.

verses.text: For behold the kings of the earth <na>(h)</na> were gathered together: they aſſembled in one.

notes.label: h
notes.text: For the aſſured certaintie of that is foreshewed, the Prophet ſpeaketh in the pretertence, as if it vvere already done in his time, which he then ſavv in ſpirite.

verses.text: They ſeing it ſo, were in admiration, were trubled, were moued:
trembling tooke them. Their ſorowes <na>(i)</na> as a woman traueling,

notes.label: i
notes.text: Nothing more moueth the hart, & affecteth al the bodie and ſoule, then ſpiritual cogitations of faith and religion, and therfore it is compared to a woman traueling with child, who hath moſt careful and greuous paines.

verses.text: In a vehement ſpirit <na>(k)</na> thou shalt breake the shippes of Tharſis.

notes.label: k
notes.text: In vvhich great confflict of mans ſpirite, God by his grace geueth force, to breake through the contrarie aſſaultes of our enimie, to remoue al impediments, and to ouercome the difficulties.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> As we haue heard, ſo haue we ſeene in the citie of the Lord of hoſtes, in the citie of our God: God hath founded it for euer.

notes.label: l
notes.text: This conſideration that al is now done, that was of old prophecied, is a meruelous confirmation and conſolation to Chriſtians.

verses.text: We haue receiued thy mercie, ô God, <na>(m)</na> in the middes of thy temple.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Grace and mercie is only granted to thoſe that are vvithin, or come vnto the Catholique Church.

verses.text: According to thy name ô God, ſo alſo is thy prayſe vnto the endes of the earth: thy right hand is ful of <na>(n)</na> iuſtice.

notes.label: n
notes.text: As God is praiſed for his mercie, ſo alſo for his iuſtice; which do neuer preiudice the one the other.

verses.text: Let mount Sion be glad, and the daughters of Iuda reioyce, becauſe of thy iudgementes ô Lord
Compaſſe Sion, and embrace ye her: <na>(o)</na> tel ye in her towers.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Conſider the fortreſſes of the Church, which are the holie Fathers, and Doctors, that watch and defend her vvalles.

verses.text: Set your hartes <na>(p)</na> on her ſtrength: and <na>(q)</na> diſtribute ye her houſes, that you <na>(r)</na> may declare it in an other generation.

notes.label: p
notes.text: So reſt you aſſured for al matters of faith in this pillar of truth.

notes.label: q
notes.text: obſerue and marke diligently how manie particular Churches were ſpedely founded in the world,

notes.label: r
notes.text: and declare this to other generations, that they may alſo hold faſt the ſame faith, or returne vnto it, if they be relapſed; or at laſt embrace it, if ſowner they haue not.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(s)</na> this is God, our God for euer, and for euer and euer: he <na>(t)</na> shal rule vs euermore.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Chriſt God incarnate that vvorketh al this, is our very God and Sauiour, not for a few yeares, an hundred, ſix hundred, or a thouſand, but for euer and euer.

notes.label: t
notes.text: he shal rule as a king, and conſequently haue a kingdom his militant Church euermore, to the very end of this vvorld. As he ſhal likevviſe haue his triumphant Church in eternitie.

chapters.summary: God moſt, and euerie where laudable, is eſpecially praiſed in the Church of Chriſt ( preſigured by Sion, and there begunne ) 9. Al thinges being fulfilled in the Church, euen as they were prophecied, and promiſed, 12. the faithful are exhorted to conſider and congratulate the ſame. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church founded and protected by God.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, <na>(a)</na> to the ſonnes of Core a Pſalme.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In this and diuers other titles, both before and yet enſuing, is ſaid, To the ſonnes, or, for the ſonnes of Core, a Pſalme, or Canticle, or vnderſtanding & the like ; but in no place, a Pſalme, Canticle &c. of the ſonnes of Core, vvhich no way proueth that they vvere the authores of ſuch Pſalmes, but rather the contrarie.

verses.text: HEARE theſe thinges <na>(b)</na> al ye Gentiles: receiue with your eares al ye, that <na>(c)</na> inhabite the earth.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Al ye nations and ſortes of people,

notes.label: c
notes.text: that dwel vpon the earth, lerne this leſſon vvhich I wil teach you.

verses.text: Al ye earthly perſons, and children of men: together in one the rich and the poore.
My mouth shal ſpeake wiſedom, and the meditation of my hart prudence.
I wil <na>(d)</na> incline mine eare vnto a parable: I wil <na>(e)</na> open my propoſition <na>(f)</na> on a Pſalter.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Holie Dauid harkened to God inſpiring him,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and declared to others that vvhich he receiued from God,

notes.label: f
notes.text: not only by his penne or tongue, but alſo for better inſtilling it into their mindes he ſounded it vpon the inſtrument called the Pſalter, vvhich had tenne ſtringes, ſignifying the obſeruation of the tenne commandments.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Why shal I feare in the euil day? <na>(h)</na> the iniquitie of my heele shal compaſſe me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: What eſpecial thing is there in this life, vvhy or for vvhich I or anie haue cauſe to feare the dreadful day of iudgement?

notes.label: h
notes.text: Marry this we muſt feare, iniquitie, by which any ſupplanteth, defraudeth, oppreſſeth, or anie vvay wrongeth others, for that vvil inuolue the offender in the ſentence of eternal damnation.

verses.text: They <na>(i)</na> that truſt in their ſtrength: and glorie in the multitude of their riches.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Such be they that truſt in their preſent powre, riches, or other wordlie thing.

verses.text: A <na>(k)</na> brother doth not redeme, <na>(l)</na> man shal redeme: he shal not geue vnto God his reconciliation.

notes.label: k
notes.text: A mans owne brother can not helpe a ſinner in that day,

notes.label: l
notes.text: much leſſe anie other man; ſo the Hebrew phraiſe by zeugma, vnderſtandeth an other negatiue particle.

verses.text: And the price of the redemption of his owne ſoule: and he shal <na>(m)</na> labour for euer,

notes.label: m
notes.text: ſtil ſuffer paine,

verses.text: and <na>(n)</na> shal liue yet vnto the end.

notes.label: n
notes.text: and not dye, but liue in eternal torments.

verses.text: He shal not ſee death, when he shal ſee <na>(o)</na> the wiſe dying <na>(p)</na> the vnwiſe, and <na>(q)</na> the foole shal perish together. And they shal leaue their riches to ſtrangers:

notes.label: o
notes.text: Al both wiſe and foolish do dye temporally: but the wiſe liuing in eternal ioy, the foolish liue in eternal paine,

notes.label: p
notes.text: thoſe that beleue not anie other life after this,

notes.label: q
notes.text: and thoſe that beleuing an other life, yet liue badly in this, shal perish in eternal damnation.

verses.text: and their <na>(r)</na> ſepulchers their <na>(s)</na> houſes for euer. Their Tabernacles in generation and generation: they haue renowmed their <na>(t)</na> names in their landes.

notes.label: r
notes.text: They shal neuer returne from their ſepulchers,

notes.label: s
notes.text: to enioy againe their houſes and earthlie poſſeſſions.

notes.label: t
notes.text: which vainely they labour to eſtablish in their poſteritie.

verses.text: And <na>(v)</na> man, when he was in honour, did not vnderſtand: he was compared to beaſts without vnderſtanding, and became like to them.

notes.label: v
notes.text: A moſt pithie and brief conſideration, for man to thinke, how abſurdly, he being endewed with reaſon, vnderſtanding, & free wil, like vnto Angels, and capable of eternal glorie, ſetteth his vvhole ſtudie, and care vpon corporal and temporal thinges, ſo making himſelfe like vnto brute beaſtes.

verses.text: This their way is <na>(w)</na> a ſcandal to them: and <na>(x)</na> afterward in their mouth they shal take pleaſure.

notes.label: w
notes.text: This care of wordlie thinges is the ſtumbling block, and cauſe of eternal ruine:

notes.label: x
notes.text: yet they ſhal be obſtinate, and praiſe their owne deſires, ſtil perſiſting therin.

verses.text: As <na>(y)</na> sheepe they are put in hel: death shal feede vpon them. And the iuſt shal rule ouer them <na>(z)</na> in the morning: and their aide shal waxe old in hel from their glorie.

notes.label: y
notes.text: Amongſt other creatures a sheepe can leaſt helpe her ſelfe in miſerie: euen ſo the damned in hel are altogether vnable to deliuer themſelues from thence, or to get any relief,

notes.label: z
notes.text: in the general reſurrection they shal be moſt of al in miſerie, as euer dying and neuer dead: the iuſt vvhom they vvronged, shal be their iudges, al freindes shal faile them, after they haue paſſed their glorie, and pleaſure in this vvorld.

verses.text: Neuertheleſſe <na>(a)</na> God wil redeme my ſoule out of the hand of hel, when he shal take me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The confidence of the iuſt.

verses.text: Feare not when a man shal be made rich: and when the glory of his houſe shal be multiplied,
Becauſe when he shal dye, he shal not take <na>(b)</na> al thinges: neyther shal his glorie goe downe with him.

notes.label: b
notes.text: He shal leaue al worldlie thinges and take nothing with him.

verses.text: Becauſe his ſoule in his life shal be <na>(c)</na> bleſſed: he wil confeſſe to thee <na>(d)</na> when thou shalt do him good.

notes.label: c
notes.text: temporally:

notes.label: d
notes.text: ſo long as he enioyeth wordlie profites he wil ſeme gratful to God;

verses.text: He shal enter in, euen to the progenies of his fathers: and he shal <na>(e)</na> not ſee light for euer.

notes.label: e
notes.text: but they shal not ſee the true light of heauen.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Man, when he was in honour, did not vnderſtand: he was compared to beaſts without vnderſtanding, and became like to them.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Remember and conſider ô worldlie man, that God made thee an excellent creature: which thou neglecting makeſt thyſelf like to a beaſt. As, v. 13.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet inuiting al ſtates and ſortes of men, to heare him attentiuely, 6 sheweth that al ought to feare eternal damnation, that liue wickedly; 9. vainly and foolishly ſeeking (13. euen like brute beaſtes) carnal pleaſures, which they can not long enioy, nor long eſcape hel. 16. confidently animating him ſelfe, and al good men, that truſt not in this world. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Exhortation to fly from ſin for fear of hell.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme <na>(a)</na> to Aſaph. THE <na>(b)</na> God of goddes our Lord hath ſpoken: and he hath called the earth, from the ryſing of the ſunne euen to the going downe.

notes.label: a
notes.text: To be ſongue or tuned by Aſaph a maiſter of muſike.

notes.label: b
notes.text: God almightie, who is greater then are al falſly ſuppoſed goddes, or holie perſons, that participating of his goodnes are called goddes (as Kinges, Prieſtes, Iudges) coming into this world in mans nature, calleth al men to ſaluation.

verses.text: Out <na>(c)</na> of Syon the beauty of his comelines.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The Church of Christ began in Sion.

verses.text: God wil come <na>(d)</na> manifeſtly: our God and he wil not kepe ſilence. <na>(e)</na> Fire shal burne forth in his ſight: and round about him a mighty tempeſt.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Chriſt that came in humilitie, and more obſcurely to ſuffer, and to redeme vs, vvil come in maieſtie, and manifeſtly to iudge.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Immediately before the general iudgement, fire shal burne al tranſitorie thinges.

verses.text: He shal <na>(f)</na> cal the heauen from aboue: and <na>(g)</na> the earth to diſcerne his people.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Geue ſignes in the firmament,

notes.label: g
notes.text: and in earth.

verses.text: Gather ye together his ſaincts vnto him: which ordaine his teſtament <na>(h)</na> aboue ſacrifices.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Which know that to keepe Gods commandments in folowing vertues, is aboue the oblation of external ſacrifice.

verses.text: And the heauens shal shew forth his iuſtice: becauſe God is Iudge.
<na>(i)</na> Heare ô my people, and I wil ſpeake: Iſrael, and I wil teſtifie to thee: God thy God am I.

notes.label: i
notes.text: God inſtructeth his people.

verses.text: I wil not rebuke thee in thy ſacrifices: and thy holocauſtes <na>(k)</na> are in my ſight alwaies.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Sacrifices are gratful to God.

verses.text: I wil <na>(l)</na> not take calues out of thy houſe: nor buckegoats out of thy flockes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: but in regard that God needeth not theſe earthly thinges, he rather requireth a gratful mind. For otherwiſe man in dede can geue nothing to God: ſeing al that is in the whole world is Gods owne in proprietie.

verses.text: Becauſe al the wilde beaſts of the woods be myne, the cattle in the mountaines and oxen.
I haue knowne al the foules of the ayer: and the beauty of the fielde is with me.
If I shal be hungrie, I wil not tel thee: for the round earth is myne, and the fulnes therof.
Wil I eate the flesh of oxen? or wil I drinke the blood of buckegoats?
<na>(m)</na> Immolate to God the ſacrifice of praiſe, and <na>(n)</na> pay thy vowes to the Higheſt.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Spiritual ſacrifice of prayſe.

notes.label: n
notes.text: & due payment of voluntarie vowes made in honour of God,

verses.text: And <na>(o)</na> inuocate me in the day of tribulation: I wil deliuer thee, and thou shalt glorifie me.

notes.label: o
notes.text: and praying to him for helpe in tribulation are most gratful.

verses.text: But to the ſinner God hath ſayde: <na>(p)</na> Why doeſt thou declare my iuſtices, and takeſt my teſtament by thy mouth?

notes.label: p
notes.text: He that wil teach others, muſt eſpecially flee from ſinne, & ſerue God ſincerly.

verses.text: But thou haſt hated diſcipline: & caſt my words behind thee.
If thou didſt ſee a theeſe, thou didſt rune with him: and with adulterers thou didſt put thy portion.
Thy mouth hath abounded with malice: and thy tongue fourged guiles.
Sitting thou ſpakeſt againſt thy brother, and againſt thy mothers ſonne thou didſt put a ſcandal:
theſe things haſt thou done, and I haue held my peace. Thou haſt thought vniuſtly that I wil be like thee: I wil reproue thee, and ſet it againſt thy face.
Vnderſtand theſe things you that forget God: leſt ſometime he take you violently and there be none to deliuer you.
The ſacrifice of prayſe <na>(q)</na> shal glorifie me: and there is the way, by which I wil shew him the ſaluation of God.

notes.label: q
notes.text: God is honored by mans gratitude, and other good workes.

chapters.summary: Chriſt in his firſt coming calleth al Nations. 3. in his ſecond wil iudge the world. 7. In the meane time God exhorteth al men to ſerue him in puritie of vertue, which he much preferreth before external ſacrifice of the old law. 17. reprehending ſuch as profeſſe or teach the right way, and liue wickedly. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
General Judgement.
The 9. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, a Pſalme of Dauid, <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Pertayning not only to Dauid, but alſo to al penitentes, eſpecially of the new teſtament

verses.text: when Nathan the Prophet came to him, after that he had ſinned with Bethſabee. (2. Reg. 12.)
HAVE mercie on me ô God, <na>(b)</na> according to thy great mercie. And according <na>(c)</na> to the multitude of thy commiſerations, take away myne iniquitie.

notes.label: b
notes.text: My ſinnes being very great, nede thy great mercie.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Yea manie ſortes of thy mercies: not only remiſſion of the crimes, but alſo mitigation of the paines due for the ſame. Thy merciful grace to be truly ſorie, to make ſome part of ſatisfaction, to beware hereafter not to fal againe, to geue better example of penance, and of vertuous life, and to perſeuer to the end.

verses.text: Wash me <na>(d)</na> more amply from mine iniquitie: & <na>(e)</na> cleanſe me from my ſinne.

notes.label: d
notes.text: O God thou haſt forgeuen me, and taken away my ſinnes, as thy prophet hath told me (2. Reg. 12. v. 13.) but my ſoule ſo fouly polluted, nedeth yet more waſhing.

notes.label: e
notes.text: cleanſe alſo the dregges that remaine, and al habites and inclinations to ſinne. So our Sauiour afterwards taught. (Ioan. 13. v. 10.) He that is waſhed nedeth not ſauing to wash his feete (il affections and reliques of former ſinnes) but is cleane wholy.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Becauſe I do know myne iniquitie: and my ſinne is <na>(g)</na> before me alwaies.

notes.label: f
notes.text: VVhiles I did not know; not conſider nor acknowledge my ſinnes, I could not be forgeuen, but now I know and acknowledge them:

notes.label: g
notes.text: and I ceaſe not to conſider of them with ſorow.

verses.text: To thee <na>(h)</na> onely haue I ſinned, and haue done euil before thee: that thou mayſt <na>(i)</na> be iuſtified in thy words, and mayſt <na>(k)</na> ouercome when thou art iudged.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Principally (for ſo this particle [only] here ſignifieth) the enormities of my ſinnes conſiſt, in that I haue offended thy Diuine Goodnes and Maieſtie, the King of the worldes, immortal, inuiſible, onlie God, to whom is due al honour and glorie for euer and euer. 1. Tim. 1. v. 17.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thou which haſt promiſed forgeuenes to al ſinners that truly conuert, ſhal herein be iuſtified by receiuing me againe to grace:

notes.label: k
notes.text: and ouerthrow thy calumniators, that iudge wickedly of thy proceedings, as if either thy iuſtice or mercie were peruerted.

verses.text: For behold I <na>(l)</na> was conceiued in iniquities: & my mother conceiued me in ſinnes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: I and al are borne in original ſinne, the reliques wherof, concupiſcence and weakenes incline vs to other ſinnes, which we haue added. In regard of which our infirmitie, thy mercie is readie to recal vs, and help vs.

verses.text: For behold thou <na>(m)</na> haſt loued truth: <na>(n)</na> the vncertaine, and hidden thinges of thy wiſdome thou haſt made manifeſt to me.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Beſides thou haſt alſo geuen me knowledge of true faith, and right doctrine, which thou euer loueſt, and art accuſtomed to reduce, and direct ſuch into the true way of penance.

notes.label: n
notes.text: yea thou haſt moreouer ſhewed to me thinges vncertaine, or vnknowen to manie others, geuen me the gift and ſpirit of prophecie, to know hidde myſteries, and to euerie one God geueth ſome particular benefites, which he loueth in him, and is ready of his part to confirme and maintaine the ſame, that they be not loſt.

verses.text: Thou shalt ſprinkle me with <na>(o)</na> hyſſope, and I shal be clenſed: thou shalt wash me, and I shal be made <na>(p)</na> whiter then ſnow.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Moſt merciful Lord thou wilt (as I ſee in the ſpirit of prophecie) ſprinkle me, and al men with thy bloud, from the Croſſe, where they shal geue thee vinegre about hyſſoppe to drinke. (Ioan. 19.)

notes.label: p
notes.text: by which washing I shal be cleane from ſinne, and become in time pure, yea whiter then ſnow. A figure of this hyſſope was obſerued in Moyſes Law. Num. 19. ſignifying the liuelie heat of Chriſts infinite charitie.

verses.text: To <na>(q)</na> my hearing thou shalt geue ioy and gladnes, and <na>(r)</na> the bones humbled shal reioyce.

notes.label: q
notes.text: When myn affections shal be cleane purged, I shal take ſingular great delight to heare of thee,

notes.label: r
notes.text: and al my powres of mind and bodie, which are now afflicted, shal reioyce.

verses.text: <na>(s)</na> Turne away thy face from my ſinnes: and wipe away al mine iniquities.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Leaue of thy cogitation of punishing, to which purpoſe firſt take away myn iniquities, for otherwiſe if they remaine, Gods iuſtice can not but punish them.

verses.text: <na>(t)</na> Create a cleane hart in me ô God: and renew a right ſpirit in my <na>(v)</na> bowels.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Create in me new grace, wherby my hart shal be pure. So S. Paul calleth a iuſt ſoul a new creature. Galat. 6. v. 15.

notes.label: v
notes.text: In my inward thoughtes.

verses.text: Caſt me not away from thy face: and thy Holie ſpirit <na>(w)</na> take not from me.

notes.label: w
notes.text: ſuffer me not ſo to fal againe, that thy grace depart from me.

verses.text: Render vnto me <na>(x)</na> the ioy of thy ſaluation? and <na>(y)</na> confirme me with the principal ſpirit,

notes.label: x
notes.text: which I had before my fal, of Chriſt promiſed of my ſeede, and alter not the ſame for my ſinnes. Dauid alſo and other penitents pray here, that God wil reſtore vnto them the ioy, which they had in the ſtate of grace, of eternal ſaluation promiſed;

notes.label: y
notes.text: confirme & conſerue in me hereafter, a ſtrong, conſtant, and willing ſpirite to perſeuere.

verses.text: I <na>(z)</na> wil teach the vniuſt thy waies: and the impious shal be conuerted to thee.

notes.label: z
notes.text: No way can a penitent better shew him ſelf gratful to God, for remiſſion of his ſinnes, then by inſtructing, exhorting, and perſwading other ſinners to repentance, to leaue their former il wayes, and turne to God.

verses.text: Deliuer me <na>(a)</na> from bloudes ô God, the God of my ſaluation: and my tongue shal exult [for] thy iuſtice.

notes.label: a
notes.text: From the guilt and puniſhment of murder, cauſing Vrias and others with him to be ſlaine. Other penitents pray to be deliuered from what ſinnes ſoeuer they haue committed, by ſheding bloud, or other wrongs and iniuries; promiſing to praiſe Gods iuſtice, in offering and geuing grace, according to his promiſe to ſinners, that they may repent.

verses.text: Lord, thou <na>(b)</na> wilt open my lippes: & my mouth shal shew forth thy prayſe.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Thou ô God firſt ſtirring me vp, opening my lippes, which of my ſelfe I can not do, then my tongue and mouth wil praiſe thee.

verses.text: Becauſe if thou <na>(c)</na> wouldeſt haue had ſacrifice, I had verily giuen it: with holocauſtes thou wilt <na>(d)</na> not be delighted.

notes.label: c
notes.text: If thou wouldeſt eſpecially legal ſacrifice, I would eaſily haue offered great ſtore:

notes.label: d
notes.text: but the beſt of that kind is not ſufficient:

verses.text: A ſacrifice to God is <na>(e)</na> an afflicted ſpirit: a contrite, and humbled hart, ô God thou wilt not deſpiſe.

notes.label: e
notes.text: true contrition of hart pleaſeth thee farre better.

verses.text: Deale fauorably ô Lord in thy good wil <na>(f)</na> with Sion: that the walles of Ieruſalem may be built vp.

notes.label: f
notes.text: After a penitent hath remiſſion of his owne ſinnes, he muſt pray for the whole Church.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Then shalt thou accept ſacrifice of <na>(h)</na> iuſtice, <na>(i)</na> oblations, & <na>(k)</na> holocauſtes: <na>(l)</na> then shal they lay calues vpon thyne altar.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The Church proſpering, her faithful children shal offer

notes.label: h
notes.text: the ſacrifice of iuſtice, rendering to euerie one that is due;

notes.label: i
notes.text: alſo free offeringes without obligation,

notes.label: k
notes.text: yea holocauſtes, which is the chiefeſt,

notes.label: l
notes.text: calues, and like hoſtes vpon the altar, according to the ſtate of the old law: but in the law of Chriſt, the moſt B. Sacrifice by him inſtituted.

chapters.summary: King Dauid in great ſorow for his ſinnes of adulterie and murder, most ſeriouſly prayeth God of his manifold mercies to remitte and purge al his offences, and paines due for them. 12. to reſtore vnto him the grace of the Holie Ghost, lost by his ſinnes; 15. that he may teach others (as in deede his ſingular example may teach the whole world true penance) 19. contrition of hart, worthely to offer ſacrifice, for the whole Church. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The fourth penitential Pſalm.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, vnderſtanding to Dauid,
when Doeg <na>(a)</na> the Idumeite came and told Saul: Dauid is come into the houſe of <na>(b)</na> Achimelech. (1. Reg. 22.) <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Of the race of Eſau, half a Iew, but either an Infidel, or fautor of Infidels, a ſpie for Saul, a perſecutor of Dauid, & a murderer of Innocents. 1. Reg. 22. v. 9. 18.

notes.label: b
notes.text: High prieſt, ſlaine with 84. more Prieſtes and others, becauſe they were ſuppoſed to fauour Dauid. ibidem.

verses.text: WHY doeſt thou <na>(c)</na> glorie in malice, which art mightie in iniquitie?

notes.label: c
notes.text: Thou perſecutor Doeg, why art thou ſo malicious, to abuſe thy credite with king Saul, to the murdering of innocents?

verses.text: Al the day hath thy tongue thought iniuſtice: as a sharp raſor thou <na>(d)</na> haſt done guile.

notes.label: d
notes.text: playing the part of a ſpie, in betraying to Saul, that I was with Achimelech?

verses.text: Thou haſt loued malice more then benignitie: <na>(e)</na> iniquitie rather then to ſpeake equitie.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Though he told a truth, yet it was iniquitie to betray innocents.

verses.text: Thou haſt loued al wordes of precipitation, a deceitful tongue.
Therfore Wil God deſtroy thee for euer, he wil <na>(f)</na> plucke thee out, & remoue thee out of thy tabernacle: & <na>(g)</na> thy roote out of the land of the liuing.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Thou shalt vtterly be deſtroyed.

notes.label: g
notes.text: & al thy race.

verses.text: The iuſt shal ſee, and feare, and shal laugh at him, and they shal ſay:
Behold the man, that hath not put God for his helper. But hath hoped in the multitude of his riches, and hath <na>(h)</na> preualed in his vanitie.

notes.label: h
notes.text: for a short time in this world.

verses.text: But I as <na>(i)</na> a fruitful oliue tree in the houſe of God, haue hoped in the mercie of God for euer: and for euer and euer.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Dauid prophecieth his owne exaltation, and conſeruation of his ſeede in the kingdom of Iſrael.

verses.text: I wil <na>(k)</na> confeſſe to thee for euer, becauſe thou haſt done it: and I wil expect thy <na>(l)</na> name, becauſe it is good in the ſight of thy ſaints:

notes.label: k
notes.text: sing praiſe, and thankes to thee.

notes.label: l
notes.text: thy Goodnes, which agreeth to thy name.

chapters.summary: Holie Dauid inueigheth against wicked Doeg a traitor. 7. prophecieth his ruine. 10. and his owne exaltation. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David's invective againſt Doeg.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for <na>(a)</na> Maeleth; <na>(b)</na> vnderſtandings of Dauid. THE foole hath ſaid in his hart: There is no God.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Weakenes, or mourning,

notes.label: b
notes.text: S. Auguſtin expoundeth this Pſalme as an inſtruction to thoſe that ſuffer perſecution and iniuries, eſpecially nere the end of the world.

verses.text: They are corrupte, and become abominable in iniquities: there is not that doth good.
God hath looked forth from heauen, vpon the children of men: to ſee if there be that vnderſtandeth, or ſeeketh after God.
Al haue declined, they are become vnprofitable together: there is not that doth good, no there is not one.
Shal they not al know that worke iniquitie, that deuoure my people as food of bread?

God they haue not inuocated: there haue they trembled for feare, where no feare was. Becauſe God hath <na>(c)</na> diſſipated the bones of them <na>(d)</na> that pleaſe men: they are confounded, becauſe God hath deſpiſed them.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God wil ouerthrow al the counſels, and forces

notes.label: d
notes.text: of worldlie politiques.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Who wil geue out of Sion the ſaluation of Iſrael? when God shal conuert the captiuitie of his people: Iacob shal reioyce, and Iſrael shal be glad.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The true Church afflicted deſireth Chriſts coming to deliuer the oppreſſed.

chapters.summary: As in the thirtenth Pſalme, Chriſts Incarnation is prophecied, after that ſinne abunded in the world: ſo here is foreshewed that after general wickednes, 5. Christ wil come to iudge the bad, 7. and deliuer the good. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The general Iudgement.
The 9. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> in ſongs vnderſtanding for Dauid

notes.label: a
notes.text: Though hiſtorically this Pſalme

notes.label: b
notes.text: was ſong by Dauid the author therof, shewing how he prayd in danger, and rendered thankes for his deliuerie,

verses.text: when the Zipheites were come, and ſaid to Saul: <na>(c)</na> Is not Dauid hid with vs? (1. Reg. 1. 23. & 26.) <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: c
notes.text: when vpon notice geuen that he abode in the mountaines, Saul ſtraictly beſeged him, with a great armie, but the Philiſtims inuading the countrie, Saul was forced to leaue Dauid, and to turne his forces againſt them, 1. Reg. 23. yet it perteyneth alſo literally to al iuſt men in diſtreſſe, eſpecially to the Church of Chriſt, praying in like dangers, and God by his like prouidence, deliuering his ſeruantes in extremities.

verses.text: O GOD ſaue me <na>(d)</na> in thy name: and in thy ſtrength <na>(e)</na> iudge me.

notes.label: d
notes.text: For the glorie of thy name

notes.label: e
notes.text: for the iuſtnes of my cauſe defend me.

verses.text: O God heare my prayer with thine eares: receiue the words of my mouth.
Becauſe <na>(f)</na> ſtrangers haue riſen vp againſt me, & the ſtrong haue ſought my ſoule: and they haue not ſet God before their eies.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Barbarous highland men haue betraide the place of myne abode to the perſecuters.

verses.text: For <na>(g)</na> behold God helpeth me: and our Lord is the receiuer of my ſoule.

notes.label: g
notes.text: But I feare them not, becauſe I am in Gods protection.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Turne away the euils to mine enimies: and in <na>(i)</na> thy truth deſtroy them.

notes.label: h
notes.text: A iuſt prayer, that God wil turne intended miſchief, vpon the deuiſers heades,

notes.label: i
notes.text: according to his promiſe, that he wil defend the innocent.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> I wil voluntarily ſacrifice to thee, and <na>(l)</na> wil confeſſe to thy name ô Lord, becauſe it is good:

notes.label: k
notes.text: Offering voluntarie ſacrifice, more then is commanded:

notes.label: l
notes.text: and praiſe thee ô God,

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> Becauſe thou haſt deliuered me out of al tribulation: and <na>(n)</na> mine eie hath looked downe vpon mine enimies.

notes.label: m
notes.text: as I am bond

notes.label: n
notes.text: I reioyce in thy iuſt iudgements against the wicked.

chapters.summary: Dauid in diſtreſſe crieth to God for helpe, 6. confidently truſting therin, 8. and promiſing ſacrifice of thankeſgeuing. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer in diſtreſs.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> in ſonges, <na>(c)</na> vnderſtanding to Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: A ſong as wel for king Dauid himſelfe, as others of al times;

notes.label: b
notes.text: to ſing,

notes.label: c
notes.text: and conſider Gods prouidence, in ſuffering one man to afflict an other in this life.

verses.text: HEARE my prayer ô God, deſpiſe not my petition,
Attend to me; and heare me.

I am made ſorowful in my <na>(d)</na> exerciſe: and am trubled at the voice of the enimie: and at the tribulation of the ſinner. Becauſe they haue <na>(e)</na> wreſted iniquities vpon me: & <na>(f)</na> in anger they were trubleſome to me.

notes.label: d
notes.text: This life is a warefare, and a continual combate.

notes.label: e
notes.text: calumniated me,

notes.label: f
notes.text: and perſecuted me in great furie.

verses.text: My hart is trubled in me: and <na>(g)</na> the feare of death is falne vpon me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: ſo inwardly afflicted, as if death were at hand.

verses.text: Feare and trembling are come vpon me: and <na>(h)</na> darkenes hath couered me.

notes.label: h
notes.text: I haue ſcarſe ſenſe, or diſcourſe of reaſon, being almoſt ouerwhelmed with trubles.

verses.text: And I ſaid: <na>(i)</na> Who wil geue me wings as of a doue, and I wil fly: and reſt?

notes.label: i
notes.text: would God I could flie, that in the ſimplicitie of a doue, I might ſpedely part away from theſe afflictions.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> Loe I haue gone far flying away: and I abode in the wildernes.

notes.label: k
notes.text: I haue fled ſo farre as I could from trubles:

verses.text: I <na>(l)</na> expected him, that <na>(m)</na> ſaued me from <na>(n)</na> puſillanimitie of ſpirit, and <na>(o)</na> tempeſt.

notes.label: l
notes.text: for the reſt I remitted to Gods wil and good pleaſure,

notes.label: m
notes.text: and he ſuffered me not to be ouerthrowne,

notes.label: n
notes.text: though I am weake,

notes.label: o
notes.text: and the tentations are great.

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> Precipitate ô Lord, and <na>(q)</na> diuide their tongues: becauſe I haue ſene <na>(r)</na> iniquitie, and <na>(s)</na> contradiction in the citie.

notes.label: p
notes.text: O God abate the pride of arrogant perſecuters,

notes.label: q
notes.text: ſuffer them not to agree amongſt them ſelues.

notes.label: r
notes.text: They are ful of al iniquitie,

notes.label: s
notes.text: they haue alſo contentions among themſelues, turne the ſame to our good.

verses.text: Day and night shal iniquitie compaſſe it vpon the walles therof; and <na>(t)</na> labour in the middeſt therof, and <na>(v)</na> iniuſtice.

notes.label: t
notes.text: VVith their continual great iniquitie, they haue their trubles,

notes.label: v
notes.text: but leaue not their iniuſtice.

verses.text: And there hath not ceaſed out of the ſtreetes therof <na>(w)</na> vſurie, and guile.

notes.label: w
notes.text: They are stil vſurers, and deceiptful oppreſſors of the poore.

verses.text: For <na>(x)</na> if myne enimie had ſpoken euil to me, I would verely haue borne it. And if he that hated me had ſpoken great thinges vpon me: I would perhaps haue hid myſelfe from him.

notes.label: x
notes.text: It is a greater griefe to ſuffer iniuries of thoſe that ſeme to be freindes.

verses.text: But <na>(y)</na> thou a man of the ſame minde: my <na>(z)</na> guide, and my familiar.

notes.label: y
notes.text: A man that was, or ſemed of the ſame mind, faith, and religion,

notes.label: z
notes.text: whom I ſo truſted, that I would haue gone, whitherſoeuer he should haue ledde me.

verses.text: Which diddeſt <na>(a)</na> take ſwete meats together with me, in the <na>(b)</na> houſe of God we walked with conſent.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Thou that didſt participate the ſame holie ſacraments with me,

notes.label: b
notes.text: in the Catholique Church.

verses.text: Let <na>(c)</na> death come vpon them: and let them goe downe quicke into hel. Becauſe there is wickednes in their habitations, in <na>(d)</na> the middes of them.

notes.label: c
notes.text: As Core & his complices: ſpoken of iuſt zele, not of deſire to reuenge: verified in thoſe that ſinne wittingly and knowing, for they deſcend, as it were, aliue into hel.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The whole crew of the wicked conſpire in iniquitie.

verses.text: But I haue cried to God, and our Lord wil ſaue me.
In <na>(e)</na> the euening, and morning, & at midday, I wil <na>[1]</na> ſpeake, and declare, and he wil heare my voice.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The prophet alludeth to three more ſpecially appointed houres of Diuine ſeruice, the daylie ſacrifice at morning, and euening, and other ſacrifices commonly about midday. VVhich alſo are the three principal times of Diuine Seruice in the Church of Chriſt. Mattins, Euenſong, and the Sacrifice of Maſſe. VVhich Eutymius and other Grecians cal Lyturgiam. S. Clement alſo (li 7. c. 25. Apoſt. Inſtit) teſtifieth that the Apoſtles ordained three ſet houres of common prayer euerie day.
* or pray

verses.text: He wil redeme my ſoule in peace from them, that approch to me: becauſe among manie <na>(f)</na> they were with me.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Manie enimies combined together approched vnto me, to ouerthrow me.

verses.text: God wil heare, and he <na>(g)</na> which is before the worldes wil humble them.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Eternal God.

verses.text: For there is <na>(h)</na> no change with them, & they feared not God: he hath ſtreached forth his hand in repaying.

notes.label: h
notes.text: They wil neuer repent of their wickednes.

verses.text: They haue contaminated his teſtament, they are <na>(i)</na> diuided by the wrath of his countenance; and <na>(k)</na> his hart hath approched. <na>(l)</na> His wordes are made ſofter then oile: and <na>(m)</na> the ſame are dartes.

notes.label: i
notes.text: They harden their hartes againſt his threatned wrath:

notes.label: k
notes.text: but Gods prouidence illuminateth others to know and teach the truth, whȇ it is impugned, or contemned.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Gods wordes, which in them ſelues are meke and ſwete,

notes.label: m
notes.text: are hard to the incredulous, & as dartes that wound them. Chriſt ſaid (Ioan. 6.) Vnles one eate my flesh, & drinke my bloud, he shal not haue life in him, which the Capharnaites not vnderſtanding ſaid one to an other: This is a hard ſpeach, who can abide it? which S. Auguſtin here ſaith was the firſt hereſie againſt our Sauiours preaching. It was not hard to S. Peter, who in the name of the reſt, anſwered, that Chriſt had the wordes of eternal life. He yet vnderſtood not the ſecrete of our Lords ſpeach, but he piouſly beleued that the wordes vvere good, vvhich he vnderſtood not.

verses.text: <na>(n)</na> Caſt thy care vpon our Lord: and he wil nourish thee: he vvil not geue <na>(o)</na> fluctuation to the iuſt for euer.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Therfore in al doubtes of doctrin, in al diſtreſſes of perſecution, and other difficulties vvhich ſurpaſſe thy vveakenes, caſt thy care vpon our Lord, and he wil nourish thee.

notes.label: o
notes.text: He vvil not ſuffer the iuſt to remaine alvvayes in fluctuation, that is, in doubtful, dangerous, and vvanering thoughtes or perplexities, as vvhen a shippe is toſſed in the vvaues of the ſea, but vvil geue quiet repoſe of mind, as in a ſure hauen vvithout danger of drovvning.

verses.text: But thou ô God wilt bring <na>(p)</na> them downe into the pitte of deſtruction. <na>(q)</na> Bloudy and deceitful men shal not liue halfe their daies. but I wil hope in thee ô Lord.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Coatrariwiſe, the wicked and obſtinate shal fal into deſtruction.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Often or for moſt part, bloud-ſuckers dye before the courſe of nature requireth, as Saul, Abſolon, Achitophel, Achab, Iezabel, and the like.

chapters.summary: The prophet (as wel in his owne, as other iuſt mens perſon) deſcribeth great calamities ſuffered, 10. praieth against the wicked, 13. Lamenting eſpecially that thoſe which profeſſe frendshipe, are aduerſaries. 17. and declareth Gods prouidence in protecting the good, and deſtroying the bad. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence towards the good and bad.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> for a people, that is made far from the Sainctes, Dauid in <na>(c)</na> the inſcription of the title, <na>(d)</na> when the foreners held him in Geth. (1. Reg. 12. v. 12.) <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Pſalme perteyneth alſo to future times,

notes.label: b
notes.text: for the vſe of anie iuſt perſons, or people, that are againſt their wil ſeperated from the publike diuine Seruice of holie Church :

notes.label: c
notes.text: moſt worthie to be noted with title, for perpetual memorie,

notes.label: d
notes.text: made by Dauid when the Philiſtims detected him to their king in Geth.

verses.text: HAVE mercie on me ô God, becauſe <na>(e)</na> man hath troden vpon me: <na>(f)</na> al the day impugning he hath afflicted me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Now one ſorte of il diſpoſed men, now an other,

notes.label: f
notes.text: neuer ceaſe to ſeeke my deſtruction.

verses.text: Myne enimies haue troden vpon me al the day: becauſe they are <na>(g)</na> manie that warre againſt me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Saul with his great armie, the Philiſtimes, and other ſtrangers, ſome in manifeſt hoſtilitie, others detecting and betraing me to myn aduerſaries. So al that liue godly in Chriſt haue manie enimies viſible and inuiſible,

verses.text: From <na>(h)</na> the height of the day I shal feare: <na>(i)</na> but I wil truſt in thee.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Of theſe moſt eminent great dangers I am in deede afeard,

notes.label: i
notes.text: but ſo that my truſt and aſſured confidence is in thee ô God.

verses.text: In God I wil praiſe <na>(k)</na> my wordes, in God haue I hoped: I wil not feare what flesh may do to me.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Wordes and promiſes made to me; or the good which I ſpeake or do by Gods grace.

verses.text: Al the day did they <na>(l)</na> deteſt my wordes; againſt me, <na>(m)</na> al their cogitations are vnto euil.

notes.label: l
notes.text: They calumniate whatſoeuer I ſay,

notes.label: m
notes.text: wreſting al my wordes to euil ſenſe.

verses.text: They wil <na>(n)</na> inhabite and keepe ſecret: they wil obſerue my heele. As they haue expected <na>(o)</na> my ſoule,

notes.label: n
notes.text: They meete together, and ſecretly conſpire to intreppe me or catch me tripping.

notes.label: o
notes.text: to take my life:

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> for nothing shalt thou ſaue them: <na>(q)</na> in wrath thou wilt breake peoples. O God,

notes.label: p
notes.text: for this their vaine purpoſe to deſtroy me, thou wilt ſaue them, as they deſerue, that is,

notes.label: q
notes.text: thou wilt breake them in peeces.

verses.text: I haue shewed my life to thee: thou haſt ſet my teares in thy ſight. As alſo in thy promiſe:
then shal mine enemies be turned backward. In what day ſoeuer I shal inuocate thee: loe I haue knowne that thou art my God.
In God I wil praiſe <na>(r)</na> the word, in our Lord wil I praiſe thee ſaying, I haue hoped in God, I wil not feare what man can do to me.

notes.label: r
notes.text: I wil alwayes gratfully acknowlege thy promiſes, and ſayings, for they are aſſured.

verses.text: In me, ô God <na>(s)</na> are thy vowes, which I wil render, praiſes to thee.

notes.label: s
notes.text: I haue purpoſed and vowed to offer ſacrifice of praiſe, and by thy helpe wil performe it.

verses.text: Becauſe thou haſt deliuered my ſoule from death, and my feete from falling: that I may <na>(t)</na> pleaſe before God, in <na>(v)</na> the light of the liuing.

notes.label: t
notes.text: do that pleaſeth God,

notes.label: v
notes.text: in true faith and pious workes.

chapters.summary: Dauid being in danger before Achis king of Geth, confidently imploreth Gods helpe, againſt the great malice and powre of his enimies; 8. foresheweth their ruine, his owne exaltation, 12. and offereth praiſes and thankes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David's prayer in danger.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> deſtroy not, to Dauid in <na>(c)</na> the inſcription of the title; <na>(d)</na> when he fled from the face of Saul into the caue. (1.Reg.22.24.) <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: The heroical facts of Dauid are for examples to al Chriſtians.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Innocent Dauid hauing opportunitie to kil his vniuſt perſecutor, obeyed the motion of God, ſuggeſting vnto him, not to deſtroy his enimie; contrarie to the counſel of his freindes:

notes.label: c
notes.text: a thing moſt worthie to be recorded for perpetual memorie,

notes.label: d
notes.text: being in ſo great and vniuſt truble, as to lye in the caue of a mountaine, yet ſpared to kil, or hurt him, that driue him into ſuch ſtraictes. See the hiſtorie 1. Reg. 24.

verses.text: HAVE mercie on me ô God, haue mercie on me: becauſe my ſoule hath truſted in thee. And I wil hope in the shadow of thy winges, vntil iniquitie paſſe.
I wil crie to God the higheſt: God that hath done me good.
He ſent <na>(e)</na> from heauen, and deliuered me: he hath geuen into <na>(f)</na> reproche them that trode vpon me. God hath ſent his mercie, and his truth,

notes.label: e
notes.text: Extraordinarie diuine helpe, paſſing mans powre.

notes.label: f
notes.text: It fel reprochfully to Saul, that Dauid might haue ſlaine him if he would, yet did neither hurt him, nor inſult vpon him, but meekely and piouſly admonished him of his error, and iniurious perſecution.

verses.text: and hath deliuered my <na>(g)</na> ſoule out of the middes of <na>(h)</na> Lions whelpes: I ſlept trubled. The ſonnes of men, their <na>(i)</na> teeth are weapons and arrowes: and their <na>(k)</na> tongue a sharpe ſword.

notes.label: g
notes.text: my life.

notes.label: h
notes.text: from moſt mightie and rauenous perſecuters.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Though they haue not lions natural teeth, yet they exerciſe crueltie by artificial weapons,

notes.label: k
notes.text: and with their cruel tongues incite their folowers to the ſame furie. 1. Reg. 22. 7. 16.

verses.text: Be exalted aboue the heauens ô God: and thy glorie vpon al the earth.
They prepared a ſnare for my feete: and bowed downe my ſoule. They <na>(l)</na> digged a pit before my face: and they are falne into it.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Saul endeuored manie wayes to ouerthrow Dauid, amongſt other meanes prouoked him to ſette vpon the Philiſtims, thincking they should haue ſlaine him, 1. Reg. 18. v. 17. but the ſame Philiſtims ouerthrew Saul. 1 Reg. 31.

verses.text: My hart is readie ô God, my hart is readie: I wil ſing, and ſay <na>[1]</na> a Pſalme.

notes.text: Pſalmes more in vſe with Chriſtian Gentils, then they were with the Iewes. See page. 12.

verses.text: Ariſe my glorie, ariſe pſalter and harpe: I wil ariſe early.
I wil confeſſe to thee among <na>(m)</na> peoples ô Lord: and I wil ſay a Pſalme to thee among <na>(n)</na> the Gentiles.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Gods benefites beſtowed vpon Dauid, and vpon faithful Chriſtians prefigured by him, are for euer to be praiſed by al peoples and nations.

notes.label: n
notes.text: See previous note

verses.text: Becauſe thy mercie is magnified euen to the heauens, and thy truth euen to the cloudes.
Be axalted aboue the heauens ô God: and thy glorie vpon al the earth.

chapters.summary: The Prophet prayeth in tribulation, 4. teſtifieth Gods helpe, 6. praiſeth his greatnes: 8. promiſing, and inuiting al nations to praiſe him. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Dauids great patience.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> deſtroy not, to Dauid in, <na>(c)</na> the inſcription of the title.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Pſalme was made vpon the ſame occaſion, and to the ſame purpoſe as the former,

notes.label: b
notes.text: to exhorte the iuſt and innocent to patience,

notes.label: c
notes.text: by Dauids memorable example.

verses.text: IF <na>(d)</na> in very dede you ſpeake iuſtice: iudge right thinges ye ſonnes of men.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Few are ſo wicked, but they ſpeake and pretend iuſt thinges:

verses.text: For in <na>(e)</na> the hart you worke iniquities: in the earth your <na>(f)</na> handes forge iniuſtice.

notes.label: e
notes.text: but neither thincke wel,

notes.label: f
notes.text: nor do wel, but both contrarie, which feaned ſanctitie is duble iniquitie.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Sinners are alienated from the matrice, they haue erred from the wombe: they haue ſpoken falſe thinges.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Theſe wicked ſinners that flatter and incite king Saul, ſeme to haue ſpent al their life from their infancie in malice.

verses.text: They haue furie according to the ſimilitude of <na>(h)</na> a ſerpent: as of <na>(i)</na> the aſpe that is deafe, and ſtoppeth his eares.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Their furie is vnquiet, til they may wound the innocent with their poiſonful ſting,

notes.label: i
notes.text: neither wil they harken to good admonitions, but ſtoppe their eares like an aſpe, that layeth one eare cloſe to the ground, and ſtoppeth the other with his taile.

verses.text: Which wil not heare the voice of the inchanters, and of the ſorcerer inchanting wiſely.
God shal breake their <na>(k)</na> teeth in their mouth, the <na>(l)</na> cheeke tooth of the lions, our Lord wil breake in peeces.

notes.label: k
notes.text: But God wil breake their cruel force,

notes.label: l
notes.text: though it ſemeth moſt ſtrong, and inſuperable.

verses.text: They shal come to nothing as water running downe: he hath <na>(m)</na> bent his bow til they be weakened.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Gods iuſt determination of punishing the wicked ſtil remaineth beat and readie, though execution be ſome while differred.

verses.text: As <na>(n)</na> waxe that melteth, shal they be taken away: <na>(o)</na> fyre hath falne on them, and they haue not ſcene the ſunne.

notes.label: n
notes.text: That force and powre which is now inuincible, hard and ſtrong like a lions ſtrongeſt teeth, shal then be as impotent and ſoft as waxe:

notes.label: o
notes.text: Gods wrath, like fire, the moſt forcible element, shal fal vpon them, and they shal be caſt into vtter darkenes, depriued of the ſunne and al comfortable light.

verses.text: Before your <na>(p)</na> thornes did vnderſtand the old bryar: as liuing ſo in wrath he swalloweth them.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Before their malice can bring to effect, the great miſchieffes which they plette and purpoſe, God ſuddainly cutteth them of before they fully vnderſtand of, either ſicknes or death, caſteth them as it were aliue into hel.

verses.text: The iuſt <na>(q)</na> shal reioice when he shal ſee reuenge: he shal wash his handes in the bloud of a ſinner.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The iuſt reioyce in the punishment of the wicked for three cauſes, firſt in zele of iuſtice, conforming his wil and mind to Gods iudgement; ſecondly, for that himſelfe through Gods mercie hath eſcaped that terrible damnation; thirdly, for that he is now deliuered from moleſtation, and continual tribulation.

verses.text: And man shal ſay: If certes there be fruite to the iuſt: <na>(r)</na> there is a God certes iudging them on the earth.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The iuſt ſeing, or by faith knowing what punishment remaineth for the wicked, is therby aſſured that the good shal reape fruict for his wel doing, and that in the meane time God ruleth and iudgeth on the earth, though as yet it appeareth not ſo euidently.

chapters.summary: Holie Dauid inueigheth againſt diſſembling wicked men. 7. deſcribeth their manifold punishment, 11. wherin the iuſt shal be comforted. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence in ſuffering evil.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, deſtroy not, to Dauid in the inſcription of the title, <na>(a)</na> when Saul ſent, and watched his houſe to kil him. (1. Reg. 19.) <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: King Saul hauing thriſe attempted in vaine to kil Dauid, (1. Reg. 18. v. 11. & c. 19. v. 9) ſent ſome of his guard to fetch him, from his owne houſe, that he might be ſlaine: but God moued the mind of Michol, to admonish him of the danger, and to helpe him away in ſaftie, though Saul thought she would haue bene a ſcandal vnto him (or cauſe of ruine) by the handes of the Philiſtians 1. Reg. 18. v. 21. Vpon which occaſion Dauid made this Pſalme. As he alſo made others, for perpetual memorie of Gods like benefites, in deliuering him in iminent dangers, when Saul ſent three troupes of ſeriants to kil him, and folowed them himſelfe. 1. Reg. 19. v. 10. likewiſe vvhen he was knowen and bewrayed before Achis king of Geth. 1. Reg. 21. alſo in Ceila, in the deſerts of Ziph, and of Maon. c. 23, in Engaddi, c. 24. in Hachila. c. 26. and againe amongſt the Philiſtians. c. 27. and 30.

verses.text: DELIVER me from mine enimies ô my God: and from them that riſe vp againſt me defend me.
Deliuer me from them that worke iniquitie: and from bloudy men ſaue me.
Becauſe loe they <na>(b)</na> haue taken my ſoule: the ſtrong haue falne violently vpon me.

notes.label: b
notes.text: They haue ſo ſtraictly beſeged me, that it is now in their handes, to take away my life.

verses.text: Neyther is it mine iniquitie, nor my ſinne ô Lord: <na>(c)</na> without iniquitie haue I runne, and gone directly.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Of my part I haue committed no fault againſt myn enimies, for which they can haue anie iuſt cauſe to perſecute me.

verses.text: Ryſe vp to meete me, and ſee: and thou ô Lord the God of powres, God of Iſrael attend to viſite <na>(d)</na> al nations: haue <na>(e)</na> no mercie on al that worke iniquitie.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The prophet foreſeing in ſpirite, that the Catholique Church shal be vniuſtly perſecuted, prayeth, and teacheth others to pray, that God wil mercifully viſite his faithful people of al nations:

notes.label: e
notes.text: and not ſpare obſtinate perſecuters.

verses.text: They wil returne <na>(f)</na> at euening: and they shal ſuffer famine <na>(g)</na> as dogges, and shal compaſſe the citie.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Perſecuters laboring how much, or how long ſoeuer, shal at night, that is, in the end of al their wicked endeuoures be vnſatisfied in their deſires,

notes.label: g
notes.text: as hungrie dogges that runne hunting al the day, & night alſo, ſtil ſeeking & not finding wherwith to fil their rauenous mouthes and deuouring bellies.

verses.text: Behold they <na>(h)</na> wil ſpeake in their mouth, and a ſworde in their lippes: <na>(i)</na> becauſe who hath heard?

notes.label: h
notes.text: They threaten and determine to vſe al crueltie,

notes.label: i
notes.text: as if there were no God, that heareth, and wil punish it.

verses.text: And thou ô Lord wilt ſcorne them: thou wilt bring to naught al the nations.
I wil keepe my ſtrength to thee: <na>(k)</na> becauſe thou art my recciuer:

notes.label: k
notes.text: Through Gods grace the Church is ſtil ſtrong and the vertuous do perſeuere.

verses.text: my God, thy mercie shal preuent.
God wil shew vnto me concerning mine enimies, kil them not <na>(l)</na> leſt ſometime my peoples forgete. Diſperſe them in thy ſtrength: and <na>(m)</na> depoſe them my protector ô Lord.

notes.label: l
notes.text: God ſuffereth afflictions to fal vpon his ſeruants to kepe them exerciſed, leſt in proſperitie they forgete their duties to him.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Depriue them of powre, that they may not do ſo much euil as they deſire.

verses.text: The ſinne of their mouth, the word of their lippes: and let them be taken in their pride. And for <na>(n)</na> curſing and lying they shal be <na>(o)</na> talked of

notes.label: n
notes.text: After that their iniquitie is complete

notes.label: o
notes.text: they shal be accuſed and punished for their blaſphemies and lies.

verses.text: in conſummation: in wrath of comſummation and they shal not be. And they shal know that God wil rule ouer Iacob: and ouer the ends of the earth.
They <na>(p)</na> shal be turned at euening, and shal ſuffer famine as dogges: and shal compaſſe the citie.
They shal be <na>(q)</na> diſperſed to eate: and if they be not filled, they <na>(r)</na> wil murmur alſo.

notes.label: q
notes.text: They shal in vaine ſeeke oyle for their lampes with the foolish virgins, repent with Iudas, and finding no helpe,

notes.label: r
notes.text: ſhal continually blaſpheme in hel.

verses.text: But I wil ſing thy ſtrength: and wil exalt thy mercie in <na>(s)</na> the morning. Becauſe thou art become my receiuer, and my refuge, in the day of my tribulation.

notes.label: s
notes.text: In the reſurrection.

verses.text: My helper, I wil ſing to thee, becauſe thou art God my receiuer: my God, my mercie.

chapters.summary: Holie Dauid (being beſieged in his owne houſe by men ſent to kil him) confidently prayeth God to deliuer him, 6. and al faithful nations in like danger: 7. and praiſeth God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Another prayer of David in danger.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for them, <na>(a)</na> that shal be changed, in <na>(b)</na> the inſcription of the title <na>(c)</na> to Dauid him ſelfe, <na>(d)</na> for doctrine,

notes.label: a
notes.text: The change of ſtate from aduerſitie to proſperitie in the people of Iſrael, was a figure of the like change in the Church of Chriſt,

notes.label: b
notes.text: worthie to be remembred,

notes.label: c
notes.text: for the inſtruction,

notes.label: d
notes.text: of Gods beloued,

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> when he ſet fire on Meſopotamia of Syria, and in Sobal, and Ioab returned, and ſtroke Idumæa in the valley of ſalt-pittes twelue thouſand. (2. Reg. 8. & 10. & 1. Paral. 18.) <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: e
notes.text: as the ſame are more largely recorded in the bookes of kinges.

verses.text: O GOD thou <na>(f)</na> haſt repelled vs, & haſt deſtroyed vs: thou waſt angrie <na>(g)</na> and haſt had mercie on vs.

notes.label: f
notes.text: God ſuffereth his people to be afflicted, as wel for their ſinnes, as for exerciſe in vertue,

notes.label: g
notes.text: after sheweth his mercie in pardoning, and fauour in aduancing them.

verses.text: Thou haſt moued the earth, and haſt trubled it: heale the breaches thereof, becauſe it is moued.
Thou haſt shewed vnto thy people <na>(h)</na> hard thinges: thou haſt made vs drinke the wine of compunction.

notes.label: h
notes.text: by punishīg ſinners.

verses.text: Thou haſt <na>(i)</na> geuen a ſignification to them that feare thee: they flee from the face of the bow.

notes.label: i
notes.text: VVarning them to amēd.

verses.text: That thy beloued <na>(k)</na> may be deliuered, ſaue me with thy right hand; and heare me.

notes.label: k
notes.text: and then reſtoreth them to former good ſtate.
