verses.text: God hath ſpoken in <na>(l)</na> his holie: I shal reioyce, and <na>(m)</na> shal diuide Sichem: and shal meſure the valley of tabernacles.

notes.label: l
notes.text: God alſo as he hath promiſed by his holie oracle,

notes.label: m
notes.text: hath aduanced king Dauid, in his temporal kingdom, and doth much more aduance him, and other elect in euerlaſting life.

verses.text: Galaad is mine, and Manaſſes is mine: and Ephraim the ſtrength of my heade.
Iuda my king: Moab <na>(n)</na> the pot of my hope. Into Edom wil I <na>(o)</na> ſtretch out my shoe: the foreners are ſubiect to me.

notes.label: n
notes.text: As a veſſel for meaner vſes

notes.label: o
notes.text: Bring it vnder my dominion.

verses.text: Who shal conduct me into a fenſed citie? who shal conduct me euen into Idumea?
Shal not thou ô God, <na>(p)</na> that haſt expelled vs: and <na>(q)</na> wilt not thou ô God goe forth in our hoſtes?

notes.label: p
notes.text: As God doth ſometimes punish:

notes.label: q
notes.text: ſo he alſo rewardeth.

verses.text: Giue vs aide from tribulation: becauſe mans ſaluation is vaine.
In God we shal doe <na>(r)</na> ſtrength: and he shal bring to nothing them that afflict vs.

notes.label: r
notes.text: ſtrongly, with fortitude.

chapters.summary: King Dauid after his owne and the peoples manie tribulations, 8. rendereth thankes for their renowmed victories, 11. atchiued by Gods only powre. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: King Dauids thankes for victories. the 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, <na>(a)</na> in hyms to Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In ſongues of praiſe and thankes to God.

verses.text: HEARE ô God my petition: attend to my praier.
From <na>(b)</na> the ends of the earth I haue cried to thee: whiles my hart was in anguish, thou <na>(c)</na> didſt exalt me on a rocke.

notes.label: b
notes.text: From al coaſtes of the earth faithful people pray to God,

notes.label: c
notes.text: the Church builded vpon an aſſured fundation, is exalted to great powre and dignitie.

verses.text: Thou haſt <na>(d)</na> conducted me, becauſe thou art made my hope: a toure of ſtrength from the face of the enimie.

notes.label: d
notes.text: God conducteth, defendeth, and deliuereth thoſe that confidently truſt in him.

verses.text: I shal inhabite in <na>(e)</na> thy tabernacle for euer: I shal be protected in the couert of thy winges.

notes.label: e
notes.text: in the Church, a place of aſſured protection.

verses.text: Becauſe thou my God haſt heard my prayer: thou haſt giuen inheritance to thoſe that feare thy name.
Thou wilt adde <na>(f)</na> dayes vpon the dayes of the king: his years euen vnto the day of generation and generation.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Chriſts kingdome the Church perpetual to the end of this world, and eternal after the general Reſurrection.

verses.text: He is permanent for euer in the ſight of God: his <na>(g)</na> mercie and <na>(h)</na> truth who shal require?

notes.label: g
notes.text: Who is able to vnderſtand, or explicate how great Chriſts mercie is in redeming vs,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and his truth in performing his promiſed rewardes?

verses.text: So <na>(i)</na> wil I ſay a Pſalme to thy name for euer and euer: that I may render my vowes <na>(k)</na> from day to day.

notes.label: i
notes.text: For ſo imeſtimable benefites, I wil alwayes praiſe thee with Pſalmes, Canticles, or other thankes in this life:

notes.label: k
notes.text: and eternally in the life to come.

chapters.summary: Faithful people of the whole earth pray, and acknowlege that God mercifully heareth their prayer. 6. expect the eternal kingdom of Chriſt, in which they shal praiſe him for euermore. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A confident prayer for Chriſt'ſ Incarnation.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for <na>(a)</na> Iduthun a Pſalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Directed to Idithun, one of the maſters of muſike, to ſing it, or to make tune for it.

verses.text: Shal <na>(b)</na> not my ſoule be ſubiect to God? for of him is my ſaluation.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The wicked threating to ruinate others, Dauid, or anie iuſt man, feareth them not, becauſe his ſoule is ſubiect to God.

verses.text: For he is my God, and my ſauiour: my receiuer <na>(c)</na> I shal be moued no more.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Therfore I firmely purpoſe neuer to be moued from God.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> How long ſet you violently vpon a man: <na>(e)</na> you al doe kil: as it were vpon <na>(f)</na> a wal, that is leaning, and a wal shaken.

notes.label: d
notes.text: In vaine do you myn aduerſaries ſtil aſſault me,

notes.label: e
notes.text: though ye be al confederate to kil me;

notes.label: f
notes.text: ſuppoſing me to be like a ruinous, or shaken wal, that is eaſily throwne downe.

verses.text: But <na>(g)</na> yet they thought to repel my price, <na>(h)</na> I ranne in thirſt: they <na>(i)</na> bleſſed with their mouth, and curſed with their hart.

notes.label: g
notes.text: They thinck ſtil to depriue me of my reward, the price of my laboures and merites,

notes.label: h
notes.text: but I runne ſo much more diligently, as thirſting after righteouſnes in this life, and glorie in the next, to finish my courſe.

notes.label: i
notes.text: A moſt dangerous tentation, when after threates and crueltie, perſecutors endeuour by ſwete wordes, and promiſes to perſwaed the iuſt to fal into ſinne.

verses.text: But yet my ſoule be thou ſubiect to God: becauſe my patience is from him.
Becauſe he is my God, and my ſauiour: my helper <na>(k)</na> I shal not remoue.

notes.label: k
notes.text: I reſolutly purpoſe not to yeld to anie tentations.

verses.text: In God is my ſaluation, and my glorie: the God of my helpe, and my hope is in God.
Hope in him <na>(l)</na> al ye the congregation of people: powre out your harts before him, God is our helper for euer.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Gods faithful ſeruantes are not only conſtant themſelues, but alſo exhorte and perſwade al others, as much as in them lieth, to ſerue God and truſt in him.

verses.text: But yet the children of men are vaine, the children of men are <na>(m)</na> liers in balances: that they may deceiue by vanitie together.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Vſing falſe weightes they defraud one an other.

verses.text: Hope not in iniquitie, and couete not robberies: if riches abound ſet not your hart vpon them.
<na>(n)</na> Once hath God ſpoken, theſe <na>(o)</na> two things haue I heard:

notes.label: n
notes.text: God hauing nce ſpoken it is moſt aſſured.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Two eſpecial attributes of God.

verses.text: That <na>(p)</na> powre is Gods, and <na>(q)</na> mercie ô Lord is to thee: becauſe thou wilt render to euery one according to his workes. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: p
notes.text: God is Omnipotent, ſo that he can both reward, and punish infinitly;

notes.label: q
notes.text: and Merciful, that he is readie to receiue al ſinners into his fauour, if they wil repent and turne vnto him.

chapters.summary: A iuſt man encoregeth his owne ſoule to ſerue God in ſincere humilitie, 9. exhorteth alſo al others to truſt in God, not in falſe and worldlie pollicie, or wealth, becauſe Gods powre and mercie wil render to euerie one as they deſerue. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Exhortation to good life, in reſpect of reward or punishment.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme <na>(a)</na> of Dauid when he was in the deſert of Iuda (1. Reg. 22.) <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Holie Dauid made this deuout meditation when he was in the foreſt of Haret, or deſert of Ziph 1. Reg. 22. & 23. and could not come to the tabernacle of God, nor to Ieruſalem, where he eſpecially deſired to be, in the inheritance of our Lord, which was to him a great affliction. As the like is now to Catholiques, when they are put in cloſe priſon for their faith, or otherwiſe hindered, that they can not be preſent at the moſt holie and daylie Sacrifice. In which caſe we muſt ſupplie as we may, this great loſſe, and comfort ourſelues with this, or like Pſalme, or prayer, ſaying : O God my God, to thee I watch.

verses.text: O GOD my God to thee I watch, <na>(b)</na> from the morning light. <na>(c)</na> My ſoule hath thirſted to thee, <na>(d)</na> my flesh to thee very manie wayes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Euen from the firſt downing of the morning,

notes.label: c
notes.text: my ſoule thirſteth after thee,

notes.label: d
notes.text: yea alſo my very flesh, and whole bodie feeleth great paines, by this affliction of mind, and deſireth releeſe and reſt.

verses.text: In a deſert land, and inacceſſible, and without water, <na>(e)</na> ſo in the holie haue I appeared to thee, <na>(f)</na> that I might ſee thy ſtrength, and thy glorie.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Being now in caſe that I can not ſerue thee, ô God, as I would, yet I exhibite myſelfe preſent in ſpirite, before thy holie place,

notes.label: f
notes.text: meditating thy powre, and thy glorie.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(g)</na> thy mercie is better then liues, my lippes shal prayſe thee.

notes.label: g
notes.text: This conſolation in banishment from thy diuine Seruice, is ſweeter to me then manie temporal liues, or anie worldlie proſperitie.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> So wil I bleſſe thee in my life: and in thy name I wil liſte vp my hands.

notes.label: h
notes.text: For as the Paſſions of Chriſt abound in vs (ſaith S. Paul 2. Cor. 1.) ſo alſo by Chriſt our comfort aboundeth.

verses.text: As with <na>(i)</na> marrow and fatnes let my ſoule be filled: <na>(k)</na> and my mouth shal praiſe with lippes of exultation.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Replenish my ſoul ô God, with the aboundance of thy grace,

notes.label: k
notes.text: ſo ſhal I be more able to praiſe thee.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> If I haue bene mindful of thee vpon my bedde, <na>(m)</na> in the morning I wil meditate on thee:

notes.label: l
notes.text: Seing in the night, alſo in my bed I meditate of thee;

notes.label: m
notes.text: I wil more diligently do the ſame in the morning.

verses.text: becauſe thou haſt bene my helper.
And in the couert of thy winges I wil reioice, my ſoule hath cleaued after thee: thy right hand hath receiued me.
But <na>(n)</na> they in vaine haue ſought my ſoule, <na>(o)</na> they shal enter into the inferiour partes of the earth.

notes.label: n
notes.text: My temporal and ſpiritual enimies:

notes.label: o
notes.text: and they shal be damned for their ſinnes.

verses.text: They <na>(p)</na> shal be deliuered into the handes of the ſworde, they shal be <na>(q)</na> the portions of foxes.

notes.label: p
notes.text: It happened literally to Saul, that he was ſlaine in battle, which he made againſt his enimies;

notes.label: q
notes.text: and his dead bodie was hung on a wal (1. Reg. 31.) expoſed to wilde beaſtes, or birdes, though it was afterwards burnt and buried.

verses.text: But <na>(r)</na> the king shal reioice in God, al shal be praiſed that ſweare by him: becauſe the mouth is ſtopped of thoſe that ſpeake wicked thinges.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Dauid was preſently after Sauls death exalted to the kingdome, in figure of Chriſt, whoſe name and glorie was exalted, after the deſtruction of the Iewes by Pagane Emperours.

chapters.summary: Dauid in banishment with great affection deſireth to vnite himſelfe with God in meditation, 4. purpoſing and promiſing euer to praiſe him : 10. prophicieth the vaine endeuoures, and condemnation of his enimies; and his owne aduancement. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David's devotion in banishment.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, a Pſalme of Dauid.
HEARE ô God my prayer when I make petition: from the feare of my enimie deliuer my ſoule.
Thou <na>(a)</na> haſt protected me from the <na>(b)</na> aſſemblie of the malignant: from the multitude of them that worke iniquitie.

notes.label: a
notes.text: By example of thy former protection,

notes.label: b
notes.text: from the conſpiracie of wicked men, I truſt moſt aſſuredly in thy helpe.

verses.text: Becauſe they haue sharpned their tongues as a ſworde: they haue bent the bow a bitter thing,
that they may shoote in ſecretes at the immaculate.
Sodanely they wil shoote at him, and wil not feare: they <na>(c)</na> haue confirmed to themſelues a wicked worde. They haue talked to hide ſnares: they haue ſaide, who shal ſee them?

notes.label: c
notes.text: They are reſolued to intrappe me,

verses.text: They haue ſearched iniquities: they <na>(d)</na> haue failed ſearching with ſcrutanie.

notes.label: d
notes.text: But as they haue failed: ſo they ſhal ſtil faile, and be ouerreached in their bad counſels; as Achitophel. 1. Reg. 17.

verses.text: Man shal come to a deepe hart: and God shal be exalted. <na>(e)</na> Childrens arrowes are made their woundes:

notes.label: e
notes.text: God hath choſen the weake of this world to confound the ſtrong.

verses.text: and their tongues are weakned againſt them. Al that ſaw them <na>(f)</na> were trubled:

notes.label: f
notes.text: much merueled, ſeing the wicked ſo punished.

verses.text: and euerie man feared. And they shewed forth the workes of God: and they vnderſtood his doinges.
The iuſt shal reioice in our Lord, and shal hope in him, and al the right of hart <na>(g)</na> shal be praiſed.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The iuſt shal be praiſed, for rightly ſeruing God.

chapters.summary: A prayer of the iuſt repoſing their whole truſt in God: 7. and reioycing that the enimies machinations are fruſtrate. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A confident prayer in tribulation.
The 7. key.

verses.text: To the end, a Pſalme of Dauid, <na>(a)</na> the Canticle of Ieremie, and Ezechiel, to the people of the tranſmigration, when they begane to goe forth.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The ſeuentie Interpreters ſeing Dauid here prophecie of the peoples returne from Babylon, added the names of Ieremie and Ezechiel, who being in that captiuitie, prophecied the ſame more largely. As likewiſe theſe and other Prophetes, foreſaw in ſpirite, and more eſpecially prophecied the going forth of al nations from Babylon, that is, forſaking Idolatrie, and embracing true Religion in the Church of Chriſt, ſo S. Auguſtin, Eutymius, and others.

verses.text: AN hymne ô God becometh thee <na>(b)</na> in Sion: & a vow shal be rendered to thee in Ieruſalem.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Not in Babylon, nor els where, but only in the Church, praiſes and vowes are gratful to God.

verses.text: Heare my prayer: <na>(c)</na> al flesh shal come to thee.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Al nations shal know thee.

verses.text: The wordes of the wicked <na>(d)</na> haue preuailed vpon vs: and thou wilt be <na>(e)</na> propitious to our impieties.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The wicked are inſolent in threatning,

notes.label: e
notes.text: but thou mercifully pardoning our ſinnes, they ſhal not hurt vs.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Bleſſed is he, whom thou haſt choſen, and taken: he shal dwel in thy courtes.

notes.label: f
notes.text: They are happie to whom thou haſt prepared grace, and glorie.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> We shal be replenished in the goods of thy houſe: holie is thy temple, <na>(h)</na> meruelous in equitie. Heare vs ô God our ſauiour, the hope of al the ends of the earth; and in the ſea farre.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The voice of the faithful, reioycing in the hope of eternal glorie. Rom. 5.

notes.label: h
notes.text: nothing polluted shal enter into heauen. Apo. 21.

verses.text: Preparing <na>(i)</na> mountanes in thy ſtrength, girded with might:

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thou which art al powreful, as appeareth by the huge montaines,

verses.text: which trubleſt <na>(k)</na> the depths of the ſea, the ſound of the waues therof.

notes.label: k
notes.text: ſeas, and other thy workes.

verses.text: The Gentiles shal <na>(l)</na> be trubled, and they that inhabite the borders shal be affraide of thy ſignes: <na>(m)</na> the outegoinges of the morning and euening thou shalt delight.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Thou wilt by thy omnipotent powre moue the hartes of obdurate men, and ſo conuert innumerable of al nations to thee.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Thou wilt draw manie to thee, with ioy and gladnes, from the vttermoſt coaſtes of the eaſt and weaſt.

verses.text: Thou haſt viſited the earth, and haſt inebriated it: thou haſt multiplied to inrich it. The <na>(n)</na> riuer of God is replenished with waters, thou haſt prepared their <na>(o)</na> meat: becauſe <na>(p)</na> ſo is the preparation therof.

notes.label: n
notes.text: God wrought diuers miracles in waters (Gen. 7. Exo. 7. 14. 15. Ioſue. 3. 4. Reg. 5. 6. &c.)

notes.label: o
notes.text: likewiſe in prouiding meate for his people. (Exo. 16. 3. Reg. 17. 4. Reg. 4. 7. &c.) which were figures of Baptiſme, Euchariſt, and other Sacraments of Chriſt, waſhing from ſinnes, and augmenting grace,

notes.label: p
notes.text: ſo replenishing the Church with moſt ſacred Myſteries.

verses.text: Inebriate <na>(q)</na> her riuers, <na>(r)</na> multiplie her fruites: in her dropps she shal reioyce ſpringing.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Endewing the Apoſtles and other preachers with ſpiritual grace and lerning,

notes.label: r
notes.text: continuing the ſucceſſion of paſtores to watter and feede the faithful people.

verses.text: Thou wilt <na>(s)</na> bleſſe the crowne of the yeare of thy goodnes: <na>(t)</na> and thy fildes shal be replenished with plentie.

notes.label: s
notes.text: God bleſſeth the whole courſe, or circle of time, of the Church militant in this world,

notes.label: t
notes.text: and the crowne, or happie end of euerie iuſt perſons life.

verses.text: The <na>(v)</na> beautiful places of the deſert shal be fat: and the <na>(w)</na> litle hilles shal be girded aboute with exultation.

notes.label: v
notes.text: u Euen thoſe which before had only a ſhew of beautie, but in dede vvere barren, ſhal yelde abundant fruict.

notes.label: w
notes.text: thoſe which are more eminent ſhal particularly reioyce in their owne, and others ſpiritual progreſſe in vertue.

verses.text: The <na>(x)</na> rammes of the shepe are clothed, and <na>(y)</na> the valleis shal abounde with corne: <na>(z)</na> they wil crie, yea they wil ſay an hymne.

notes.label: x
notes.text: The principal paſtores ſhal in proportion reioyce aboue the reſt, for the grace and glorie of al their flocke.

notes.label: y
notes.text: the ſubiectes alſo and inferior people shal be ſatiate vvith their happie lotte.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Al together, prelates and people, higher and lovver ſhal with vniforme voice ſing praiſes to God, and perpetual hymnes.

chapters.summary: God is rightly praiſed in Sion and Ieruſalem (in his Church only) for his benefites beſtowed and promiſed. 8. Vnto which alſo in the time of grace, al nations shal be called. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Converſion of Gentiles.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, a Canticle <na>(a)</na> of reſurrection. MAke ye <na>(b)</na> iubilation to God al the earth,

notes.label: a
notes.text: Myſtical reſurrection, Gentiles ſucceding in place of the Iewes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Shew your internal ioy by external wordes and deedes.

verses.text: ſay a pſalme to his name: geue glorie to his praiſe.
Say ye to God: <na>(c)</na> How terrible are thy workes ô Lord! in the multitude of thy ſtrength thine enimies <na>(d)</na> shal lie to thee.

notes.label: c
notes.text: In drovvning the vvorld, in confounding the tongues in Babel, in burning Sodom and Gomorrha with brimſton, in plaging the Ægyptians, in drovvning Pharao and his vvhole armie in the read ſea; in deſtroying the Chananites and other infideles, in puniſhing the tenne tribes, and aftervvards the other tvvo by captiuitie, and innumerable other puniſhments, al for ſinnes,

notes.label: d
notes.text: for vvhich euen the vvicked, though not ſincerly conuerted, yet of ſeruile feare, feaned and falſly promiſed to amend, but performed it not: as Pharao afflicted vvith plagues, vvas forced to promiſe libertie to the children of Iſrael, vvhich he aftervvards denied.

verses.text: Let al the earth adore thee, and ſing to thee: let it ſing a pſalme to thy name.
Come ye, and ſee the workes of God: terrible in counſels ouer the chidren of men.
Who turneth <na>(e)</na> the ſea into drie land, in <na>(f)</na> the riuer they shal paſſe on foote, <na>(g)</na> there we shal reioyce in him.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The read ſea,

notes.label: f
notes.text: when Ioſue brought the people ouer Iordan,

notes.label: g
notes.text: in remembring and reciting theſe ſingular benefites.

verses.text: Who ruleth in his ſtrength for euer his eyes looke vpon the gentiles: <na>(h)</na> they that exaſperate him let them <na>(i)</na> not be exalted in themſelues.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Gods choſen people the Iewes did often exaſperate God by their ingratitude, murmuring, and other ſinnes: whom the prophet therfore admoniſheth,

notes.label: i
notes.text: not to be proud, leſt they be ſaboued, and brought lowe.

verses.text: Ye <na>(k)</na> Gentiles bleſſe our God: and make the voice of his prayſe hearde.

notes.label: k
notes.text: By way of inuitation the Pſalmiſt prophecieth the conuerſion of Gentiles.

verses.text: Who hath put <na>(l)</na> my ſoule in life: and hath not geuen my feete to be moued.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The voice of the whole Church: confeſſing Gods prouidence and protection, that she neuer faleth; for the Iewes falling from Chriſt the Gentiles beleued in him; and ſome nations, or countries failing from Religion, others are conuerted.

verses.text: Becauſe thou <na>(m)</na> haſt proued vs ô God: by fire thou haſt tried vs, as ſiluer is tried.

notes.label: m
notes.text: God ſuffereth his Church to be perſecuted with al kindes of tribulation, as ſome are here recited.

verses.text: Thou haſt brought vs into a ſnare, thou haſt laide tribulations on our backe: thou haſt ſet men vpon our heades.
<na>(n)</na> We haue paſſed through fire and water: and thou haſt brought vs out into refreshing.

notes.label: n
notes.text: But through Gods aſſiſtance his ſeruants paſſe through, and ouercome al tentations.

verses.text: I wil goe into thy houſe with <na>(o)</na> holocauſtes: I wil render thee <na>(p)</na> my vowes:

notes.label: o
notes.text: Sacrifice of thankes,

notes.label: p
notes.text: and voluntarie vowes,

verses.text: which my lippes haue diſtinguished. And <na>(q)</na> my mouth hath ſpoken in my tribulation.

notes.label: q
notes.text: that which anie promiſeth to God in tribulation, they muſt performe accordingly.

verses.text: <na>(r)</na> Holocauſtes with marrow wil I offer to thee, with incenſe of rammes: I wil offer to thee oxen with bucke goates.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Theſe were the beſt external ſacrifices of the old law.

verses.text: <na>(s)</na> Come ye, heare, and I wil tel al ye that feare God, what great things he hath done for my ſoule.

notes.label: s
notes.text: But both then and now the internal ſacrifices of contrite hart, of iuſtice, and of diuine praiſe beſt pleaſe God.

verses.text: To him haue I cried with my mouth, and haue exulted <na>(t)</na> vnder my tongue.

notes.label: t
notes.text: from the hart, which is vnder the tongue, and directeth the tongue what to ſpeake.

verses.text: <na>(v)</na> If I haue beheld iniquitie in my hart, our Lord wil not heare.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Whoſoeuer wil be heard in prayer, muſt repent of his ſinnes.

verses.text: Therfore hath God heard, and hath attended to the voice of my petition.
Bleſſed be God who hath not remoued my prayer, and his mercie from me.

chapters.summary: The prophet inuiteth al men to praiſe God for his meruelous workes, and benefites donne to the Iewes. 7. Who being vngratful, 8. Gentiles are called, 16. and bring forth better fruict. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Gentiles ſucceed the Jews.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, in hymes, a Pſalme <na>(a)</na> of Canticle to Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Pſalme beginning to be ſongue by voices, inſtruments were adioyned.

verses.text: GOd <na>(b)</na> haue mercie vpon vs, and <na>(c)</na> bleſſe vs: <na>(d)</na> illuminate his countenance vpon vs, and <na>(e)</na> haue mercie on vs.

notes.label: b
notes.text: God firſt remitte our ſinnes:

notes.label: c
notes.text: then geue vs thy manifold graces,

notes.label: d
notes.text: grant faith and repentance,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and ſo forgeuenes of ſinnes.

verses.text: That we may know thy way vpon earth: in al nations thy ſaluation.
Let peoples ô God, confeſſe to thee: <na>(f)</na> let al peoples confeſſe to thee.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Al nations shal be conuerted.

verses.text: Let nations be glad & reioice: becauſe thou iudgeſt peoples in equitie, and the nations in earth thou doeſt direct.
Let peoples ô God confeſſe to thee, let al peoples confeſſe to thee:
the earth hath yelded her fruite. <na>(g)</na> God, <na>(h)</na> our God bleſſe vs,

notes.label: g
notes.text: God the Fater,

notes.label: h
notes.text: God the Sonne,

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> God bleſſe vs: and let al the endes of the earth feare him.

notes.label: i
notes.text: God the Holie Ghoſt, ſaue the peoples of al nations, by Euangelical preaching of thee, the moſt Bleſſed Trinitie.

chapters.summary: The prophet prayeth for (and withal foresheweth) the propagation of the Church of Chriſt. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Propagation of the Church.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, a Pſalme of Canticle, to Dauid himſelf.
LEt <na>(a)</na> God ariſe, and let his enimies be diſperſed, and let them that hate him <na>(b)</na> flee from his face.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In maner of praying that God wil vouchſafe to defend the Church, the Pſalmiſt prophecieth that God wil ariſe,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and the enimies ſhal flee away, not daring to abide the combate.

verses.text: As ſmoke vanisheth, let them vanish away: as waxe melteth at the preſence of fire, ſo let ſinners perish at the preſence of God.
And <na>(c)</na> let the iuſt make merrie, and reioyce in the ſight of God: and let them be delighted in mirth.

notes.label: c
notes.text: As God is terrible to the wicked: ſo he is comfortable to the iuſt.

verses.text: Sing to God, ſay a Pſalme to his name: <na>(d)</na> make way to him, who <na>(e)</na> mounteth vpon the weſt, <na>(f)</na> Lord is his name. Reioyce ye in his ſyght, they shal be trubled at the preſence of him:

notes.label: d
notes.text: Reſiſt not Gods inſpiration, but receiue it with ioy and thankes.

notes.label: e
notes.text: who triumpheth ouer death

notes.label: f
notes.text: God is Lord, not only of theſe or thoſe nations, countries or other creatures, but abſolutly and vniuerſally of al.

verses.text: the father of orphanes, and iudge of widowes. God in his <na>(g)</na> holie place:

notes.label: g
notes.text: That is the true holie Church, which hath

verses.text: God that maketh men to inhabite <na>(h)</na> of one manner in a houſe. That bringeth forth them, <na>(i)</na> that be bound, in ſtrengh, likewiſe them, that <na>(k)</na> exaſperate, that dwel <na>(l)</na> in ſepulchers.

notes.label: h
notes.text: vnitie in doctrin, touching faith and maners. · S.Cypr.ep.76.

notes.label: i
notes.text: That be bond in ſinne.

notes.label: k
notes.text: euen rebellious willes are altered by Gods mercie, and freely embrace his law

notes.label: l
notes.text: alſo the dead and drie hartes that cared not for ſpiritual thinges, are ſoftened, and quickned with new grace.

verses.text: O God <na>(m)</na> when thou wenteſt forth in the ſight of thy people, when thou didſt paſſe through the deſert.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The benefites beſtowed on the Iſraelites, are written in the bookes of Moyſes, Ioſue, and Iudges.

verses.text: The earth was moued, and the heauens alſo diſtilled, at the preſence of the God of Sina, at the face of the God of Iſrael.
<na>(n)</na> Voluntarie rayne shalt thou ſeperat ô God to thine inheritance: and it was <na>(o)</na> weakned, but thou haſt perfited it.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Not mans deſeruing, but Gods mere good wil, and free grace cauſed Chriſt to come, and by himſelfe and his Apoſtles to preach the Euangelical doctrin, which watereth the whole world,

notes.label: o
notes.text: God choſe the weake, but made them ſtrong.

verses.text: Thy <na>(p)</na> liuing creatures shal dwel in it: thou haſt prepared <na>(q)</na> in thy ſwetnes for the poore, ô God.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Thoſe whom thou haſt choſen, and ſo made thyn owne peculiar people, ſhal enioy this grace.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Thou gaueſt Manna in the deſert, the B. Sacrament in the new teſtament.

verses.text: Our Lord shal geue <na>(r)</na> the word to them that euanglize, <na>(s)</na> with great powre.

notes.label: r
notes.text: God geueth to the preacher what to ſpeake,

notes.label: s
notes.text: and to ſome he geueth alſo powre to worke miracles, in confirmation of their doctrin. Mar. 16.

verses.text: The <na>(t)</na> king of hoaſtes the beloued of the beloued: and <na>(v)</na> to the beautie of the houſe, to diuide the ſpoyles.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Some potent king, or ( as it is in the Hebrew ) kinges being beloued, of the beloued of God, the only Sonne of God, ſhal yeld themſelues to the ſame beloued Sonne of God:

notes.label: v
notes.text: which ſhal redound to the glorie and beautie of his Church, gayning ſuch ſpiritual prayes from the diuel.

verses.text: If ye <na>(w)</na> ſleepe among the middeſt of the lottes, the winges of a doue layde ouer with ſiluer, and the hinder parts of her backe in the palenes of gold.

notes.label: w
notes.text: If you be in ſuch danger, that the aduerſaries caſt dice, or lottes for your perſons, and goodes, yet you ſhal be deliuered, as if a doue, with her gliſtering fethers, like ſiluer and gold, flie away into a ſecure place, without loſſe or diminution, but rather with increaſe of vertues.

verses.text: Whiles <na>(x)</na> the heauenlie diſcerneth kings ouer her, <na>(y)</na> with ſnow they shal be made white in Selmon.

notes.label: x
notes.text: VVhen the heauenlie king determineth thus of earthlie kinges,

notes.label: y
notes.text: they shal be purged from their ſinnes, and made white like ſnow, that falleth in mount Selmon, which is a ſhadowed hil, thicke with trees, in mount Ephraim nere to Iordan.

verses.text: The <na>(z)</na> mountane of God a fat mountane. A mountane <na>(a)</na> crudded as cheeſe, a <na>(b)</na> fatte mountane:

notes.label: z
notes.text: The Church of God is viſible, and durable like to a mountane.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Combined, or ioyned together, as when milke is turned into curde, and ſo into cheeſe.

notes.label: b
notes.text: fructful, enriched by ſpiritual giftes of the Holie Ghoſt.

verses.text: why <na>(c)</na> ſuppoſe you crudded mountanes? A mountane, in which it hath wel pleaſed God to dwel therin: for in dede our Lord wil dwel euen to the end.

notes.label: c
notes.text: ye that are not of this Church, do in vaine and erroniouſly imagine, that anie other mountaines are vnited.

verses.text: The <na>(d)</na> chariote of God is ten thouſand folde, thouſands of them that reioyce, our Lord in them, <na>(e)</na> in Sina in the holie place.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Innumerable Angels miniſters of Gods wil, do continually attend vpon his Diuine Maieſtie, as if he ( who otherwiſe nedeth no ſeruice ) were caried by them, as in a chariotte of infinite magnificence. Dan 7.

notes.label: e
notes.text: So God appeared in Maieſtie, when he gaue his law in mount Sinai.

verses.text: Thou art <na>(f)</na> aſcended on hygh, thou <na>(g)</na> haſt taken captiuitie: thou <na>(h)</na> haſt receiued gifts in men: for euen thoſe <na>(i)</na> that do not beleue, our Lord God to inhabite. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: f
notes.text: Chriſt aſcended with innumerable Angels attending vpon him,

notes.label: g
notes.text: caried with him the fathers of the old teſtament, that had benne captiue,

notes.label: h
notes.text: as man he receiued giftes of God, in and for men, his faithful ſeruantes,

notes.label: i
notes.text: yea alſo he receiued for his merite, that innumerable, which before were incredulous, were conuerted, and God dwelt in their ſoules.

verses.text: Bleſſed be our Lord day by day: the God of our ſaluations wil make vs a proſperous iourney.
Our God is the God of ſauing: and <na>(k)</na> the iſſues of death are of our Lord, our Lord.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Our Lord, I ſay, our Lord, and none but he could ouercome death by dying.

verses.text: But yet God <na>(l)</na> ſtil breake the heads of his enimies: the hearie croune of them, that walke in their ſinnes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Though Chriſt died to deliuer al men from death. yet he wil geue capital ſentence of eternal death to al that obſtinatly remaine his enimies, and multiplie ſinnes vpon ſinnes, to the end of their temporal life.

verses.text: Our Lord Said: Out <na>(m)</na> of Baſan I wil conuert, I wil conuert <na>(n)</na> into the depth of the ſea.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Euen of the rudeſt barbarous nations, manie shal be conuerted to Chriſtiantie

notes.label: n
notes.text: namely Gods grace is extended into the Ilandes of the Ocean, and other ſeas.

verses.text: That thy foote (o) may be dipped in bloude: the tongue of thy dogges [made redde] with the ſame [bloud] of the enimies. [1]

notes.label: o
notes.text: But ſuch ſeuere ſlaughter shal fal vpon the obſtinate contemners of this grace, that mens feete shal be defiled in their bloud, and dogges ſhal lappe it.
Ex inimicis ab ipſo.

verses.text: They <na>(p)</na> haue ſeene thy entringes in ô God, the entrings of my God: of my King Who is <na>(q)</na> in the holie place.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Manie haue ſene, or knowen in general, but the faithful more exactly know how Chriſt came into this world, his conuerſation therin, and his going forth:

notes.label: q
notes.text: his reigning now in heauen our Mediatour, by whom al other interceſſors haue acceſſe to God.

verses.text: <na>(r)</na> Princes came before <na>(s)</na> ioyned with them that ſang, in the middes <na>(t)</na> of young wemen plaing on tymbrels.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The Apoſtles ſowing the firſt ſeede of Euangelical doctrin,

notes.label: s
notes.text: with whom other Apoſtolical men,

notes.label: t
notes.text: and other ſoules of al nations conuerted by their preaching, moſt ioyfully ſing together in hart, voice, and inſtruments: eſpecially in good workes, ſhew their gratful affections to our Redeemer.

verses.text: In <na>(v)</na> churches bleſſe ye God our Lord, of <na>(w)</na> the fountains of Iſrael.

notes.label: v
notes.text: And al this in the particular Churches of diuers Kingdomes, and partes of the world:

notes.label: w
notes.text: beginning with the Iſraelites in Ieruſalem, and ſo proceding into al Iurie, and Samaria, and to the vtmoſt of the earth. Act. 1.

verses.text: There <na>(x)</na> Beniamin a youngman, in exceſſe of minde. <na>(y)</na> The Princes of Iuda: their leaders: the Princes of Zabulon, the Princes of Nephthali.

notes.label: x
notes.text: S. Paul of Iacobs yongeſt ſonne Beniamin, laſt called to Apoſtleſhip, was chiefly ſent to the Gentiles.

notes.label: y
notes.text: Other Apoſtles of diuers tribes ſent firſt to the Iewes, ſecondarily to Gentiles.

verses.text: Command thy ſtrength ô God: <na>(z)</na> confirme this ô God, which thou haſt wrought in vs.

notes.label: z
notes.text: As the Church begane by the omnipotent powre of God; ſo by the ſame only powre it is conſerued.

verses.text: From thy temple in Ieruſalem, kinges shal offer giftes to thee.

Rebuke <na>(a)</na> the wilde beaſts of the reede, the congregation <na>(b)</na> of bulles in the kine of thy peoples: <na>(c)</na> that they may exclude them, which are tried with ſiluer. Diſſipate the nations that wil warres:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Chaſtice therfore ô God, al perſecuters of thy Church, who are but as weake wauering reedes, in compariſon of thy powre:

notes.label: b
notes.text: no better then bulles, with kyne, that is, captaines and popular people,

notes.label: c
notes.text: endeuoring to alienate the conſtant proued confeſſors from their faith.

verses.text: Legates shal come <na>(d)</na> out of Ægypt: Æthiopia shal preuent his handes to God.

notes.label: d
notes.text: A prophecie that manie ſhould be conuerted to Chriſt in Ægypt, and Æthiopia: as appeareth by the innumerable multitude of religious Monkes, & Nunnes in thoſe countries, ſhortly after the Apoſtles dayes.

verses.text: Ye kingdomes <na>(e)</na> of the earth ſing to God: ſing to our Lord:

notes.label: e
notes.text: The like afterwards in al other nations, whom therfore the prophet inuiteth to praiſe God, for ſo ineſtimable benefites in the whole world.

verses.text: Sing ye to God, that mounteth vpon the heauen of heauen, to the Eaſt. Behold he wil giue to his voice <na>(f)</na> the voice of ſtrength,

notes.label: f
notes.text: Chriſt will come to judge, in terror of voice, and vvith magnificence, accompanied vvith holy Angels and other Saints.

verses.text: giue you glorie to God vpon Iſrael, his magnificence, and his powre in the cloudes.
God is meruelous in his ſaintes, the God of Iſrael he wil giue powre, and ſtrength to his people, God be bleſſed.

chapters.summary: Notwithſtanding great perſecutions the Church proſpereth. 10. Eſpecially in the new teſtament, by Apoſtolical function, 18. miniſterie of Angels, Chriſts Aſcenſion, coming of the Holie Ghoſt, 31. confirming the faithful, repreſſing the inſolent, and conuerting manie. 35. For al which the prophet inuiteth al men to praiſe God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church ſtill conſerved.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> for them that shal be changed, <na>(c)</na> to Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the new Teſtament,

notes.label: b
notes.text: for gentiles conuerted to Chriſtianitie, and from vice to vertue,

notes.label: c
notes.text: prefigured in Dauid.

verses.text: SAve me ô God: becauſe <na>(d)</na> waters are entered into my ſoule.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Vehement afflictions inuiron my hart.

verses.text: I <na>(e)</na> ſticke faſt in the myre of the depth: and there is no ſure ſtanding. I am come into the depth of the ſea: and a tempeſt hath ouerwhelmed me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: I am as one intangled with quickesand, or quadmyre in the bottom of a great water.

verses.text: I haue <na>(f)</na> labored crying, my iawes are made hoarſe: my eies haue failed, whiles I hope in my God.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Our Lord ſvveat bloud for anguiſh in his prayer, and vvas not deliuered from his Paſſion, neither are his ſeruantes preſently deliuered from tribulations, but as is moſt to Gods honour and their owne good.

verses.text: They are multiplied aboue the heares of my head, that hate me without cauſe. <cr>[1]</cr> Mine enimies are made ſtrong, that haue perſecuted me vniuſtly: <na>(g)</na> then did I pay the thinges that I tooke not.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Ioan. 15. · Our Sauiour who had no ſinne, payde the ranſom for al ſinnes.

verses.text: O God thou knoweſt my <na>(h)</na> foolishnes: and <na>(i)</na> mine offences are not hide from thee.

notes.label: h
notes.text: O God thou knoweſt, that this which ſemeth follie to worldlie men, is true wiſdom;

notes.label: i
notes.text: and though men charge me vvith offences, thou knoweſt that I am innocent.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> Let them not be ashamed vpon me, which expect thee ô Lord, Lord of hoſtes. Let them not be confounded vpon me that ſeeke thee, ô God of Iſrael.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Suffer not the weake to be ſcandalized in my paſſions.

verses.text: Becauſe for thee haue I ſuſtained reproch, confuſion hath couered my face.
I am become a forener to my brethren, and a ſtranger to the ſonnes of my mother.
Becauſe <na>(l)</na> the zele of thy houſe hath eaten me: and the reproches of them that reproched thee, fel vpon me. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: l
notes.text: Ioan. 2. Rom. 15. · The zele of ſeeking Gods honour, in propagating and aduancing his Church, is the cauſe of perſecution. As vve ſee thoſe are leſſe perſecuted, which haue leſſe godlie zele.

verses.text: And I couered my ſoule in faſting: and iton <na>(m)</na> was made a reproch to me.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The wicked do reproch thoſe that mortifie themſelues.

verses.text: And I put heare cloth my garment, & I became a parable to them.
They ſpake aganſt me <na>(n)</na> that ſat in the gate; and they ſoong aganſt me that dranke wine.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The great men and iudges, alſo the drunkards and raſcalitie of the people.

verses.text: But I, <na>(o)</na> my prayer to thee ô Lord: a time of thy good pleaſure ô God. <na>(p)</na> In the multitude of thy mercie heare me, in the truth of thy ſaluation:

notes.label: o
notes.text: But I direct my prayer to thee.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Expecting the time of thy good pleaſure.

verses.text: Deliuer me out of the myre, that I ſtick not faſt: deliuer me from them that hate me, and from the depthes of <na>(q)</na> waters.

notes.label: q
notes.text: tribulations.

verses.text: Let not the tempeſt of water drowne me, nor the depth ſwallowe me: <na>(r)</na> neyther let the pit shut his mouth vpon me.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Though Chriſt died and vvas buried, and in ſoule deſcended into hel, yet he could not be holden in his ſepulchre, nor in limbo, but roſe againe.

verses.text: Heare me ô Lord becauſe thy mercie is benigne: according to the multitude of thy commiſerations haue reſpect to me.
And turne not away thy face from thy ſeruant: becauſe I am in tribulation, heare me ſpeedily.
Attend to my ſoule and, deliuer it: <na>(s)</na> becauſe of mine enimies deliuer me.

notes.label: s
notes.text: That they may either be conuerted, or confounded, and ſo do no more hurt.

verses.text: Thou knoweſt my reproch, & my confuſion, & my shame.

In thy ſight are al they that afflict me, my hart hath looked for reproch and miſerie. And I expected ſome bodie that would be ſorie together with me, and there <na>(t)</na> was none: and that would confort me, and I founde not.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Not anie that could mitigate our Sauiours affliction, vvould shew compaſſion tovvards him.

verses.text: And they gaue <na>(v)</na> gal for my meate: & in my thirſt they gaue me vinegre to drinke.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Mat. 27. Ioan. 19. · But contrariwiſe when he complained of thirſt, they gaue him gal and vinegre to drinke.

verses.text: <na>(w)</na> Let their table be made a ſnare before them, & for retributions, and for a ſcandal. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: w
notes.text: Rom. 11. · A prophecie of the deſtruction of the Iewes, at the time of Paſch, when they ſhould thinke to eate their paſchal lamb with ioy.

verses.text: Let <na>(x)</na> Their eies be darkned that they ſee not: and make <na>(y)</na> their backe crooked alwaies.

notes.label: x
notes.text: They are alſo blinde in hart, that they wil not ſee the truth of Chriſts doctrine:

notes.label: y
notes.text: but bow themſelues to earthlie thinges, and vvorldlie gaines euen to this day.

verses.text: Poure out thy wrath vpon them: and let the furie of thy wrath ouertake them.
Let their habitation be made deſert: and in their tabernacles let there be none to dwel. <cr>[1]</cr>
Becauſe <na>(z)</na> whom thou haſt ſtriken, they haue perſecuted: and vpon the ſorrow of my wounds they haue added.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Chriſt, vvhom God of this mercie deſigned to ſuffer death, for redemption of mankind, the Iewes of mere enuie and malice perſecuted to death.

verses.text: Adde thou <na>(a)</na> iniquitie vpon their iniquitie: and let them not enter into thy iuſtice.

notes.label: a
notes.text: A prophecie that God would ſuffer them, to fal from one iniquitie to an other.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Let them be put out of the booke of the liuing: and with the iuſt let them not be written.

notes.label: b
notes.text: In the end of their liues, they shal not be found in the booke of life, where they ſuppoſe themſelues to be written.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> I am poore and ſorowful: <na>(d)</na> thy ſaluation ô God hath receiued me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The voice of Chriſt, humbling himſelfe to death, euen to death of the Croſſe:

notes.label: d
notes.text: from which he roſe againe.

verses.text: I wil praiſe the name of God with canticle: and wil magnifie him in prayſe.
And <na>(e)</na> it shal pleaſe God more then a young calfe: that bringeth forth hornes and hoofes.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Deuout praiſe and thankeſgeuing pleaſe God more then ſacrifices of the moſt tender calues, which were othervviſe alſo gratful ſacrifices.

verses.text: Let the poore ſee and reioyce: ſeeke ye God, and your ſoule shal liue.
Becauſe our Lord hath heard the poore: and he hath not deſpiſed <na>(f)</na> his priſoners.

notes.label: f
notes.text: God doth aſſuredly comfort al ſuch, as are impriſoned for profeſſing the truth.

verses.text: Let <na>(g)</na> the heauens and earth praiſe him, the ſea, and al the creeping beaſtes in them.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Al the creatures of God.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Becauſe God wil ſaue Sion: and <na>(i)</na> the cities of Iuda shal be built vp. And they shal inhabite there, & by inheritance they shal get it.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God wil alwayes eſtablish and protect the Catholique Church:

notes.label: i
notes.text: and particular Churches, members of the vniuerſal ſhal alſo proſper.

verses.text: And <na>(k)</na> the ſeede of his ſeruants shal poſſeſſe it, and they that loue his name shal dwel in it.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Perpetual ſucceſſion of the Catholique Church.

chapters.summary: Chriſt in middes of afflictions (as one in dangerous waters) 5. deſcribing the malice of perſecutors, and his owne true zele, 14. prayeth his heauenlie Father for helpe. 23. By way of iuſt imprecation, forsheweth the ſeuere punishment of his aduerſaries, 30. his owne glorious Reſurrection, and proſperous building of his Church. For which he inuiteth al creatures to praiſe God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt's afflictions and victory.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, a Pſalme of Dauid, in remembrance, that our <na>(b)</na> Lord ſaued him.

notes.label: a
notes.text: An apt prayer alſo for the afflicted in the new Teſtament,

notes.label: b
notes.text: from the danger of Abſolom. (2. Reg. 18.) or from anie perſecutor.

verses.text: O God <na>(c)</na> intend vnto my helpe: Lord <na>(d)</na> make haſt to helpe me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Al men at al times nede Gods helpe:

notes.label: d
notes.text: but moſt preſent nede, in preſent dangers. The reſt of this Pſalme is conteyned in the 39. Pſalme, from the 15. verſe. but there the whole Church prayeth for helpe, the world being almoſt drowned in ſinnes; here Dauid, or other particular perſons, or peoples pray in their ſeueral diſtreſſes,

verses.text: Let them be confounded, and be ashamed, that ſeeke my ſoule. <cr>[1]</cr>
Let them be turned away backeward, and be ashamed that wil me euils. Let them be turned away forthwith ashamed, that ſay to me: Wel, wel.
Let al that ſeeke thee reioyce, and be glad in thee, and let them ſay alwayes: Our Lord be magnified: which loue thy ſaluation.
But I am needie and poore: ô God helpe me thou art my helper, and deliuerer: ô Lord be not ſlacke.

chapters.summary: An other prayer of Dauid, when he was perſecuted by Abſolom : made in a Pſalme after his deliuerie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David's prayer in perſecution.
The 8. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme <na>(a)</na> for Dauid, <na>(b)</na> of the ſonnes of Ionadab, and <na>(c)</na> the former captiues. IN thee ô Lord <na>(d)</na> I haue hoped, let me not be confounded for euer:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Though this Pſalme (as alſo diuers others) is intitled to, or for Dauid, it proueth not that ſome other was the author therof, but the Seuentie Interpreters inſinuate hereby, that it perteyneth in more particular ſorte to Dauid, growing old;

notes.label: b
notes.text: they adde alſo the ſonnes of Ionadab a moſt holie familie,

notes.label: c
notes.text: who for their ſingular pietie, were ſuffered to remaine in Ieruſalem, in the firſt captiuitie. Ierem. 35.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The wordes of Dauid, or anie faithful iuſt perſon.

verses.text: in <na>(e)</na> thy iuſtice deliuer me, and receiue me. Incline thine eare to me, and ſaue me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God of his iuſtice reuengeth the iniuries done to his ſeruantes.

verses.text: Be vnto me for a God protector, and for a fenſed place: that thou maiſt ſaue me: Becauſe thou art my firmament, and my refuge.
My God deliuer me out of the hand of the ſinner, and out of the hand of him that doth aganſt the law, and of the vniuſt.
Becauſe thou art <na>(f)</na> my patience ô Lord: ô Lord my hope from my youth.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Through thy grace I haue patience to expect thy pleaſure, when I shal be releeued.

verses.text: Vpon thee haue I bene confirmed from the wombe: from my mothers bellie thou art my protector. In thee is my ſinging alwaies:
I was made to manie as <na>(g)</na> a wonder: and thou art a ſtrong helper.

notes.label: g
notes.text: It ſemeth ſtrange to moſt men, why the iuſt haue more trubles then the wicked.

verses.text: Let my mouth be filled with praiſe, that I may ſing thy glorie: <na>(h)</na> al the day thy greatnes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: A neceſſarie prayer for perſeuerance, which none can haue without ſpecial and continual helpe of grace.

verses.text: Reiect me not in the time of olde age: <na>(i)</na> when my ſtrength shal faile, forſake me not.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Againſt this ſpecial danger, and laſt aſſaultes of the enimie, Chriſt hath inſtituted the Sacrament of Extreme Vnction.

verses.text: Becauſe mine enimies haue ſaid to me: and they that watched my ſoule, conſulted together,
Saying: God hath forſaken him, purſew, and take him: becauſe there is none to deliuer.
O God be not farre from me: my God haue reſpect to mine ayde.
Let them be confounded, and fayle that detract from my ſoule: let them be couered with confuſion, and shame, that ſeeke euils to me.
But I wil alwaies hope: and <na>(k)</na> wil adde vpon al thy praiſe.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The beſt meanes to conſerue vertue, is to exerciſe the ſame, adding good workes towardes our neighbours, and praiſes to God.

verses.text: My mouth shal shew forth thy iuſtice: al the day thy ſaluation. Becauſe <na>(l)</na> I haue not knowne lerning, <na>(m)</na> I wil enter into the <na>(n)</na> powres of our Lord:

notes.label: l
notes.text: I profeſſe not exact knowlege of natural thinges;

notes.label: m
notes.text: but I conſider and contemplate the infinite powre of God, which appeareth in his workes,

notes.label: n
notes.text: and his iuſt iudgements, as partly haue appeared in puniſhing, and rewarding ſome in this life, but eſpecially wil be manifeſt in the end of this world.

verses.text: ô Lord I wil be mindful of thy iuſtice onely.
O God thou haſt taught me from my youth: and vntil now I wil pronounce thy meruelous workes.
And vnto ancient age, and olde age: ô God forſake me not? Vntil I shew forth thy arme to al the generation, that is to come. Thy might,
and thy iuſtice ô God euen to the higheſt, great meruailes which thou haſt done: ô God who may be like to thee?
How great tribulations haſt thou shewed me, manie and euil: and turning thou <na>(o)</na> haſt quickened me: and from the depthes of the earth thou haſt brought me backe againe.

notes.label: o
notes.text: After tribulations recreated me.

verses.text: Thou haſt multiplied thy magnificence: and being turned thou haſt comforted me.
For I alſo wil confeſſe to thee in the inſtruments of Pſalme thy truth: ô God I wil ſing to thee on the harpe, holie one of Iſrael.
My <na>(p)</na> lippes shal reioyce when I shal ſing to thee; and my ſoule, which thou haſt redemed.

notes.label: p
notes.text: I wil praiſe thee with mouth and hart.

verses.text: Yea and my tongue al the day shal meditate thy iuſtice: when they shal be confounded and ashamed that ſeeke euils to me.

chapters.summary: King Dauid, or anie other iuſt perſon, prayeth God to continew his grace, and protection againſt the malice of the enimie. 5. Recounteth Gods mercie in deliuering him from falling into tentations. 6. prayeth for the ſame in old age, or weakenes of bodie and ſpirite, 20. and promiſeth perpetual gratitude and praiſes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer for perſeverance in virtue.
The 7. key.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Concerning Salomon.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Pſalme is of Chriſt, perfigured by Salomon, whoſe kingdom was moſt glorious of al the kinges of Gods people; for of king Salomon himſelfe manie thinges in this Pſalme can not be truly vnderſtood. S. Aug.

verses.text: O God giue thy iudgement to <na>(b)</na> the king: and thy iuſtice to <na>(c)</na> the ſonne of the king. To iudge thy people in <na>(d)</na> iuſtice, and thy poore in iudgement.

notes.label: b
notes.text: O God moſt bleſſed Trinitie, geue powre and authoritie, to the Sonne of Man, God incarnate, King of al kinges,

notes.label: c
notes.text: the Sonne of king Dauid, to iudge for mankind againſt the diuel.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Chriſt paying ranſom for al mankind, and ſo man renouncing the diuel, and ſeruing God iuſtly, not iniuriouſly deliuered from captiuitie of ſinne, and of the diuel.

verses.text: Let <na>(e)</na> the mountains receiue peace for the people: and <na>(f)</na> the litle hilles iuſtice.

notes.label: e
notes.text: A prophecie of the Apoſtles receiuing powre to preach Chriſts Goſpel, of peace and reconciliation of men to God by penance;

notes.label: f
notes.text: and of other Apoſtolical men that folow their ſteppes.

verses.text: He <na>(g)</na> shal iudge the poore of the people, and shal ſaue the children of the poore: and he shal humble the calumniator.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Salomon in figure of Chriſt was for a time a iuſt and good king.

verses.text: And he shal <na>(h)</na> continew with the ſunne, and before the moone in generation and generation.

notes.label: h
notes.text: But only Chriſt, not Salomon, nor anie other king of that people, contineweth, or reigneth for euer.

verses.text: He <na>(i)</na> shal deſcend as rayne vpon a fleece: and as droppes diſtilling vpon the earth.

notes.label: i
notes.text: The maner of Chriſts incarnation moſt ſilent, ſweete, and gratful.

verses.text: There shal riſe in his dayes iuſtice, and aboundance of peace, <na>(k)</na> vntil the moone be taken away.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Agane the prophet inculcateth that Chriſts kingdom, his Church, shal continew for euer.

verses.text: And he shal rule <na>(l)</na> from ſea vnto ſea: and from the riuer euen to the ends of the round world.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The Church is not only vniuerſal in al times, but alſo in places.

verses.text: Before him shal the Æthiopians fal downe: and his enimies shal lick the earth. <cr>[1]</cr>
The <na>(m)</na> kinges of Tharſis, and <na>(n)</na> the Ilands shal offer preſentes: the kings of the Arabians, and of Sabá shal bring giftes. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: m
notes.text: The three Sages or Kinges, which adored our Sauiour, and offered gold, frankencenſe, and myrrh, were the firſt that fulfilled this prophecie : and afterwards Conſtantin the great, and other Emperors, Kinges, and Princes.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Amongſt other Ilandes great Bryttannie (the greateſt of Europe) was conuerted to Chriſt, according to this prophecie : firſt ſome few in the Apoſtles time (Metaphraſtes apud Surium, Theodoret, epiſt. ad Timoth. Sophronius, Ser. de Nat. Apoſt, & alij.) More in the time of Eleutherius. Laſtly our Engliſe nation by S. Auguſtin and others ſent by S. Gregorie.

verses.text: And al kinges of the earth shal adore him: al nations shal ſerue him.
Becauſe he shal deliuer the poore from the mightie: and the poore which had no helper.
He shal ſpare the poore and needy: and he shal ſaue the ſoules of the poore.
From vſuries and iniquitie he shal redeme their ſoules: and their name shal be honorable before him.
And <na>[1]</na> he shal liue, and there shal be giuen him of the gold of Arabia, and they shal adore it alwaies: al the day they shal bleſſe him.

notes.text: How is this prophecie verified, except the Church be alwayes viſible?

verses.text: And there shal be a firmament in the earth, in the toppes of mountanes, the fruite therof shal be extolled farre aboue Libanus: and they shal florish of the citie, as the graſſe of the earth.
Be his name bleſſed for euer: before the ſunne his name is permanent. And al the tribes of the earth shal be bleſſed in him: al nations shal magnifie him.
Bleſſed be our Lord the God of Iſrael, <na>(o)</na> who only doth meruelous thinges.

notes.label: o
notes.text: No miracles can be donne but by Gods powre.

verses.text: And bleſſed be the name of his maieſtie for euer: and al the earth shal be filled with his maieſtie. <na>(p)</na> Be it, be it.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Aboue al other deſires the holie prophet wiſhed Gods glorie, and praiſes in al the earth, as it is in heauen.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> The praiſes of Dauid, <na>(r)</na> the ſonne of Ieſſe are ended.

notes.label: q
notes.text: It ſemeth by this appendix added by Eſdras, that this Pſalme was laſt compoſed, though not put in the laſt place, but as it came to his handes.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Dauid the natural ſonne of Ieſſe, made no more Hymnes, that is, no more muſical praiſes of God after this Pſalme, but the prefigured Dauid Chriſt our Sauiour, the Sonne of God, in his bodie the Church, ſingeth ſtil new praiſes. S. Aug. in enarrat. Pſal. ſequentis. 72.

chapters.summary: By way of prayer the Pſalmiſt prophecieth Chriſts coming, our King and Iudge: 4. the deliuerer of mankind from the thraldom of the diuel. 8. the greatnes of his ſpiritual kingdom in the Gentiles. 16. and his continual glorie and praiſe. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt our King & Judge.
The 5. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme <na>(a)</na> to Aſaph. HOw <na>(b)</na> good is God to Iſrael, to them, that are of a right hart! <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: To be ſongue by Aſaph the maſter of muſike, and his companie.

notes.label: b
notes.text: God is ſo excellent good, as no tongue can expreſſe, no hart can conceiue.

verses.text: But <na>(c)</na> my feete were almoſt moued, my ſteppes almoſt ſlipped.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The peace and proſperitie of the wicked tempted me, to leaue the right narrow way, and to goe the brode eaſie way with them.

verses.text: Becauſe I haue had zele vpon the wicked, ſeing the peace of ſinners.
Becauſe there is <na>(d)</na> no reſpect to their death: and <na>(e)</na> ſtabilitie in ther plague.

notes.label: d
notes.text: They neuer thincke of death;

notes.label: e
notes.text: and if they ſuffer ſome affliction, they quickly remoue it from them.

verses.text: In <na>(f)</na> the labours of men they are not, and with men they shal not be ſcourged.

notes.label: f
notes.text: They trauel not ſo much as good men do, neither are they ſo often punished.

verses.text: Therfore <na>(g)</na> hath pride helde them, they are couered with their iniquitie and impietie.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Which maketh them proud, and ſo they runne into al ſortes of iniquitie.

verses.text: Their iniquitie hath proceded as it were of fatte: they haue paſſed into <na>(h)</na> the affection of the hart.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Whatſoeuer miſchief came in their mind, they feared not to committe it in fact.

verses.text: They haue thought, and haue ſpoken wickednes they haue ſpoken iniquitie <na>(i)</na> on high.

notes.label: i
notes.text: boldly extolling their owne wordes and workes, and deſpiſing others.

verses.text: They haue ſette their mouth vnto heauen: ãd their tongue hath paſſed in the earth.
Therfore wil my people <na>(k)</na> returne here: and <na>(l)</na> ful daies shal be found in them.

notes.label: k
notes.text: For this proſperitie of the wicked, ſome of Gods people wil fall from the right way,

notes.label: l
notes.text: and their dayes wil abound with calamities.

verses.text: And they haue ſaide: <na>(m)</na> How doth God know, and is there knowledge in the higheſt?

notes.label: m
notes.text: The voice of the weake, inclining to diffidence, and doubt of Gods knowlege, and prouidence.

verses.text: Loe the ſinners them ſelues, and they that abounde in the world, haue obtained riches.
And I ſaide: Then haue I iuſtified my hart without cauſe, and haue washed my handes amongſt innocentes:
And haue bene ſcourged al the day, and my chaſtiſing in the morninges.
If I ſaide: I wil ſpeake this: behold <na>(n)</na> I reproued the nation of thy children.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The prophet in his owne perſon anſwereth, that if he ſhould ſay ſuch thinges, he ſhould reproue Gods children, as faultie, vnworthie of his protection, and to be neglected; wheras it is Gods prouidence to chaſtice his children whom he loueth.

verses.text: I <na>(o)</na> thought to know this thing, it is labour before me:

notes.label: o
notes.text: In this life we can not know the particular cauſes, why the iuſt are afflicted, and manie wicked proſper in this world.

verses.text: Vntil I may enter into the ſanctuarie of God: and may vnderſtand concerning their latter endes.
But yet <na>(p)</na> for guiles thou haſt put it to them: thou haſt caſt them downe whiles they <na>(q)</na> were eleuated.

notes.label: p
notes.text: But only in general we are taught, that euils are prepared for the guiles, or deceptes,

notes.label: q
notes.text: pride, and other ſinnes of the wicked.

verses.text: How are they brought into deſolation, they haue failed ſodanely: they haue perished for their iniquitie.
As the dreame of them that riſe ô Lord, in thy citie thou shalt bring their <na>(r)</na> image to nothing.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Not real but imaginarie felicitie.

verses.text: Becauſe my hart is <na>(s)</na> inflamed, and my reynes are changed:

notes.label: s
notes.text: Almoſt burned vp with afflictions.

verses.text: And I am brought to nothing, and knew not.
As <na>(t)</na> a beaſt am I become with thee: and I <na>(v)</na> alwaies with thee.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Charged with heauie burdens, without knowlege how long, or to what end,

notes.label: v
notes.text: yet not deſtitute of thy protection.

verses.text: Thou haſt helde my right hand: and in thy wil thou haſt conducted me, and with glorie thou haſt receiued me.
For what is to me <na>(w)</na> in heauen? and beſides thee what would I vpon the earth?

notes.label: w
notes.text: Nothing to be deſired in heauen, nor in earth but God.

verses.text: My <na>(x)</na> flesh hath fainted, and my hart: God of my hart, and God my portion for euer.

notes.label: x
notes.text: In bodie and mind I thirſt after thee, my true inheritance.

verses.text: For behold, they <na>(y)</na> that make them ſelues farre from thee, shal perish: thou <na>(z)</na> haſt deſtroyed al, that fornicate from thee.

notes.label: y
notes.text: Men by their freewil make themſelues enimies to God.

notes.label: z
notes.text: determined their damnation, forſeing their final ſinnes.

verses.text: But it is good for me to cleaue to God: to put my hope in our Lord God: That I may shew forth al thy prayſes, in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet, firſt profeſſing the vnſpeakable goodnes of God, 2. in the perſon of the weake complaineth, that the wicked proſper, and the iuſt are afflicted. 15. reprehendeth the murmuration, for though we can not comprehend the ſecrete iudgements of God. 18. yet they are moſt iuſt. 25. So with deſire to reſt in God, he promiſeth euer to praiſe him. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Affliction in this world is recompenſed in the end.
The 9. key.

verses.text: Vnderſtanding <na>(a)</na> to Aſaph. WHy haſt thou ô God <na>(b)</na> repelled for euer: is thy furie wrath vpon the sheepe of thy paſture?

notes.label: a
notes.text: Inſtruction for the congregation of the faithful in diſtreſſe, not to ſeeke temporal rewardes and proſperitie, but to expect ſpiritual and eternal. S. Aug.

notes.label: b
notes.text: In long perſecution the weake beginne to feare, or ſuſpect, that God hath vtterly abandoned them.

verses.text: Be <na>(c)</na> mindful of thy congregation, <na>(d)</na> which thou haſt poſſeſſed from the beginning. Thou haſt <na>(e)</na> redemed the rod of thine inheritance: mount Sion, in which thou haſt dwelt.

notes.label: c
notes.text: But the ſtronger pray with confidence,

notes.label: d
notes.text: being aſſured that God who hath conſerued his Church hitherto, from the beginning of the world, wil conſerue it ſtil to the end.

notes.label: e
notes.text: An other reaſon why God wil conſerue his Church is, becauſe he hath deliuered it often in a ſtrong armie; as from bondage in Ægypt, from perſecution and oppreſſion in the time of Iudges, and kings, and laſtly redemed it from the tyrannie of the diuel by Chriſts death.

verses.text: Lift vp thy handes vpon <na>(f)</na> their prides for euer: how great things hath the enimie done malignantly in the holy place:

notes.label: f
notes.text: Thirdly the pride of the enimies moueth God to reuenge their wickednes, and ſo to deliuer his owne people.

verses.text: And they that hate thee haue gloried: in the middes of <na>(g)</na> thy ſolemnitie. They haue ſette <na>(h)</na> their ſignes, for ſignes:

notes.label: g
notes.text: They pretend to kepe ſolemne feaſtes like to thyne.

notes.label: h
notes.text: They ſet vp altares againſt thyn altares, or ſome new deuiſed external shew, againſt the holie Rites of the Church :

verses.text: and haue not knowne, <na>(i)</na> as in the iſſue on high. As <na>(k)</na> in a wood of trees they haue with axes

notes.label: i
notes.text: and that in publike places, in the endes of high wayes, or portes, and pinnacles.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The prophet deſcribeth the maner how perſecutors deſtroy temples, and al ſacred thinges.

verses.text: cut out the gates therof together: in hatchet, and chippeaxe they haue caſt it downe.
They haue burnt thy ſanctuarie with fire: they haue polluted the tabernacle of thy name in the earth.
Their <na>(l)</na> kinred together haue ſaide in their hart: Let vs make al the feſtiual daies of God to ceaſe from the earth.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The whole crew, or band of perſecutors.

verses.text: Our <na>(m)</na> ſignes we haue not ſeene, there is now no prophet: and he wil know vs no more.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The weake complaine that God ſheweth not wonted ſignes, nor ſendeth ſuccourſe to his people, by raiſing ſome prophet, or other meanes to helpe them.

verses.text: How long ô God shal the enimie vpbraide: the aduerſarie prouoke thy name for euer?
Why doeſt thou turne away thy hand, and thy right hand, out of the middes of thy boſome for euer?
But <na>(n)</na> God our king before the worldes: he hath wrought ſaluation in the middes of the earth. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: n
notes.text: The perfect do anſwer, that God both hath, and wil releeue his people.

verses.text: Thou in thy ſtrength haſt confirmed <na>(o)</na> the ſea: thou haſt <na>(p)</na> crushed the head of Dragons in the waters.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Made the redde ſea like walles.

notes.label: p
notes.text: drowned Pharao and his hoſte.

verses.text: Thou haſt broken the heads of the dragon: thou haſt giuen him for meate to the peoples <na>(q)</na> of the Æthiopians.

notes.label: q
notes.text: of blacke diuels.

verses.text: Thou haſt <na>(r)</na> broken vp fountaines, and torrentes: thou haſt dried the riuers <na>(s)</na> of Ethan.

notes.label: r
notes.text: geuen water out of rockes,

notes.label: s
notes.text: made paſſage ouer Iordan.

verses.text: The day is thine, and the night is thine: thou haſt made the morning and the ſunne.
Thou haſt made al the coaſtes of the earth: the ſummer and the ſpring thou haſt formed them.
Be mindeful of this, the enimie hath vpbraided our Lord: and a foolish people hath prouoked thy name.
Deliuer not to beaſts the ſoules that confeſſe to thee: and the ſoules of thy poore forget not for euer.
Haue reſpect vnto thy teſtament: becauſe they that are <na>(t)</na> obſcure of the earth, are filled with houſes of iniquities.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Ignorant, blind, and barbarous infidels, lodge al kindes of iniquitie in their conſciences.

verses.text: <na>(v)</na> Let not the humble be turned away being confounded: the poore and needy shal praiſe thy name.

notes.label: v
notes.text: And therfore it is vnmeete, that faithful people should be in bondage vnder them.

verses.text: Ariſe God, iudge thy cauſe: be mindful of thoſe thy reproches, that are <na>(w)</na> from the foolish man al the day.

notes.label: w
notes.text: Theſe foolish audacious men do continually blaſpheme al holie thinges.

verses.text: <na>(x)</na> Forget not the voices of thine enimies: the <na>(y)</na> pride of them that hate thee, hath aſcended alwaies.

notes.label: x
notes.text: Omitte not to punish them,

notes.label: y
notes.text: ſeing they are obſtinate and obdurate in pride, and in hatred.

chapters.summary: Faithful people preſſed with perſecution lamentably complayning, beſecheth God to reſpect his owne inheritance, cruelly afflicted; 10. and leift long without helpe, 12. wheras heretofore he releeued his people in like diſtreſſes. 18. And therfore confidently hopeth he wil renenge the blaſphemers of his name, <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer in long affliction.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, <na>(a)</na> Corrupt not, a Pſalme of Canticle to Aſaph.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Either this was the beginning of a ſongue, to the tune wherof this Pſalme was ſong; as ſome Hebrew Rabbins teſtifie; or, as S. Auguſtin and other fathers explicate, the Septuagint do admonish vs, by occaſion of this Pſalme, not to faile in our hope, for that God wil in no caſe violate his promiſe nor purpoſe, but wil render to euerie one in the day of Iudgement, as they deſerue.

verses.text: We <na>(b)</na> wil confeſſe to thee ô God: <na>(c)</na> we wil confeſſe, and wil inuocate thy name. We wil tel thy meruelouſe workes:

notes.label: b
notes.text: Chriſt with his Apoſtles, and other aſſeſſorie iudges, wil praiſe and thanke God, for his admirable good prouidence, and gouernement of this world.

notes.label: c
notes.text: This duplication of the ſame word, confirmeth vs of the aſſured performance of that, which is here prophecied.

verses.text: when <na>(d)</na> I shal take a time, I wil iudge iuſtices.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Chriſt our ſingular, principal, and proper Iudge only, and no mere creature, knoweth the determinate time of general iudgement.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> The earth is melted, and al that dwel in it: <na>(f)</na> I haue confirmed the pillers thereof.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The earth at that time ſhal be purged with flaming fire :

notes.label: f
notes.text: yet shal not be deſtroyed, but changed in qualities.

verses.text: I ſaid to the wicked: <na>(g)</na> doe not wickedly: and to them that offend: <na>(h)</na> Exalt not the horne.

notes.label: g
notes.text: An epitome, or briefe ſumme of Chriſts doctrine, to flee from ſinne.

notes.label: h
notes.text: be not proud, abuſe not the powre you haue, to do what you pleaſe.

verses.text: Exalt not your horne on high: ſpeake not iniquitie aganſt God.
For neither from the Eaſt, nor from the Weſt, nor from the deſert mountanes:
<na>(i)</na> becauſe God is Iudge. <na>(k)</na> This man he humbleth, and him he exalteth,

notes.label: i
notes.text: VVhen other Iudges ſitte on tribunales, ſome may be abſent, or eſcape from their ſentences : but al without exception ſhal be brought in perſons, when Chriſt God and Man ſhal iudge.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Some ſhal haue ſentence of eternal paine in hel; ſome of eternal reward in glorie,

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> becauſe there is a cuppe in the hand of our Lord <na>(m)</na> of mere wine ful of mixture. And he hath powred it out <na>(n)</na> of this into that, but yet the dregges therof are not emptied: al the ſinners of the earth shal drinke.

notes.label: l
notes.text: though (partly in this world, partly in particular iudgement of euerie ſoule) God hath alreadie, and wil before the laſt day puniſh ſinners, yet there reſteth more puniſhment, and no impenitent ſinners ſhal eſcape, but al ſhal drinke of the bitter cuppe of eternal damnation.

notes.label: m
notes.text: ſtrong wine not delayde with water, but mingled with bitter ſharpe thinges, as gal, vinegre, brimſtone &c. and ſo powred into feſtered woundes, ſo they shal ſuffer vntolerable endles paine, mixed with the worme of conſcience, loſſe of glorie, rancor of hart, and eternal deſperation.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Varietie of hellish torments, from one extreme to another : as from ſnowwaters to exceeding heate. Iob. 24.

verses.text: But I wil shewforth for euer: I wil ſing to the God of Iacob.
And I wil breake al the hornes of ſinners: and <na>(o)</na> the hornes of the iuſt shal be exalted.

notes.label: o
notes.text: The iuſt for wel vſing their powre of freewil, and of al powre geuen them in this life, are rewarded in heauen.

chapters.summary: Chriſt (with his Aſſeſſors) wil iudge the whole world, at the laſt day: in the meane time exhorteth ſinners to amend their life; 7. for none shal eſcape iuſt iudgement. 11. The wicked shal be punished, and the good rewarded. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
General iudgement.
The 9. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, in prayſes, a Pſalme <na>(a)</na> to Aſaph, a Canticle to <na>(b)</na> the Aſſirians.

notes.label: a
notes.text: For the congregation of faithful and godlie people.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Amongſt others, one notorious example of Gods prouidence is recorded of an hundred foureſcore & fiue thouſand Aſſirians, ſlaine in one night by an Angel. 4.Reg.19.

verses.text: God is knowne <na>(c)</na> in Iewrie: in Iſrael his name is great.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God was not only knowen in general, as to pagane Philoſophers, and ſome others, but more particularly to the Iewes, the iſſue of Abraham, Iſaac, and Iacob, by his ſpecial benefites towards them.

verses.text: And <na>(d)</na> his place is made in peace: and <na>(e)</na> his habitation in Sion.

notes.label: d
notes.text: God ſuffering al other nations to erre for their ſinnes, in their fond phanteſies of falſe goddes, reſerued the Iſraelites for his Church,

notes.label: e
notes.text: eſtablishing the principalitie therof in Sion.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> There he brake the powres of bowes, the shilde, the ſword, and the battle.

notes.label: f
notes.text: For obtaining and conſeruing of Sion from wicked Infidels, God ouerthrewe al ſortes of contrarie forces.

verses.text: Thou <na>(g)</na> doeſt illuminate meruelouſely from the eternal mountaynes:

notes.label: g
notes.text: God not only gaue his people temporal victories ouer their enimies, but alſo illuminated their mindes with knowlege of true religion:

verses.text: al the foolish of hart <na>(h)</na> were trubled. They <na>(i)</na> ſlept their ſleepe: and al the men of riches found nothing in their handes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: others are often trubled in mind, hearing the truth, but are not conuerted through their obſtinate follie.

notes.label: i
notes.text: VVorldlie men in ſupine careleſnes as in a ſleepe, paſſe ouer this life, and afterwards find themſelues excluded from heauen, for lacke of merites, and good workes, with the foolish virgins.

verses.text: At <na>(k)</na> thy reprehenſion ô God of Iacob, they <na>(l)</na> haue al ſlumbered that mounted on horſes.

notes.label: k
notes.text: God vndertaking the defence of his people, and threatning the aduerſe part,

notes.label: l
notes.text: they failed in courage, as men ouercome with drowſines of ſleepe.

verses.text: Thou art terrible, and who shal reſiſt thee? <na>(m)</na> from that time thy wrath.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Euen from the firſt notice of thy wil, the aduerſaries were deiected, fearing thy potent wrath.

verses.text: From <na>(n)</na> heauen thou <na>[1]</na> haſt made thy iudgement hearde: <na>(o)</na> the earth trembled and was quiet.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Terrible ſignes from the firmament appearing before the day of iudgement,

notes.label: o
notes.text: perſecutors and others being terrified ſhal be aſtonied and ſilent.
The Prophetes do often ſpeake in the preter-tence, for the aſſurance of the thinges to come.

verses.text: When God aroſe vnto iudgement, <na>(p)</na> that he might ſaue al the meeke of the earth.

notes.label: p
notes.text: God wil come to iudge the vvorld, more eſpecially for the iuſts ſake.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(q)</na> the cogitation of man shal confeſſe to thee: and <na>(r)</na> the remanes of the cogitation shal keepe feſtiual day to thee.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Men that ſhal ſeriouſly thinke and meditate vpon theſe thinges, vvil praiſe and thanke God for them:

notes.label: r
notes.text: and the effect, and ſweete repaſt of ſuch meditation, shal make as it vvere a great feſtiual day, in the deuout ſoule ſpiritually ioyned with God.

verses.text: <na>(s)</na> Vowe ye, and <na>(t)</na> render to our Lord your God: al ye that round about him bring <na>(v)</na> giftes.

notes.label: s
notes.text: The ſoule thus inflamed with Gods loue, is then apt of gratitude, for his goodnes tovvardes man, to make vowes of thinges wherto vve are not obliged,

notes.label: t
notes.text: but moſt neceſſarie it is to be maturely aduiſed, and not raſhly, nor lightly to vow; for being once vovved, vve are ſtrictly bound to whatſoeuer vve haue lavvfully promiſed. And it is great ſinne to vow vndiſcretly.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Remembring that for vovves, and al other workes we muſt anſwer to God, who is a terrible iudge, readie to punish in bodie and ſoule, ſparing none for their greatnes, not princes, nor kinges, nor vulgar ſorte, for al are to him alike.

verses.text: To vthe terrible, and him that taketh away the ſpirite of princes, terrible to the kinges of the earth.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet ſingeth Gods praiſes, for his particular prouidence towards the Iewes: 10. further to be extended to al the meeke of the whole earth. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence towards his people.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for <na>(a)</na> Idithun, a pſalme <na>(b)</na> to Aſaph.

notes.label: a
notes.text: For Idithun to ſing, or to make tune for it.

notes.label: b
notes.text: For the faithful congregation to conſider Gods benefites.

verses.text: With <na>(c)</na> my voice I haue cried to our Lord: with my voice to God <na>(d)</na> and he attended to me. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: c
notes.text: Hauing heretofore prayed,

notes.label: d
notes.text: I haue obtayned.

verses.text: In the day of my tribulation I ſought God, with my handes <na>(e)</na> in the night before him: and I <na>(f)</na> was not deceiued. My <na>(g)</na> ſoule refuſed to be comforted,

notes.label: e
notes.text: Eſpecially being in tribulation, and praying vvith hart and handes lifted vp, as vvel in the night as day:

notes.label: f
notes.text: I was not fruſtrate of my prayer.

notes.label: g
notes.text: I was ſometimes in ſuch anguish that nothing ſemed comfortable,
