verses.text: I <na>(h)</na> was mindeful of God, and was delighted, and was exerciſed: and <na>(i)</na> my ſpirite fainted.

notes.label: h
notes.text: but I relied vpon God ſo firmly,

notes.label: i
notes.text: that my ſpirite came into an extaſie, or traunce.

verses.text: Myne eies <na>(k)</na> preuented the watches: I was <na>(l)</na> trubled, & ſpake not.

notes.label: k
notes.text: I aroſe early before the ordinarie time of avvayking,

notes.label: l
notes.text: my hart being attentiue inwardly, I vttered nothing vvith my tongue.

verses.text: I thought vpon old daies: and the eternal yeares I had in minde.
And I meditated in the night with my hart, and I was exerciſed, and I <na>(m)</na> ſwept my ſpirite.

notes.label: m
notes.text: I diligently examined my conſcience.

verses.text: Why, <na>(n)</na> wil God reiect for euer: or wil he not adde to be better pleaſed as yet?

notes.label: n
notes.text: Aſſuredly God wil not reiect for euer, but he wil be pleaſed with his Church.

verses.text: Or wil he cutte of his mercie for euer, from generation vnto generation?
Or wil God forget to haue mercie? or wil he in his wrath keepe in his mercies?
And I ſayde: <na>(o)</na> Now haue I begune: <na>(p)</na> this is the change of the right hand of the Higheſt.

notes.label: o
notes.text: VVhiles I thus thought, I erred greatly, novv I ſee and confeſſe that God ſuffereth al calamities for the good of his ſeruantes:

notes.label: p
notes.text: and this I knew not by my ſelfe, but by the inſpiration of God, making this change in me by his gracious hand.

verses.text: I haue bene mindful of the workes of our Lord: becauſe I wil be mindful, from the beginning of thy meruelous workes.
And I wil meditate in al thy workes: and in thy inuentions I wil be exerciſed.
O God in the holie is thy way: what God is great as our God?
thou art the God that doeſt meruelous thinges. Thou haſt made thy powre knowne among peoples:
thou haſt with thine arme redemed thy people, the children of <na>(q)</na> Iacob, and Ioſeph.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The progenie of Iacob, receiued and nourished in Ægypt for Ioſephs ſake, as his adopted children.

verses.text: The waters <na>(r)</na> ſaw thee ô God, the waters ſaw thee: and they were afrayd, and the depthes were trubled.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The read ſea, and Iordan felt thy diuine powre, and obeyed thy wil.

verses.text: A <na>(s)</na> multitude of the ſounding of waters: the cloudes gaue a voice. For in deede arrowes doe paſſe:

notes.label: s
notes.text: Noiſe of vvaters meeting after the Iſraelites vvere paſſed, thunders and lightninges alſo hapened, to the terror of the perſecutors, though not mentioned in Exodus.

verses.text: the voice of thy thunder in a wheele. Thy lightenings shined to the rounde world: the earth was moued and trubled.
Thy way in the ſea, and thy pathes in many waters: and thy ſteppes shal not be knowne. <cr>[1]</cr>
Thou haſt conducted thy people as sheepe: <na>(t)</na> in the hand of moyſes and Aaron.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Exo. 14 · By the miniſterie of Moyſes and Aaron.

chapters.summary: Anie faithful deuout perſon meditating Gods benefites, 7. examineth his cõſcience, that nothing be in his ſoule, that may offend God. Who is alwayes readie to forgeue: 11. and therfore he ſtil reneweth his purpoſe to ſerue God ſincerly, 15. particularly remembring the deliuerie of Iſrael from Ægypt. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Gods ſpecial protection of the Iewes. the 4. key.

verses.text: Vnderſtanding <na>(a)</na> to Aſaph. MY people attend ye to <na>(b)</na> my law: incline your eare vnto the wordes of my mouth.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Commended to Aſaph a chiefe muſitian, that the people might vnderſtand and conſider Gods benefites.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Neither the law, nor the people vvas Dauids, but preſenting Gods perſon, he ſpeaketh in his name or authoritie, with whoſe inſpiration he was repleniſhed. S. Greg. Præfat. in Iob. c. 2.

verses.text: I wil open my mouth in <na>(c)</na> parables: I wil ſpeake <na>(d)</na> propoſitions from the beginning.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Albeit the prophet reciteth hiſtorically thinges donne, yet the ſame were parables, ſimilitudes, and figures of other thinges:

notes.label: d
notes.text: yea of ſecret hidden Myſteries, obſcurly ſignified in the old Teſtament, and reueled in the new.

verses.text: How great thinges haue we heard and <na>(e)</na> haue knowne them, and <na>(f)</na> our fathers haue told vs.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Which partly we know by written holie Sriptures:

notes.label: f
notes.text: partly by Traditions.

verses.text: They were not hid from their children, in an other generation. Telling the prayſes of our Lord, and his powers, and his meruelous workes which he hath done.
And he <na>(g)</na> raiſed vp a teſtimonie in Iacob: and <na>(h)</na> made a law in Iſrael. How great thinges he commanded our fathers, <na>(i)</na> to make

notes.label: g
notes.text: God of his mercie without precedent merite, raiſed vp a peculiar people of Abraham, Iſaac, and Iacob,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and gaue them a particular law, firſt of Circunciſion, & more largely by Moyſes.

notes.label: i
notes.text: So Abraham inſtructed his children and his houſe after him, Gen. 18.

verses.text: the ſame knowne to their children: that <na>(k)</na> an other generation may know. The children that shal be borne, and shal riſe vp, and shal tel their children.

notes.label: k
notes.text: in like ſorte others taught their children.

verses.text: That they may <na>(l)</na> put their hope in God, and may <na>(m)</na> not forget the workes of God: and may <na>(n)</na> ſeeke after his commandmentes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: For three cauſes God gaue his law, that his people may haue confidence in him, he shewing his care to inſtruct and gouerne them;

notes.label: m
notes.text: that they remember his benefites;

notes.label: n
notes.text: and kepe his commandmentes.

verses.text: That they become not as their fathers: <na>(o)</na> a peruerſe generation and exaſperating. A generation, that hath not directed their hart, their ſpirit hath not bene faithful towards God. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: o
notes.text: The Iewish nation very often, and in great numbers murmured, rebelled, and committed other great ſinnes, and therfore Dauid exhorted the people of his time, not to do the like. And this exhortation perteyneth more eſpecially to Chriſtianes. as S. Paul teacheth. 1. Cor. 10.

verses.text: The <na>(p)</na> children of Ephrem bending, and shooting with bow: were turned in the day of battel.

notes.label: p
notes.text: They firſt (truſting in their owne ſtrength) without Gods commandment (Num. 14.) went forth to batle and were ouerthrowne. 1. Par 7. v. 11.

verses.text: They kept not the teſtament of God: and in his law they would not walke.
And they forgate his benefites, and his meruelous workes, which he shewed them.
Before their fathers he did meruelous thinges in the land of Ægypt, in the filde <na>(q)</na> of Tanis.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Tanis the principal citie in Ægypt nere the riuer Nilus, where Moyſes wrought his great miracles.

verses.text: He diuided the ſea & brought them through: and he made the waters to ſtand as in a bottle. <cr>[1]</cr>
And he <na>(r)</na> conducted them in a cloude by day: and al the night by light of fire.

notes.label: r
notes.text: This cloude shadowed them from the heate of the ſunne in the day, and the fire ſhined in the night, al the time that they were in the deſert.

verses.text: He ſtroke the rocke in <na>(s)</na> the deſert: and gaue them water to drinke as in a great depth.

notes.label: s
notes.text: In mount Horeb: and there was continual water in al the campe, which occupied nere foure miles in length and breadth.

verses.text: And he brought forth water out of the rocke: and made waters runne downe as riuers.
And they added as yet to ſinne vnto him: they prouoked the Higheſt to wrath in the place <na>(t)</na> without water.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Which naturally wanted water: but by miracle had abundance.

verses.text: And they tempted God in their hartes: ſo that they asked <na>(v)</na> meats for their liues.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Not content with Manna, they demanded to haue flesh.

verses.text: And they ſpake euil of God: they ſaide: Can God prepare a table in the deſert?
Becauſe he ſtroke the rocke and waters ranne, & torrentes flowed: <na>(w)</na> Can he alſo giue <na>(x)</na> bread, or prepare a table for his people?

notes.label: w
notes.text: Stil incredulous, not beleuing Gods omnipotencie, they thought that, albeit he had geuen them manna, and water, yet he could not geue them fleſh.

notes.label: x
notes.text: By bread in general is vnderſtood al competent meate vſual for a table.

verses.text: Therfore our Lord heard, and <na>(y)</na> made delay: and <na>(z)</na> fire was kindled in Iacob, and wrath aſcended vpon Iſrael.

notes.label: y
notes.text: For this incredulitie, murmuring, and other ſinnes God kept the children of Iſrael fourtie yares in the deſert, til al that were of age, when they came from Ægypt, were dead, except only Ioſue and Caleb.

notes.label: z
notes.text: In the meane time amongſt other puniſhments, manie murmurers were burnt to death with ſtrange fire. Num. 11.

verses.text: Becauſe they beleued not in God, nor hoped in his ſaluation.
And he commanded the cloudes from aboue, and opened the gates of heauen.
And he rayned them Manna to eate, and bread of heauen he gaue to them.
Bread <na>(a)</na> of Angels did man eate: he ſent them victuals in abundance.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Manna made by Angels.

verses.text: He <na>(b)</na> tranſported the Southwinde from heauen: and in his powre he brought in the Southweſt winde.

notes.label: b
notes.text: God ſo changed the wind, that it brought abundance of quailes and other birdes, into their campe. Exo. 16. Nu. 11.

verses.text: And he rayned vpon them flesh as duſt: and as the ſand of the ſea fethered fowles.
And they fel in the middes of their campe: about their tabernacles.
And they did eate and were filled excedingly, and their deſire he brought to them:
They were not defrauded of their deſire. <na>(c)</na> As yet their meats were in their mouth:

notes.label: c
notes.text: Immediatly after a moneth (for ſo long they had abundance of theſe birdes ibid. v. 20,) they were ſtriken with a plague, and manie died, for their concupiſcence.

verses.text: And the wrath of God aſcended vpon them. And he killed their fat ones, and <na>(d)</na> the choſen of Iſrael he hindered.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The moſt fresh ſtrong men died, and ſo were hindered from poſſeſſing the promiſed land of Chanaan.

verses.text: In al theſe things they ſinned as yet: and they beleued not in his meruelous workes.
And their daies failed in vanitie: and their years <na>(e)</na> in haſt.

notes.label: e
notes.text: In fourtie yeares aboue ſix hundred thouſand died.

verses.text: When he ſlew them, they ſought him: and they returned, and <na>(f)</na> early they came to him.

notes.label: f
notes.text: They offered morning ſacrifice.

verses.text: And they remembred that God is their helper: and the high God is their redemer.
And they loued him <na>(g)</na> with their mouth, and with their tongue they did lie to him.

notes.label: g
notes.text: But were not ſincere in their hartes.

verses.text: But their hart was not right with him: neither were they counted faithful in his teſtament.
<na>(h)</na> But he is merciful, and wil be propicious to their ſinnes: and he wil not deſtroy them. And he abunded to turne away his wrath: and he kindled not al his wrath.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Howſoeuer multitudes of people committe great ſinnes, and are ſeuerely puniſhed, yet Gods mercie preſerueth ſome by his effectual grace, and neuer ſuffereth the whole Church to faile, nor to be deſtroyed.

verses.text: And he remembred that they are flesh: <na>(i)</na> ſpirit going, and not returning.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Mans life is like the winde, that ſtil paſſeth, and the ſame returneth not. As Ariſtotel teacheth. Here the Hebrewes note the middes of the Pſalter, in 1263. verſes. and ſo manie in the reſt.

verses.text: How <na>(k)</na> often haue they exaſperated him in the deſert: prouoked him to wrath in the place without water.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The people of Iſrael murmured ſo often in the deſert, that it was not eaſie to tel how often. See the Annotation.

verses.text: And <na>(l)</na> they returned, and tempted God: and the holie one of Iſrael they exaſperaed.

notes.label: l
notes.text: For efſoones repenting they offended God againe and againe.

verses.text: They did not remember his hand: in the day that he redemed them from the hand of the afflicter.
As he put <na>(m)</na> his ſignes in Ægypt, and his wonders in the filde of Tanis.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The firſt ſigne was in turning a rodde into a ſerpent, which was a miracle, but no plague, the other ſignes were alſo plagnes to the Ægyptians.

verses.text: And he turned <na>(n)</na> their riuers into bloude, & their <na>(o)</na> showers that they might not drinke.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The firſt plague.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Pooles, lakes, and al ſortes of water, yea showers, or raine water, which ſeldome happeneth in Ægypt.

verses.text: He ſent vpon them <na>(p)</na> a ſwarme of flies, and it eate them: and <na>(q)</na> the frogge, and it deſtroyed them. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: p
notes.text: The fourth plague, in order as they are recited in Exodus.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The ſecond plague.
* Coenomyiam.

verses.text: And he gaue their fruites to <na>(r)</na> the blaſt, and their labors to <na>(s)</na> the locuſte.

notes.label: r
notes.text: This was ∷ leſſe plague, not mentioned in with the greater.

notes.label: s
notes.text: The eight plague.

verses.text: And he killed their vineyeardes with <na>(t)</na> haile: and their mulberie trees with <na>(v)</na> horefroſt.

notes.label: t
notes.text: The ſeuenth plague.

notes.label: v
notes.text: This alſo is omitted in. · Exodus.

verses.text: And he deliuered <na>(w)</na> their beaſt to haile: and their poſſeſſion <na>(x)</na> to fire.

notes.label: w
notes.text: Not only al trees, and plantes, but alſo beaſtes were ſubiect to the haile.

notes.label: x
notes.text: and to firie leghtnings.

verses.text: He ſent vpon them <na>(y)</na> the wrath of his indignation: indignation, & wrath, and tribulation: immiſſions <na>(z)</na> by euil angels.

notes.label: y
notes.text: In theſe general termes, of wrath, indignation, and tribulation, the Prophet comprehendeth al the other plagues, to witte, the third of ſcinies, the fifth of peſtilence, the ſixt of boyles in men and beaſtes, the ninth of darknes three dayes together.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Al which God ſent by the miniſterie of diuels, euil angels.

verses.text: He made a way to the path of his wrath, he ſpared not their liues from death: and their cattel he shut vp in death.
And <na>(a)</na> he ſtroke al the firſtborne in the land of Ægypt: the firſt fruites of al their labors in the tabernacles <na>(b)</na> of Cham.

notes.label: a
notes.text: a The tenth and greateſt plague, 11. v. 5. & c. 12. v. 29.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Egyptians alſo deſcended from cham, by his ſonne Meſraim. Gen. 10. v. 6.

verses.text: And he <na>(c)</na> tooke away his people as sheepe: and led them as a flock in the deſert.

notes.label: c
notes.text: After that Ægypt was thus plagued, God brought Iſrael out of their ſeruitude, as a shepheard leddeth his sheepe, and defendeth them.

verses.text: And he brought them forth in hope, and they feared not: and the ſea couered their enemies.

And he brought them into <na>(d)</na> the mount of his <na>(e)</na> ſanctification, the mount, which his right hand purchaſed. And he caſt <na>(f)</na> out the gentiles from their face: and by lot he diuided the land of them in a corde of diſtribution:

notes.label: d
notes.text: Iudea a hillie countrie.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Into that countrie which God choſe, and endewed with manie bleſſinges.

notes.label: f
notes.text: As is written in Ioſue.

verses.text: And he made the tribes of Iſrael to dwel in their tabernacles.
And <na>(g)</na> they tempted, and exaſperated God the higheſt, and they kept not his teſtimonies.

notes.label: g
notes.text: After the conqueſt and quiet poſſeſſion, the Iſraelites often fel into groſſe ſinnes, eſpecially in the time of Iudges.

verses.text: And they turned away themſelues, & kept not the couenant: euen as their fathers, they were turned as a <na>(h)</na> crooked bow.

notes.label: h
notes.text: A croked bow deceiueth the archer, ſo this people failed to ſerue God, and deceiued themſelues.

verses.text: They incenſed him to wrath in their <na>(i)</na> hilles: and in their <na>[1]</na> grauens they prouoked him <na>(k)</na> to emulation.

notes.label: i
notes.text: In their altares erected in hilles to Idoles.

notes.label: k
notes.text: By grauen imagies of Idoles, they prouoked God to indignation.
* Sculptilibus.

verses.text: God heard, and contemned: and he brought Iſrael to nothing <na>(l)</na> excedingly.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Not abſolutely to nothing, but punished them exceedingly, til they repented, and then ſpared and deliuered them from tribulation, as appeareth in the booke of Iudges.

verses.text: And he reiected the tabernacle <na>(m)</na> of Silo, his tabernacle, <na>(n)</na> where he dwelt among men.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The Arke of God ſometime kept in Silo, Ioſue 18. in the tribe of Ephraim, was taken by the Philiſtims. 1. Keg. 4. and neuer returned thither agane.

notes.label: n
notes.text: but wherſoeuer the Arke was, there God more eſpecially heard their petitions, and gaue anſwers.

verses.text: And he deliuered <na>(o)</na> their force into captiuitie: and their beautie into the hands of the enemie.

notes.label: o
notes.text: For their ſinnes God ſuffered the Arke to be taken.

verses.text: And he <na>(p)</na> shut vp his people in the ſword: and he diſpiſed his inheritance.

notes.label: p
notes.text: And the Iſraelites to be ſore afflicted by their enimies.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> Fyre deuoured their young men: and their virgins were not lamented.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The zele, and iuſt wrath of God ſuffered theſe calamities to happen.

verses.text: Their <na>(r)</na> Prieſtes fel by the ſworde: and their widowes were not wept for.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Ophni and Phinees the ſonnes of Heli ſlaine and Heli himſelfe hearing that the Arke was taken fel from his ſtoole and broke his neck. 1. Reg 4.

verses.text: And <na>(s)</na> our Lord was raiſed vp as one that ſleepeth: as a mightie man hauing ſurfited of wine.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Neuertheles God plagued the infidels, and conſerued his Church. 1. Reg. 5.

verses.text: And he ſtroke his enimies on the hinder partes: an euerlaſting reproch he gaue to them.
And he reiected the tabernacle <na>(t)</na> of Ioſeph: and the tribe of Ephraim he choſe not.

notes.label: t
notes.text: As before. v. 60.

verses.text: But he choſe the tribe <na>(v)</na> of Iuda, mount Sion which he loued.

notes.label: v
notes.text: After a time the Arke was brought into the tribe of Iuda.

verses.text: And he built <na>(w)</na> his ſanctuarie as of vnicornes in the land, which he hath founded for euer.

notes.label: w
notes.text: The Church was firme, and euer preſerued in the old teſtament til Chriſt, and from Chriſts time to the end of the world.

verses.text: And <na>(x)</na> he choſe Dauid his ſeruant, and tooke him from the flockes of sheepe: from after the ewes with yong he tooke him.

notes.label: x
notes.text: Gods particular grace in chooſing, and exalting Dauid, was a ſpecial benefite to the Iſraelites.

verses.text: To <na>(y)</na> feede Iacob his ſeruant, and Iſrael his inheritance.

notes.label: y
notes.text: To rule and gouerne the people of Iſrael.

verses.text: And he fedde them in the innocencie of his hart: and in the vnderſtandings of <na>(z)</na> his hands he conducted them.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Prudently vſing his powre and authoritie.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet exhorting the people to attend, 5. reciteth manie great benefites of God towards their forefathers (whoſe ingratitude, often rebellion, and chatiſement he ſtil noteth) 9. 11 in their entrance into the land of Chanaan: 12. alſo before the ſame in Ægypt, and in the deſert. 42. How God plagued the Ægyptians: 52. protected, and conducted his people into the promiſed land. 56. where likewise they often offended, were punished: 65. yet were ſtil conſerued: 69. and the tribe of Iuda exalted in king Dauid. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God'ſ great Benefits beſtowed upon the Jews, and their ingratitude.
The 4. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme <na>(a)</na> to Aſaph. O God <na>(b)</na> the Gentiles are come into thine inheritance, they <na>(c)</na> haue polluted thy holie temple: they haue made Ieruſalem <na>(d)</na> as a watch toure of fruits.

notes.label: a
notes.text: to be ſungue by Aſaph and his companie, in the behalfe of people vnited in faith.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Cruel infidels haue inuaded thoſe thinges, which perteyne to thy Church:

notes.label: c
notes.text: euen poſſeſſed and prophaned the holie temple of the Iewes, and Churches of Catholique Chriſtians. Fulfilled by Antiochus, in Ieruſalem; by the Vandals in Afrike, by Proteſtants, and Puritanes, in diuers partes of Europe, and wil be more vniuerſally by Antichriſt in al Chriſtendom.

notes.label: d
notes.text: In ſteed of great and faire Churches, Gods ſeruantes are fane to vſe meane houſes, yea poore cotages.

verses.text: They haue made <na>(e)</na> the carcaſes of thy ſeruants, meats for the foules of the aire: the flesh of thy ſainctes for the beaſtes of the land.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Some perſecutors ſuffer not Martyrs bodies to be buried, but hang them on polles, and pinnacles, where birdes may eate them.

verses.text: They haue poured out their bloude as water round about Ieruſalem: and there was none to burie them.
We are <na>(f)</na> become a reproch to our neighboures: a ſcorne and mocke to them that are round about vs.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Chriſtianes Gallileans, Catholiques Homouſians, and now Papiſtes, in ſpite and reproch.

verses.text: How long ô Lord wilt thou <na>(g)</na> be angrie for euer: shal thy zele be kindled as a fire?

notes.label: g
notes.text: Sinnes prouoking Gods wrath, are one cauſe why he ſuffereth his people to be perſecuted.

verses.text: Poure out thy wrath vpon the Gentiles, <na>(h)</na> that haue not knowne thee: & vpon the kingdomes, that haue not inuocated thy name.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Though the faithful committe ſome ſinnes, yet in reſpect that they beleue righly, haue zele in Gods cauſe, and denie not God, they are nerer to grace and fauour.

verses.text: Becauſe they haue deuoured Iacob: and his place they haue made deſolate.
<na>(i)</na> Remember not our old iniquities, let thy mercies quickly preuent vs: becauſe we are become exceding <na>(k)</na> poore.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Eſpecially when they repent, and confeſſe their ſinnes, then thoſe that neither know nor wil know God; but obſtinatly impugne and reſiſt the truth,

notes.label: k
notes.text: ſo much afflicted, and deſpiſed, that none wil regard the truth which we profeſſe.

verses.text: Help vs ô God our ſauiour: and for the glorie of thy name ô Lord deliuer vs: and be propicious to our ſinnes for thy names ſake.

Leſt they ſay perhaps amongſt the Gentiles: <na>(l)</na> where is their God? and <na>(m)</na> be notified in the nations before our eies. The reuenge of the bloud of thy ſeruants, which hath benne shed:

notes.label: l
notes.text: Albeit ô Lord, thou ſuffer vs to be puniſhed, yet ſuffer not thyn enimies to inſult, as though thou were not our God; and conſequently thou haddeſt no people at al in the world.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Therfore we pray, that the reuenge of thy ſeruantes bloud may be ſo notified, that it can not be denied, nor doubted of. Which is alſo here propheſied, that it wil ſo come to paſſe in the end.

verses.text: let the groning of the fettered enter in thy ſight. According to the greatnes of thine arme, poſſeſſe thou <na>(n)</na> the children of them that are put to death.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Preſerue alſo, ô God, the reliques of thy ſeruantes, the ſucceſſors of thy Martyrs.

verses.text: And <na>(o)</na> tender to our neighboures ſeuenfold in their boſome: their reproch wherewith they haue reproched thee ô Lord.

notes.label: o
notes.text: This alſo is a propheſie, that God wil moſt ſeuerely reuenge the blaſphemie of perſecutors.

verses.text: But <na>(p)</na> we thy people, and the sheepe of thy paſture, wil confeſſe to thee for euer: Vnto generation and generation we wil shew forth thy praiſe.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Gods people deliuered from perſecution, and perpetually conſerued, wil alwayes praiſe God for the ſame.

chapters.summary: The Prophet, in perſon of the Church, lamenteth the crueltie of perſecutors (both in the old and new teſtament) 5. prayeth for releaſe, with iuſt reuenge againſt Gods enimies, that blaſpheme his name, 3. and promiſeth to be gratful in diuine praiſes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church ſuffereth very great perſecutions.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, for <na>(b)</na> them, that shal be changed, teſtimonie to <na>(c)</na> Aſaph, a Pſalme.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the new Teſtament,

notes.label: b
notes.text: eſpecially to Gentiles, that shal be conuerted to Chriſt.

notes.label: c
notes.text: for perpetual memorie to the congregation of faithful.

verses.text: Thou that ruleſt Iſrael, attend: that <na>(d)</na> conducteſt Ioſeph as a sheepe. Which ſitteſt vpon the cherubs <na>(e)</na> be manifeſt <na>(f)</na>

notes.label: d
notes.text: By Ioſeph the prophet vnderſtandeth al Iſrael; becauſe the firſt birthright being taken from Ruben was geuen to him, to witte duble portion of enheritance, two tribes of twelue.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Appeare, and shew thy mightie hand before thy people:

notes.label: f
notes.text: wherof Ephraim, Beniamin, and Manaſſes folowing the Arke, when they marched or camped, ſhould moſt directly ſee what appeared therin, the other nine tribes being placed before it, and on both ſides. Num. 2.

verses.text: before Ephraim, Beniamin, and Manaſses. Raiſe vp <na>(g)</na> thy might, and come, to ſaue vs.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Thou which alwayes can helpe vs, now vſe thy powre in deliuering vs from this temporal miſerie.

verses.text: O God <na>(h)</na> conuert vs: and shew <na>(i)</na> thy face, & we shal be ſaued.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Set vs in a better ſtate.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Shew thy benigne countenance and fauoure, Myſtically, ſend the promiſed Meſſias, Chriſt, the eſſential Image of God. 1. Cor. 4. v. 4. Collos. 1. v. 15.

verses.text: O Lord the God of hoſtes, how long wilt thou be angrie <na>(k)</na> vpon the prayer of thy ſeruant?

notes.label: k
notes.text: How long wilt thou differre to heare our prayer?

verses.text: Thou wilt feede vs with the bread of teares: and giue vs drinke with teares <na>(l)</na> in meſure.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Thou doſt iuſtly punish vs, but thou tempereſt the ſame with meaſure, that it exceede not to our ruines.

verses.text: Thou haſt made vs to be a contradiction to our neighboures and our enimies haue ſcorned vs.
O God of hoſts <na>(m)</na> conuert vs: and shew thy face, and we <na>(n)</na> shal be ſaued.

notes.label: m
notes.text: God firſt preuenting with his grace,

notes.label: n
notes.text: man may cooperate therwith to his iuſtification, and ſaluation.

verses.text: Thou didſt tranſport <na>(o)</na> the vineyeard out of Ægypt: thou didſt caſt out <na>(p)</na> the Gentiles, and plantedſt it.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Thy Church and people,

notes.label: p
notes.text: the Chananites.

verses.text: Thou waſt the guide of the way <na>(q)</na> in the ſight therof: thou didſt plant the rootes therof, and it <na>(r)</na> filled the earth.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The cloude, and piller of fire were viſible guides.

notes.label: r
notes.text: and it multiplied mightely.

verses.text: <na>(s)</na> The shadow of it couered the mountanes: and the bowghes of it the ceders of God.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Hyperbolical ſpeach to ſignifie the great multiplication of the Iſraelites.

verses.text: It extended her branches euen to <na>(t)</na> the ſea; and her boughes vnto <na>(v)</na> the riuer.

notes.label: t
notes.text: from the mediterranean ſea of Paleſtin,

notes.label: v
notes.text: to the riuer Euphrates. Exo. 23. v. 31. Deut. 11. v. 24.

verses.text: Why haſt thou deſtroyed the hedge therof: and al that paſſe by the way doe plucke it.
The <na>(w)</na> boare of the wood hath deſtroyed it: and <na>(x)</na> the ſingular wilde beeſt hath eaten it.

notes.label: w
notes.text: cruel enimies more like to moſt cruel beaſtes then to men.

notes.label: x
notes.text: yea ſo cruel, as none els in the world are like vnto them.

verses.text: O God of hoaſts returne: regard <na>(y)</na> from heauen, and ſee, and viſite this vineyeard.

notes.label: y
notes.text: The Prophet now prayeth for the coming of Chriſt, which he ſaw in ſpirite.

verses.text: And <na>(z)</na> perfite it, which thy right hand hath planted: and vpon <na>(a)</na> the ſonne of man whom thou haſt confirmed to thee.

notes.label: z
notes.text: The Church of the old teſtament, in her beſt ſtate, wanted the perfection, which the Church of Chriſt hath.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Chriſt our Meſſias moſt commonly calleth by this title: The Sonne of man.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Thinges burnt with fyre, and digged doune at the increpation of thy countenance shal perish.

notes.label: b
notes.text: So thy vinyard can not indure if it be ſtil afflicted, and trodden downe.

verses.text: Let <na>(c)</na> thy hand be vpon the man of thy right hand: and vpon the ſonne of man, whom thou haſt confirmed to thee.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Chriſt working by Gods powre redreſſeth al miſeries.

verses.text: And we depart not from thee, thou wilt quicken vs: and we wil inuocate thy name.
<na>(d)</na> O Lord the God of hoaſtes conuert vs: and shew thy face, and we shal be ſaued.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The ſame is the 8. and the 15 verſe (with litle alteration) and here repeted the third time, In which we alſo pray for three thinges firſt to be purged, and conuerted from ſinne, ſecond to be illuminated by Chriſt, the Image of God, Thirdly to be ſanctified, and ſaued in eternal glorie to haue the fruition of the moſt bleſſed Trinitie.

chapters.summary: The Prophet prayeth for the releaſe of Iſrael in great tribulation. 15. forsheweth the coming of Chriſt to redeme man from ſinne, and from thraldome of the diuel. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt our Redeemer from ſin and captivity.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, for <na>(b)</na> wine preſſes, a Pſalme to <na>(c)</na> Aſaph him ſelfe.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Pſalme perteyneth not only to the old teſtament, but alſo to the new,

notes.label: b
notes.text: Gods ſeruants oppreſſed with tribulations,

notes.label: c
notes.text: to be ſongue by Aſaph a chief maſter of muſike.

verses.text: Reioice to God our helper: make Iubilation to the God of Iacob.
Take ye Pſalme, and <na>(d)</na> giue timbrel: pleaſant Pſalter with the harpe.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Make readie al theſe muſical inſtruments.

verses.text: Sound ye with trumpet in <na>(e)</na> the <na>[1]</na> new moone, in <na>(f)</na> the <na>[2]</na> notable day of your ſolemnitie.

notes.label: e
notes.text: In the Calendes, or firſt day of euerie moneth, in remembrance of Gods prouidence, and perpetual gouernment of al creatures:

notes.label: f
notes.text: and moſt eſpecial ſolemnitie in the firſt day of the ſeuenth moneth, in memorie of Iſaac conſerued from death, in whom God promiſed Abraham, to multiplie his ſeede, and to bleſſe al nations. Gen. 17. v. 21. c. 21. v. 12. c. 22. v. 18.
The feaſt of Neomenia.
Feaſt of trumpetes.

verses.text: Becauſe it is a precept in Iſrael, and iudgement to the God of Iacob.
He put it for a teſtimonie in <na>(g)</na> Ioſeph, when he came out of the Land of Ægypt: he heard a tongue which he knew not.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The people of Iſrael ſignified by Ioſeph, as Pſal. 79. v. 2.

verses.text: He <na>[1]</na> turned away his backe <na>(h)</na> from burdens: his handes ſerued in baskettes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God deliuered the ſame people from their vntolerable bondage of carying burdens in baskettes, from geathering ſtraw, making brickes, and other ſeruitude. Exo. 1. v. 14. c. 5. v. 7.
In memorie of this benefite Paſch was inſtituted.

verses.text: In <na>(i)</na> tribulation thou dideſt inuocate me, and I heard thee: I heard thee in the ſecret of the tempeſt: I <na>(k)</na> proued thee at the water of contradiction.

notes.label: i
notes.text: The admonition of God to the people:

notes.label: k
notes.text: yet after ſo great benefites thou dideſt murmure, and contradict me. Exo. 17. Num. 20.

verses.text: Heare ô my people: and I <na>(l)</na> wil conteſt thee: Iſrael <na>(m)</na> if thou wilt heare me.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Seriouſly admonish thee.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Man by free wil may chooſe whether he wil obey or no.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> There shal be <na>(n)</na> no new God in thee, neither shalt thou adore a ſtrange God.

notes.label: n
notes.text: This was an other great benefite, to geue an expreſſe law, for their inſtruction.
The feaſt of Pentecoſt in memorie of the lawe.

verses.text: For I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Ægypt: <na>(o)</na> dilate thy mouth and I wil fil it.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Obſeruing my commandments, aske what thou wilt, and I wil geue it thee.

verses.text: And my People heard not my voice: and Iſrael attended not to me.
And I let them alone, according to the deſires of their hart, they shal goe in their owne inuentions. <cr>[1]</cr>
If my people had heard me: if Iſrael had walked in my wayes:
I had <na>(p)</na> for nothing, <na>(q)</na> perhaps humbled their enimies: and had laide my hand vpon thoſe that afflict them.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Very eaſely.

notes.label: q
notes.text: of my freewil and liberalitie, without neceſſitie or obligation.

verses.text: The enimies of our Lord haue lied to him: and <na>(r)</na> their time shal be for euer.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The wicked that promiſe to ſerue God, and do it not shal be in eternal torments:

verses.text: And <na>(s)</na> he fedde them of the fatte of corne: and out of the rocke, with honie he filled them.

notes.label: s
notes.text: In the meane time God beſtowed theſe benefites vpon them, for the iuſts ſake.

chapters.summary: Al men are inuited to celebrate feſtiual dayes, 6. which were inſtituted in memorie of benefites receiued. 9. the deuont shal be protected, and the negligent leift in diſtreſſe. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Invitation to celebrate feſtival days devoutly.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme to Aſaph. God ſtood in the aſſemblie <na>(a)</na> of goddes, and in the middes he <na>(b)</na> iudgeth goddes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The wordes of the prophet, admoniſhing al magiſtrates, that when they ſitte in iudgement, or determine anie cauſe, God who is there, and euerie where preſent,

notes.label: b
notes.text: attendeth their proceſſe: and therfore it behoueth them to be aduiſed what they doe: euen as if they heard God ſpeaking as here foloweth:

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> How long iudge ye iniquitie: and accept ye the perſons of ſinners.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The wordes of God, though not vttered ſenſibly, yet in effect intimated by his law, according:· wherto he wil procede in iudgement againſt vniuſt Iudges.

verses.text: Iudge ye for the needie and the pupil: iuſtifie ye the humble, and the poore.
Take away the poore: and deliuer the needie from the hand of the ſinner.
They <na>(d)</na> knew not, neither did they vnderſtand, they walke in darkeneſſe: <na>(e)</na> al the fundations of the earth shal be moued.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Such iudges procede in groſſe ignorance, not caring to vnderſtand, but content to walke in darknes.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Ye are ſo euil diſpoſed, that you would turne al vpſide downe, iuſtifying the wicked, and condemning the iuſt.

verses.text: I ſaide: Yow are <na>(f)</na> goddes, and the ſonnes of the higheſt al.

notes.label: f
notes.text: For your office which you participate of me, you are certaine goddes vpon earth:

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> But you shal die as men: and fal <na>(h)</na> as one of the princes. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: g
notes.text: But when you die you shal find that you are men, ſubiect to Gods iudgement.

notes.label: h
notes.text: yea your punishment wil be greuous, and importable: for the mightie shal mightely ſuffer torments. sap.

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> Ariſe ô God, iudge the earth: <na>(k)</na> becauſe thou shalt inherite in al the Gentiles.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Againe the wordes of the prophet praying God,

notes.label: k
notes.text: that eing he is Lord of al he wil iudge al.

chapters.summary: The Prophet declareth, 2. that God reprehendeth vniuſt Iudges and Magiſtrates: premonisheth them of his ſeuere & eternal punishment: 8. Wherto the prophet conforming his wil prayeth for the ſame. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Admonition to Magiſtrates.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Canticle of Pſalme to Aſaph.
O God <na>(a)</na> who shal be like to thee? <na>(b)</na> hold not thy peace, <na>(c)</na> neither be thou appeaſed ô God:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Seing none is like to thee ô God,

notes.label: b
notes.text: shew thy powre and maieſtie,

notes.label: c
notes.text: be not ſilent.

verses.text: For behold <na>(d)</na> thine enimies haue made a ſound: they that hate thee, <na>(e)</na> haue lifted vp the head.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The cruel perſecuters are moſt inſolent,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and proud.

verses.text: They haue taken malignant counſel vpon thy people: and they haue deuiſed againſt thy ſaincts.
They haue ſaide: Come, and let vs deſtroy them out of <na>(f)</na> the nation: and let <na>(g)</na> the name of Iſrael be remembred no more.

notes.label: f
notes.text: That there be no more anie faithful people,

notes.label: g
notes.text: anie Catholiques left aliue.

verses.text: Becauſe they haue deuiſed with one conſent: they haue together made a couenant againſt thee.
The tabernacles of <na>(h)</na> the Idumeians, and <na>(i)</na> the Iſmahelites <na>(k)</na> Moab, and <na>(l)</na> the Agarens.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The progenie of Eſau,

notes.label: i
notes.text: the ſeede of Iſmael.

notes.label: k
notes.text: deſcending from the elder ſonne of Lot.

notes.label: l
notes.text: the iſſue of Abraham by Agar, who falſly cal themſelues Saraſcens, as if they were of Sara.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> Gebal, and <na>(n)</na> Ammon, and <na>(o)</na> Amalec: <na>(p)</na> the foreners, with <na>(q)</na> the inhabitantes of Tyre.

notes.label: m
notes.text: People of Gebal à citie of Syria,

notes.label: n
notes.text: of the other ſonne of Lot.

notes.label: o
notes.text: thoſe that firſt oppugned the Iſraelites, after they were parted from Ægypt. Exo. 17.

notes.label: p
notes.text: The Philiſtians,

notes.label: q
notes.text: and Tyrians, al nere neighboures, and ſome of them nere akine to the Iſraelites, were their great enimies.

verses.text: Yea and <na>(r)</na> Aſſur alſo is come with them: they are made an aide to the children of Lot.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Others alſo coming further of, ioyned againſt Gods people, in figure that al heretikes, and other infidels conſpire together againſt Catholiques.

verses.text: Doe to them as <na>(s)</na> to Madian, and <na>(t)</na> Siſara: as to <na>(v)</na> Iabin in the torrent Ciſſon.

notes.label: s
notes.text: The Pſalmiſt therfore prayeth (and withal prophecieth) that God wil at laſt deſtroy them, as he did Madian. Num 31. Iudic. 6. & 7.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Siſara captaine general,

notes.label: v
notes.text: for Iabin king of Aſor nere Ciſſon. Iudic. 4. v. 7. & 23.

verses.text: They perished <na>(w)</na> in Endor: they were made as <na>(x)</na> the dung of the earth.

notes.label: w
notes.text: Within the territorie of Manaſſes (Ios. 17.) which they inuaded.

notes.label: x
notes.text: ſlaine and not buried.

verses.text: Put their princes as <na>(y)</na> Oreb, and Zeb, and Zebee, and Salmana.

notes.label: y
notes.text: Theſe foure princes of the Madianites were ſlaine by Gedeons forces Iudic. 7. & 8.

verses.text: Al their princes: which haue ſaide: Let vs poſſeſſe the Sanctuarie of God for an inheritance.
My God put them <na>(z)</na> as a wheele: and as ſtubble before the face of the winde.

notes.label: z
notes.text: By foure ſimilitudes the prophet deſcribeth the punishment that shal fal vpon perſecuters.

verses.text: Euen as fire that burneth a wood: & as a flame that burneth the mountaines:
So shalt thou purſew them in thy tempeſt: and in thy wrath thou shalt truble them.
Fil their faces with ignominie: and <na>(a)</na> they wil ſeeke thy name, ô Lord.

notes.label: a
notes.text: God by punishing ſeeketh the conuerſion of ſinners, not their eternal death.

verses.text: Let <na>(b)</na> them be ashamed, and trubled for euer and euer: and let them be confounded, and perish.

notes.label: b
notes.text: But ſuch as be ſtil obſtinate, and finally impenitent do perish for euer.

verses.text: And let them know that <na>(c)</na> Lord is thy name, thou onlie the Higheſt in al the earth.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God only the creator of heauen and earth is properly called LORD: VVhoſe eſſential, and incommunicable name is VVHICH IS. Exo. 3. v. 14. & 6. v. 3.

chapters.summary: The Church impugned by al ſortes of enimies 10. prayeth God to confound them, as she hath donne diuers the like, 17. wherby ſome shal be conuerted. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Perſecuters of the Church confounded or converted.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, <na>(a)</na> for wine preſſes, <na>(b)</na> the children of Core, a Pſalme.

notes.label: a
notes.text: For men afflicted in this vale of miſerie.

notes.label: b
notes.text: By the children of Core not being muſitians (but porters in the temple, 1. Par. 26.) S. Auguſtin here and in other titles of Pſalmes, vnderſtandeth the faithful children of Chriſt.

verses.text: How beloued are <na>(c)</na> thy tabernacles ô Lord of hoaſtes!

notes.label: c
notes.text: The glorious manſions in heauen, which God hath prepared for the iuſt.

verses.text: My ſoule coueteth, and <na>(d)</na> fainteth vnto the courtes of our Lord. My hart, and <na>(e)</na> my flesh haue reioyced toward the liuing God.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Vehement deſires do ſometimes depriue vs of external ſenſe.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The mind reioycing in hope, the bodie is alſo recreated, releeued, and reuiued, which before was dulle and heauie.

verses.text: For <na>(f)</na> the ſparow alſo hath found her an houſe: and <na>(g)</na> the turtledoue a neſt for her ſelfe, where she may lay her young ones. Thine <na>(h)</na> altars ô Lord of hoaſtes: my King, and my God.

notes.label: f
notes.text: As ſparowes by natural inſtinct ſeeking habitations, finde houſes to dwel in,

notes.label: g
notes.text: and turtles haue neſtes, wherin to lay their young ones: ſo faithful ſoules ſeeke to dwel in heauen, and in the meane time to lay vp good workes within the Catholique Church; out of which (ſayth S. Auguſtin in this place) how good ſoeuer workes do ſeme (as when paganes, and heretikes feede the hungrie, cloth the naked, receiue ſtrangers into their houſes, viſite the ſicke, comforte priſoners) being not laid in the neſt, conculcabuntur, & conterentur: non ſeruabuntur, non cuſtodientur: they ſhal be trodde vnder foote, they ſhal be bruiſed in peeces: they shal not be conſerued, they ſhal not be kept: but (that ſuch workes may be profitable and be conſerued) they muſt be donne in true faith, in the Catholique faith, in ſocietie of the vnitie of the Church.

notes.label: h
notes.text: VVorkes are good, and rightly laide vp when they are donne in vnitie, and participation of Gods Altares, the moſt proper places of Diuine Seruice, of external Sacrifice in this life, and ſpiritual ſacrifice of perfect praiſes in eternal glorie; where al Sainctes without ceaſing ſing: Holie, holie, holie, Lord God of hoaſtes. Iſaiæ 6. Apoc. 4.

verses.text: Bleſſed are they, that dwel in <na>(i)</na> thy houſe ô Lord: for euer and euer they shal praiſe thee.

notes.label: i
notes.text: The Catholique Church.

verses.text: Bleſſed is the man, whoſe helpe is from thee: he <na>(k)</na> hath diſpoſed aſcenſion in his hart,

notes.label: k
notes.text: The iuſt by Gods grace and helpe, may reſolue to aſcend by ſteppes and degrees, from vertue to vertue (v. 8.) euen to heauen,

verses.text: in <na>(l)</na> the vaile of teares, in the place, which he hath appointed.

notes.label: l
notes.text: though he be now in this vaile of teares, by reaſon of mans ſinne, who otherwiſe was before ſinne in paradiſe, a place of delight.

verses.text: For <na>(m)</na> the lawgeuer shal geue <na>(n)</na> bleſſing, they shal goe <na>(o)</na> from vertue into vertue: <na>(p)</na> the God of goddes shal be ſeene in Sion.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Chriſt our lawgeuer,

notes.label: n
notes.text: geueth abundance of graces,

notes.label: o
notes.text: with continual increaſe.

notes.label: p
notes.text: but our only omnipotent God, is to be ſenne by this effect of his grace, in the Church and not elswhere.

verses.text: Lord God of hoaſtes heare my prayer: receiue with thine eare ô God of Iacob.
Behold ô God our protectour: and <na>(q)</na> looke vpon the face of thy Chriſt.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Agreably to this the Church maketh al her petitions, concluding al prayers; By Chriſt our Lord.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(r)</na> better is one day in thy courtes, aboue thouſands. I haue choſen to be <na>(s)</na> an abiect in the houſe of my God: rather then to dwel <na>(t)</na> in the tabernacles of ſinners.

notes.label: r
notes.text: In reſpect of the future retribution, which euerie one shal receiue according to their deſertes, one day in Gods Church is better then thouſands out of it.

notes.label: s
notes.text: And better to be in the pooreſt ſtate of Catholique Chriſtians,

notes.label: t
notes.text: then in greateſt palaces or hiegheſt dignities amongſt ſinners.

verses.text: Becauſe God <na>(v)</na> loueth mercie and truth: our Lord wil geue <na>(w)</na> grace, <na>(x)</na> and glorie.

notes.label: v
notes.text: The Diuine wiſdom ſo vſeth mercie, and veritie, that neither may preiudice the other:

notes.label: w
notes.text: and ſo geueth grace in this life,

notes.label: x
notes.text: and glorie in the next.

verses.text: He wil not depriue them of good thinges, that <na>(y)</na> walke in innocencie: ô Lord of hoaſtes bleſſed is the man, that hopeth in thee.

notes.label: y
notes.text: Beſides innocencie conſerued without ſinne, there is alſo innocencie after remiſſion of ſinne, of which the prophet here ſpeaketh.

chapters.summary: Deuout perſons feruently deſire eternal glorie, 6. accounting it, in the meane time, a happie ſtate to be in the militant Church, 12. where God firſt geuing grace, wil geue glorie in the triumphant. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Eternal glory.
The 10. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, to the children of Core, a Pſalme.
O Lord thou <na>(a)</na> haſt bleſſed thy land: thou <na>(b)</na> haſt turned away the captiuitie of Iacob.

notes.label: a
notes.text: God beſtowed manie great benefites vpon the people of Iſrael:

notes.label: b
notes.text: he brought them out of the bondage of Ægypt.

verses.text: Thou <na>(c)</na> haſt forgeuen the iniquitie of thy people: thou <na>(d)</na> haſt couered al their ſinnes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Remitted their manifold ſinnes:

notes.label: d
notes.text: pardoned alſo a great part of due punishment.

verses.text: Thou haſt mitigated al thy wrath: thou haſt turned away from the wrath of thine indignation.
<na>(e)</na> Conuert vs ô God our ſauiour: and <na>(f)</na> auert thy wrath from vs.

notes.label: e
notes.text: As thou haſt ſpared thy peculiar people, ſo we beſech thee ô God creator and general Sauiour of al mankind,

notes.label: f
notes.text: mitigate thy wrath towards vs al.

verses.text: Wilt thou be wrath with vs for euer? or wilt thou extend thy wrath from generation vnto generation?
O God thou <na>(g)</na> being turned shalt quicken vs: and thy people <na>(h)</na> shal reioyce in thee.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Til God firſt shew his mercie, ſinners lye dead in guilt of ſinne, but by his grace they are ſturred vp, and quickned:

notes.label: h
notes.text: and ioyfully retutne to God.

verses.text: Shew vs ô Lord thy mercie and giue vs thy ſaluation.

I wil <na>(i)</na> heare what our Lord God wil ſpeake in me: <na>(k)</na> becauſe he wil ſpeake peace vpon his people. And vpon <na>(l)</na> his ſainctes: and vpon them, that are conuerted to the hart.

notes.label: i
notes.text: The wordes of the prophet,

notes.label: k
notes.text: ſignifying that God had reueled vnto him the redemption of mankind.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Not al men are iuſtified, and ſaued, but thoſe that are hartely and ſincerely conuerted.

verses.text: But yet his ſaluation is nigh to them that <na>(m)</na> feare him: that glorie may inhabite in our land.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Though al be not ſaued (becauſe manie wil not cooperate to Gods grace) yet very manie hauing the feare of God, which is the beginning of godlie wiſdom, freely accept of Gods mercie, and ſo the Church is gloriouſly propagated.

verses.text: <na>(n)</na> Mercie and truth haue met each other: <na>(o)</na> iuſtice and peace haue kiſſed.

notes.label: n
notes.text: VVheras Gods mercie would ſaue al, and his truth, or iuſtice requireth that ſinnes be duly punished, by Chriſts Paſſion and death, ſufficient ſatisfaction is offered for al ſinnes, and thoſe that wil be partakers by penance, and conformitie to Gods law, may haue remiſſion,

notes.label: o
notes.text: and ſo iuſtice is obſerued, and peace made betwen God and his ſubiects.

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> Truth is riſen out of the earth: <na>(q)</na> and iuſtice hath looked downe from heauen.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Integritie of conſcience reigneth in good men,

notes.label: q
notes.text: God ſending iuſt meanes from heauen to ſaue them.

verses.text: For <na>(r)</na> our Lord certes wil geue benignitie: and <na>(s)</na> our land shal giue her fruite.

notes.label: r
notes.text: God geueth grace,

notes.label: s
notes.text: and ſo men yeld fruict.

verses.text: <na>(t)</na> Iuſtice shal walke before him: and shal ſet his ſteppes in the way.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Yea they walke in iuſtice, and right path of Gods law.

chapters.summary: With commemoration of Gods former benefites, 5. Chriſts Incarnation is prophecied, 9. bringing peace and ſaluation, 11. mercie and iuſtice concurring together. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Incarnation of Chriſt.
The 5. key.

verses.text: A praier <na>(a)</na> to Dauid him ſelfe. Incline thine eare ô Lord, and <na>(b)</na> heare me: <na>(c)</na> becauſe I am needie and poore.

notes.label: a
notes.text: A forme of prayer for king Dauid, and for anie faithful perſon.

notes.label: b
notes.text: There be ſundrie iuſt cauſes which moue God to heare our prayers:

notes.label: c
notes.text: firſt our neceſſitie requireth Gods helpe.

verses.text: Keepe my ſoule, becauſe <na>(d)</na> I am holie: ſaue thy ſeruant my God, that <na>(e)</na> hopeth in thee.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Secondly becauſe we profeſſe, and promiſe to lead a holie life.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Thirdly, becauſe we truſt and hope in God.

verses.text: Haue mercie on me ô Lord, becauſe I haue cried to thee <na>(f)</na> al the day:

notes.label: f
notes.text: Fourtly, becauſe we perſeuere in prayer.

verses.text: make ioyful the ſoule of thy ſeruant, becauſe to thee ô Lord haue I <na>(g)</na> lifted vp my ſoule.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Fiftly, if we pray with attention of mind.

verses.text: Becauſe thou ô Lord art <na>(h)</na> ſwete, and <na>(i)</na> milde: and <na>(k)</na> of ſo much mercie to al that inuocate thee. <na>(l)</na>

notes.label: h
notes.text: Sixtly becauſe God of his owne nature is benigne, readie to beſtow benefites.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Seuently, he is meeke to remitte offences.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Eighily, he is merciful to mitigate the puniſhment, to thoſe that make recourſe vnto him.

notes.label: l
notes.text: For theſe cauſes we pray as foloweth.

verses.text: Receiue ô Lord my praier with thine eares: and attend to the voice of my petition.
In the day of my tribulation I haue called to thee: becauſe thou haſt heard me.
There is not the like to thee amongſt goddes ô Lord: and there is not according to thy workes.
<na>(m)</na> Al nations whatſoeuer thou haſt made, shal <na>(n)</na> come, and shal adore before thee ô Lord: and they shal <na>(o)</na> glorifie thy name.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Vocation of Gentiles.

notes.label: n
notes.text: They shal come by faith.

notes.label: o
notes.text: and glorifie God by good workes. Mat. 5.v.17.

verses.text: Becauſe thou art great and doing meruelous thinges: thou onlie art God.
Conduct me ô Lord in thy way, and I wil walke in thy truth: let my hart reioyce that it may feare thy name.
I wil <na>(p)</na> confeſſe to thee ô Lord my God with al my hart, and wil glorifie thy name for euer:

notes.label: p
notes.text: Cofeſſion of praiſe.

verses.text: Becauſe thy mercie is great vpon me: and thou haſt deliuered my ſoule out of <na>(q)</na> the lower hel.

notes.label: q
notes.text: From the ſtate of eternal damnation.

verses.text: O God the wicked are riſen vp vpon me, and the ſynagogue of the mightie haue ſought my ſoule: and they haue not ſet thee in their ſight.
And thou ô Lord the God of compaſſion and merciful, patient, and of much mercie, and <na>(r)</na> true.

notes.label: r
notes.text: In performing al promiſes.

verses.text: Haue reſpect to me, and haue mercie on me, <na>(s)</na> giue thine empire to thy ſeruant: and ſaue the ſonne of thy handmaide.

notes.label: s
notes.text: A digreſſion (vſual to prophetes) of Chriſts Empyre and Kingdom the Church, geuen to him, being the ſonne of an immaculate virgin, the handmaide of God.

verses.text: Make with me <na>(t)</na> a ſigne vnto God, that they may ſee which hate me, and may be confounded: <na>(v)</na> becauſe thou ô Lord haſt holpen me.

notes.label: t
notes.text: The chief and principal ſigne of Chriſts, and his Churches glorie, is his Reſurrection, præfigured in Ionas.

notes.label: v
notes.text: VVhereby al enimies are confounded, either to their conuerſion, or to eternal damnation. See 6. Auguſtin.

chapters.summary: In conſideration of his owne imperfections, the royal prophet, or other faithful perſon prayeth God, 5. according to his mercie and goodnes, 9. shewed in conuerting Gentiles, 13. and in deliuering the ſupplicant him ſelf from the ſtate of damnation, 16. that he wil ſtil direct and defend him againſt al enimies. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer for continual grace.
The 7. key.

verses.text: To the children of Core, a Pſalme of Canticle. THE fundations thereof in the holie <na>(a)</na> mountaynes:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Chriſts Church was firſt founded in Ieruſalem on whitſunday, Act 2 in mount Sion, which hath two coppes, in one of which the Temple ſtood, in the other Dauids towre or palace.

verses.text: our Lord loueth the gates of Sion, aboue al the tabernacles of Iacob.
Glorious thinges are ſaide of thee, ô cittie of God.
<na>(b)</na> I wil be mindeful of <na>(c)</na> Raab, and Babylon knowing me. Behold <na>(d)</na> the foreners, and Tyre, & the people of the Æthiopians, theſe <na>(e)</na> were there.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The Prophet in the perſon of Chriſt, ſaith he wil commend vnto his Apoſtles, and other Apoſtolical men, that they conuert al nations (as our Sauiour gaue expreſſe commiſſion and commandment. Math. 28. Luc. 24. v. 47. Act. 1. v. 8.)

notes.label: c
notes.text: naming here Raab (which is Ægypt) and Babylon:

notes.label: d
notes.text: The Philiſtims, Tyrians, Æthiopians,

notes.label: e
notes.text: & the reſt, ſhal be regenerate in this Church, which for the aſſured certaintie therof (after the prophets maner of ſpeaking) is affirmed in the pretertence, as if it were then donne.

verses.text: Shal it not be ſaid of Sion <na>(f)</na> Man and man, is borne in her; and <na>(g)</na> the Higheſt himſelfe founded her?

notes.label: f
notes.text: It shal be reported, or one ſhal ſay to an other: Loe this and that man, al theſe and al theſe men are regenerate by Baptiſme in the Church of Chriſt.

notes.label: g
notes.text: God himſelfe, Chriſt God and Man, founded this Church.

verses.text: Our Lord wil declare <na>(h)</na> in ſcriptures of peoples, and <na>(i)</na> of princes: of thoſe that haue bene in her.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The multitude of the elect is ſo great, that only God knoweth the number,

notes.label: i
notes.text: and the qualities of al ſortes, of Princes, Prelates, and Peoples.

verses.text: The <na>(k)</na> habitation in thee, is as it were of al reioycing.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Great ſpiritual ioy with peace of conſcience, is in true Chriſtian Catholiques in the militant Church; but the bleſſed haue the moſt abſolute & ſecure ioy of al, in the Church triumphant.

chapters.summary: The Church of Chriſt beginning in Ieruſalem, 3. is extended to al Nations, 5. glorious, 6. and permanent, 7. in holie ioy. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer for continual grace.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Canticle of a Pſalme, to the children of Core, vnto the end, for <na>(a)</na> Maheleth <na>(b)</na> to anſwer, <na>(c)</na> of vnderſtanding to Eman the Ezrahite.

notes.label: a
notes.text: An inſtrument of muſike apt for lamentable ſongues. Not expreſſed in the title of anie other Pſalme. Perhaps becauſe this Pſalme mixeth not anie conſolation with mourning, as other Pſalmes do, which are alſo prayers in affliction. As the 30. 33. 63. 73.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Neither is this word in anie other title. It is added here to admonish vs, that as this Pſalme, and ſome others were ſongue by two quires, one anſwering the other, ſo we muſt in anſwer and imitation of Chriſt, ſuffer long and great afflictions with patience, ſeeing he in his paſſion was leift without ordinarie côſolation.

notes.label: c
notes.text: By ſome interpreted [his bretheren] For Chriſt (ſaith S. Auguſtin) vouchſaſſeth to make them his bretheren, which vnderſtand the myſterie of his Croſſe, and not only are not aſhamed therof, but alſo faithfully glorie therin.

verses.text: O Lord the God of my ſaluation: <na>(d)</na> in the day haue I cried, and in the night before thee.

notes.label: d
notes.text: I haue cried to thee very often both by day, and by night.

verses.text: Let my prayer enter in thy ſight: incline thine eare to my petition.
Becauſe my ſoule is replenished with euils: and <na>(e)</na> my life hath approched to hel.

notes.label: e
notes.text: I am almoſt dead.

verses.text: I <na>(f)</na> am accounted with them that deſcend into the lake. I am become as a man without helpe,

notes.label: f
notes.text: Accounted as dead, and readie to be buried.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> free among the dead, as the wounded ſleeping in the ſepulchres, of whom thou art mindeful no more: and they are caſt of from thy hand.

notes.label: g
notes.text: If I were dead, I ſhould be free from theſe afflictions. Eſpecially it agreeth to Chriſt, who was free, yea of infinite powre amongſt the dead.

verses.text: They haue put me in <na>(h)</na> the lower lake: in the darke places, and in the shadowe of death.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Myn enimies haue endeuored not only to bereue me of temporal life, wherby I ſhould goe into limbus, but alſo to kil my ſoule ſpiritually, wherby I should deſcend into the lower hel of the damned.

verses.text: Thy <na>(i)</na> furie is confirmed vpon me: and al thy waues thou haſt brought in vpon me.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thy iuſt wrath alſo ô God hath excedingly afflicted me.

verses.text: Thou haſt made my familiars far from me: they haue put me abomination to themſelues. I was deliuered and came not forth:
myne eies languished for pouertie. I cried to thee ô Lord al the day: I ſtretched out my handes to thee.
Wilt thou <na>(k)</na> doe meruels to the dead: or shal phiſicians raiſe to life, and they confeſſe to thee?

notes.label: k
notes.text: O God deliuer me whiles I am yet liuing, for I may not looke for extraordinarie, and miraculous helpe, as to be raiſed againe after death:

verses.text: Shal any <na>(l)</na> in the ſepulchre declare thy mercie, and thy truth in perdition?

notes.label: l
notes.text: when I shal be dead & buried, I can not denounce thy praiſes as now I can to mortal men.

verses.text: Shal thy meruelous workes be knowne <na>(m)</na> in darkenes: and thy iuſtice in the land of obliuion.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Much leſſe shal the damned praiſe thee in eternal perdition.

verses.text: And I ô Lord haue cried to thee: and in the morning shal my praier preuent thee.
Why doeſt thou o Lord reiect my prayer: turneſt away thy face from me?
I am poore, and in labours <na>(n)</na> from my youth: and being <na>(o)</na> exalted, humbled and troubled.

notes.label: n
notes.text: As wel young,

notes.label: o
notes.text: as waxing elder I haue bene ſtil afflicted.

verses.text: Thy wrathes haue paſſed vpon me: and thy terrouts haue trubled me.
They haue compaſſed me as water al the day: they compaſſed me together.
Thou <na>(p)</na> haſt made frend, and neighboure far from me: and my familiars becauſe of miſerie.

notes.label: p
notes.text: My miſerable eſtate hath alienated al freindes, neighbours, & acquantances from me.

chapters.summary: A faithful perſon ſore and long afflicted, lamentably complaineth, praying God, 15. not ſtil to repel him, being leift deſolate, 19. without al conſolation of freindes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: A prayer in long affliction. The 7 key.

verses.text: Of vnderſtanding <na>(a)</na> to Ethan the Ezrahite.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Otherwiſe called Idithun. 1. Paral. 25. or rather Ethan, who was very wiſe, mentioned with others, to whom Salomon is preferred for wiſdom. 3. Reg. 4. v. 31, and ſignifieth ſtrong, applied here to thoſe that are ſtrong in aſſured hope of Chriſts promiſes, notwithſtanding it ſemeth ſometimes to the weake, that his promiſes are not performed.

verses.text: THE mercies of our Lord I wil ſing for euer. In generation <na>(b)</na> and generation I wil shewe forth thy truth, in my mouth.

notes.label: b
notes.text: In al generations.

verses.text: Becauſe thou ſaidſt: Mercie shal be built vp for euer <na>(c)</na> in the heauens: thy truth shal be prepared in them.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The heauens ſhal rather fal, then Gods truth faile. Myſtically, in the Apoſtles, and by their preaching, the Church of Chriſt is built for euer.

verses.text: I haue ordained a teſtament with mine elect, I haue ſworne to Dauid my ſeruant:
<na>(d)</na> for ever wil I prepare thy ſeede. And I wil build thy ſeat vnto generation and generation.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Dauids ſeede conſerued til Chriſt was borne of his virgin mother: and in his ſpiritual ſeede, his kingdom the Church is for euer conſerued. Otherwiſe not verified of Dauids temporal kingdom, which decayed in the captiuitie of Babylon, and is now wholly deſtroyed.

verses.text: The heauens shal confeſſe thy meruelous workes ô Lord: yea and thy truth in the church of ſaintes.
For who in the cloudes shal be equal to our Lord: shal be like to God among <na>(e)</na> the ſonnes of God?

notes.label: e
notes.text: The Angels.

verses.text: God, who is glorified in the counſel of ſaintes: great and terrible ouer al that are round about him.
O Lord God of hoaſtes who is like to thee? thou art mightie ô Lord, and thy truth round about thee.
Thou ruleſt ouer the powre of the ſea: and the mouing of the waues therof thou doeſt mitigate.
Thou <na>(f)</na> humbledſt the proud one, as one wounded: in the arme of thy ſtrength thou haſt diſperſed thine enimies.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The prophet aludeth to the plagues and miracles in Ægypt, and in other enimes.

verses.text: The heauens are thine, and the earth is thine, the round earth, and the fulnes therof thou haſt founded:
the north, and the ſea thou haſt created. <na>(g)</na> Thabor and Hermon shal reioice in thy name:

notes.label: g
notes.text: Conuerſion of Gentiles.

verses.text: thy arme is with might. Let <na>(h)</na> thy hand be confirmed, and thy <na>(i)</na> righthand exalted:

notes.label: h
notes.text: VVhether God punish, as with the left hand,

notes.label: i
notes.text: or beſtow benefites, as with the right hand, al is to his glorie, and according to mercie, and truth.

verses.text: iuſtice and iudgement is the preparation of thy ſeat. Mercie and truth shal goe before thy face:
<na>(k)</na> bleſſed is the people that knoweth iubilation. Lord they shal walke in the light of thy countinance,

notes.label: k
notes.text: They are ſpiritually happie, that do thus conſider of Gods meruelous procedings, praiſe the ſame, and reioyce therin.

verses.text: and in thy name they shal reioyce al the day: and in thy iuſtice they shal be exalted.
Becauſe thou art the glorie of their ſtreingth: and in thy good pleaſure shal our <na>(l)</na> horne be exalted.

notes.label: l
notes.text: powre, and kingdom.

verses.text: Becauſe our protection is of our Lord: and of the holie one of Iſrael our king.
Then didſt thou ſpeake in viſion to thy ſaintes, and ſaidſt <na>[1]</na> I haue put helpe on the mightie one: and haue exalted an elect one of my people.

notes.text: Thus God promiſed to eſtabliſh the kingdom of the Iewes in Dauid and his familie. 1. Reg. 16. 2. Reg. 5. and other places. which was performed as in a figure but more fully in Chriſt. Act. 13. v. 22.

verses.text: I haue found Dauid my ſeruant: with myne holie oyle haue I anointed him.
For mine hand shal helpe him: and myne arme shal ſtrengthen him.
The enimie shal nothing preuale in him: and the ſonne of iniquitie shal not adde to hurt him.
And I wil cut downe his enimies before his face: and them that hate him I wil put to flight.
And my truth, and my mercie with him: and in my name shal his horne be exalted.
And I wil put his hand in the ſea: and his righthand in the riuers.
He shal inuocate me: Thou art my Father: my God, and the protector of my ſaluation.
And I wil put him the firſtbegotten, high aboue the kings of the earth.
I wil kepe my mercie vnto him for euer: and my teſtament faithful to him.
I wil put his ſeed for euer and euer: and his throne as the daies of heauen.
But if his children shal forſake my lawe: and wil not walke in my Iudgementes:
If they shal profane my iuſtices: and not kepe my commandmentes:
I wil viſite their iniquities with a rod: and their ſinnes with ſtripes:
But, my mercie I wil not take away from him: neither wil I hurt in my truth:
Neither wil I profane my teſtament: and the words that procede from my mouth I wil not make fruſtrate.
Once I haue ſworne in my holie, if I lie to Dauid:
his ſeede shal continewe for euer. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: I wil not lie.

verses.text: And <na>(m)</na> his throne as the Sunne in my ſight, and as the <na>(n)</na> Moone perfect for euer: and a faithful witneſſe in heauen.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Chriſtian iuſt ſoules as the ſunne,

notes.label: n
notes.text: and as the perfect, or full moone. See the firſt Tome. page 716. S. Auguſtin alſo expoundeth this verſe in the Anagogical ſenſe, of the iuſt after the Reſurrection in glorie, where the ſoule shal be like the ſunne, and the bodie, which now is mutable, ſhal be like the moone, not as now alwayes changing, but as the ful moone, alwayes perfect.

verses.text: But <na>[1]</na> thou haſt repelled and diſpiſed: thou <na>(o)</na> haſt differred thy Chriſt.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Amongſt manie penſiue thinges, this one word doth comforte vs, thy promiſe remaineth, thou haſt not denied to ſend Chriſt, but differred him,

God hauing promiſed al the aforſaide the prophet in the perſon of the weake, lamenteth that the contrarie shal happen as wel in the temporal kingdom oppreſſed by the Aſſirians Babylonians, Perſians, Grecians, and Romanes: as in the Church impugned by innumerable ſortes of Heretikes and other Infidels.

verses.text: Thou haſt ouerthrowne the teſtament of thy ſeruant: thou haſt profaned his ſanctuarie on the earth.
Thou haſt deſtroyed al the hedges therof: thou haſt made the firmament therof feare.
Al that paſſe by the way haue ſpoiled him: he is become a reproch to his neighbours.
Thou haſt exalted the righthand of them that oppreſſe him: thou haſt made al his enimies ioyful.
Thou haſt turned away the helpe of his ſword: and haſt not holpen him in battel.
Thou haſt deſtroied him from <na>(p)</na> emundation: and his ſeat thou haſt broken downe to the ground.

notes.label: p
notes.text: From the vſe of Sacrifice and Sacraments, wherby ſinners were wount to be cleanſed.

verses.text: Thou haſt leſſened the daies of his time: thou haſt ouerwhelmed him with confuſion.
<na>[1]</na> How long ô Lord doeſt thou turne away for euer: shal thy wrath burne as a fire?

notes.text: The Pſalmiſt prayeth and prophecieth that God wil reſpect the weaknes of man, maintaine his Church in manie natiôs, & ſaue manie ſoules.

verses.text: Remember what my ſubſtance is: for haſt thou made al the children of men in vaine?
Who is the man that shal liue, and shal not ſee death: shal deliuer his ſoule from the hand of hel?
Where are thyne old mercies ô Lord, as thou ſwareſt to Dauid in thy truth?
Be mindeful ô Lord of the aeproch of thy ſeruantes (which I haue held in my boſome) of manie nations.
Which thine enimies haue reproched ô Lord, which they haue reproched <na>(q)</na> the commutation of thy Chriſt.

notes.label: q
notes.text: As though Chriſt were changed and turned from vs.

verses.text: Bleſſed be our Lord for euer: <na>(r)</na> Be it, be it.

notes.label: r
notes.text: So we wish and pray that al may bleſſe and praiſe thee. Amen.

chapters.summary: Gods mercie and truth, with his great promiſes to Dauid, 6. his powre in the whole world, and iuſt iudgements, are the true ioy of his ſeruantes. 20. Chriſts kingdom shal remaine for euer: 31. yea manie offending yet al shal not perish, 39. but after great affliction, 47. God wil reſpect mans infirmitie, 50. his owne promiſe, and the enimies reproching his ſeruantes and himſelfe: 53. who is bleſſed for euer. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church of Chriſt never faileth.
The 6. key.

verses.text: A prayer <na>(a)</na> of Moyſes the man of God. Lord, thou art made a refuge for vs: <na>(b)</na> from generation vnto generation.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Some Expoſitors thincke Moyſes was the author of this Pſalme, and of the tenne next folowing. But others hold that Dauid vvas author of al, and that Moyſes his name is here put in the title by Eſdras, becauſe this Pſalme is like to the prayer of Moyſes, when the people prouoked Gods wrath by their ſinnes in the deſert. And becauſe mans creation, fal, punishmẽt, and Gods mercie towards him, are here deſcribed: which Moyſes firſt writte, as going before the vvritten law. And that Moyſes made not this Pſalme is probably gethered by the 10. verſe, where the ordinarie age of men is deſcribed to be (in ſtreingth and vigore) ſeuentie yeares, or of ſome fourſcore: and the greater part (of the one or the other) is in labour and ſorow. And it is euident ( Deut. 34. ) that Moyſes liued in al an hundred and tvventie yeares, and his eye was not dimme, neither were his teeth moued. So Aaron, Ioſue, and others commonly liued longer then is here mentioned. But Dauid was old and impotent at ſeuentie yeares. 3. Reg. 1. S. Hilarion, liuing neere ſeuentie yeares in his heremitage, S. Remigius gouerning the Church of Rhemes, ſeuentie yeares, and the like are accounted to haue bene ful of dayes, and ſuch as liued longer are reputed extraordinarie. Agane it is more euidenly proued that Moyſes vvas not author of the 94. and 95. Pſalmes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Alwayes from the beginning of the world to the end.

verses.text: Before <na>(c)</na> the mountaines were made, or the earth and the world formed: <na>(d)</na> from euerlaſting euen vnto euerlaſting thou art God.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The Prophet sheweth that the world was created in and with time, not eternal.

notes.label: d
notes.text: And that only God is eternal.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Turne not away man into humiliation: thou ſaidſt: Be conuerted ye children of men.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God hath often ſaide, that he vvould not the death of ſinners, but rather that they be conuerted and liue for euer.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(f)</na> a thouſand years before thine eies, are as yeſterday, that is paſt. And as a watch in the night,

notes.label: f
notes.text: Though ſome liued long ( none for al that did reach to a thouſand yeares ) yet it is nothing before God, and in reſpect of eternitie.

verses.text: thinges that are counted nothing shal their years be.
In <na>(g)</na> the morning as an herbe he shal paſſe, in the morning he shal florish, and paſſe: in <na>(h)</na> the euening he shal fal, be hardened, and withered.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The youth of man quickly paſſeth:

notes.label: h
notes.text: old age can not laſt long: wherof cometh our English prouerb: A young man may dye ſowne, an old man can not liue long.

verses.text: Becauſe we haue faynted in thy wrath, and in thy furie we are trubled.
Thou haſt put <na>(i)</na> our iniquities in thy ſight: our age in the light of thy countinance. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: i
notes.text: Sinne the cauſe of shortnes of mans life.
Sæculum.

verses.text: Becauſe al our daies haue failed: and in thy wrath we haue failed. Our yeares shal be conſidered <na>(k)</na> as a ſpyder:

notes.label: k
notes.text: ſpider. Man's life as brittle as a ſpider's web: or man's life vvaſteth continually, as a ſpider waſteth herſelf by ſpinning, and conſuming her own ſubſtance.

verses.text: the daies of our yeares in them, are <na>(l)</na> ſeuentie yeares. And if in ſtrong ones <na>(m)</na> eightie years: and the more of them, labour and ſorrow. Becauſe <na>(n)</na> mildnes is come vpon vs: and we shal be chaſtiſed.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Theſe numbers literarly shew the ſhortnes of the longer ſorte of mens liues. Myſtically, ſeuen ſignifie the reſt after laboures of this world, and perteyn to the old teſtament: eight ſignifie the revvard in the reſurrection, perteyning to the nevv teſtament. VVhich multiplied by tenne, a perfect number, make ſeuentie and eightie. VVhich ioyned together make an hundred and fiftie. The number of al theſe Pſalmes.

notes.label: m
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: n
notes.text: It is of Gods milde prouidence, that mans life is ſhort, for that manie if they vvere ſure, or had probabilitie to liue long, vvould preſume to ſinne more.

verses.text: <na>(o)</na> Who knoweth the powre of thy wrath: and for feare

notes.label: o
notes.text: Seing God of his iuſtice puniſhed al mankind, for one ſinne of our firſt parente, his wrath muſt nedes be very great to euerie ſinner, for his ovvne proper ſinnes.

verses.text: to number thy wrath? So make thy righthand knowne: and men learned in hart, in wiſedome.
Turne ô Lord, how long? and be intreated for thy ſeruants.
<na>(p)</na> We are replenished in the morning with thy mercie: and we haue reioyced, and are delighted al our daies.

notes.label: p
notes.text: The hope of glorious reſurrection turneth our calamities into ſpiritual ioy.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> We haue reioyced for the daies wherin thou haſt humbled vs: the yeares, wherin we haue ſeene euils.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Yea the more we ſuffer in this life for the truth, the greater is our comforth in hope of reward.

verses.text: Looke vpon <na>(r)</na> thy ſeruants, and vpon thy workes: and <na>(s)</na> direct their children.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Not only in that we are thy creatures, but alſo in that we are thy ſeruants, we are thy proper worke, therfore in both theſe reſpectes, ô God looke vpon vs with clemencie.

notes.label: s
notes.text: lead alſo our poſteritie into the right way, and make them thy ſeruantes.

verses.text: And <na>(t)</na> let the brightnes of our Lord God be vpon vs, and <na>(v)</na> direct thou the workes of our handes ouer vs: and <na>(w)</na> the worke of our handes doe thou direct.

notes.label: t
notes.text: O God illuminate our vnderſtanding,

notes.label: v
notes.text: make our actions by thy grace profitable to vs:

notes.label: w
notes.text: and make perfect in vs the worke of charitie. In which one worke, al good workes are included and to which al other are directed. For then workes are right ( ſayth S. Auguſtin ) when they are directed to this one end.

chapters.summary: Vnder the forme of prayer, the Pſalmiſt deſcribeth the shortnes of mans life and other calamites. 7. Gods ſtrict iudgement. 13. but firſt his comfortable mercie: 16. and perpetual regard of his owne worke. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Man rightly created fell by ſin into miſeries.
The 6. key.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Prayſe of a <na>(b)</na> Canticle to Dauid. He <na>(c)</na> that dwelleth in the helpe of the Higheſt, shal abide in the protection of the God of heauen.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Praiſe of Gods prouidence, with thankes,

notes.label: b
notes.text: Which Dauid ſonge with voice.

notes.label: c
notes.text: He that firmely relieth and reſteth vpon Gods prouidence, is aſſuredly protected by him.

verses.text: He shal ſay to our Lord: Thou art my protectour, and my refuge: my God I wil hope in him.
Becauſe he hath deliuered me from <na>(d)</na> the ſnare of the hunters, and from <na>(e)</na> the sharpe word.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Al ſecret and ſutle machinations :

notes.label: e
notes.text: and from al crueltie of tyrants.

verses.text: With his shoulders shal he ouershadowe thee: and vnder his winges thou shalt hope.
With shilde shal his truth compaſſe thee: thou shalt not be afrayed <na>(f)</na> of the feare in the night.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Terrors obſcurly ſuggeſted by euil men or ſpirites, with erronious conceipte that men are not bond in time of temporal dangers, to confeſſe the truth.

verses.text: Of <na>(g)</na> the arrow flying in the day, <na>(h)</na> of buſines walking in darkenes: <na>(i)</na> of inuaſion, and the midday diuel.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Open perſecution threatning preſent death, except men denie the truth which they know.

notes.label: h
notes.text: circumuention of craftie enimies by ſutle arguing, and drawing men into error, and ſo to decline from Catholique Religion,

notes.label: i
notes.text: long torments, euen to death, except Gods ſeruants wil relent, and denie the truth, which they aſſuredly beleue, and know in their conſcience, that they are bond to profeſſe it.

verses.text: A <na>(k)</na> thouſand shal fal on thy ſyde, & <na>(l)</na> ten thouſand: on thy righthand: but to thee it shal not approch.
