notes.label: k
notes.text: On thy left ſide, in aduerſitie manie fal from God,

notes.label: l
notes.text: & on thy right ſide, in proſperitie manie more forgete, and forſake God.

verses.text: But thou shalt conſider with thine eies: and shalt ſee the retribution of ſinners.
Becauſe <na>(m)</na> thou ô Lord art my hope: thou haſt made the Higheſt thy refuge.

notes.label: m
notes.text: In ſincerely ſaying thou art my hope: thou makeſt God thy refuge.

verses.text: There shal no euil come to thee: and ſcourge shal not approch to thy tabernacle.
Becauſe he hath geuen <na>(n)</na> his Angels charge of thee: <na>(o)</na> that they keepe thee in al thy waies.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Angels haue protection of men by Gods ordinance .

notes.label: o
notes.text: The diuel corruptly alleageth this ſcripture (Mat. 4) omitting the latter part of this verſe: which ſheweth when Angels protect iuſt men, to witte, when they walke in a right path, obſeruing ordinarie courſe in their actions, not in geuing themſelues headlong into needles danger, as the ſame diuel propoſed to our Sauiour, to caſt himſelf downe from the pinnacle of the temple. Such falling is not the way of the iuſt, but of Lucifer, that fel from heauen. So S. Bernard noteth Ser. 15. in hunc Pſal.

verses.text: In their handes they shal beare thee: leſt perhaps thou knocke thy foote againſt a ſtone.
Vpon the aſpe, and the baſiliſcus thou shalt walke: & thou shalt tread vpon the lion, and the dragon.
<na>(p)</na> Becauſe he hath hoped in me, I wil deliuer him: I wil protect him, becauſe he hath knowne my name.

notes.label: p
notes.text: God ſpeaketh the reſt that foloweth in this Pſalme.

verses.text: He shal crie to me, and I wil heare him: with him I am in tribulation: I wil deliuer him, and <na>(q)</na> wil glorifie him.

notes.label: q
notes.text: In eternal ſaluation.

verses.text: With length of daies I wil replenish him: and I wil shew him my ſaluation.

chapters.summary: Whoſoeuer faithfully and firmly truſteth in Gods prouidence, is ſecure from al dangers of ſecrete, ſutle, and open enimies. 7. his aduerſaries shal come to ruine. 11. Angels shal defend him. 13. no kind of ſerpent, nor beaſt shal hurt him. 14. God himſelf aſſureth him of his protection, and of eternal ſaluation. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence.
The 3. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme <na>(a)</na> of Canticle, <na>(b)</na> in the ſabbath day.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Voices beginning inſtrumentes proſecute this ſong:

notes.label: b
notes.text: when we reſt from worke then eſpecially vve ought to thincke vpon Gods vvorkes, praiſe and thanke him for the ſame.

verses.text: IT is good <na>(c)</na> to confeſſe to our Lord; and to ſing to thy name ô Higheſt.

notes.label: c
notes.text: To geue thankes.

verses.text: To shewforth thy mercie in <na>(d)</na> the morning: and thy truth in <na>(e)</na> the night.

notes.label: d
notes.text: In proſperitie,

notes.label: e
notes.text: in aduerſitie.

verses.text: In <na>(f)</na> the inſtrument of tenſtrings, in <na>(g)</na> Pſalter: with Canticle, on <na>(h)</na> the Harpe.

notes.label: f
notes.text: On euerie inſtrument of tenne ſtringes, ſignifying the obſeruation of the tenne commandments:

notes.label: g
notes.text: namely on the Pſalter.

notes.label: h
notes.text: alſo on the harpe, which ſignifieth mortification.

verses.text: Becauſe thou haſt delighted me ô Lord in thy workemanship: and in the workes of thy handes I wil reioyce.
How are thy workes magnified ô Lord! thy cogitations are made very profounde.
The <na>(i)</na> vnwiſe man wil not know; and the <na>(k)</na> foule wil not vnderſtand theſe thinges.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Carnal and ſenſual man,

notes.label: k
notes.text: he that thinketh only of preſent thinges, not of future.

verses.text: When ſinners shal ſpring vp as graſſe: and al that worke iniquitie shal appeare. That they may perish for euer:
but thou the Higheſt for euer ô Lord.
Becauſe loe thine enimies ô Lord, becauſe loe thine enimies shal perish: and al that worke iniquitie shal be diſperſed.
And <na>(l)</na> my horne shal be exalted, as the vnicorns: <na>(m)</na> and my old age in plentiful mercie.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The iuſt in confidence of a good conſcience, expect exaltation of their powre:

notes.label: m
notes.text: and great conſolation in the end of their life.

verses.text: And <na>(n)</na> mine eie hath looked vpon mine enimies: and the malignant ryſing vp againſt me, mine ears shal heare.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Then shal the iuſt ſee their enimies depreſſed: and themſelues florish, like the palme, and ceder trees as folovveth.

verses.text: The iuſt, shal florish as a palme tree: as the ceder of Libanus shal he be multiplied.
They that are planted in <na>(o)</na> the houſe of our Lord, shal florish in <na>(p)</na> the courtes of the houſe of our God.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Militant Church:

notes.label: p
notes.text: triumphant.

verses.text: As yet shal they be multiplied in plentiful old age: and they shal be wel affected,
that they <na>(q)</na> may shewforth: That the Lord our God is righteous, and there is no iniquitie in him.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Publikly profeſſe Gods praiſes, as in the wordes folowing:

chapters.summary: God is by al maner of voices and inſtruments to be praiſed in his admirable workes. 7. which the foolish not doing are punished; 11. and the wiſe are rewarded. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The works of God admirable.
The 2. key.

verses.text: Prayſe <na>(a)</na> of Canticle <na>(b)</na> to Dauid himſelfe, in <na>(c)</na> the day before the ſabbath, <na>(d)</na> when the earth was founded. OVr Lord <na>(e)</na> hath reigned, he <na>(f)</na> hath put on beutie: our Lord hath <na>(g)</na> put on ſtrength, and hath girded him ſelfe. For he hath eſtablished <na>(h)</na> the round world, which <na>(i)</na> shal not be moued.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Praiſe to be ſongue vvith voice:

notes.label: b
notes.text: compoſed by Dauid:

notes.label: c
notes.text: the ſixth day of the weeke, vvhich is our friday,

notes.label: d
notes.text: in vvhich day the Church of Chriſt vvas founded, by his bloud ſhed on the croſſe.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Our Sauiour founding his Church by his death begane then to reigne therin:

notes.label: f
notes.text: glorioſly deſcending a ſoule into limbus, and in bodie to his graue:

notes.label: g
notes.text: he then put on al armour of ſtrength to reforme the world, and to inlarge his kingdom, according to his owne prediction where he ſaide: If I be exalted from the earth, I wil draw al thinges vnto myſelfe. Ioan. 12. v. 31.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Not only in Iurie and Samaria, but the whole earth:

notes.label: i
notes.text: and the ſame Church ſhal not be deſtroyed.

verses.text: Thy ſeat is prepared from that time: thou <na>(k)</na> art from euerlaſting.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Chriſt being eternal, hath an euerlaſting Church.

verses.text: The <na>(l)</na> riuers ô Lord haue lifted vp: the riuers haue lifted vp their voice. The riuers haue lifted vp their waues,

notes.label: l
notes.text: Al ſortes of perſecuters, the High prieſtes (who ſometimes vvatered the ſpiritual land, like riuers) vvith Scribes, Phariſes, and other incredulous Ievves, alſo Paganes, Turkes, and Heretikes haue oppugned the Church.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> aboue the voices of manie waters. The ſurges of the ſea are meruelous; <na>(n)</na> meruelous is our Lord on high.

notes.label: m
notes.text: With more force then anie perſecutions in the old Teſtament.

notes.label: n
notes.text: but though al theſe aſſaultes be great, and meruelous, yet Chriſt in protecting his Church, is more meruelous.

verses.text: Thy teſtimonies are made <na>(o)</na> credible exceedingly: <na>(p)</na> holines becometh thy houſe ô Lord <na>(q)</na> for length of daies.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Articles of faith are not euidently apparent to knovvlege, but euident to credibilitie, to thoſe that are diſpoſed by Gods grace, illuminating their vnderſtanding, and mouing their free vvil, to geue conſent of beleefe if they vvil

notes.label: p
notes.text: It behoueth therfore al members of the Church to conuerſe piouſly, and religiouſly in this life, ſeing she hath ſo excellent a ſpouſe, protector, and inſtructor,

notes.label: q
notes.text: euen to the end of the vvorld.

chapters.summary: Chriſt reigneth for euer in his Church: 3. notwithſtanding manie and great perſecution againſt the faithful. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Perpetuitie of the Church.
The 6. key.

verses.text: To <na>(a)</na> Dauid himſelfe, in <na>(b)</na> the fourth of the ſabbath. OVr Lord God of reuenges: the God <na>(c)</na> of reuenges hath done <na>(d)</na> freely.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The Hebrevv letter Lamed, vvhich ordinarily is prefixed to the datiue caſe, or ſignifieth to, being ſet before proper names, is a ſigne of the genetiue caſe. Yet the Septuagint, expreſſe it by the datiue, and ſo doth the latin, ipſi Dauid, and conſequently our Engliſh hath, to Dauid himſelfe, to shevv a difference betvven ſacred and profane vvriters. For in humane bookes the vvriter and auctor is al one; but in diuine, the Holie Ghoſt is the proper auctor, and a man is the vvriter. To ſignifie therfore the principal auctor, Dauid is ſometimes named as the inſtrumental cauſe, to vvhom the Holie Ghoſt inſpired this, and other Pſalmes, and by vvhom they vvere vvritten. And vvhen the titles expreſſe othervviſe: A Pſalme of Dauid, yet it is ſo to be vnderſtood, that the Holie Ghoſt is alvvayes the principal auctor, and Dauid the inſtrumental, miniſterial, or ſecondarie auctor. But vvhen other names are expreſſed, either in the genetiue or datiue caſe, or hovvſoeuer, it proueth not that thoſe men vvere the vvriters of the ſame Pſalmes, but importeth ſome other thing, as by S. Auguſtins iudgement, vve noted in the proemial Annotations page 3. & 4. vvherby is proued that this Pſalme vvas not written, nor compoſed by Moyſes, as Hebrevv Rabbins ſuppoſe, but by the Royal Pſalmiſt Dauid.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Made and ordinarily ſongue in the fourth day of the vveke, our vveneſday, in vvhich day Iudas the traitor ſold our Sauiour Chriſt to his enimies. The reuenge of vvhich vvickednes, and of al other ſinnes, is here prophecied.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God more commonly called the God of mercie (vvhich vertue in him is aboue al his vvorkes, Pſal. 144) is alſo the God of reuenges, according to his iuſtice.

notes.label: d
notes.text: He proceedeth in iudgement reſolutly, not depending, nor fearing, not reſpecting anie perſon, povvre, dignitie, vviſdome or other like qualitie, but their iuſt merites.

verses.text: Be <na>[1]</na> exalted thou that iudgeſt the earth: render retribution to the proude.

notes.text: A prayer of iuſt zele,

verses.text: How long shal ſinners ô Lord: how long shal ſinners glorie?
Shal they vtter, and ſpeake iniquitie? shal al they ſpeake, <na>(e)</na> that worke iniuſtice?

notes.label: e
notes.text: Shal moſt wicked men ſtil be ſuffered to ſpeake ſo inſolently?

verses.text: Thy <na>[1]</na> people ô Lord they haue humbled: and thine inheritance they haue vexed.

notes.text: A deſcription of heathnish and heretical crueltie.

verses.text: The widow, and the ſtranger they haue ſlaine: and the pupilles they haue killed.
And <na>[1]</na> they haue ſaide: The Lord shal not ſee, neither shal the God of Iacob vnderſtand.

notes.text: Scarſe anie Atheiſtes are ſo blind, as thus to thinke but manie ſinners ſo behaue themſelues, as if God ſaw not, knew nor, or at leaſt cared not vvhat they do.

verses.text: Vnderſtand ye foolish in the people: and ye fooles be wiſe at ſometime.
He that planted the eare, shal he not heare? Or he that made the eie doth he not conſider?
He that chaſtiſeth nations, shal he not rebuke: he that teacheth man knowledge?
Our Lord knoweth <na>(f)</na> the cogitations of men: that they be vaine.

notes.label: f
notes.text: So vnpoſſible is it that God should be ignorant, or careles vvhat men do, that he alſo knovveth and obſerueth moſt ſecret thoughtes.

verses.text: Bleſſed is the man, whom thou shalt inſtruct ô Lord: and shalt teach out of thy lawe.
That thou maiſt <na>(g)</na> geue him quietnes from the euil daies: til a pitte be digged for the ſinner.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Mitigate and temper his afflictions, that by patience and fortitude, the iuſt may perſeuere, and not be ouervvhelmed.

verses.text: Becauſe our Lord <na>(h)</na> wil not reiect his people: and his inheritance he wil not forſake.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The whole Church shal neuer be reiected, nor forſaken.

verses.text: Vntil iuſtice <na>(i)</na> be turned into iudgement: and <na>(k)</na> they who are neere it, are al that are right of hart.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Iuſtice is conuerted into iudgement, vvhen iuſt meaning is put in vvorke and practiſe, that it may appeare in iudgement. Alſo God vvho doth & ſuffereth al iuſtly, vvil conſerue his inheritance the Church, euen vnto the day of iudgement.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The ſenſe is eaſie by tranſpoſing the vvordes: al that are right of hart, are nere it, that is, ſhal like and approue Gods iuſtice, vvhen the vvicked shal repine, and blaſpheme it.

verses.text: Who shal riſe for me againſt the malignant? or who shal ſtand with me againſt them that worke iniquitie?
But that our Lord hath holpen me: within very litle my ſoule had dwelt in hel.
If I ſaid: <na>(l)</na> My foote is moued: thy mercie ô Lord did help me

notes.label: l
notes.text: When I felt, and complained that I was in danger, thou didſt aſſiſt me.

verses.text: According to the multitude of my ſorrowes in my hart: thy conſolations haue made my ſoule ioyful.
Doth the ſeat of iniquitie cleaue to thee: which makeſt <na>(m)</na> labour in precept?

notes.label: m
notes.text: Onlie faith ſufficeth not, but careful laboure, in keping Gods commandmnts is required.

verses.text: They wil hunt after the ſoule of the iuſt: and wil condemne innocent bloud.
And our Lord became my refuge: and my God the helpe <na>(n)</na> of my hope.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The iuſt do hope for eternal ſaluation, to which God wil bring them.

verses.text: And he <na>(o)</na> wil repay them their iniquitie: and in their malice he wil deſtroy them: the Lord our God wil deſtroy them.

notes.label: o
notes.text: And God, the reuenger of vvronges, vvil at laſt caſt the wicked into eternal torments.

chapters.summary: The faithful ſeruant of God aſſuredly profeſſeth, that al the pride, 5. crueltie, 7. foolish imaginations, and ſecret thoughts of the wicked are manifeſt to God, 12. acknowlegeth himſelf happie, that he is better inſtructed of God: wheras he had otherwiſe bene damned. 20. sharply reprehendeth thoſe that conſider not of Gods iudgements: concluding that the iuſt shal be glorified, and the wicked damned. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Eternal ſalvation and damnation.
The 10. key.

verses.text: Praiſe <na>(a)</na> of Canticle, <na>(b)</na> to Dauid him ſelfe. COME, <na>[1]</na> let vs <na>(c)</na> reioyce to our Lord: let vs make iubilation to God <na>(d)</na> our ſauiour.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Praiſe ſongue with voices:

notes.label: b
notes.text: inſpired to Dauid, & written by him.

notes.label: c
notes.text: VVith great and ſolemne exultation:

notes.label: d
notes.text: God our Creator, is alſo our Protector & Sauiour.
This Inuitation is moſt fitly ordayned by the Church for the proeme or beginning of Mattins.

verses.text: Let vs <na>(e)</na> preuent his face in confeſſion: and <na>(f)</na> in Pſalmes let vs make iubilation to him.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Let vs be more diligent, and preuent our accuſtomed time. For no man can preuent Gods grace with anie good worke, who firſt preuenteth vs; els we can neither doe, nor thincke anie good thing.

notes.label: f
notes.text: not only in ſinging his praiſe with voice, but alſo with muſical inſtruments.

verses.text: Becauſe our Lord is a great God: and a great King aboue al goddes.
Becauſe in his hand are the endes of the earth: and the heightes of the mountaines be his.
Becauſe the ſea is his, and he made it: and his handes formed the drie land.
Come let vs adore, <na>(g)</na> and fal downe: and wepe before our Lord, that made vs.

notes.label: g
notes.text: So alſo Iſaias (c. 45. v. 23.) and S. Paul (Philip. 2.) teach that kneeling or bowing the knees, as an external religious ceremonie, is acceptable to God.

verses.text: Becauſe he is the Lord <na>(h)</na> our God; and we the people of his paſture, and the shepe <na>(i)</na> of his hand.

notes.label: h
notes.text: It is moſt iuſt and neceſſarie that we adore God, becauſe he made vs, and al this world for vs, hath alſo redemed vs, and made vs his people, as ſhepe of his paſture, and as a Paſtor feedeth and gouerneth vs.

notes.label: i
notes.text: of his making.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> To day if ye shal heare his voice, harden not your hartes;

notes.label: k
notes.text: Though ſome haue often repelled, and reſiſted Gods grace, yet if they receiue it being offered againe, it wil auaile them to remiſſion of ſinnes.

verses.text: As in the prouocation according to the day <na>(l)</na> of the tentation in the deſert: where your fathers tempted me, proued me, and ſaw my workes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The Iſraelites in the deſert tempted God, by deſiring water, and flesh, of voluptuous concupiſcence without neceſſitie. For Manna did both extinguiſh their thirſt, and taſted vnto them, whatſoeuer they deſired: Exo. 16. That alſo which was left vngathered when the ſunne waxed hotte, melted (v. 21.) and ſerued their cattel for drincke. So this tentation was a figure of thoſe, which require to communicate vnder both kindes, as if one did not conteine as much as both.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> Fourtie years was I <na>(n)</na> offended with that generation, and ſaid: Theſe alwaies erre in hart.

notes.label: m
notes.text: By this mention of the offence of fourtie yeares, as long before paſſed, is conuinced that Moyſes writte not this Pſalme, who died in the very fourtith yeare of their abode in the deſert. And S. Paul citing the wordes of this Pſalme. (Heb. 4.) manifeſtly acknowlegeth Dauid the writer therof, and that it was written long after Moyſes time in theſe wordes: (v. 7.) Againe he limiteth a certaine day; To day, in Dauid ſaying after ſo long time, s is aboue ſaide. To day if you shal heare his voice, do not obdurate your hartes. For if Ieſus (that is Ioſue) had geuen them reſt, he would neuer ſpeake of an other day afterward.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Being greatly offended, I approched nere vnto them, in puniſhing the offenders.

verses.text: And theſe haue not knowne my waies: as I ſware in my wrath: <na>(o)</na> if they shal enter into my reſt.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Thoſe that murmured died in the deſert, and entered not into the promiſed land, euen ſo thoſe that finally offend Chriſt, ſhal not enter into euerlaſting reſt: Heb. 3. & 4.

chapters.summary: An inuitation to ſerue and adore Chriſt our Lord and Meſſias, 3. aswel for the benefites of creating al thinges, 7. as for his Incarnation, and not to harden our hartes as the Iewes did. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt our Lord and King.
The 5. key.

verses.text: A Canticle <na>(a)</na> to Dauid <cr>[1]</cr> himſelfe, <na>(b)</na> when the houſe was built after the captiuitie. SING ye to our Lord <na>(c)</na> a new ſong: ſing to our Lord al the earth.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Inſpired to Dauid, and written by him:

notes.label: b
notes.text: prophecying the reſtauration of the temple, after the future captiuitie. And that in figure of the vniuerſal redemption of mankind by Chriſt, from the captiuitie of the diuel.

notes.label: c
notes.text: For a new benefite, farre greater then the deliuerie of Iſrael from Ægypt.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Sing ye to our Lord, and bleſſe his name: shewforth his ſaluation from day to day.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The ſame wordes [Sing to our Lord] thriſe repeted, ſignifie the Bleſſed Trinitie, as ſome Fathers note. Likewiſe v. 7. and 8. Bring ye to our Lord, &c. in both places concluding in the ſingular number, bleſſe his name, bring to his name, importing one God.

verses.text: Shewforth his glorie among the Gentiles, his meruelous workes in al peoples.
Becauſe our Lord is great, and exceeding laudable: he is terrible aboue al goddes.
Becauſe al the goddes of the Gentiles are <na>(e)</na> diuels, but our Lord <na>(f)</na> made the heauens.

notes.label: e
notes.text: VVhat creatures ſoeuer ſpiritual or corporal, viſible or inuiſible the paganes ſerue for goddes, ſtil they be diuels that deceiue them, and diuers wayes vſurpe diuine honour, making ſuch idolaters to thinke, that there is diuine powre, where none is.

notes.label: f
notes.text: He only is true God, who is Creator of heauen, and of al creatures. For no creature can create anie thing at al, that is, make anie thing of nothing but only God.

verses.text: Confeſſion, and beauty in his ſight: holineſſe, and magnificence in his ſanctification.
Bring to our Lord ye families of Gentiles, bring ye to our Lord glorie and honour:
bring to our Lord glorie vnto his name. Take vp hoaſtes, and enter into his courtes:
adore ye our Lord in his holie court. Let al the earth be moued before his face:
ſay ye among the Gentiles that our Lord <na>(g)</na> hath reigned. For he hath corrected the round world which shal not be moued: he wil iudge peoples in equitie.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Diuers ancient Doctors read more in this place: Our Lord hath reigned from the wood, to witte, Chriſt by his death on the croſſe conquered the diuel, ſinne, and death, and thence begane to reigne. S. Iuſtinus Martyr, dialogo aduers. Triphonem. Tertullian li. aduers. Iudæos. c. 9. & 13 & aduerſ Marcionem. li 1. c. 19. & 21. S. Auguſtin in this place, according to the old Roman Pſalter Before him Arnobius, and after him Caſſiadorus and others, wherby it is probable, that it was ſometimes in the Hebrew text, and blotted out by the Iewes.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Let the heauens be glad, and the earth reioyce, the ſea be moued, and the fulneſſe therof:

notes.label: h
notes.text: The Pſalmiſt in abundance of ſpirite inuiteth al creatures to praiſe God, as Daniel in his Canticle. c. 3.

verses.text: the fieldes shal be glad, and al things, that are in them. Then shal the trees of the woodes reioyce
before the face of our Lord, becauſe he cometh: becauſe he cometh to iudge the earth. He <na>(i)</na> wil iudge the round world in equitie, and peoples in his truth.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Chriſt iudgeth now in the world by his miniſters diſcerning and deciding cauſes, rewarding and puniſhing, but eſpecially he wil iudge al in the laſt day.

chapters.summary: Al peoples & nations are inuited to praiſe the bleſſed Trinitie, 3. for Chriſts Incarnation, and ſpiritual kingdom in al the world. 10. euen ſenſles creatures acknowledging his maieſtie, 13. and iudicial powre. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt's divine power.
The 5. key.

verses.text: To <na>(a)</na> this Dauid, <na>(b)</na> when his land was reſtored agane to him. OVr Lord hath reigned, let the earth reioyce: let <na>(c)</na> manie Ilands be glad.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In figure of Chriſt,

notes.label: b
notes.text: whoſe bodie roſe the third day after his death: to whom manie returned beleuing in him after his reſurrection, which fel from him in his paſſion: and to whom al thinges shal be ſubdued, as to their true Lord, in the day of iudgement.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Holie Dauid, and other Prophetes hauing great ioy to ſee long before in ſpirite only, Chriſts kingdom extended in the whole earth, yea to the Ilandes, we Ilanders haue great cauſe to be gladde, that God hath not only ſo bleſſed vs long ſince, but as yet conſerueth ſeede, wherby we truſt the whole Iland ſhal be againe reſtored vnto him.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Cloude, and miſt round about him: iuſtice, and iudgement <na>(e)</na> the correction of his ſeat.

notes.label: d
notes.text: As in a cloud with terror God gaue his law to the Iewes: ſo in a cloud with greater terror and maieſtie, he wil iudge the world;

notes.label: e
notes.text: not as manie corrupted ſeates of iudgement, in this world, but as a corrected tribunal, where iuſtice and right iudgement ſhal be practiſed.

verses.text: Fire shal goe before him, and shal inflame his enimies round about.
His lightninges <na>[1]</na> shined to the round world, the earth ſawe, and was moued,

notes.text: Theſe thinges are denounced as if they were alredy donne, for the aſſured certaintie therof.

verses.text: The mountaines melted as waxe, before the face of our Lord: before the face of our Lord al the earth.
The heauens haue shewed forth his iuſtice: and al peoples haue ſeene his glorie.
Let them al be confounded, that adore <na>(f)</na> ſculptils: and that glorie in their idoles. Adore him al ye his Angels:

notes.label: f
notes.text: As wel the worſhippers of grauen, or painted images of Iupiter, Mars, Bacchus and the like, as the worſhippers of the ſame imagined falſe goddes shal be confounded.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Sion heard, and was glad. And <na>(h)</na> the daughters of Iuda reioyced, becauſe of thy iudgements ô Lord.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The Catholique Church.

notes.label: h
notes.text: And al particular Churches, members of the vniuerſal.

verses.text: Becauſe thou Lord moſt high ouer al the earth: thou art exalted excedingly aboue al goddes.
You that loue our Lord, hate ye euil: our Lord keepeth the ſoules of his ſaintes, out of the hand of the ſinner he wil deliuer them.
Light is riſen to the iuſt, and ioy to the right of hart.
Be glad ye iuſt in our Lord: and confeſſe ye to the memorie <na>(i)</na> of his ſanctification.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Praiſe our Lord Chriſt who is ſanctitie it ſelfe, and ſanctifieth others.

chapters.summary: Al the earth is inuited to reioyce in Chriſts kingdom, 3. with deſcription of the ſignes coming before the day of Iudgement. 7. Idolaters shal be confounded. 8. Holie Angels and iuſt men shal adore Chriſt, and reioyce. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The laſt iudgement,
The 9. key.

verses.text: A pſalme <na>(a)</na> to Dauid himſelfe. SING ye to our Lord <na>(b)</na> a new ſong: becauſe he hath done meruelous thinges. His righthand hath wrought ſaluation <na>(c)</na> to himſelfe: and his arme is holie.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Prefiguring Chriſt, who hath made his ſaluation knowen in al nations.

notes.label: b
notes.text: A new benefite of grace, making men new in ſpirite, requireth a new ſongue of gratitude.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Raiſed vp himſelfe from death.

verses.text: Our Lord hath <na>(d)</na> made knowne his ſaluation: in the ſight of the Gentiles he hath reueled his iuſtice.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Made his grace effectually knowen by raiſing men from ſinne, and deliuering them from the powre of the diuel.

verses.text: He hath remembred his mercie, and his truth to <na>(e)</na> the houſe of Iſrael. Al the ends of the earth haue ſeene the ſaluation of our God.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Some of the Iewes conuerted to Chriſtianitie. Rom. 11.

verses.text: Make ye iubilation to God al the earth: <na>(f)</na> chaunt, and <na>(g)</na> reioyce, and <na>(h)</na> ſing. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: f
notes.text: In voice.

notes.label: g
notes.text: In hart.

notes.label: h
notes.text: In inſtruments.
Cantat, exultate, pſallite.

verses.text: Sing to our Lord on harpe, on harpe and voice of pſalme:
on long drawen trumpets, and voice of cornet of horne. Make iubilation in the ſight of the king our Lord:
let the ſea be moued, and the fulnes therof: the round world, and they that dwel therin:
The riuers shal clappe with hand, the mountaynes together shal reioyce
at the ſight of our Lord: <na>(i)</na> becauſe he cometh to iudge the earth. <na>(k)</na> He wil iudge the round earth in iuſtice, and the peoples in equitie.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Chriſt directeth and diſpoſeth al thinges rightly in this world.

notes.label: k
notes.text: And wil accordingly geue iuſt ſentence in the end.

chapters.summary: Al men are againe inuited ioyfully to celebrate the meruelous conqueſt of Chriſt in al nations, 4. with hart, voice, and inſtruments. 8. al creatures acknowledging his coming to iudge the world. <na>[1]</na>

summary_continuation.text: his coming to iudge the world. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: The Church in al nations. The 6. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme to Dauid himſelfe. OVr Lord hath reigned, <na>(a)</na> let peoples be angrie: he that ſitteth vpon the Cherubs, let <na>(b)</na> the earth be moued.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Though manie enimies do rage, and impugne Chriſt:

notes.label: b
notes.text: though the whole earth be trubled thervvith, yet Chriſt vvho ſitteth Lord ouer the higheſt Angels, Cherubins and Seraphins, obteyneth the victorie, reigneth, and doth his vvil in al the earth.

verses.text: Our Lord great in Sion: and high aboue al peoples.
Let them confeſſe to thy great name: becauſe it is terrible, and holie.
And the honour of the king <na>(c)</na> loueth iudgement. Thou haſt prepared directions: thou haſt done iudgement and iuſtice <na>(d)</na> in Iacob.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Requireth diſcretion.

notes.label: d
notes.text: in fauour of thyn elect people.

verses.text: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore <na>(e)</na> his footſtoole: becauſe it is holie.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Hebrevv Doctors expound this of the Arke in the old teſtament, but the Doctors of the Church vnderſtand Chriſts humanitie, in the holie Euchariſt.

verses.text: Moyſes, and Aaron in his <na>(f)</na> prieſtes: and Samuel among them, that inuocate his name: They inuocated our Lord <na>(g)</na> and he heard them:

notes.label: f
notes.text: Here it is euident (and S. Auguſtin ſayth this place taketh avvay al doubt) that Moyſes vvas a Prieſt, againſt thoſe that for maintaining the hereſie of Laicheadshippe, denie it.
q. 23. in Levit.

notes.label: g
notes.text: By example of their praying and obtaining, the Pſalmiſt confirmeth his prophecie, that Prieſtes of the new Teſtament ſhal pray, and obtaine mercie of Chriſt for the Church.

verses.text: in a piller of a cloud he ſpake to them. They kept his teſtimonies, & the precept which he gaue them.
O Lord our God thou heardeſt them: God thou waſt propitious to them, and taking vengeance vpon al <na>(h)</na> their inuentions.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God reuenged the machinations made againſt them, punishing the rebellion of chore, Dathan and Abyron. Num. 16.

verses.text: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore ye in his holie mount: becauſe the Lord our God is holie.

chapters.summary: Chriſt reigneth, notwithſtanding his enimies repine, is adored (5. alſo his footeſtoole) 6. whom ancient Prophetes did inuocate. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt our Meſſias.
The 5. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme <na>(a)</na> in confeſſion.

notes.label: a
notes.text: of praiſe.

verses.text: MAKE ye iubilation to God <na>(b)</na> al the earth: ſerue ye our Lord in gladneſſe. Enter ye in <na>(c)</na> before his ſight, in exulration.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Not only Iewes, but alſo al Gentiles.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God eueryvvhere preſent, yet more peculiarly heareth his ſuppliants, praying in the temple, or place dedicated to his ſeruice.

verses.text: Know ye that our Lord <na>(d)</na> he is God: he made vs, and not we ourſelues. His people, and the sheepe of his paſture:

notes.label: d
notes.text: He only whom we ſerue as our Lord is the only God, and there is no other.

verses.text: enter ye into <na>(e)</na> his gates in confeſſion, his courtes in hymnes: confeſſe ye to him. Praiſe ye his name:

notes.label: e
notes.text: Peculiar dedicated place, as v. 2.

verses.text: becauſe our Lord is ſweete, his <na>(f)</na> mercie for euer, and <na>(g)</na> his truth euen vnto generation and generation.

notes.label: f
notes.text: As God is alwayes merciful in geuing, and promiſing:

notes.label: g
notes.text: ſo he is euer faithful in performing.

chapters.summary: Al are inuited to reioyce in God, Creator of al. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
One Creator of all things.
The 1. key.

verses.text: A Pſalme to Dauid himſelfe. MERCIE <na>(a)</na> and iudgement I wil ſing to thee ô Lord: I wil ſing,

notes.label: a
notes.text: Theſe two capital diuine vertues are euer ioyned in al Gods vvorkes, for both vvhich experienced tovvards him ſelfe, the Pſalmiſt rendereth thankes and praiſes.

verses.text: and I <na>(b)</na> shal vnderſtand in the immaculate way, <na>(c)</na> when thou shalt come to me. I walked through in the inocencie of my hart, in the middes of my houſe.

notes.label: b
notes.text: I wil do myn endeuoure to know the immaculate vvay,

notes.label: c
notes.text: vvhich I can not do, but by thy grace coming vnto me. For by helpe therof I did as followeth.

verses.text: I did not propoſe before mine eies any vniuſt thing: I hated them that do preuarication.
A peruerſe hart hath not cleaued to me: the malignant declining from me I knew not.
<na>(d)</na> One ſecretly detracting from his neighbour, him did I perſecute. One of a proud eye, and vnſatiable hart, with him I did not eate.

notes.label: d
notes.text: That is, al and euerie one thus wickedly diſpoſed I abhorred.

verses.text: Mine eies are towards the faithful of the earth that they may ſit with me. A man that walketh in the immaculate way, <na>(e)</na> he did miniſter to me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: I kept ſuch vnder, as a ſeruant or ſlaue.

verses.text: He that doth proudly shal not dwel in the middes of my houſe: he that ſpeaketh vniuſt thinges, hath <na>(f)</na> not directed in the ſight of mine eies.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Proſpered not, gotte no benefite by me.

verses.text: In <na>(g)</na> the morning did I kil al the ſinners of the earth: that I might deſtroy <na>(h)</na> out of the citie of our Lord, al thoſe that worke iniquitie.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Speedely and without delay I cutte of al diſordered people:

notes.label: h
notes.text: that others might not be corrupted by them.

chapters.summary: King Dauid gratfully celebrateth the two general diuine vertues, Mercie and Iuſtice: 2. by his owne example exhorteth al, eſpecially Superiors, to direct their wayes in ſinceritie, 4. and to ſeperate the wicked from conuerſation of the good. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Inſtruction to gouerne.
The 7. key.

verses.text: The prayer of the poore, when he shal be anxious, and shal make his petition before our Lord.
LORD heare my <na>(a)</na> prayer: and let my <na>(b)</na> crie come to thee.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Euerie petition is a prayer,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and that which proceedeth from more feruent affection, is called a crie, though it burſt not out into clamoure, nor perhaps into anie voice at al. For God ſaide to Moyſes, praying in mere ſilence, but with vehemencie of ſpirite (Exod. 14) VVhy crieſt thou to me?

verses.text: Turne <na>(c)</na> not away thy face from me: in what day ſoeuer I am in tribulation, incline thine eare to me. In what day ſoeuer I shal inuocate thee, heare me ſpeedely.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Though ſinne prouoke Gods wrath, becauſe we by ſinning turne from him, and not he firſt from vs: yet we pray God not ſo to leaue vs, but to geue vs new grace, that by humilitie, and penance we may returne to him, and not dye in ſinne.

verses.text: Becauſe my dayes haue vanished as <na>(d)</na> ſmoke: and my <na>(e)</na> bones are withered as <na>(f)</na> a drie burnt firebrand.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Mans dayes, and al his workes are nothing worth, but vaniſh like ſmoke, ſo long as he is in mortal ſinne:

notes.label: e
notes.text: yea his beſt workes, as if he geue almoſe, faſt, pray, and dye for the truth, yet al thoſe auaile nothing (1. Cor. 13.) but are

notes.label: f
notes.text: like dryed ſtickes, or chippes, ſitte to kindle the fire.

verses.text: I <na>(g)</na> am ſtriken as graſſe, and my hart is withered: becauſe <na>(h)</na> I haue forgotten to eate my bread.

notes.label: g
notes.text: My ſoule ſeparated by ſinne from God, withereth as graſſe, that is cutte from the roote:

notes.label: h
notes.text: becauſe I haue loſt al ſauour and appetite to ſpiritual meate.

verses.text: For <na>(i)</na> the voyce of my groning, my <na>(k)</na> bone hath cleaued to my flesh.

notes.label: i
notes.text: In this miſerable ſtate.

notes.label: k
notes.text: I am as bones and flesh cleauing together without moyſture, or radical humour.

verses.text: I am become like <na>(l)</na> a pellicane of the wildernes: I am become as <na>(m)</na> a nightcrow in the houſe.

notes.label: l
notes.text: I fled from conuerſation of men for ſorow, and shame of my ſinnes:

notes.label: m
notes.text: as a crow that only flieth by night: or as an owle, or batte.

verses.text: I haue watched, and am become as <na>(n)</na> a ſparow ſolitarie in the houſetoppe.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Alſo as a ſparow hauing loſt her mate, remaineth mourning and ſolitarie in the accuſtomed neſt, or mere vnto it,

verses.text: Al the day did mine enemies vpbrayde me: and they <na>(o)</na> that praiſed me, ſware againſt me.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Thoſe that were wont to praiſe or flatter me, now are as ſworne enimies againſt me.

verses.text: Becauſe I did <na>(p)</na> eate ashes as bread, & mingled <na>(q)</na> my drinke with weeping.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Bread ſauoured to me no better then ashes.

notes.label: q
notes.text: and drinke gaue me no comfort, but ſtil I wept.

verses.text: At <na>(r)</na> the face of thy wrath and indignation: becauſe <na>(s)</na> lifting me vp thou haſt throwne me <na>(t)</na> downe.

notes.label: r
notes.text: I am moſt eſpecially afflicted, becauſe thou art angrie.

notes.label: s
notes.text: In that thou didſt ſometime aduance me in proſperitie,

notes.label: t
notes.text: my fall is ſo much greater, and more grieuous.

verses.text: My daies haue declined <na>(v)</na> as a ſhadow: and I am withered <na>(w)</na> as graſſe.

notes.label: v
notes.text: As a ſhadow declineth to nothing, and al becometh darknes, when the ſunne, and other light departeth, euen ſo I, that am but a ſhadow, decline to mere darknes, when thy fauoure parteth from me.

notes.label: w
notes.text: and I loſe my beautie, as graſſe cutte from the ground withereth.

verses.text: <na>(x)</na> But thou ô Lord endureſt for euer: and <na>(y)</na> thy memorial in generation and generation.

notes.label: x
notes.text: But I am meruelouſly comforted, conſidering that thou our Meſſias, the Sonne of God, art immutable for euer:

notes.label: y
notes.text: and thy memorable promiſe of redeeming mankind, wil haue effect in al generations.

verses.text: Thou <na>(z)</na> ryſing vp shal haue mercie on Sion: becauſe it is <na>(a)</na> time to haue mercie on it, becauſe <na>(b)</na> the time cometh.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Thou riſing to helpe, who ſemedſt to haue forgote, wilt protect the Church, and euerie faithful ſoule.

notes.label: a
notes.text: becauſe thou haſt differred long:

notes.label: b
notes.text: and becauſe the time by thee deſigned ſemeth to approch

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(c)</na> the ſtones therof haue pleaſed thy ſeruantes: and they shal haue pittie on <na>(d)</na> the earth <na>(e)</na> therof.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Men that ſhal heare thyn Apoſtles preach, shal proue good and fitte matter, for the building of thy Church:

notes.label: d
notes.text: and the ſimpleſt poore people, as it were, the earth or duſt;

notes.label: e
notes.text: shal participate of this mercie.

verses.text: And <na>(f)</na> the Gentiles shal feare thy name ô Lord, and al <na>(g)</na> the kinges of the earth thy glorie.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Beſides thoſe Iewes that ſhal beleue in Chriſt, much more the Gentiles ſhal feare and ſerue him.

notes.label: g
notes.text: His glorie is ſo euident that al kinges know it, though al be not conuerted.

verses.text: Becauſe our Lord hath built Sion: and he shal be ſeene in his glorie.
He hath had reſpect to the prayer <na>(h)</na> of the humble: and he hath not deſpiſed their petition.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Of holie Patriarches, Prieſtes, Prophetes, and of al true penitents,

verses.text: Let theſe thinges be written vnto an other generation: and the people, that shal <na>(i)</na> be created, shal praiſe our Lord.

notes.label: i
notes.text: That shal be made a new creature in Chriſt.

verses.text: Becauſe he hath lookedforth from his high holie place: our Lord from heauen hath looked vpon the earth.
That he might heare the gronings of the fettered: that he might looſe the children of them that are ſlayne:
That they may <na>(k)</na> shewforth the name of our Lord in Sion: and his praiſe in Ieruſalem.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The faithful people of the Church, according to their habilitie endeuour to ſerue Chriſt.

verses.text: In the aſſembling of the people together in one, and kinges to ſerue our Lord.
He anſwered him in the way of his ſtrength: Shew me the fewnes of my daies.
Cal me not backe <na>(l)</na> in the halfe of my daies: thy yeares are vnto generation and generation.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Grant me time and meanes to be mature in vertue in this life.

verses.text: In the beginning ô Lord thou didſt found the earth: and the heauens are the workes of thy hands.
They <na>(m)</na> shal perish, but thou art permanent: and they shal al waxe old as a garment. <cr>[1]</cr> And as a veſture thou shalt change them, and they shal be changed:

notes.label: m
notes.text: Be changed in qualitie.

verses.text: but thou art the ſelfe ſame, and thy yeares shal not faile.
The children of thy ſeruantes shal inhabite: and <na>(n)</na> their ſeede shal be directed for euer.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The Church of Chriſt perpetual.

chapters.summary: A ſinner in affliction of mind prayeth God to deliuer him, 10. deſolate of al other helpe. 13. conceiueth comforth in Gods eternal goodnes, and ſingular mercie, in redeming mankind, and propagating the Church. 24. Prayeth to be made mature in vertue before he dye, that he may liue with God: 26. who only and wholly being immutable, eſtablisheth his ſeruantes for euer. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The fifth penitential Pſalm.
The 7. key.

verses.text: To <na>(a)</na> Dauid himſelf. MY ſoule <na>(b)</na> bleſſe thou our Lord: and <na>(c)</na> al thinges, that are within me, his holie name.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Inſpired to Dauid, and written by him.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Shew forth praiſes, and thankes:

notes.label: c
notes.text: al my cogitations, affections, ſenſes, and powres.

verses.text: My ſoule bleſſe thou our Lord: and forget not al his retributions.
Who is <na>(d)</na> propitious to al thine iniquities: who <na>(e)</na> healeth al thine infirmities.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The firſt benefite of grace is remiſſion of ſinnes:

notes.label: e
notes.text: the ſecond, is curing euil habites, or diſpoſitions.

verses.text: Who <na>(f)</na> redemeth thy life from deadly falling: who <na>(g)</na> crowneth thee in mercie and commiſerations.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The third, to conſerue from falling againe:

notes.label: g
notes.text: the fourth, to geue victorie and reward in abundant meaſure.

verses.text: Who <na>(h)</na> replenisheth thy deſire in good thinges: thy youth <na>(i)</na> shal be rewed as the eagles.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The fifth, to grant al lawful petitions temporal and ſpiritual, which are good for the ſoule,

notes.label: i
notes.text: the ſixth, reſurrection of flesh in glorie.

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(k)</na> doth mercies: and <na>(l)</na> iudgement to al that ſuffer wrong.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Our Lord, whoſe ſpecial propertie is to shew mercie,

notes.label: l
notes.text: when the ſame is neglected, he reuengeth the wrongs, deliuering the oppreſſed, and puniſhing the oppreſſors.

verses.text: He made his waies <na>(m)</na> knowne to Moyſes, his willes to the children of Iſrael.

notes.label: m
notes.text: By geuing them a written law.

verses.text: Our Lord is <na>(n)</na> pitieful, and <na>(o)</na> merciful: <na>(p)</na> long ſuffering, and very merciful.

notes.label: n
notes.text: God is naturally pittiful, to releeue the afflicted.

notes.label: o
notes.text: merciful towards ſinners.

notes.label: p
notes.text: loath to be angrie, or to punish.

verses.text: He wil <na>(q)</na> not be angrie alwayes: neither wil he threaten for euer.

notes.label: q
notes.text: God puniſheth not penitents with eternal paine, but with temporal: for though (as in the next verſe) our ſinnes of their owne nature, deſerue eternal puniſhment, yet Chriſt paying our ranſome, true penitents are only punished temporally.

verses.text: He hath not done to vs according to our ſinnes: neither according to our iniquities hath he rewarded vs.
For according to the height of heauen from the earth: hath he ſtrengthned his mercie vpon them that feare him.
As far <na>(r)</na> as the Eaſt is diſtant from the Weſt: hath he made our iniquities far from vs.

notes.label: r
notes.text: See here the perfect washing away, and ſeparation of ſinnes.

verses.text: As a father hath compaſſion of his children, ſo hath our Lord compaſſion on them that feare him:
becauſe he hath knowen <na>(s)</na> our making. He remembred that we are duſt:

notes.label: s
notes.text: In reguard of our frailtie he hath compaſſion: yet his mercie only auaileth to them that feare him: as in the next wordes before, and v. 17.

verses.text: man, his daies are as graſſe, as the floure of the filde ſo shal he florish.
Becauſe the ſpirit shal paſſe in him, and he shal not ſtand: and he shal know his place no more.
But the mercie of our Lord from euerlaſting, and vnto euerlaſting vpon them that feare him. And his iuſtice is vpon the childrens children, to them that keepe his teſtament.
And are mindful of his commandmentes, to <na>(t)</na> doe them.

notes.label: t
notes.text: A iuſt man not only knoweth, and remembreth, but alſo doth the commandments.

verses.text: Our Lord hath prepared his ſeate in heauen: and his kindom shal haue dominion ouer al.
Bleſſe our Lord al ye his Angels: mightie in powre, doing his word, that feare the voice of his wordes.
Bleſſe our Lord al ye his hoaſtes: you his miniſters, that doe his wil.
Bleſſe ye our Lord <na>(v)</na> al his workes: in euerie place <na>(w)</na> of his dominion, my ſoule bleſſe thou our Lord.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Al creatures, though naturally ſenſeles, yet praiſe God, becauſe they are his worke,

notes.label: w
notes.text: and becauſe they are in his dominion.

chapters.summary: Thankes to God for priuate, 6. and publike benefites. 17. His mercie, iuſtice, and other proprieties are immutable. 20. Angels, and al other creatures are inuited to praiſe him. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Gratitude for God's benefits.
The 7. key.

verses.text: To Dauid him ſelf. MY ſoule bleſſe thou our Lord: ô Lord my God thou art magnified excedingly.
Thou haſt put on <na>(a)</na> confeſſion and beautie: being clothed with light as with a garment: Stretching out the heauen as a skinne:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Thou poſſeſſeſt al maieſtie, and matter of praiſe.

verses.text: which couereſt the higher partes therof <na>(b)</na> with waters. Which <na>(c)</na> makeſt the cloude for thee to aſcend on: which walkeſt vpon the winges of windes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Thou haſt compaſſed the ſphere of the fixed ſtarres, with a ſphere of chriſtalline ſubſtance which is as water congeled.

notes.label: c
notes.text: According to our capacitie the prophet deſcribeth the ſpeedie coming, or vvorking of God as if he came in a ſwift cloud, or vvith winges of the vvind, to ſignifie that he vvorketh wel and vvhen he pleaſeth vvithout delay: He ſaide, and thinges were made: he commanded and they vvere created, Pſal. 32.

verses.text: Which makeſt ſpirites thine <na>(d)</na> Angels: and thy <na>(e)</na> miniſters a burning fyre.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Thy meſſengers to execute thy vvil:

notes.label: e
notes.text: & the ſame Angels are as a burning fire in operation yea they diſpatch more eaſily, and more ſpedely then vve can conceiue,

verses.text: Which haſt founded the earth vpon <na>(f)</na> the ſtabilitie therof: it shal not be inclined for euer and euer

notes.label: f
notes.text: Moſt firmly eſtablished by natural weight, in the center of the world:

verses.text: The <na>(g)</na> depth, <na>(h)</na> as a garment, is his clothing: vpon the mountaines shal waters ſtand.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The water hi

notes.label: h
notes.text: should naturally couer al the earth:

verses.text: At <na>(i)</na> thy reprehention they shal flee: at the voice of thy thunder they shal feare.

notes.label: i
notes.text: But by thy commandment the waters are conteined in their limited places.

verses.text: The <na>(k)</na> mountaines aſcend: and the plaine fildes deſcend into the place, which thou haſt founded for them.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The waters being conteyned in their appointed chanels, both hilles and fieldes appeare which otherwiſe would be couered.

verses.text: Thou haſt ſet a bound, which <na>(l)</na> they shal not paſſe ouer: neither shal they returne to couer the earth.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The wate…

verses.text: Which ſendeſtforth fontaines in the valles: betwen the middeſt of mountaines shal waters paſſe.
Al the beaſtes of the filde shal drinke: the wilde aſſes shal <na>(m)</na> expect in their thirſt.

notes.label: m
notes.text: hope for and receiue

verses.text: Ouer them shal the foules of the ayre inhabite: out of the middes of rockes they shal geueforth voices.
Watering the mountaines from his higher places: of the fruite of thy worke shal the earth be filled:
Bringing forth graſſe for beaſtes, and herbe for the ſeruice of men. That thou mayſt bring forth <na>(n)</na> bread out of the earth:

notes.label: n
notes.text: By theſe three principal kindes of foode, breade, wine, and oyl, al ſortes of nutriment are vnderſtood.

verses.text: and <na>(o)</na> wine may make the hart of man ioyful: That he may make the face chereful with <na>(p)</na> oile: and bread may confirme the hart of man.

notes.label: o
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: p
notes.text: See previous note

verses.text: The trees of the filde shal be filled, and the ceders of Libanus, which he hath planted:
there ſparowes shal make their neſt. The houſe of the hearne is the leader of them:
the high mountaines for hartes: the rocke a refuge for the Irchins.
He made the moone for ſeaſons: the ſunne knoweth his going downe.
Thou didſt appoint darkenes, and night was made: in it shal al the beaſtes of the wood paſſe.
The whelpes of lions roaring, to rauen, and to ſeeke of God meate for themſelues.
The ſunne is riſen, and they are gathered together: and in their couches they shal be placed.
Man shal goe forth to his worke: and to his working vntil euening.
How magnified are thy workes ô Lord! thou haſt made al thinges in wiſedom: the earth is filled with <na>(q)</na> thy poſſeſſion.

notes.label: q
notes.text: With thy creatures.

verses.text: This great ſea, and very large, there are <na>(r)</na> creeping beaſtes, wherof <na>(s)</na> there is no number. Litle beaſtes with great:

notes.label: r
notes.text: Fiſhes, ſerpents, wormes, and al liuing creatures that lacke feete.

notes.label: s
notes.text: No kind of liuing creatures multiplieth ſo much as fishes Ariſtotel li. 9. Animal. c. 17.

verses.text: there shippes shal paſſe. This <na>(t)</na> dragon, whom thou madeſt to <na>(v)</na> delude:

notes.label: t
notes.text: A moſt huge fish called Leuiathan. Iob. 40. v. 20.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Albeit in the water he paſſeth mans ſtreingth, yet depriued of water he is not able to defend himſelfe. v. 19.

verses.text: al expect of thee that thou geue them meate in ſeaſon.
Thou geuing vnto them, they shal gather it: thou opening thy hand, al shal be filled with bountie.
But thou turning away the face, they shal be trubled: thou shalt take away their ſpirite, and they shal faile, and shal returne into their duſt.
Thou shalt ſendforth thy ſpirit, and they shal be created: and thou shalt renewe the face of the earth.
Be the glorie of our Lord for euer: our Lord wil reioice in his workes:
Who looketh vpon the earth, & maketh it to tremble: who toucheth the mountaines, and they ſmoke.
I wil chaunte to our Lord in my life: I wil ſing to my God as long as I am.
Let my ſpeach be acceptable to him: but I wil take delight in our Lord.
<na>(w)</na> Let ſinners faile from the earth, and the vniuſt, ſo that they be not: my ſoule bleſſe thou our Lord.

notes.label: w
notes.text: A prediction that impenitent ſinners ſhal be damned, wherin the Prophet conforming his wil to Gods, vttereth it in forme of a prayer.

chapters.summary: The Pſalmiſt inuiteth himſelf and others to praiſe God, for his meruelous workes in the heauens, 5. the earth, and water, 9. limiting their bondes, producing al thinges neceſſarie for al liuing creatures, in conuenient ſeaſons. 27. with continual prouidence of al. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's works marvelous.
The 2. key.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Alleluia. CONFESSE ye to our Lord, and inuocate his name: <na>(b)</na> shew forth his workes among the Gentiles. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Alleluia ſignifieth more then Laudate Dominum, Praiſe ye our Lord. For by theſe two hebrew wordes, Allelu a, the Prophet inuiteth al men to praiſe God, with gladnes, and iubilation, with hart, voice, and geſture, with inſtruments, and howſoeuer we are able. And therfore S Ierom, S. Auguſtin, and al Catholique writers kepe the ſame worde, and tranſlate it not, neither in the titles of Pſalmes, not ordinarily in anie place of holie Scripture. This is the firſt Pſalme thus titled, and is the ſame Pſalme in ſenſe, and in good part of the wordes, which the royal Prophet made, and cauſed to be ſongue, when he brought the Arke of God from the houſe of Obededom into his owne houſe. 1. Par. 16. v. 8.

notes.label: b
notes.text: How much more gratful is it now to God, that we celebrate the greater myſteries of the new Teſtament.
For an expoſition of this Pſalme read the places quoted in the inner margen.

verses.text: Chaunt to him, and ſing to him: tel ye al his meruelous workes.
Prayſe ye him in his holie name: let the hart of them reioice that ſeeke our Lord.
Seeke ye our Lord, and be confirmed: ſeeke <na>(c)</na> his face alwayes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: His preſent helpe.

verses.text: Remember ye his meruelous workes, which he hath done: his wonders, and the iudgments of his mouth.
The ſeede of Abraham, his ſeruantes: the children of Iacob his elect.
He is the Lord our God: in <na>(d)</na> al the earth are his iudgementes.

notes.label: d
notes.text: not only in Iſrael, but in al the world.

verses.text: He hath bene mindeful for euer of his teſtament: of the word, which he commanded <na>(e)</na> vnto a thouſand generations. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: e
notes.text: For euer, to the end of the world.

verses.text: Which he diſpoſed to Abraham: and of his oath to Iſaac.
And he appointed it to Iacob for a precept: and to Iſrael for an eternal teſtament.
Saying: To thee wil I geue the land of Chanaan, the corde of your inheritance.
When they were <na>(f)</na> of ſmal number, very few and ſeiourners therof:

notes.label: f
notes.text: But 70. perſons.

verses.text: And they paſſed from nation into nation, & from kingdom to an other people.
He leift not a man to hurt them: and he rebuked kings for their ſake.
Touch not my annointed, and toward my prophetes be not malignant.
And <na>(g)</na> he called a famine vpon the land: and he deſtroyed al the ſtrength of bread. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: g
notes.text: By his prouidence ſuffered.

verses.text: He ſent a man before them: Ioſeph was ſold to be a ſeruant.
They humbled his feete in fetters, yron paſſed through his ſoule, <cr>[1]</cr>
vntil his word came. The word of our Lord inflamed him:
the king ſent, and looſed him; the prince of the people, and releaſed him.
He appointed him lord of his houſe: and prince of al his poſſeſſion.
That he might inſtruct his princes as himſelfe: and might teach his ancientes wiſedom.
And Iſrael entered into Ægypt, and Iacob was a ſeiourner in the land <na>(h)</na> of Cham. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: h
notes.text: Ægypt, poſſeſſed by Meſraim Chams ſecond ſonne. Gen. 10. v. 13.
Gen 46.

verses.text: And he increaſed his people excedingly: and ſtrengthned them ouer their enemies. <cr>[1]</cr>
He <na>(i)</na> turned their hart, that they hated his people: and to worke guile toward his ſeruantes.

notes.label: i
notes.text: May it be vnderſtood, or beleued (ſaith S. Auguſtin) that God turneth the hart of man to committe ſinnes? Or is it no ſinne, or is it a ſmal ſinne, to hate the people of God? Or to worke guile towards his ſeruants? VVho wil ſay this? VVhat then, is God author of theſe ſo greeuous ſinnes, who is not to be ſuppoſed the author of a moſt ſmal ſinne? This lerned Father therfore anſwereth, that God peruerted not a right hart, but turned that was of it ſelfe peruerſe, to the hatred of his people, where he might vſe that euil wel, not by making them euil, but by beſtowing vpon his owne people good thinges, which the euil might eaſily enuie. VVhich hatred of theirs how God vſed both to the exerciſe of his people (which is profitable to vs) & to the glorie of his owne name, the thinges that folow do teach vs, which are here remembred to his praiſe.

verses.text: He ſent Moyſes his ſeruant: Aaron, <na>(k)</na> him ſelfe whom he choſe. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: k
notes.text: In whom God eſtablished the Prieſthood of Moyſes law.

verses.text: He did put in them the wordes of his ſignes, and of his wonders in the Land of Cham.
He ſent <na>(l)</na> darkenes, and obſcured: and did <na>(m)</na> not exaſperate his wordes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The ninth plague of the Ægyptians.

notes.label: m
notes.text: God willingly, not as one loath or vnwilling, performed al that he threatned.

verses.text: He turned their <na>(n)</na> waters into bloud: and killed their fishes.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The firſt plague.

verses.text: Their land broughtforth <na>(o)</na> frogges in <na>[1]</na> the inner chambers of their kinges.

notes.label: o
notes.text: The ſecond plague.
Dauid knew this by reuelation, or by tradition for it is not in Exodus.

verses.text: He ſayd, and <na>(p)</na> the <na>[1]</na> cænomyia came: and the <na>(q)</na> ciniſes in al their coaſtes.

notes.label: p
notes.text: The fourth plague.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The third plague.
p A ſvvarme of flies.

verses.text: He made theyr raynes <na>(r)</na> haile: fire burning in their land.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The ſeuenth plague.

verses.text: And he ſtroke their vines, and their figtrees: and he deſtroyed the wood of their coaſtes.
He ſaid, & <na>(s)</na> the locuſt came, and the <na>(t)</na> bruchus wherof there was no number.

notes.label: s
notes.text: The eight plague.

notes.label: t
notes.text: A worme that ſpoyleth corne, graſſe, and fruict.

verses.text: And it did eate al the graſſe in their land: and it did eate al the fruicte of their land.
And he ſtroke euerie <na>(v)</na> firſt begotten in their land: the firſt fruictes of al their labour.

notes.label: v
notes.text: The tenth plague. · The fifth & ſixt of peſtilence and boyles are omitted.

verses.text: And he brought them forth with gold and ſiluer, and there was not in their tribes a feeble perſon.
Ægypt was glad at their departure: becauſe the feare of them lay vpon them.
He ſpred a cloude for their protection, and fire to shine vnto them by night. <cr>[1]</cr>

cross_refs.text: Exod. 13. v. 21. Exod. 16. v. 13. Exod. 17. v. 6. Gen. 12.

verses.text: They made petition, and the quaile came: and he filled them with the bread of heauen.
He diuided the rocke, and waters flowed: riuers ranne in the drie ground.
Becauſe he was mindful of his holie word, which he had vttered to Abraham his ſeruant.
And he broughtforth his people in exultation, and his elect in ioy.
And he gaue them the countries of the Nations: and they poſſeſſed the labours of peoples: <cr>[1]</cr>
That they might keepe his iuſtifications, and ſeeke after his lawe.

chapters.summary: The Iſraelites are exhorted to ſing praiſes to God, 5. for his meruelous benefites towards Abraham, Iſaac, and Iacob. 11. whoſe particular familie, being then ſmal, went from Chanaan into Ægypt (17. Whither Ioſeph by Gods prouidence was caried before) there increaſed in number, was perſecuted, 26. deliuered by Moyſes and Aaron, working manie great miracles, 36. protected, and fedde in the deſert, 44. and finally poſſeſſed Chanaan. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's ſpecial benefits towards the Jews.
The 4. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. CONFESSE ye to our Lord <na>(a)</na> becauſe he is good: becauſe his mercie is for euer. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: God is of himſelfe and eſſentially good, al other goodnes is participated of him.
Iudith. v. 21.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Who shal ſpeake the powers of our Lord, shal make al his praiſes to be heard?

notes.label: b
notes.text: No creature can fully expreſſe Gods perfections.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Bleſſed are they, that keepe iudgement, and <na>(d)</na> doe iuſtice at al time.

notes.label: c
notes.text: It is a happie ſtate in this life, either to kepe Gods law :

notes.label: d
notes.text: or to repent and do worthie penance for tranſgreſſing.

verses.text: Remember vs ô Lord <na>(e)</na> in the good pleaſure of thy people: viſite vs in thy ſaluation:

notes.label: e
notes.text: According to thy wonted beneuolence, promiſed to thy people.

verses.text: To <na>(f)</na> ſee in the goodnes of thyne elect, to reioyce in the ioy of thy nation: that thou maiſt be praiſed with thine inheritance.

notes.label: f
notes.text: That we may ſee, and enioy the benefites promiſed to thyne elect.

verses.text: We haue <na>(g)</na> ſinned with our fathers: we haue <na>(h)</na> dealt vniuſtly, we haue <na>(i)</na> done iniquitie.

notes.label: g
notes.text: We haue erred and hurt ourſelues :

notes.label: h
notes.text: we haue wronged our neighboures :

notes.label: i
notes.text: we haue offended againſt God.

verses.text: Our fathers in Ægypt did not vnderſtand thy meruelous workes: they were not mindeful of the multitude of thy mercie. And they prouoked thee to wrath going vp vnto the ſea, the Read ſea.
And he ſaued them <na>(k)</na> for his name ſake; that he might make his power knowen. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: k
notes.text: Albeit the people by their murmuring deſerued more punishment, yet God for the glorie of his owne name ſaued them from vtter deſtruction.

verses.text: And he rebuked the Read ſea, and it was made drie: and he led them in the depths as in a deſert.
And he ſaued them from the hand of them that hated them: and he redemed them out of the hand of the enemie.
And water ouerwhelmed thoſe that afflicted them: there did not one of them remaine.
And they beleued his wordes: and they ſang his praiſe.
They had <na>(l)</na> quickly donne, they forgot his workes: and they <na>(m)</na> expected not his counſel.

notes.label: l
notes.text: They perſeuered not long in their dutie towards God, ſeing his omnipotent powre by his meruelous workes :

notes.label: m
notes.text: nor were content with his prouidence, but carnally coueted thinges, not neceſſarie.

verses.text: And they coueted concupiſcence in the deſert: and tempted God in the place without water. <cr>[1]</cr>
He gaue them their petition: and ſent ſaturitie into their <na>(n)</na> ſoules. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: n
notes.text: According to their carnal deſires.

verses.text: And they prouoked Moyſes in the campe: Aaron the <na>(o)</na> holie of our Lord.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Holie by his function.

verses.text: The earth was opened, and ſwalowed Dathan: and ouerwhelmed the congregation of Abiron.
And a fire flamed vp in their ſinagogue: the flame burnt the ſinners.
And they made a calfe in Horeb: and they adored <na>(p)</na> the ſculptil. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: p
notes.text: They adored the image that repreſented a calf, not God.

verses.text: And they <na>(q)</na> changed their glorie into the ſimilitude of a calfe that eateth graſſe.

notes.label: q
notes.text: God being their true glorie, they changed him, for a falſe god of the Ægyptians (who eſpecially honoured a calfe called Apis) making an image therof, and attributed their deliuerie from Ægypt to this imagined god. Exo. 32. v. 4. 8. Of which and the like foolish, and abominable idolatrie S. Paul writeth, Rom. 1. v. 23. They changed the glorie of the incorruptible God, into a ſimilitude of the image of a corruptible man, and of foules, and of foure footed beaſtes, and of them that crepe : where we ſee what maner of imagies holie Scriptures condemne, and not the imagies of Chriſt and his Sainctes.

verses.text: They forgat God, which ſaued them, which did great thinges in Ægypt,
meruelous thinges in the land of Cham, terrible thinges in the Read ſea.
And <na>(r)</na> he ſayd to deſtroy them: if Moyſes his elect had not ſtood in the way before him: <cr>[1]</cr>To turne away his wrath that he should not deſtroy them:

notes.label: r
notes.text: He ſayd, he would deſtroy them, but for Moyſes prayer ſpared them.

verses.text: and they eſtemed for naught the land that was to be deſired. <cr>[1]</cr> They did not beleue his word,
and they murmured in their tabernacles: they heard not the voice of our Lord.
And he lifted vp his hand ouer them: to ouerthrowe them in the deſert: <cr>[1]</cr>
And to caſt doune their ſeede among the Nations: and to diſperſe them in the countries.
And they were profeſſed to <na>(s)</na> Beelphegor: and they did eate the ſacrifices <na>(t)</na> of the dead. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: s
notes.text: The Idol of Moabites, and Madianitees,

notes.label: t
notes.text: As God is in deede the liuing God, that liueth of himſelfe, and geueth life to others : ſo falſe goddes are called dead goddes, that can not geue life to anie, but doe kil al that ſerue them at leaſt ſpiritually, and often corporally.

verses.text: And they prouoked him in their inuentions: and ruine was multiplied on them.
And Phinees ſtood, and <na>(v)</na> pacified: and the ſlaughter ceaſed.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Phinees moued by the zele of God (as the holie text witneſſeth. Nu. 25. v. 11.) in killing the adulterers pleaſed God, and merited reward.

verses.text: And it was reputed to him vnto iuſtice, in generation and generation euen for euer.
And they prouoked him at the waters of contradiction: and <na>(w)</na> Moyſes was vexed for them: <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: w
notes.text: Moyſes afflicted in ſpirite, by the enormious murmuring of the people, doubted whether God would geue them water out of the rocke or no, not doubting of his powre, but of his wil : and ſo when he ſhould haue ſpoken to the rocke, Num. 20. v. 8. he ſpoke to the incredulous people. v. 10. and therin offended God. for which he was temporally puniſhed. v. 12. Deut. 1. v. 37. & c. 3. v. 26. c. 4. v. 21.

verses.text: becauſe they exaſperated his ſpirit. And he plainly affirmed in his lips:
they deſtroyed not the nations, of which our Lord ſpake to them.
And they were mingled among the nations, and learned their workes: <cr>[1]</cr>
and they ſerued their ſculptils: and it became a ſcandal to them.
And they immolated their ſonnes, and their daughters to diuels.
And <na>(x)</na> they shed innocent bloud: the bloud of their ſonnes and of their daughters, which they ſacrificed to the ſculptils of Chanaan. And the land was infected with bloud,

notes.label: x
notes.text: Some Iewes offered theſe moſt cruel, vnnatural, and abominable ſacrifices ; perhaps in the times of Iudges, when they were mingled with idolatrous people, and ſerued their goddes ; Iud. 2. v. 11. c. 3. v. 6. But it is more expreſſe after Dauids time, wherof he here prophecieth, and was verified by Achaz. 4. Reg. 16 v. 3. and by Manaſſes. 4. Reg. 21. v. 6. VVhich with other idolatrie king Ioſias deſtroyed. 4. Reg. 23. v. 10.

verses.text: and was contaminated in their workes: and they did fornicat in their inuentions.
And our Lord was wrath with furie vpon his people: and he abhorred his inheritance.
And he deliuered them into the handes of the nations: and they that hated them, had the dominion of them.
And their enimies afflicted them: and they were humbled vnder their handes:
he did often deliuer them. But they exaſperated him in their counſel: and they were humbled in their iniquities.
And he <na>(y)</na> ſaw when they were afflicted: and he heard their prayer.

notes.label: y
notes.text: God reſpected them with his merciful eye, and gaue them grace to repent.

verses.text: And he was mindeful of his teſtament: and it repented him according to the multitude of his mercie.
And he gaue them into mercies in the ſight of al, that had taken them. <na>(z)</na>

notes.label: z
notes.text: Here the Pſalmiſt concludeth both the hiſtorie and prophecie of this Pſalme, with prayer and praiſe, as foloweth :

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> Saue vs ô Lord our God: and geather vs out of the Nations: That we may confeſſe to thy holie name: & may glorie in thy prayſe.

notes.text: A verie fitte prayer in time of ſchiſme.

verses.text: Bleſſed be our Lord the God of Iſrael from euerlaſting vnto euerlaſting: and al the people shal ſay: Be it, be it.

chapters.summary: The prophet exhorteth the people to render thankes and praiſes to God, 6. for remitting their manifold ſinnes, in the deſert. 34. and in the conquered land : 38. foreshewing like ſinnes to come, Gods wrath and punishment for the ſame. 44. and that he wil geue grace of repentance : to ſome 47. for which he prayeth, and praiſeth God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Iſraelites often ſinned, and were mercifully punished.
The 4. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. CONFESSE <na>(a)</na> ye to our Lord becauſe he is good: becauſe his mercie is for euer. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Praiſe God by confeſſing his mercie, prouidence, and goodnes.

verses.text: Let them ſay that are <na>(b)</na> redemed of our Lord, whom he redemed out of the hand of the enemie: and out of the countries he gathered them:

notes.label: b
notes.text: God of his mercie promiſed the Redemer of mankind ſtreight after Adams fal.

verses.text: From <na>(c)</na> the riſing of the ſunne, and the going downe: from the north, and the ſea.

notes.label: c
notes.text: VVhich redemption was intended for al, and faileth not of Gods part in anie, but of mens owne wilful refuſing to be duly penitent, and to kepe Gods precepts.

verses.text: They <na>(d)</na> wandered in the wildernes, in a place without water: the way of citie for habitation they found not.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Literally of ſuch as wander in this world, hauing no ſetled place to dwel in : ſpiritually of al mankind after his fal.

verses.text: Hungrie, and thirſtie: their ſoule fainted in them.
And <na>(e)</na> they cried to our Lord when they were in tribulation: and he deliuered them out of their neceſſities.

notes.label: e
notes.text: VVhenſoeuer they cal vpon God, he helpeth them, as is beſt for their ſpiritual health.

verses.text: And he conducted them into the right way: to goe into a citie of habitation.
Let <na>(f)</na> the mercies of our Lord confeſſe to him: and his meruelous workes to the children of men.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Al Gods benefites, which are of his mercie, not of mans deſerte, are iuſt matter of praiſing God.

verses.text: Becauſe he hath filled the emptie ſoule: and the hungrie ſoule he hath filled with good thinges.
Them that ſate in darkenes, and in the shadow of death: bound in needines, and yron.
Becauſe they <na>(g)</na> exaſperated the wordes of God: and they prouoked the counſel of the Higheſt.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Calamities in this world are commonly inflicted for ſinnes.

verses.text: And their hart was humbled in labours: they were weakened, neither was there anie to helpe.
And they cried to our Lord when they were in tribulation: and he deliuered them out of their neceſſities.
And he brought them out of darkenes, and the shadow of death: and brake their bondes aſunder.
Let the mercies of our Lord confeſſe to him: and his meruelous workes to the children of men.
Becauſe he hath deſtroyed the gates of braſſe: and the barres of yron he hath broken.
He hath receiued them out of the way of their iniquitie: for they were humbled for their iniuſtices.
Their ſoule did abhorre al meate: & they approched euen to the gates of death.
And they cried to our Lord when they were in tribulation: and he deliuered them out of their neceſſities.
He ſent his word, and healed them: and deliuered them out of their deſtructions.
Let the mercies of our Lord confeſſe to him: and his meruelous workes to the children of men.
And let them ſacrifice the ſacrifice of praiſe: and shew forth his workes in exulation.
They that goe downe into the ſea in shippes, making trafike in the great waters.
They haue ſene the workes of our Lord, and his meruelous thinges in the depth.
He ſayd, and the blaſt of the ſtorme ſtood: and the waues therof were exalted.
They aſcend euen to the heauens, and they deſcend euen to the depthes: their ſoule pyned away in euils.
They were trubled, and were moued as a drunken man: and al their wiſedom was deuoured.
And <na>(h)</na> they cried to our Lord when they were in tribulation, and he brought them out of their neceſſities.

notes.label: h
notes.text: As before in the 6, 13, and 19, verſes,

verses.text: And he turned his ſtorme into calme: and the waues therof were quiet.
And they reioyced becauſe they were quiet: and he conducted them into the hauen of their wil.
Let <na>(i)</na> the mercies of our Lord confeſſe to him: and his meruelous workes to the children of men.

notes.label: i
notes.text: This verſe alſo is foure times in this Pſalme. v. 8. 15. 21. and 31. to admonish vs, that as there is one meanes to eſcape from al dangers by crying to God, as v. 6. 13. 19. and 28 : with mourning and penance : ſo there is one cauſe of praiſe and thankes for our deliuerie, which is Gods mercie and grace.

verses.text: And let them exalt him in the church of the people: and the chayre of the ancientes let them praiſe him.
<na>(k)</na> He turned <na>(l)</na> the riuers into a deſert: and the iſſues of waters into drineſſe.

notes.label: k
notes.text: God to shew ſometimes his powre, alſo to benefite ſome, and to puniſh others, changeth the accuſtomed courſe of thinges, and ſtates of men, at his diuine pleaſure : as here the Royal prophet reciteth ſome examples. And ſome others are recorded in diuers times and places.

notes.label: l
notes.text: No doubt much change was made in the earth by Noes flood. And manie thincke that the land of Chanaan, was made more fruictful in the time of the Iewes inhabiting, and now is more barrane againe.

verses.text: The <na>(m)</na> fruiteful land into a ſalt ground, for the malice of them that inhabite it.

notes.label: m
notes.text: He alludeth to the countrie about Sodome, and Gomorre, which was moſt fruictful, and moſt pleaſant, Gen. 13. v. 10, but shortly after vvas burnt vvith fire and brimſton, Gen. 19, v. 24, ſubuerted, and turned into a dead and ſalt ſea.

verses.text: He turned the deſert into pooles of waters: and the land without water into iſſues of waters.
And he placed the hungrie there, and they built a citie of habitation.
And they ſowed fildes, and planted vineyardes: and they made fruicte <na>(n)</na> of natiuitie.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Made abundance of fruict to grow.

verses.text: And he bleſſed them, and they were multiplied excedingly: and their beaſtes he leſſened not.
And <na>(o)</na> they were made fewe: and were vexed by the tribulation of euiles, and with ſorow.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Againe ſome countries punished for ſinnes.

verses.text: Contempt was powred out vpon princes: and he made them wander where was no way, and not in the way.
And he <na>(p)</na> did helpe the poore out of pouertie: and made families as sheepe.

notes.label: p
notes.text: An other change in releeuing the poore being humbled.

verses.text: The iuſt shal ſee, and shal reioyce: & al iniquitie shal ſtoppe her mouth.
Who is wiſe and wil keepe theſe thinges? and wil vnderſtand the mercies of our Lord?

chapters.summary: Againe the Pſalmiſt inuiteth al men to render thankes to God for their deliuerie from dangers, or euils in general : 4. particularly from dangers in iorney, 10. in priſon, or captiuitie, 17. in ſicknes ſpiritual and corporal, 23. in nauigation, 33. deſcribing the changeable course of thinges in this world, 38. eſpecially of mens ſtates, 42. for al which the iuſt wil praiſe God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: God'ſ perpetual providence towards all men.

verses.text: A Canticle <na>(a)</na> of Pſalme, to Dauid himſelfe.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Pſalme was ſongue with inſtruments beginning the muſike, and voices folowing.

verses.text: MY HART is readie ô God, my hart is readie: <cr>[1]</cr> I wil chaunte, and wil ſing in my glorie. <na>[2]</na>

notes.text: The former part of this Pſalme to the 7. verſe, is the ſame in ſenſe, and almoſt in wordes, with the latter part of the 56 from the 8. verſe.

verses.text: Ariſe my glorie, ariſe pſalter, and harpe: I wil ariſe early.
I <na>(b)</na> wil confeſſe to thee in peoples ô Lord: and I wil ſing to thee <na>(c)</na> in the Nations.

notes.label: b
notes.text: King Dauid ſubdued not only ſome partes of Chanaan, not ſubiect to the Iewes before ( 2. Reg. 5. 1. Par. 11. ) but alſo brought the Philiſtims, Moabites, Ammonites, Idumeans, Amalechites, the kinges of Soba, Syria, and Emath, to pay tribute, 2. Reg. 8. 1. Par. 18.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Yet al theſe victories and conqueſtes were but a figure of Chriſts powre and dominion in al nations. And therfore, the reſt of this Pſalme, by S. Auguſtin, and other fathers iudgement, was rather prophetically vttered by Dauid, in the perſon of Chriſt, and more perfectly performed by Chriſt in his Church, then hiſtorically ſuffered of Dauid himſelfe.

verses.text: Becauſe thy mercie is great aboue the heauens: and thy truth euen to the cloudes.
Be exalted aboue the heauens ô God, and thy glorie ouer al the earth: <cr>[1]</cr>
<na>[1]</na> that thy beloued may be deliuered. Saue with thy righthand; and heare me:

notes.text: The reſt of this Pſalme is the ſame with the latter part of the 59 from the 7. verſe.

verses.text: God ſpake in his holie: I wil reioyce, and wil diuide Sichem; and I wil meſure the vale of tabernacles.
Galaad is mine, and Manaſſes is mine: and Ephraim the protection of my head.
Iuda is my king: Moab the potte of my hope. Vpon Idumea I wil extend my shoe: the ſtrangers are made my freindes.
Who wil conduct me into a fenſed citie? who wil conduct me into Idumea?
Wilt not thou ô God, which haſt repelled vs, and wilt not thou goeforth ô God in our hoaſtes?
Geue vs helpe out of tribulation: becauſe mans ſaluation is vayne.
In God we shal doe ſtrength: and he wil bring our enemies to nothing.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet promiſeth, 5. and rendereth praiſes to God, 7. for his deliuerie from trubles, and aduancement in the kingdom, 13. praying God ſtil to helpe mans infirmitie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David ſingeth praiſes for benefits received.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, a Pſalme of Dauid.
