O <na>(a)</na> God conceale not my prayſe: becauſe the mouth of the ſinner, and the mouth of <na>(b)</na> the deceitful man is open vpon me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The wordes of Chriſt.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The Phariſees and Herodians ( Mat. 22. ) with their mouth acknowleged Chriſt a true ſpeaker, and a teacher of the way of God in truth, therby to draw him into danger, and to ſheede his bloud.

verses.text: They <na>(c)</na> haue ſpoken againſt me with deceitful tongue, and with wordes of hatred they haue compaſſed me: and they haue impugned me without cauſe.

notes.label: c
notes.text: At other times they accuſed him of great crimes, laſtly of treaſon againſt Cæſar.

verses.text: For that they should loue me, they backbited me: but I prayed.
And they ſet againſt me euil thinges for good: and hatred for my loue.
Appoint <na>(d)</na> a ſinner ouer him: and <na>(e)</na> let the diuel ſtand on his righthand.

notes.label: d
notes.text: A prediction that Iudas would not make recourſe to anie good counſeller, but complaine of his miſerable tormented conſcience to the wicked, who gaue him no comfort at al,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and ſo deſparing, the diuel perſwaded him to hang himſelfe.

verses.text: When he is iudged, let him comeforth condemned: and let his prayer be turned into ſinne.
Let his dayes be made fewe: and let an other take his <na>(f)</na> bishopricke. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: f
notes.text: The office of Apoſtleshippe.

verses.text: Let <na>(g)</na> his children be made orphans: and his wife a widow.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The poſte title, or ſucceſſors of wicked perſecuters proſper not long in this world.

verses.text: Let his children be tranſported wandering, and let them begge: and let them be caſt out of their habitations.
Let the vſurer ſearch al his ſubſtance: and let ſtrangers ſpoile his labours.
Let there be none to helpe him: neither let there be anie to haue pittie on his pupilles.
Let his children come to deſtruction: in <na>(h)</na> one generation let his name be cleane put out.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Arch heretikes that deuiſe newe opinions, are shortly forſaken, their followers ſtil coining new hereſies of their owne, differing from their falſe maſters.

verses.text: Let the iniquitie of his fathers returne to memorie in the ſight of our Lord: and let not the ſinne of his mother be blotted out.
Let them be before our Lord alwayes, and let the memorie of them perish out of the earth:
For that he remembred not to doe mercie.
And he perſecuted the poore, and needie man, and the compunct in hart to kil him.

And he <na>(i)</na> loued curſing, and it shal come to him: and he would not bleſſing, and it shal be far from him. And he put on curſing as a garment, and it entred as water into his inner partes, and as oile in his bones.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Let them obſerue this, that vſe more ſwearing and blaſpheming, then praying or meditating.

verses.text: Be it to him as a garment, wherwith he is couered: and as a girdle, wherwith he is alwayes girded.
This is the worke of them, that detract from me before our Lord: and that ſpeake euils againſt my ſoule.
And thou Lord, Lord, doe with me for thy names ſake: becauſe thy mercie is ſwete.
Deliuer me becauſe I am needie, and poore: and <na>(k)</na> my hart is trubled within me.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Chriſts ſoule was penſiue when he prayed in the garden, and he did workes of penance for our ſinnes al his life.

verses.text: As a shadow when it declineth, am I taken away: and I am shaken as locuſtes.
My knees are weakened with faſting: and my flesh is changed by reaſon of oile.
And I am made a reproch to them: they ſaw me, and wagged their heades.
Helpe me ô Lord my God: <na>(l)</na> ſaue me according to thy mercie.

notes.label: l
notes.text: He prayed alſo for his reſurrection, and glorification.

verses.text: And let them know that this is thy hand: and thou ô Lord haſt done it.
They wil curſe, and thou shalt bleſſe: let them that riſe vp againſt me, be confounded: but thy ſeruant shal reioyce.
Let them that detract from me, be clothed with shame: and let them be couered with their confuſion, as with a <na>(m)</na> duble patched cloke.

notes.label: m
notes.text: With al poſſible confuſion.

verses.text: I wil confeſſe to our Lord excedingly with my mouth: and in the middes of manie I wil prayſe him:
Becauſe he hath ſtood on the righthand of the poore, that he might ſaue my ſoule from the perſecutors.

chapters.summary: Chriſt ( by the mouth of Dauid ) requeſteth of God to be iuſtly declared innocent, and his enimies punished, 6. particularly deſcribing Iudas the traitors malice, 21. and his owne temporal afflictions, 26. prayeth, 30. and praiſeth God for his deliuerie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt perſecuted & his enemies punished.
The 5. key.

verses.text: A pſalme of Dauid. OVR <na>(a)</na> Lord ſayd <na>(b)</na> to my Lord: Sitte on my right hand: <na>(c)</na> til I make thine enemies, thy footeſtoole of thy feete. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: God the Father.

notes.label: b
notes.text: To God the Sonne, the Lord of Dauid; and of al mankind, yet the ſonne of Dauid, according to his humanitie.

notes.label: c
notes.text: He limiteth not the time, but excludeth al time, wherin the enimie might imagine, that Chriſts kingdom should ceaſe : ſignifying that Chriſt shal reigne, til al his enimies be ſubdued, much more afterwards in al eternitie.

verses.text: Our Lord wil ſendforth the rod of thy ſtrength <na>(d)</na> from Sion: rule thou in the middes of thine enemies.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The Church of Chriſt beginning in Ieruſalem on whitſunday, the fiftith day from his Reſurrection, continueth euer more.

verses.text: With thee <na>(e)</na> the beginning in the day <na>(f)</na> of thy ſtrength, in <na>(g)</na> the brightnes of holie thinges: from the wombe <na>(h)</na> before the day ſtarre I begat thee.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Thou shalt haue principalitie,

notes.label: f
notes.text: in the day of thy powrful conqueſt, and riſing from death.

notes.label: g
notes.text: in excellencie of al holie ſpiritual myſteries and graces :

notes.label: h
notes.text: becauſe, I God the Father of my ſubſtance begate thee, God the Sonne in eternitie. The ſame which Micheas ſaith ( c. 5. v. 2. ) His comingforth from the beginning, from the dayes of eternitie.

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(i)</na> ſware, and it shal not repent him: Thou art a Prieſt <na>(k)</na> for euer according to <na>(l)</na> the order of Melchiſedech. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: i
notes.text: God moſt firmly, and vnchangeably affirmed : that thou ( Chriſt our Meſſias ) art not only a King, but alſo a Prieſt :

notes.label: k
notes.text: not for a time, as Aaron was, but for euer,

notes.label: l
notes.text: neither of Aarons order, but according to the Order of Melchiſedec.

verses.text: Our Lord on thy righthand, <na>(m)</na> hath broken kinges in the day of his wrath.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Kinges that ſometimes perſecute Chriſtians, are ſubdued with other people to Chriſt.

verses.text: He <na>(n)</na> shal iudge in nations, he <na>(o)</na> shal fil ruines, he <na>(p)</na> shal crush the heads in the land of manie.

notes.label: n
notes.text: He shal iudge and punish the incredulous people,

notes.label: o
notes.text: make great ſlaghters amongſt thoſe that reſiſt :

notes.label: p
notes.text: and bring princes with their populous kingdoms to nothing.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> Of the torrent in the way he shal drinke: <na>(r)</na> therfore shal he exalt the head.

notes.label: q
notes.text: He shal in the meane time (and alſo his beſt ſeruants) ſuffer much tribulation in this life :

notes.label: r
notes.text: and for the ſame be highly exalted in life euerlaſting.

chapters.summary: Chriſt riſing and aſcending into heauen ſitteth on the right hand of God: 2. beginning in Ieruſalem reigneth in the Church of the whole earth. 4. vſeth the Prieſthood of Melchiſedechs order to the end of the world. 6. and shal iudge the world. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt's exaltation.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. I wil confeſſe to thee ô Lord with al my hart: in <na>(a)</na> the counſel of the iuſt, and <na>(b)</na> the congregation. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: I wil praiſe God both in ſecret for diſcharge of myn owne conſcience;

notes.label: b
notes.text: and in publique for edification of others.
This Pſalme in the Hebrew is compoſed with euerie verſe and midle of verſe, beginning with a diſtinct letter, in order of the Alphabet.

verses.text: The workes of our Lord are great: exquiſite according <na>(c)</na> to al his willes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Gods wil is the whole cauſe of al his workes.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Confeſſion and magnificence his worke: and his iuſtice continueth for euer and euer.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Euerie worke of his is praiſe worthie, and magnifical.

verses.text: He hath made <na>(e)</na> a memorie of his meruelous workes; merciful and pittiful Lord:

notes.label: e
notes.text: God hath leift one moſt ſpecial and beneficial memorie of al other benefites, his owne bodie and bloud, in memorie of his Paſſion, and our redemption,

verses.text: he hath geuen <na>(f)</na> meate to them that feare him. He wil be mindful for euer <na>(g)</na> of his teſtament:

notes.label: f
notes.text: the ſpiritual foode and ſuſtinance of al the ſoules that rightly feare him.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Of his promiſe to conſerue his Church perpetually.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> the force of his workes he wil shew forth to his people:

notes.label: h
notes.text: the powrable operation of his death, and of al his myſteries.

verses.text: To geue them the inheritance of the gentiles: the workes of his handes truth, and iudgement.
Al his commandmentes <na>(i)</na> are faithful: confirmed for euer and euer, made in truth and equitie.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Gods commandments do iuſtifie al that kepe them.

verses.text: He ſent <na>(k)</na> redemption to his people: he commanded his teſtament for euer. Holie, and terrible is his name:

notes.label: k
notes.text: He alſo of his mercie redemed man; that he might be able to kepe his precepts.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> the feare of our Lord is the beginning of wiſedom. Vnderſtanding is good to al that doe it: his prayſe remaineth for euer and euer.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Begingning with feare of God, bringeth at laſt by other degrees to true wiſdom, which two are the firſt and laſt of the ſeuen giftes of the Holie Ghoſt.

chapters.summary: Praiſe of God for benefites, 4. eſpecially for the B. Sacrament of the Euchariſt, 6. with other graces imperted to the Catholique Church. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Graces given to the Church.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Alleluia, <na>(a)</na> Of the returne of Aggeus, and Zacharie. <cr>[1]</cr> BLESSED is the man that feareth our Lord: <na>(b)</na> he shal haue great delight in his commandmentes. <na>[2]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: The Septuagint Interpreters added this mention of Aggeus and Zacharie, returning from captiuitie, to ſignifie that this Pſalme was very proper, & meete to be comended to the people at that time, wherby they might lerne, that their ſinnes were the cauſe of their captiuitie, and of al their miſeries: and if they deſired temporal, or ſpiritual proſperitie, they muſt obſerue the meanes here preſcribed to obtayne the ſame.

notes.label: b
notes.text: He that ſincerly feareth God, wil take great delight in keping his commandments.
This Pſalme is alſo compoſed by the Alphabet, as the next before.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> His ſeede shal be mightie in the earth: the generation of the righteous shal be bleſſed,

notes.label: c
notes.text: So doing he and his shal proſper.

verses.text: Glorie, and riches in his houſe: and <na>(d)</na> his iuſtice abideth for euer and euer.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The iuſt shal not only proſper in this world but alſo in the next.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Light is riſen vp in darkenes to the righteous: he is merciful, and pitiful, and iuſt.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God wil alſo comfort the iuſt in tribulations.

verses.text: Acceptable is the man, that is merciful and lendeth, that <na>(f)</na> shal diſpoſe his wordes in iudgement:

notes.label: f
notes.text: That shal geue diſcrete and wholſome counſel to the afflicted.

verses.text: Becauſe he shal not be moued for euer.
The iuſt shal be in eternal memorie: he shal not feare at the hearing of euil.
His hart is readie to hope in our Lord, his hart is confirmed:
he shal not be moued til he looke ouer his enemies.
He diſtributed, he gaue to the poore: <na>(g)</na> his iuſtice remaineth for euer and euer <na>(h)</na> his horne shal be exalted in glorie. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: g
notes.text: Workes of mercie are alſo called iuſtice, becauſe they concurre to mans iuſtification,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and to his ſaluation.

verses.text: The ſinner shal ſee, and wil be angrie, he shal gnash his teeth and pine away: the deſire of ſinners shal perish.

chapters.summary: True happines conſiſteth in fearing God, keping his commandments, 5. and in doing workes of mercie. 10. The contrarie bringeth to miſerie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The meanes to be happie.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. PRAYSE our Lord ye <na>(a)</na> children: praiſe ye the name of our Lord.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Al Gods ſeruants.

verses.text: Be the name of our Lord bleſſed, from henceforth now and for euer.
From the riſing of the ſunne vnto the going downe, the name of our Lord is laudable.
Our Lord is high aboue al nations, and his glorie aboue the heauens.
Who is as the Lord our God, that dwelleth on high,
and beholdeth the low thinges <na>(b)</na> in heauen and in earth?

notes.label: b
notes.text: In reſpect of God al creatures are low, though they be in heauen.

verses.text: Raiſing vp the needie from the earth, and lifting vp the poore out of the dung:
<na>(c)</na> To place him with princes, with the princes of his people.

notes.label: c
notes.text: See the example of Ioſeph ſo aduanced

verses.text: Who maketh the <na>(d)</na> barren woman to dwel in a houſe, a ioyful mother of children.

notes.label: d
notes.text: of Sara, Rebecca, Rachael, and other wemen made fruitful.

chapters.summary: God is to be praiſed, who being hiegh regardeth, and prouideth for the needie in this world. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God'ſ providence.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Allelu ia. IN the comming forth of Iſrael out of Ægypt, of the houſe of Iacob from <na>(a)</na> the barbarous people.

notes.label: a
notes.text: People of falſe religion counted barbarous, eſpecially ſuch as alſo perſecute the true Religion; for otherwiſe the Ægyptians were both ciuil in maners, and lerned in manie ſciences.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Iewrie was made his ſanctification, Iſrael his dominion.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The people of Iewes were more notoriouſly renowmed in the world from the time of their deliuerie out of Ægypt, for the peculiar people, whom God ſanctified, and in whom, as in his elected enheritance or dominion, he dwelled and reigned.

verses.text: The <na>(c)</na> ſea ſaw, and <na>(d)</na> fled: Iordan <na>(e)</na> was turned backeward. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: c
notes.text: The Pſalmiſt writing in verſe doth often deſcribe thinges in poetical maner, but more truly then prophane poetes: for that in very dede, al creatures otherwiſe ſenſles, as the ſea, do in a ſorte feele the powre of their Creator, & obey his wil,

notes.label: d
notes.text: VVhen the Iſraelites went forth of Ægypt,

notes.label: e
notes.text: when they entred into Chanaan,

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> The mountaines leaped as rammes: and the litle hilles as the lambes of sheepe.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Either there was an earthquake, or ſome other mouing of hilles not mentioned by Moyſes, or els the Pſalmiſt ſpeaketh of the rockes of the torrentes which bowed, that the Iſraelites might reſt in Ar, and lie in the borders of the Moabites, Num, 21, v, 15,

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> What ayleth thee ô ſea that thou didſt flee: and thou ô Iordan, that thou waſt turned backeward?

notes.label: g
notes.text: By the figure Apoſtrophe he ſpeaketh to the ſea, riuer, and hilles : vſing alſo Proſopopœia: as if ſenſles thinges, vnderſtood, and should anſwer.

verses.text: Ye mountaines leaped as rammes, and ye litle hilles as the lambes of shepe.
At the face of our Lord was the earth moued, at the face of the God of Iacob.
Who turned <na>(h)</na> the rocke into pooles of waters, and ſtonie hil into fountaines of waters.

notes.label: h
notes.text: An other miraculous benefite, that the rocke yelded them water in their neceſſitie.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> <sc>NOT TO VS O LORD, NOT</sc> TO VS: but to thy name geue the glorie.

notes.text: Here ſome Hebrewe Rabbins beginne an other Pſalme, but by the coherence of the matter, S. Auguſtin proueth that it is but one Pſalme, where is shewed that the true inuiſible God is knowen by ſuch workes as are here recited: and contrariwiſe, that the Gentils idoles are not goddes, becauſe they are made of ſiluer, gold, or other matter, by mens handes, hauing reſemblance of liuing thinges are altogether ſenſles.

verses.text: For <na>(i)</na> thy mercie, and <na>(k)</na> thy truth: leſt at any time <na>(l)</na> the Gentiles ſay: Where is their God?

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thou didſt al this ô God, of mere mercie towards thy people :

notes.label: k
notes.text: for thy truths ſake, ſeing thou didſt promiſe to protect them :

notes.label: l
notes.text: that the Gentiles should not take occaſion to blaſpheme.

verses.text: But our God is in heauen: he hath done al thinges whatſoeuer he would.
The idols of the gentiles are ſiluer, and gold, the workes of mens handes.
They haue mouth, and shal not ſpeake: they haue eies, and shal not ſee.
They haue eares, and shal not heare: they haue noſthrels and shal not ſmel.
They haue handes, and shal not handle: they haue feete, and shal not walke: they shal not crie in their throte.
<na>(m)</na> Let them that make them become like to them: and al that haue confidence in them.

notes.label: m
notes.text: This is a iuſt prayer of the zelous, conforming their deſires to Gods wil But if God geue idolaters grace to amend, then al the iuſt wil alſo reioice in their conuerſion.

verses.text: <na>(n)</na> The houſe of Iſrael hath hoped in our Lord: he is their helper and their protector.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Though manie Iewes fel to idolatrie, yet there alwayes remained ſo manie in Gods true ſeruice, that it might ſtil be truly ſaide : The houſe of Iſrael hath hoped in our Lord, as is here auerred.

verses.text: The houſe of Aaron hath hoped in our Lord: he is their helper and their protector.
They that feare our Lord, haue hoped in our Lord: he is their helper and their protector.
Our Lord hath beene mindful of vs: and hath bleſſed vs: He hath bleſſed the houſe of Iſrael: he hath bleſſed the houſe of Aaron.
He hath bleſſed al, that feare our Lord, the litle with the great.
Our Lord adde vpon you: vpon you, & vpon your children.
Bleſſed be you of our Lord, which made heauen, and earth.
<na>(o)</na> The heauen of heauen is to our Lord: but <na>(p)</na> the earth he hath geuen to the children of men.

notes.label: o
notes.text: This in effect al worldlie politikes ſay in their hartes : as it were quitting their intereſt of heauen to God,

notes.label: p
notes.text: and contenting themſelues with earthlie poſſeſſions.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> The dead shal not prayſe thee ô Lord: nor al they, <na>(r)</na> that goe downe hel.

notes.label: q
notes.text: But when ſuch prophane men are dead, they make no ſhew at al of praiſing God :

notes.label: r
notes.text: for parting from the earth, they deſcend into hel, and there eternally blaſpheme God.

verses.text: But we <na>(s)</na> that liue, doe bleſſe our Lord, from this time, and for euer.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Contrarivviſe the iuſt, aſpiring to heauen, vvhich is the proper kingdom of God, & vſing this world as they ought to do, for a meanes to aſcend into heauen, ſhal bleſſe and praiſe God for euermore.

chapters.summary: For the meruelous paſſage of Iſrael out of Ægypt, 3. the red ſea, the riuer of Iordan, 7. and the hilles geuing them place, 8. the rockes yelding them water, 9. God, not themſelues, is to be praiſed. 12. Idoles and Idolaters are vaine, and shal be confounded: 17. the faithful truſt in God, 20. are bleſſed, and for euer praiſe God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The marvelous paſſage of Iſrael from Ægypt.
The 4. key.

verses.text: Allelu ia. I <na>(a)</na> haue loued, becauſe our Lord <na>(b)</na> wil heare the voice of my prayer.

notes.label: a
notes.text: I am induced to loue God,

notes.label: b
notes.text: becauſe he alwayes heareth my prayers.

verses.text: Becauſe he hath inclined his eare to me: and <na>(c)</na> in my daies I wil inuocate.

notes.label: c
notes.text: So long as I shal liue.

verses.text: The ſorowes <na>(d)</na> of death haue compaſſed me: and <na>(e)</na> the perils of hel haue found me. <na>(f)</na> I haue found tribulation and ſorow:

notes.label: d
notes.text: VVhen I erred like a ſtray sheepe from thee, the paines of death,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and the danger of hel-torments, both due for ſinne, inuironed me, and I was not ware therof:

notes.label: f
notes.text: But by tribulation falling vpon me, I came to knowe my dangerous eſtate :

verses.text: and I <na>(g)</na> inuocated the name of our Lord. O Lord deliuer my ſoule:

notes.label: g
notes.text: turned to thee, and prayed as foloweth :

verses.text: our Lord is merciful, and iuſt, and our God doth mercie.
Our Lord kepeth litle ones: <na>(h)</na> I was humbled, and he hath deliuered me.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Afflicted with tribulations.

verses.text: Turne ô my ſoule into thy reſt: becauſe our Lord hath done good to thee.
Becauſe he hath deliuered my ſoule from death: mine eies from teares, my feete from ſliding.
I <na>(i)</na> wil pleaſe our Lord in the countrie of the liuing.

notes.label: i
notes.text: I wil endeuoure to pleaſe God, in the congregation of thoſe that liue here in grace, and in heauen in glorie.

chapters.summary: The prayer of a iuſt man in tribulation, with confidence and gratitude towards God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer, with praiſe of God.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. I <na>(a)</na> beleued, <na>(b)</na> for which cauſe I ſpake: but I <na>(c)</na> was humbled excedingly. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: I beleued that God would helpe me:

notes.label: b
notes.text: therfore I freely profeſſed that I truſted in him. For then in dede faith is perfect, when we confeſſe with mouth, that which we beleue in hart:

notes.label: c
notes.text: I was vehemently afflicted in tribulations.
This in the Hebrew is ioyned to the next Pſalme before.

verses.text: I ſaid <na>(d)</na> in mine exceſſe: Euerie man is a lyer.

notes.label: d
notes.text: In the middes of my great affliction I profeſſed, that al mans helpe is vaine, falſe, deceipful, and defectiue, and therfore our truſt muſt be in God only.

verses.text: What <na>(e)</na> shal I render to our Lord, for al thinges that he <na>(f)</na> hath rendred to me?

notes.label: e
notes.text: Conſidering that God hath not only geuen, and beſtowed manie great benefites vpon me, and al mankind, but alſo hath rendered good for euil, mercie for our ſinnes, we hauing rendered euil for good : what now ſhal I render, ſayth a true penitent, for al that he hath thus rendered to me, deſeruing ſo euil?

notes.label: f
notes.text: See previous note

verses.text: I <na>(g)</na> wil take the chalice of ſaluation: and <na>(h)</na> I wil inuocat the name of our Lord.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Seing I am not able to render anie thing worthie of Gods fauoure to me, yet I wil do that I can : I wil gratfully accept his great benefite. the cuppe of Chriſts paſſion, which he druunke for mankind,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and wil praiſe, and cal vpon his name.

verses.text: I wil <na>(i)</na> render my vowes to our Lord <na>(k)</na> before al his people:

notes.label: i
notes.text: I wil pay voluntarie vowes,

notes.label: k
notes.text: for Gods glorie, and edification of others.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> precious in the ſight of our Lord is the death of his Sainctes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: yea I wil offer my life, and ſuffer death, when Gods glorie shal require it, in whoſe ſight, the death of Sainctes is precious, and moſt highly eſteemed.

verses.text: O Lord becauſe <na>(m)</na> I am thy ſeruant: I am thy ſeruant, and <na>(n)</na> the ſonne of thy handmaide. Thou haſt <na>(o)</na> broken my bondes:

notes.label: m
notes.text: Alvvayes vnderſtood, that ſuch as ſuffer perſecution, be in good ſtate of their ſoules, the true ſeruantes of God,

notes.label: n
notes.text: the children of the Church his handmaide.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Deliuered me from captiuitie of ſinne.

verses.text: I wil ſacrifice to thee the hoaſt of praiſe, and I wil inuocate the name of our Lord.
I wil render my vowes to our Lord in the ſight of al his people:
in the courtes of the houſe of our Lord, in the middes of <na>(p)</na> thee ô Ieruſalem.

notes.label: p
notes.text: In the Church of the faithful.

chapters.summary: A iuſt man acknowledging that ſpiritual life beginneth by faith, and by publique profeſſion therof, 4. gratfully accepteth of Chriſts Redemption, 5. dedicateth his life, and al he hath to Gods ſeruice. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Thanks-giving for our Redeemer.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Allelu ia. PRAYSE our Lord <na>(a)</na> al ye Gentiles: prayſe him <na>(b)</na> al ye peoples. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Not only ſome, but al nations of the Gentiles :

notes.label: b
notes.text: and al Ievves, (Chriſts Redemption being abundantly ſufficient for al) are inuited to praiſe God.

verses.text: Becauſe <na>(c)</na> his mercie is confirmed vpon vs: and his <na>(d)</na> truth remaineth for euer.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Becauſe he hath multiplied his mercie to vs Gentiles, to vvhom he made no promiſe :

notes.label: d
notes.text: and moſt truly performed his promiſe made to the Ievves,

chapters.summary: Gods mercie is largely extended to al Gentiles by Chriſt, and his promiſe withal is performed to the Iewes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church of Chriſt in al nations.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Allelu ia. CONFESSE ye to our Lord becauſe he is <na>(a)</na> good: becauſe <na>(b)</na> his mercie is for euer. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Let vs praiſe God, for his goodnes, in making vs of nothing, geuing vs manie benefites,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and remitting our ſinnes.

verses.text: Let Iſrael <na>(c)</na> now ſay that he is good: that his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Let the Church of the new teſtament eſpecially confeſſe his goodnes, which hath receiued more mercie and grace.

verses.text: Let the houſe of Aaron <na>(d)</na> now ſay: that his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Let al the Clergie praiſe God now in the time of more grace, and of greater ſpiritual functions.

verses.text: Let them now ſay <na>(e)</na> which feare our Lord: that his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Yea let the whole bodie of the Church, al that feare, and ſerue God praiſe his mercie.

verses.text: From <na>(f)</na> tribulation I inuocated our Lord: and our Lord heard me in largenes.

notes.label: f
notes.text: As wel ſpiritual as temporal.

verses.text: Our Lord is my helper: I wil not feare what man can doe to me.
Our Lord is my helper: and I wil looke ouer mine enemies.
It is good to hope in our Lord, rather then to hope in man.
It is good to hope in our Lord, rather then to hope in princes.
<na>(g)</na> Al nations haue compaſſed me: and in the name of our Lord am I <na>(h)</na> reuenged on them.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Though innumerable oppoſe, and endeuour to hurt me (ſaith the Church, or anie iuſt perſon)

notes.label: h
notes.text: yet by Gods povvre, not by myn ovvne, I am defended, and they puniſhed, and ſo the iuſt hath the victorie, and triumpheth,

verses.text: Compaſſing they haue compaſſed me: and in the name of our Lord I was reuenged on them.
They compaſſed me as <na>(i)</na> bees, and were inflamed as <na>(k)</na> fyre in thornes: and in the name of our Lord I was reuenged on them.

notes.label: i
notes.text: In great trooper, and furie,

notes.label: k
notes.text: vvith ſharpe though ſhorte force, and vvith ſpecial noiſe, to terrifie me, but in God I ouercame al.

verses.text: Being thruſt <na>(l)</na> I was ouerturned to fal: and our Lord <na>(m)</na> receiued me.

notes.label: l
notes.text: I was ſometimes by vehemencie of tentation, declining to ſinne :

notes.label: m
notes.text: but Gods grace aſſiſted and ſtrengthned me.

verses.text: Our Lord is my ſtrength, and my prayſe: and he is made my ſaluation.
The voice of exultation, and of ſaluation in the tabernacles of the iuſt.
The right hand of our Lord hath wrought ſtrength: the right hand of our Lord hath exalted me, <na>(n)</na> the right hand of our Lord hath wrought ſtrength.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The ſame vvord [ right hand ] thriſe mentioned, ſignifieth the B. Trinitie. Alſo [ Our Lord] ſignifying Chriſt in his humanitie the chief inſtrument of God, is here often repeted, to ſignifie the ſingular efficacie therof.

verses.text: I shal not die, but shal liue: and I wil tel the workes of our Lord.
Our Lord <na>(o)</na> chaſtiſing hath chaſtiſed me: and <na>(p)</na> to death he hath not deliuered me.

notes.label: o
notes.text: God chaſtiſeth his children,

notes.label: p
notes.text: becauſe he would not that they ſhould dye eternally. So he puniſheth as a father, not as an enimie.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> Open ye the gates of iuſtice to me, being entred into them I wil confeſſe to our Lord:

notes.label: q
notes.text: The Prophet now ſpeaketh in the perſon of iuſt ſoules, requiring ſpiritual doctrin, and foode,

verses.text: <na>(r)</na> this is the gate of our Lord, the iuſt shal enter into it.

notes.label: r
notes.text: and promiſing to ſerue God.

verses.text: I wil confeſſe to thee becauſe thou haſt heard me: and art become my ſaluation.
<na>(s)</na> The ſtone, which the builders reiected: the ſame is made into the head of the corner.

notes.label: s
notes.text: An euident prophecie of Chriſt vttered by the Royal Pſalmiſt, and now confeſſed by euerie Chriſtian, that our Sauiour reiected by the Ievves, is neuertheles the builder of his Church, by ioyning the tvvo peoples of Iewes and Gentiles, as two vvalles into one houſe.

verses.text: This was done by our Lord: and it is meruelous in our eies.
This <na>(t)</na> is the day, which our Lord made: let vs reioice, and be glad therein.

notes.label: t
notes.text: God ordayned this acceptable time of grace. · Mat. 21. Luc. 10. Act. 4. Rom. 9. 1. Pet. 2.

verses.text: <na>(v)</na> O Lord ſaue me, ô Lord geue good ſucceſſe: Bleſſed be he that cometh in the name of our Lord. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: v
notes.text: The tongue of the Hebrew children, when Chriſt entered Ieruſalem with palmes of triumph, and acclamations.

verses.text: <na>(w)</na> We haue bleſſed you of the houſe of our Lord:

notes.label: w
notes.text: The voice of Chriſt, and his Apoſtles and other Clergie bleſſing the people as they deſire.

verses.text: Our Lord is God, and he hath geuen light to vs. Appoint a ſolemne day with <na>(x)</na> thicke bowes, euen to <na>(y)</na> the horne of the altar.

notes.label: x
notes.text: This was fulfilled when Chriſt was brought with bowes of palme, and other ſignes of triumph, from Bethania,

notes.label: y
notes.text: through the whole citie, euen into the Temple and vnto the Altar : Mat. 21.

verses.text: Thou art my God, and I wil confeſſe to thee: thou art my God, and I wil exalt thee. I wil confeſſe to thee becauſe thou haſt heard me: and art become my ſaluation.
<na>(z)</na> Confeſſe ye to our Lord becauſe he is good: becauſe his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Our firſt, chiefe, and final dutie is to praiſe God. v. 1. & vlt.

chapters.summary: Faithful people collected in the Church of Chriſt, exhorte each other to render thankes to God, for their deliuerie from ſpiritual and temporal tribulations. 16. The Laitie demand participation of Chriſts Myſteries, promiſing to ſerue him duly: 25. Which the Paſtors freely impert, and together with the people, ſolemnely celebrate Gods praiſe. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Chriſt beneficial Myſteries are celebrated by his Church.
The 6. key.

verses.heading: Aleph. Doctrine.
verses.text: <na>[1]</na> Allelu ia. BLESSED <na>(a)</na> are <na>(b)</na> the immaculate in the vvay: which <na>(c)</na> walke in the law of our Lord.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Whereas al, without exception, deſire to be happie and bleſſed ;

notes.label: b
notes.text: they are in dede happie (according to the perfecteſt happines of this life) that are immaculate :

notes.label: c
notes.text: and they are immaculate, that walke in the law of God. Where the holie Pſalmiſt preſuppoſeth, that ſome can and do kepe the law of God, and ſo are immaculate, and bleſſed in the way of this life.
This title vvas added by the Septuagint, to admoniſh vs that this Pſalme conteyneth that ſingular maner of praiſing God, ſignified by the two Hebrew vvordes Alleluia, as before. Pſal 104.

verses.text: Bleſſed are they, <na>(d)</na> that ſearch his teſtimonies: that <na>(e)</na> ſeeke after him with al their hart.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Thoſe that are immaculate, are againe bleſſed, by ſearching Gods teſtimonies, that is, his lavv teſtifying that the good ſhal be revvarded, and the vvicked punished, but ſearching theſe teſtimonies, vvhiles one is contaminate vvith ſinnes againſt Gods law, maketh not bleſſed :

notes.label: e
notes.text: neither doth euerie ſuperficial careles ſearch bring this bleſſing, but ſearching with true affection of the hart.

verses.text: For <na>(f)</na> they that worke iniquitie, haue not walked in his <na>(g)</na> waies.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Contrariwiſe they that vvorke iniquitie are not bleſſed ;

notes.label: g
notes.text: becauſe they haue not walked in the vvayes of God, towitte, not kept his commamdments and law, which are the vvay to happines.

verses.text: Thou haſt <na>(h)</na> very much commanded thy commandmentes to be kept.

notes.label: h
notes.text: For mans owne good, that he may come to true happines, God hath moſt ſeriouſly commanded vs to kepe his commandments, that is, to obſerue his Law commanded by moſt ſouueraine diuine authoritie.

verses.text: Would God my waies <na>(i)</na> might be directed, to keepe thy <na>(k)</na> iuſtifications.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Therfore the faithful ſeruant of God, knowing his owne inſufficiencie, deſireth that God by his grace vvil direct and ſtreingthen him,

notes.label: k
notes.text: to kepe his lavv, called Iuſtifications, becauſe therby man is made iuſt.

verses.text: Then shal I <na>(l)</na> not be confounded, when I shal looke throughly in al thy commandmentes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: They shal be ſafe from eternal confuſion, when they ſhal kepe not only part, but al thy commandments, becauſe breach of anie bringeth confuſion.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> I wil confeſſe to thee <na>(n)</na> in direction of hart: in that I haue lerned the <na>(o)</na> iudgements of thy iuſtice.

notes.label: m
notes.text: So shal I praiſe thee, and render thankes,

notes.label: n
notes.text: with ſincere not fayned affection,

notes.label: o
notes.text: for this great benefite, that I haue lerned, that thy law is according to moſt iuſt iudgement.

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> I wil keepe thy iuſtifications: <na>(q)</na> forſake me not wholy.

notes.label: p
notes.text: I haue therfore a firme purpoſe, & do faithfully promiſe to kepe thy law, which maketh the keper therof iuſt.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Albeit thou ſuffer me ſometimes to be in tribulation, or in tentation, yet forſake me not wholy. The Pſalmiſt knew wel (ſaith S. Gregorie) that he might be profitably leiſt a while, who prayed, that he should not be wholy forſaken.

verses.heading: Beth. House.
verses.text: Wherein <na>(a)</na> doth a yongman correct his way? <na>(b)</na> in keeping thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In this ſecond Octonarie, as alſo in al the reſt, the Holie Ghoſt by the prophets penne teacheth the meanes how to come to perfection & happines. Here by way of interrogation, as it were demanding how a youngman, that is euerie man prone to worldlie pleaſure, & ſlow in Gods ſeruice, ſhal beginne to correct his courſe ?

notes.label: b
notes.text: Wherto the ſame Holie Ghoſt anſwereth, that he muſt kepe Gods law, called here his wordes. For al the wordes which God vttereth, are lawes to his ſeruants.
ſermones.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> With my whole hart I haue ſought after thee: <na>(d)</na> repel me not from thy commandmentes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The Pſalmiſt now ſpeaketh in the perſon of perfect iuſt men, or of the whole Church in general. VVhoſe common ſpirite ſeeketh God intyrely.

notes.label: d
notes.text: And conſidering that this perfect good wil is the gift of God, prayeth that he wil conſerue the ſame, and not ſuffer it to be altered, or to erre from his commandments.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> In my hart I haue hid thy <na>[1]</na> wordes: that I may not ſinne to thee.

notes.label: e
notes.text: An other ſincere profeſſion of a reſolute good purpoſe not to ſinne.
eloquia.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Bleſſed art thou o Lord: <na>(g)</na> teach me thy iuſtifications.

notes.label: f
notes.text: A gratful aſpiration praiſing God.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Againe the iuſt prayeth to be more and more inſtructed in iuſtifications : that which S. Iohn exhorteth vnto : He that is iuſt, let him yet be iuſtified. Apoc. 22.

verses.text: In my lippes, I haue pronounced al the <na>(h)</na> iudgementes of thy mouth.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Gods law is alſo called his Iudgements, becauſe ſitting in iudgement he geueth ſentence according to his Law.

verses.text: I am <na>(i)</na> delighted in the way of thy teſtimonies, as in al riches.

notes.label: i
notes.text: As the iuſt profeſſeth by mouth, ſo he delighteth in hart.

verses.text: I <na>(k)</na> wil be exerciſed in thy commandmentes: and I wil conſider thy waies.

notes.label: k
notes.text: practiſeth in worke :

verses.text: I <na>(l)</na> wil meditate in thy iuſtifications: I wil not forget thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: and diligently meditateth Gods law.
ſermones.

verses.heading: Gimel. Fulnes.
verses.text: Render <na>(a)</na> to thy ſeruant, <na>(b)</na> quicken me: <na>(c)</na> and I shal keepe thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: O Lord liberally geue me that which I here craue,

notes.label: b
notes.text: quicken me with ſpiritual life, thy grace.

notes.label: c
notes.text: ſo I shal kepe thy law, which otherwiſe I can not.
ſermones.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Reuele mine eies: <na>(e)</na> and I shal conſider the meruelous thinges of thy law.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Illuminate myn vnderſtanding, by thy grace,

notes.label: e
notes.text: that I may be able to ſee the meruelous great and iuſt reaſons of thy law, inſtructing al, threatning the peruerſe, encoreging the wel diſpoſed, punishing the wicked, rewarding the good, doing right to al.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> I am a ſeiourner in the land, <na>(g)</na> hide not thy commandmentes from me.

notes.label: f
notes.text: I that haue but a ſmal time in this world,

notes.label: g
notes.text: deſire to be inſtructed in thy law, what is therein commanded.

verses.text: My ſoule hath coueted to deſire thy iuſtifications, at al time.
Thou haſt <na>(h)</na> rebuked the prowde: <na>(i)</na> curſed are they that decline from thy commandmentes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: I conſider that thou o God, doſt sharply reproue the prowd contemners of thy commandments :

notes.label: i
notes.text: laying curſes vpon them for declining from thyn obedience.

verses.text: Take from me reproch, and contempt: becauſe I haue ſought after thy teſtimonies.
For <na>(k)</na> princes ſate, and they ſpake againſt me: but <na>(l)</na> thy ſeruant was exerciſed in thy iuſtifications.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Though perſecutors were very potent,

notes.label: l
notes.text: yet the faithful ſeruant of God perſeuered in his ſeruice.

verses.text: For both <na>(m)</na> thy teſtimonies are my meditation: and <na>(n)</na> thy iuſtifications my counſel.

notes.label: m
notes.text: In time of perſecution and tentation we muſt thincke and meditate, that Gods law teſtifieth eternal revvard, or punishment,

notes.label: n
notes.text: and in our deliberation or conſultation, we muſt conſider that keping Gods law maketh iuſt : and conſequently meriteth reward.

verses.heading: Daleth. Of Tables.
verses.text: My ſoule <na>(a)</na> hath cleaued to the pauement: <na>(b)</na> quicken me according to thy word.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This alſo is vttered in the perſon of the iuſt, who is often brought to great diſtreſſe : as it were, euen nere to death,

notes.label: b
notes.text: in which caſe he confidently prayeth to be relieued, according to Gods word, law, and promiſe.

verses.text: I haue vttered my wayes, and thou haſt heard me: teach me thy iuſtifications.
Inſtruct me the way of thy iuſtifications: and I shal be exerciſed in thy meruelous workes.
My ſoule <na>(c)</na> hath ſlumbered for tediouſnes: <na>(d)</na> confirme me in thy wordes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Being in ſo great anxietie that my minde is almoſt diſtracted, or ouercome,

notes.label: d
notes.text: I cal to thee o God, that thou wilt conſerue me, that I ſtil kepe thy law, vttered by thy wordes.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Remoue from me the way of iniquitie: and according to thy law, <na>(f)</na> haue mercie on me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Protect me that I fal not to iniquitie.

notes.label: f
notes.text: And of thy mercie conſerue me in ſtate of grace.

verses.text: I haue choſen the way of truth: I haue not forgotten thy iudgements.
I haue cleaued to thy teſtimonies o Lord: <na>(g)</na> do not confound me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Suffer me not to be confounded.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> I ranne the way of thy commandments: <na>(i)</na> when thou didſt dilate my hart.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Man is able, and doth runne in the right vvay of Gods commandments,

notes.label: i
notes.text: yet not of himſelfe, but when God replenisheth his hart with grace.

verses.heading: He. This thing.
verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Set me a law o Lord the way of thy iuſtifications: <na>(b)</na> and I wil ſeeke after it alwayes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Impreſſe o God thy law in myn affection, make me to loue it, and to deſire to be iuſtified,

notes.label: b
notes.text: ſo shal I hartely and alwayes ſeeke it.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Geue me vnderſtanding, <na>(d)</na> and I wil ſearch thy law: and I wil keepe it with my whole hart.

notes.label: c
notes.text: After thou haſt geuen me a deſire to kepe thy lavv, geue me alſo vnderſtanding.

notes.label: d
notes.text: then ſhal I fruictfully ſearch it. For this is the right order (as before in the firſt and ſecond verſes) firſt to loue Gods lavve, to be iuſtified, and to become immaculate ; and then to ſearch to knovv the lawe, and ſo it is more eaſily lerned.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Conduct me into the path of thy commandments: <na>(f)</na> becauſe I would it.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Gods grace firſt draweth and leadeth,

notes.label: f
notes.text: then freewil inflamed with deſire effectually concurreth.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Incline my hart into thy teſtimonies: and <na>(h)</na> not into auarice.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Stil the Prophet inculcateth the neceſſitie of Gods grace, as wel to make vs deſire that is good,

notes.label: h
notes.text: as to flee from euil.

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> Turne away mine eies that they ſee not vanitie: <na>(k)</na> in thy way quicken me.

notes.label: i
notes.text: It is neceſſarie alſo to pray that God wil take away occaſions, which might moue to ſinne :

notes.label: k
notes.text: and ſtil to grant his helping grace in progreſſe of vertue.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> Eſtablish thy <na>[1]</na> word to thy ſeruant, in thy feare.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Againe the iuſt prayeth for confirmation in grace, to be eſtablished in the feare of God.
eloquium.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> Take away my reproch, which I haue feared: <na>(n)</na> becauſe thy iudgements are pleaſant.

notes.label: m
notes.text: To be deliuered alſo from al the effectes of former ſinnes,

notes.label: n
notes.text: for ſinne is therfore reprochful and odious, becauſe it is contrarie to Gods law, and true iudgements, vvhich are moſt pleaſant.

verses.text: Behold I haue coueted thy commandments: in thine equitie <na>(o)</na> quicken me.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Being thus affected with deſire to kepe the commandments, the ſoule prayeth to be ſtil quickned, more and more vvith good ſpirite, and ſo to perſeuere to the end.

verses.heading: Vau. And.
verses.text: And <na>(a)</na> let thy mercie come vpon me o Lord: <na>(b)</na> thy ſaluation according to thy <na>[1]</na> word.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Againe conſidering that without Gods grace preuenting, man can not do anie good thing, the prophet renevveth his prayer, requeſting Gods mercie,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and his helpe freely promiſed to al that aske it.
eloquium.

verses.text: And <na>(c)</na> I shal anſwer a word to them that vpbrayde me: <na>(d)</na> becauſe I haue hoped in thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: VVhervvith being aſſiſted and ſtreingthned, he that before vvas vveake wil boldly anſvver al calumniators ; that reprochfully ſay : God wil not helpe him :

notes.label: d
notes.text: that in dede he hath not in vaine truſted in Gods promiſed helpe.
ſermonibus.

verses.text: And <na>(e)</na> take not away out of my mouth the word of truth vtterly: <na>(f)</na> becauſe I haue much hoped in thy iudgementes.

notes.label: e
notes.text: He alſo prayeth, though he be ſometimes fearful, that God vvil not ſuffer him vvholly to omitte manifeſt profeſſion of faith and true religion,

notes.label: f
notes.text: ſeing by thy former grace I haue already repoſed my truſt in thy promiſes, made to them that are reſolued to kepe thy law.

verses.text: And <na>(g)</na> I wil keepe thy law alwayes: for euer, and for euer and euer.

notes.label: g
notes.text: For I do firmly purpoſe euer and alwayes to kepe thy law.

verses.text: And <na>(h)</na> I walked in largeneſſe: <na>(i)</na> becauſe I haue ſought after thy commandments.

notes.label: h
notes.text: In this I haue had great ioy and comforte of mind :

notes.label: i
notes.text: becauſe I did in dede ſeeke after thy commandements, which is ſpecially vttered (as alſo the three next verſes) in the perſon of thoſe, that are in trial of perſecution for their faith :

verses.text: And <na>(k)</na> I ſpake of thy teſtimonies in the ſight of kinges: and was not confounded.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Who boldly in time of perſecution, euen before perſecuting Kinges and Emperors, profeſſe Chriſts true Religion. Verified in innumerable glorious Martyrs, yea alſo of the fraile ſexe, in S Catharin, S. Cecilie, S. Lucie, S. Margaret, S. VVenefrede, S. Vrſula, and her felovves, and manie more, moſt conſtantly anſwering al vvordes of reproch obiected, as if it vvere a baſe or contemtible thing to be Chriſtians, to be Catholiques, to be Papiſtes No, al theſe and the like, are honorable and glorious titles ; importing the true ſeruice of Chriſt ; in vnitie of the Catholique Church ; and ſpiritual participation with the viſible head therof, Chriſts Vicar in earth.

verses.text: And <na>(l)</na> I meditated in thy commandments, which I loued.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Such confeſſors as yet mortal, reioyce in that they haue meditated in Gods commandments, which they haue feruently loued.

verses.text: And <na>(m)</na> I haue lifted vp my handes to thy commandments, which I loued: and <na>(n)</na> I was exerciſed in thy iuſtifications.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Alſo ſhevved the ſame in external worke, not diſſembling by ſilence, by word, nor fact.

notes.label: n
notes.text: euerie way exerciſing Gods lavv, which maketh the obſeruers iuſt.

verses.heading: Zain. This.
verses.text: Be <na>(a)</na> mindeful of thy word to thy ſeruant, wherein thou haſt geuen me hope.

notes.label: a
notes.text: That which God hath decreed, and promiſed, being in itſelfe moſt certaine and aſſured, yet includeth the meanes, vvherby it ſhal be put in execution : and therfore the iuſt, his elect, do pray for the performance of his vvil.

verses.text: This hath comforted me in my humiliation: becauſe <na>(b)</na> thy <na>[1]</na> word hath quickened me.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Expectation of thy promiſe hath geuen me corege.
eloquium.

verses.text: The <na>(c)</na> prowd did vniuſtly exceedingly: <na>(d)</na> but I declined not from thy law.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Provvde contemners of Gods lavv, haue euerie vvay moleſted me, by detracting, deriding, calumniating, and violently perſecuting me.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Al which I haue borne patiently, and not declined from thy law.

verses.text: I <na>(e)</na> haue bene mindful of thy iudgements from <na>(f)</na> euerlaſting o Lord: <na>(g)</na> and was comforted.

notes.label: e
notes.text: I remembred and conſidered thy iuſt punishments inflicted vpon the impious,

notes.label: f
notes.text: euen from the beginning of the world (both vpon the diuels, and wicked men) and that thou wilt exerciſe the like hereafter,

notes.label: g
notes.text: which conſideration of thy iuſtice comforted me.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Faynting poſſeſſed me, becauſe of ſinners forſaking thy law.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Otherwiſe if I had not ſene thy iuſtice, my zele againſt contemners of thy law, would haue killed me.

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> Thy iuſtifications were ſongue by me, in the place of my peregrination.

notes.label: i
notes.text: In this place of my perigrination from heauen, I am comforted by remembring, celebrating, and ſinging thy iuſt commandments and lawe, vvhich make thy ſeruant iuſt.

verses.text: I haue bene mindful in <na>(k)</na> the night of thy name o Lord: and haue kept thy law.

notes.label: k
notes.text: In perſecution, and in al tribulation, I kept thy law becauſe I would not dishonour thy name.

verses.text: This was done to me: <na>(l)</na> becauſe I ſought after thy iuſtifications.

notes.label: l
notes.text: And my tribulation eſpecially fel vpon me, becauſe I ſought to be iuſtified by keping thy law.

verses.heading: Heth. Life.
verses.text: My <na>(a)</na> portion o Lord, I ſayd to keepe thy law.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The Prophet procedeth ſpeaking in the perſon of the iuſt tending to perfection, and ſaying : This is my happie choiſe, that I deſire no other enheritance, nor poſſeſſion, but to kepe Gods Law.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> I beſought thy face, with al my hart: haue mercie on me according to thy <na>[1]</na> word.

notes.label: b
notes.text: And ſeeing this excedeth my proper ſtreingth, I prayed God of his mercie to make me able to kepe it.
eloquium.

verses.text: I <na>(c)</na> thought vpon my wayes: and conuerted my feete vnto thy teſtimonies.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Pondering my former actions, I turned my pathes to obſerue more perfectly the Law, which God hath teſtified to be the right way.

verses.text: I <na>(d)</na> am prepared, and am not trubled: to keepe thy commandments.

notes.label: d
notes.text: With prompnes of mind, and without heſitation I reſolued to kepe the commandments.

verses.text: The <na>(e)</na> cordes of ſinners haue wrapped me round about: and <na>(f)</na> I haue not forgotten thy law.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The wicked laide cordes, nettes, or ſnares to intrappe, and hinder me,

notes.label: f
notes.text: but I kept thy law fresh in memorie.

verses.text: At <na>(g)</na> midnight I roſe to confeſſe to thee; for the iudgements of thy iuſtification.

notes.label: g
notes.text: That this is not vnderſtood only myſtically in time of affliction, but alſo literally and prophetically, that ſome ſpecial ſeruantes of God, ſhould obſerue a godlie profeſſion of praying at midnight, the vvord [I roſe] maketh it probable. S. Paul & Silas, either of a holie cuſtome, or at leaſt vpon ſpecial occaſion (and ſuch occaſions were to them, and others frequent) prayed, and praiſed God at midnight. And novv in the Church of Chriſt ſome religions men pray, and praiſe God continually at midnight ; beſides other houres, mentioned more diſtinctly v. 164.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> I am partaker of al that feare thee: and that keepe thy commandments.

notes.label: h
notes.text: A great benefite, and a ſingular conſolation, that al true liuing members of Chriſt, are partakers of al the prayers, good workes, and merites, of the whole Church militant and triumphant. VVhich in our Crede is called, The Communion of Sainctes.

verses.text: The <na>(i)</na> earth o Lord is ful of thy mercie: <na>(k)</na> teach me thy iuſtifications.

notes.label: i
notes.text: So great is the mercie of God, extended, communicated, and multiplied in the whole earth :

notes.label: k
notes.text: Inſtruct me, and direct me therfore o God, that I may lerne and obſerue thy law, and ſo be iuſtified, and made participant of ſo great mercie.

verses.heading: Teth. Good.
verses.text: Thou haſt <na>(a)</na> done bountie with thy ſeruant o Lord: <na>(b)</na> according to thy word.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Dealt very bountifully

notes.label: b
notes.text: as thou didſt promiſe.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Teach me goodneſſe, <na>(d)</na> and diſcipline, and <na>(e)</na> knowledge: <na>(f)</na> becauſe I haue beleued thy commandments.

notes.label: c
notes.text: He that hath bountifully receiued grace at Gods hand, prayeth for more grace, that he may be beneficial to others in releuing the needie ;

notes.label: d
notes.text: in inſtructing the ignorant,

notes.label: e
notes.text: in perſwading to kepe the law of God :

notes.label: f
notes.text: becauſe he hath lerned and beleueth the commandments, by which he is bond to loue, and haue care of his neighbour.

verses.text: Before I <na>(g)</na> was humbled I offended: <na>(h)</na> therfore haue I kept thy <na>[1]</na> word.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Before I was afflicted, I often fel into ſinne :

notes.label: h
notes.text: but vexation gaue me vnderſtanding, therfore now I kepe thy law.
eloquium.

verses.text: Thou art good: and in thy goodneſſe teach me thy iuſtifications.
The iniquitie of <na>(i)</na> the prowd is multiplied vpon me: <na>(k)</na> but I in al my hart wil ſearch thy commandments.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Contemners of thy law haue endeuored to intangle me,

notes.label: k
notes.text: but I perſiſt in keping thy commandments. As before. v. 51. 61.

verses.text: Their hart is <na>(l)</na> crudded together as milke: <na>(m)</na> but I haue meditated thy law.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Though the wicked combine themſelues together againſt me,

notes.label: m
notes.text: yet I conſider, that it is neceſſarie to perſeuer in thy law.

verses.text: It is good for me that thou haſt humbled me: that I may learne thy iuſtifications.
The law of thy mouth is <na>(n)</na> good vnto me, aboue thouſands of gold, and ſiluer.

notes.label: n
notes.text: A clere compariſon, that it is better to kepe Gods law, which bringeth life euerlaſting, then to haue al the riches & kingdoms of this world.

verses.heading: Iod. Beginning.
verses.text: Thy handes haue made me, and formed me: <na>(a)</na> geue me vnderſtanding, and I wil learne thy commandmentes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: God being our Creator, we may with confidence pray him to illuminate our mindes, that we may lerne what is his pleaſure, and ſo endeuour to fulfil it.

verses.text: They that feare thee <na>(b)</na> shal ſee me, & shal reioyce: becauſe I haue much hoped in thy wordes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Others that loue God wil be gladde to ſee me alſo ſerue him.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> I know o Lord that thy iudgements are equitie: and in thy truth thou haſt humbled me. <na>(d)</na>

notes.label: c
notes.text: The iuſt being afflicted, and not ſeing the particular cauſe therof, yet knoweth and confeſſeth, that God doth it for moſt iuſt cauſe.

notes.label: d
notes.text: And therfore with patience prayeth for comforth, as foloweth :

verses.text: Let thy mercie be done to comfort me, according to thy <na>[1]</na> word vnto thy ſeruant.

notes.text: eloquium.

verses.text: Let thy commiſerations come to me, and I <na>(e)</na> shal liue: becauſe thy law is my meditation.

notes.label: e
notes.text: who am almoſt dead in tribulation.

verses.text: Let the prowde <na>(f)</na> be confounded, becauſe they haue done vniuſtly toward me: but I wil be exerciſed in thy commandments.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The iuſt alſo prayeth that the wicked may be ashamed, and conuerted, for ſo the hebrew word here ſignifieth, though it is alſo lawful to deſire tho iuſt punishment of obſtinate ſinners.

verses.text: Let them <na>(g)</na> be conuerted to me that feare thee: and that know thy teſtimonies.

notes.label: g
notes.text: He prayeth againe for conuerſion of the wicked, and to haue peace with them.

verses.text: Let my hart be made immaculate in thy iuſtifications, that I be not confounded.

verses.heading: Caph. Hand, or Palme of the hand.
verses.text: My ſoule hath fainted for <na>(a)</na> thy ſaluation: and I haue much hoped in thy word.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Manie iuſt of the old teſtament moſt feruently deſired the coming of Chriſt our Sauiour, as our Lord himſelfe teſtifieth, Mat. 13. v. 17. And now the iuſt deſire his coming in glorie, 2. Tim. 4. v. 8.

verses.text: Myne eies haue fayled for thy <na>[1]</na> word, ſaying: <na>(b)</na> When wilt thou comfort me?

notes.label: b
notes.text: Delayed hope afflicteth.
eloquium.

verses.text: Becauſe I am made <na>(c)</na> as a bottel in the hoare froſt: I haue not forgotten thy iuſtifications.

notes.label: c
notes.text: As a leather bottel made of a beaſts skinne, congeled with the froſt, and after partched in ſmoke, ſo is the bodie of the iuſt mortified by diuers ſortes of afflictions, made a new bottel fitte to receiue new wine, that is, perfect doctrin of Chriſtian life, as of faſting, and other auſteritie, wherof our Sauiour ſpeaketh, Mat. 9. v. 17.

verses.text: How manie are <na>(d)</na> the daies of thy ſeruant: when wilt thou doe iudgement on them that perſecute me?

notes.label: d
notes.text: Such is mans infirmitie, yea of the iuſt, that he apprehendeth tribulations to be very long, and therfore deſireth conſummation ; and that without ſinne, ſo he ſtil ſubmitte his wil to Gods wil.

verses.text: The vniuſt haue told me <na>(e)</na> fables: but not as thy law.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Friuolous idle tailes, which are not according to Gods law.

verses.text: Al thy commandmentes are truth: they haue vniuſtly perſecuted me, helpe me.
They haue welnere <na>(f)</na> made an end of me in the earth: but I haue not forſaken thy commandments.

notes.label: f
notes.text: I was in great danger, but am not ouerthrowne.

verses.text: According to <na>(g)</na> thy mercie quicken me: and I shal keepe the teſtimonies of thy mouth.

notes.label: g
notes.text: And by thy merciful grace shal perſiſt.

verses.heading: Lamed. Discipline.
verses.text: For euer Lord <na>(a)</na> thy word is permanent in heauen.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The praiſe of Gods workes ; which are firme and parmanent in the order, wherin he ſet them.

verses.text: Thy truth in generation and generation: thou haſt founded the earth, and it is permanent.
By thy ordinance the day contineweth: becauſe <na>(b)</na> al thinges ſerue thee.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Al thinges of this world, man excepted, do Gods wil.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> But that thy law is my meditation: I had then <na>(d)</na> perhaps perished in my humiliation.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Man, except he meditate Gods law, and therby be holden vp, is in danger,

notes.label: d
notes.text: perhaps in eternal tentation to perish eternally. For he can neuer riſe out of mortal ſinne, by his owne powre, and al should perish, if Gods mercie did not ſpare ſome, and geue them new effectual grace to repent.

verses.text: I wil not forget thy iuſtifications for euer: becauſe in them thou haſt quickned me.
I am thine, ſaue me: becauſe <na>(e)</na> I haue ſought out thy iuſtifications.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Alwayes vnderſtood, that Gods grace preuented, els no man can ſeeke to obſerue the commandments.

verses.text: Sinners haue expected me to deſtroy me: I vnderſtood thy teſtimonies.
<na>(f)</na> Of al conſummation I haue ſene the end: <na>(g)</na> thy commandment is exceding large.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Al worldlie thinges haue their conſummation and end :

notes.label: g
notes.text: Gods commandment continueth euer. For we are perpetually bond, to loue and ſerue God : to loue our neighboures, yea and enimies. The reward alſo for keping Gods commandments, & punishment for breaking them, are eternal without end.

verses.heading: Mem. Of them.
verses.text: <na>(a)</na> How haue I loued thy law ô Lord! al the day it is my meditation.

notes.label: a
notes.text: It is meruel to a perfect iuſt man, that he hath ſo much loued, and obſerued Gods law. By acknowleging wherof, he yeldeth praiſe and thankes to God, whoſe gift it is.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Aboue mine enemies thou haſt made me wiſe by thy commaundment: becauſe it is to me for euer.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The fruictes of obſeruing Gods law are manie and great. Amongſt others, it maketh the obſeruer, wiſer then his enimies.

verses.text: Aboue <na>(c)</na> al that taught me haue I vnderſtood: becauſe thy teſtimonies are my meditation.

notes.label: c
notes.text: It maketh the obſeruer wiſer, then his temporal maiſters, that taught him, towit, then thoſe that teach wel, and do not performe the ſame.

verses.text: Aboue <na>(d)</na> ancientes haue I vnderſtood: becauſe I haue ſought thy commandments.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Yonger in yeares that kepe Gods commandments, are wiſer then the more ancient that kepe them not.

verses.text: I haue ſtaied my feete from al euil way: that I may keepe thy wordes.
I haue not declined from thy iudgements: becauſe thou haſt ſet me a law.
<na>(e)</na> How ſweete are thy <na>[1]</na> wordes to my iawes, more then honie to my mouth!

notes.label: e
notes.text: An other fruict is the ſwetnes, which the iuſt feeleth in his owne ſoule.
eloquia.

verses.text: By thy commandments I haue vnderſtood: therfore haue I <na>(f)</na> hated al the way of iniquitie.

notes.label: f
notes.text: It brideth alſo iuſt hatred to ſinne.

verses.heading: Nun. Euerlasting.
verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Thy word is a lampe to my feete, and a light to my pathes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The word or law of God declared by Prophets, Paſtors, or other Preachers is the ordinarie meanes for others to lerne, how to direct their wayes, and actions.

verses.text: I <na>(b)</na> ſware, and haue determined to keepe the iudgements of thy iuſtice.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Such profeſſion Gods people made in the old law, in Circumciſion, or at other times : Chriſtians make it in Baptiſme.

verses.text: I am <na>(c)</na> humbled exceedingly ô Lord: quicken me according to thy word.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Al that wil liue godly in Chriſt Ieſus, shal ſuffer perſecution. 2. Tim. 3. v. 12.

verses.text: The <na>(d)</na> voluntaries of my mouth make acceptable ô Lord: and teach me thy iudgementes.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Beſides the commandments, the iuſt alſo offer voluntarie workes of ſupererogation, acceptable to God.

verses.text: My <na>(e)</na> ſoule is in my handes alwaies: and I haue not forgotten thy law.

notes.label: e
notes.text: By this Hebrew prouerb is ſignified, that a iuſt mans temporal life is in continual danger, as the thing that is in ones hand, is readie to be laide by, put out of his hand, or to be by and by diſpoſed of, or may forthwith fal from his hand.

verses.text: Sinners laid a ſnare for me: and I haue not erred from thy commandments.
For inheritance I haue purchaſed thy teſtimonies for euer: becauſe they are the ioy of my hart.
I haue inclined my hart to doe thy iuſtifications for euer, <na>(f)</na> for reward.

notes.label: f
notes.text: A moſt euident place, that the keping of Gods commandments merite reward, and are rightly obſerued in reſpect of reward.

verses.heading: Samech. Helpe.
verses.text: I haue <na>(a)</na> hated the vniuſt: and I haue <na>(b)</na> loued thy law.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Not anie mortal man is to be hated, in his perſon, but his iniquitie, by which he is an enimie to Gods law,

notes.label: b
notes.text: vvhich euerie iuſt man loueth.

verses.text: Thou art my helper, and protectour: and vpon thy word I haue much hoped.
<na>(c)</na> Depart from me ye malignant: and I wil ſearch the commandmentes of my God.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Whoſoeuer wil ſeriouſly and ſecurely ſearch the law of God, muſt auoide the conuerſation of euil men.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Recciue me according to thy <na>[1]</na> word, <na>(e)</na> and I shal liue: and <na>(f)</na> confound me not of myn expectation.

notes.label: d
notes.text: A general and very fitte prayer, when we addict ourſelues by a firme reſolution to ſerue God, beſeching him to receiue vs into his protection :

notes.label: e
notes.text: wherby ſpiritual life is conſerued :

notes.label: f
notes.text: which we pray vvith great confidence, becauſe he hath promiſed to heare thoſe that ſeeke, aske, and knocke at the dore of his grace.
eloquium.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Helpe me, and I shal be ſaued: and I wil meditate in thy iuſtifications alwayes.

notes.label: g
notes.text: VVe muſt pray alſo that he ſuffer vs not to be confounded, or made fruſtrate of the reward which we expect ; for hope confoundeth not, if charitie be povvred in our hartes, by the Holie Ghoſt, which is geuen vs. Rom. 5. v. 5.

verses.text: Thou haſt <na>(h)</na> deſpiſed al that reuolt from thy iudgementes: <na>(i)</na> becauſe their cogitation is vniuſt.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God reiecteth ſinners :

notes.label: i
notes.text: ſo long as they thincke peruerſly : that is, vntil by his grace, ſome returne to a better mind, which of themſelues they can neuer do.

verses.text: Al the ſinners of the earth I <na>(k)</na> haue reputed preuaricatours: therfore haue I loued thy teſtimonies.

notes.label: k
notes.text: As God accounteth of ſinners, ſo the iuſt alſo eſtemeth them, conforming his iudgement to Gods.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> Pearſe my flesh with thy feare: for I am afrayd of thy iudgementes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Seruil feare is profitable as this place maketh euident : though perfect charitie afterwards ſucceding, expelleth that feare, and moueth to do vvel for the loue of God, not for feare of punishment. 1. Ioan. 4.

verses.heading: Ain. A fountaine, or an eye.
verses.text: I <na>(a)</na> haue done iudgement and iuſtice: <na>(b)</na> deliuer me not to them that calumniate me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The iuſt againe in feruent zele, not arrogantly, but confidently profeſſing his innocencie,

notes.label: b
notes.text: prayeth to be defended from calumniators.

verses.text: Recciue thy ſeruant <na>(c)</na> vnto good: let not the prowde calumniate me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Grant therfore o God the good, and lawful requeſt which I demand.

verses.text: Mine eies haue fayled. <na>(d)</na> after thy ſaluation: and for the <na>[1]</na> word of thy iuſtice.

notes.label: d
notes.text: By long expecting to be deliuered, and ſaued from tribulation.
eloquium.

verses.text: Doe with thy ſeruant according to thy mercie: and teache me thy iuſtifications.
I am thy ſeruant: geue me vnderſtanding, that I may know thy teſtimonies.
<na>(e)</na> It is time to doe ô Lord: <na>(f)</na> they haue diſſipated thy law.

notes.label: e
notes.text: It is time, and hiegh time, ſaith feruent zele of the iuſt man, that God deliuer the innocent :

notes.label: f
notes.text: vvhen the vvicked haue not only perſecuted the good, but haue alſo contemptuouſly made hauooke of Gods lavv, and true religion.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Therfore haue I loued thy commandementes, aboue gold and topazius:

notes.label: g
notes.text: For this zele of Gods law ſo deſpiſed, and diſputed, the iuſt more and more loueth, that vvhich the vvicked ſo deadly hate.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Therfore was I directed to al thy commandementes: <na>(i)</na> al wicked way I haue hated.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Euen by the mortal hate of the vvicked I ſaw, that Gods law is moſt excellent, and therfore addicted myſelfe ſo much the more to loue it,

notes.label: i
notes.text: and to hate al wicked wayes.

verses.heading: Phe. Mouth.
verses.text: Thy <na>(a)</na> teſtimonies are meruelous: <na>(b)</na> therfore hath my ſoule ſearched them.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Gods meruelous povvre and vviſdom, teſtified by his workes and commandments,

notes.label: b
notes.text: worthely inuite iuſt ſoules, to meditate and contemplate the ſame.

verses.text: The <na>(c)</na> declaration of thy <na>[1]</na> wordes doth illuminate: and geueth vnderſtanding to litle ones.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Firſt entrance into knowlege of holie Scripture, illuminateth the vnderſtanding of the humble, wherby they procede to know more.
ſermonum.

verses.text: I <na>(d)</na> opened my mouth, and drew breath: becauſe I deſired thy commandments.

notes.label: d
notes.text: By this Metaphor, of gaping, or vvide opening the mouth, and drawing breath, the Prophet deſcribeth the great deſire of the iuſt, to know and kepe Gods commandments.

verses.text: Looke vpon me, and haue mercie on me, according to <na>(e)</na> the iudgement of them that loue thy name.

notes.label: e
notes.text: According to thy accuſtomed equitie, in shewing mercie to them that loue thy name.

verses.text: Direct my ſteppes according to thy <na>[1]</na> word: and let not anie iniuſtice haue domination ouer me.

notes.text: eloquium.

verses.text: Redeme me from the calumnies of men: that I may kepe thy commondmentes.
Illuminate <na>(f)</na> thy face vpon thy ſeruant: and teach me thy iuſtifications.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Let thy diuine Maieſtie looke vpon me with fauorable countenance.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Mine eies haue gushed forth iſſues of waters: becauſe they haue not kept thy law.

notes.label: g
notes.text: True repentance conſiſteth not only in purpoſe to auoide ſinne hereafter, which in dede is firſt required, but alſo in ſorow and lamentation for ſinnes paſt.

verses.heading: Sade. Iustice.
verses.text: Thou art iuſt ô Lord: and <na>(a)</na> thy iudgement is right.

notes.label: a
notes.text: God being eſſentially iuſt of himſelfe, maketh men iuſt according to right iudgement, by geuing them grace of mercie, wherwith they cooperating, are iuſt by iuſtice in dede inherent in their ſoules, not by imputation only : for it were not right iudgement to impute, or account man iuſt, vvho is not ſo in dede.

verses.text: Thou haſt commanded <na>(b)</na> iuſtice thy teſtimonies: and thy veritie excedingly.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The ſame is more confirmed, by theſe three ſynonyma, Iuſtice, Teſtimonies, Veritie, ſignifying the law of God, moſt earneſtly commanded.

verses.text: My Zele hath made me to pine away: becauſe mine enimies haue forgotten thy wordes.
Thy <na>[1]</na> word is <na>(c)</na> fired excedingly: and thy ſeruant hath loued it.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Gods law is as pure as anie thing purged by fire.
eloquia.

verses.text: I am <na>(d)</na> a yongman, and contemned: I <na>(e)</na> haue not forgotten thy iuſtifications.

notes.label: d
notes.text: A iuſt man is often iudged ignorant, immature, vnexperienced, by the worldlie wiſe ;

notes.label: e
notes.text: but in dede is wiſe, in that he forgetteth not to kepe the law, which maketh him iuſt.

verses.text: Thy iuſtice, is iuſtice for euer: and thy law is veritie.
Tribulation, and diſtreſſe haue found me: thy commandments are my meditation.
Thy teſtimonies are equitie for euer <na>(f)</na> geue me vnderſtanding, and I shal liue.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Hauing profeſſed the neceſſitie of perfect iuſtice, he concludeth this Octonarie, praying to be illuminated in his vnderſtanding, that ſo he may attaine iuſtice, and liue therby.

verses.heading: Coph. Vocation.
verses.text: I <na>(a)</na> haue cried in my whole hart, heare me ô Lord: I wil ſeeke after thy iuſtifications.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Moſt precious and feruent inuocation of God for his grace, is neceſſarie, to the fulfilling of his law.

verses.text: I haue cried to thee, ſaue me: that I may keepe thy commandmentes.
I haue preuented in <na>(b)</na> maturitie, and <na>(c)</na> haue cried: becauſe I hoped much in thy wordes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: I haue preuented the mature, and ordinarie time of the night, and haue prayed

notes.label: c
notes.text: very attentiuely.

verses.text: Mine eies <na>(d)</na> haue preuented early vnto thee: that I might meditate thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Againe in the morning I haue preuented the accuſtomed time of prayer.
eloquia.

verses.text: Heare my voice according to thy mercie ô Lord: and according to <na>(e)</na> thy iudgement quicken me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: According to thy accuſtomed maner of shewing mercie, ſhew it me, that therby I may liue.

verses.text: They that perſecute me haue approched to iniquitie: but from thy law they are made far of.
Thou art <na>(f)</na> nigh ô Lord: and al thy wayes are truth.

notes.label: f
notes.text: God is alwayes readie to heare al that ſincerly inuocate him.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> From the beginning I knewe of thy teſtimonies: that thou haſt founded them for euer.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Gods law is the ſame in ſubſtance from the beginning of the world, and wil be for euer.

verses.heading: Res. Head.
verses.text: See <na>(a)</na> my humiliation, and deliuer me: becauſe I haue not forgotten thy law.

notes.label: a
notes.text: An other prayer of the iuſt in affliction.

verses.text: Iudge my iudgement, & redeme me: for thy <na>[1]</na> word <na>(b)</na> quicken thou me.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Conſerue me in thy grace.
eloquium.

verses.text: Saluation is far from ſinners: becauſe they haue not ſought after thy iuſtifications.
Thy mercies are manie ô Lord: <na>(c)</na> according to thy iudgement quicken me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: As before v. 149.

verses.text: There are manie that perſecute me, and afflict me: I haue not declined from thy teſtimonies.
I ſaw the preuaricatours, and I pyned away: becauſe they kept not thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.text: eloquia.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> See that I haue loued thy commandmentes ô Lord: in thy mercie quicken me.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Sincere profeſſion of innocencie is no arrogancy.

verses.text: The <na>(e)</na> beginning of thy wordes is truth: <na>(f)</na> al the iudgementes of thy iuſtice are for euer.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Gods eſſencial veritie is the beginning from vvhence, as from the fountaine al other truthes are deriued :

notes.label: f
notes.text: And al commandments proceding from this firſt truth, are for euer immutable.

verses.heading: Sin. Tooth.
verses.text: Princes haue perſecuted me <na>(a)</na> without cauſe: and my <na>(b)</na> hart hath bene afrayd of thy wordes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Potent wicked men perſecute the godlie without cauſe, that is, vvithout anie iuſt reaſon mouing them ; & without the effect intended by them, which is to drawe Gods ſeruants from truth, and equitie ;

notes.label: b
notes.text: vvhoſe hart being poſſeſſed vvith the true feare of God, they perſiſt in keping Gods commandments.

verses.text: I <na>(c)</na> wil reioyce at thy <na>[1]</na> wordes: as he that findeth manie ſpoyles.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Yea they alſo reioyce in keping the commandments, vvith ſuch difficultie, as thoſe doe, that gaining the victorie ouer their enimies, carie away great and rich ſpoyles.
eloquia.

verses.text: I haue hated iniquitie, and abhorred it: but thy law I haue loued.
<na>(d)</na> Seuentimes in the day. I haue ſayd praiſe to thee, for the iudgements of thy iuſtice.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Euerie day the iuſt praiſe God often, ſignified by the number of ſeuen. From hence alſo the Church of Chriſt tooke example to inſtitute the ſeuen Canonical Houres, which is the ordinarie Eccleſiaſtical Office ; conſiſting, as S. Iſidorus, and manie other Fathers teſtifie, of Hymnes, Pſalmes, Canticles, Antiphones, Leſſons, Reſponſories, & other Prayers & Praiſes, diſtributed into diſtinct times, beginning in the night, wherof that part is called the Nocturne (one or three according to the diuerſitie of the Office) and perteineth to one or more of the foure Vigiles, into vvhich ſouldiars diuide the vvhole night. Whereto alſo the Laudes are added. Then Prime, in the morning. Aftervvards, the Third houre, Sixt, Ninth ; and in the euening, Euenſongue, and Compline. Againſt vvhich moſt ancient and religious Conſtitution, eſpecially againſt the part called Vigiles, or Nocturnes, certaine Heretikes repined, and calumniated the Churches cuſtome, as ſuperfluous and vnfructful to ſpiritual worke, violating of Gods ordinance, who made the night for reſt, and the day for laboure. For which cauſe they were called Nyctazontes, Somnicoloſi, Drowſy heretikes, As the ſame S. Iſidorus teſtifieth li. 1. c. 22. de Offic. Eccles. S. Ierom Epiſt. ad Riparium, noteth the ſame hereſie in Vigilantius, calling him Dormitantius, becauſe he reprehended holie Vigiles, as if it were better to ſleepe, then wake in time of Diuine ſeruice. VViclif alſo raiſed vp the ſame hereſie, as witneſſeth Thomas VValdenſis. To. 3. Tit. 3. c. 21. Laſtly Luther and al his broode. But the holie obſeruation of Canonical Houres is proued, by manie ancient Fathers to be altogether agreable to the holie Scriptures, both of the old and new Teſtament. So S. Beda. in 18. Luc. & li. 4. c. 7. Hiſt. Angl. S. Gregorie the Great li. 3. Dialogi. c. 14. S. Auguſtin (Ser. 55. de temp.) exhorting the people to riſe early to the Vigiles (or Nocturnes) and in aniewiſe to come to the Third houre, Sixt, and Ninth. Let none (ſaith he) withdraw himſelfe from the holie worke, but whom either ſicknes, or publique vtilitie, or perhaps ſome great neceſſitie holdeth backe. S. Ierom. Epiſt. 22. ad Euſtoch. & in Epitaph. Paule. c. 10. maketh expreſſe mention of the Third houre. Sixt, Ninth, Morning, and Euening ; alſo of Midnight, adding that no Religious is ignorant that ſometimes they muſt riſe to Diuine Seruice, twiſe, yea thriſe in the night. S. Baſil, in Regulis fuſius diſput. ad Interrog 37. & de Inſtit. Monachorum. firſt. sheweth this ordinance to be agreable to the holie Scriptures, and namely to this place of the Pſalmiſt. S. Cyprian in fine expoſit. Orat. Domini. affirmeth that beſides the three houres in which Daniel and his felovves prayed, the Church of Chriſt hath added more. And (as manie ſuppoſe) S. Clement li. 8. Conſtitut.
